News.title: We don’t need a deal with Iran, Trump says as he sidelines JD Vance peace talks despite election bloodbath
News.content:
Next

DONALD Trump has said he does not need a peace deal with Iran following the midterm election bloodbath.

The US leader also ordered vice president JD Vance to shift his attention away from securing peace with Tehran and onto “Democrat corruption” in American states.



Trump said in a Truth Social post: “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed.

“We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!”



The US leader added that Vance would be focusing more on alleged “crime and corruption” in Democrat-run cities and states rather than the spiralling Iran war.

In the days leading up to the midterms earlier this month, Vance reportedly reached out to mullah regime hardliner Mohsen Rezaei.



The olive branch was extended in a bid to restart peace talks, according to the Wall Street Journal.

His attempts came amid mounting speculation US voters were becoming frustrated by the Iran war.



Trump has also reportedly been blasting the memorandum of understanding that Vance helped broker in June over recent weeks.

He argued the pause in fighting gave Tehran enough time to rebuild its military before Washington imposed its blockade in the Strait of Hormuz.

Vance directly blamed the recent Republican hammering – where they lost their majority in both houses of Congress – on the Iran war.

Trump admitted the analysis was “largely true”.

But he insisted he doesn’t regret anything despite the huge Democratic win last week.



Trump claimed several times before the midterms that a peace deal was within reach.

He said on the eve of the election: “Oil Prices are DROPPING LIKE A ROCK, down almost $10 a Barrel, A RECORD, because people feel that there will not be a War with Iran.

“Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible. It could happen!”

The US president also said earlier this week he expected the war was “going to be ending fairly soon”.

Trump had said on Monday following talks in the Gulf region: “Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, and others, would prefer the status quo, in other words, a continuation of the Greatest Naval Blockade in History.”



He added: “Should there be any change with respect to developments in the Middle East, the United States of America is ‘locked and loaded’ and ready to go.

“At this point, however, that seems to be quite unlikely.

“Israel, and the entire Middle East, are protected from Iranian danger and threats.

“We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this Conflict, and will ensure that America’s interests are at all times protected.”

Trump also told C-SPAN when asked how long the conflict could last: “We could knock it out fast, or we could knock it out over a short, not a long period of time.”



The US leader had said at the United Nations General Assembly in September Iran was likely waiting to see the outcome of the midterm elections to make a deal.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said: “I believe we’ll make a deal right after the election because it doesn’t make sense for them not to.

“They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election.”

News.title: Navy chiefs admit ‘we must do better’ as nuclear sub crew forced to spend record SEVEN MONTHS underwater
News.content:
Next

NAVY chiefs yesterday admitted they must do better after the crew of one of our few working subs was forced to spend a record seven months at sea.

The extraordinary feat aboard HMS Vengeance was needed to maintain the UK’s nuclear deterrent — with other subs hit by maintenance problems.



The 490ft vessels were only designed for 80-day missions.

But six of the previous seven patrols have lasted more than 200 days owing to a shortage of working alternatives.



Crew get one text a week from home but cannot transmit back for fear of revealing the vessel’s location.

First Sea Lord General Sir Gwyn Jenkins said: “I have nothing but tremendous respect for our sailors who crew the deterrent.

“Roughly 150 people are on patrol, 365 days a year in order to keep the whole of Nato safe.” But he admitted: “We need to improve our submarine maintenance.”

HMS Vengeance, armed with Trident 2 nuclear missiles, notched 214 days at sea yesterday.

It was due to return last week but had to extend its patrol when HMS Vanguard, the sub sent to replace it, returned unexpectedly for repairs.

Sir Gwynn added: “Of all the things I do in my daily activities, improving submarine maintenance and readiness is what I focus on by far the most — because it is the most important thing that we do.”



The previous record patrol was 205 days, set by HMS Vanguard this year.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said his admiration for nuclear submariners was “second to none”.

But he acknowledged the UK needed to invest more upgrading the deterrent submarines.

The four nuclear Vanguard-class subs were all due to retire between 2018-24. The replacement Dreadnought class are a decade behind schedule.

News.title: Fourteen dead in 23-vehicle smash that turned into inferno after truck driver loses control
News.content:
Next

AT least 14 people have been killed and dozens more injured after a 23-car smash which sparked a huge inferno.

Chaos broke out on a road in the United Arab Emirates after a truck driver lost control of his vehicle just before midnight on Thursday.



The fatal smash unfolded on a highway with “slow-moving traffic” by the entrance of the eastern emirate.

The truck’s impact sparked a fire before the horror blaze spread to several other cars.



It resulted in a “heavy loss of life”, authorities said.

At least 30 people were injured and rushed to hospital.

DNA tests are being run to identify the bodies of the victims.

Some were Emirati nationals, they said.

It is also understood there were several Indian citizens caught up in the deadly pile-up.

Officials said the truck collided with another car before rolling over and striking other vehicles.



Emergency services rushed to the scene to extinguish the blaze.

Victims were raced to hospitals and the site was cordoned off.

Emirati authorities thanked police and expressed their deepest sympathies to those affected.

Around half of the wounded victims have since been discharged while the others remain in hospital.

They are from the UAE, Oman, Brazil, India, Pakistan, Jordan and Egypt, according to authorities.

News.title: Moment thief nicks £800 orangutan statue before fleeing on bike with giant figure on handlebars
News.content:
Next

THIS is the moment a cheeky thief nicks an orangutan statue before fleeing on a bike with the pillaged primate riding shotgun.

Bizarre CCTV shows prolific thief Derek Lundgren, 61, forcing open the doors at a Horningsea garden centre while awkwardly hauling an orangutan under his arm.



Lundgren then placed the monkey on his handlebars before pedalling off.

The £800 statue was pinched from Scotsdales Garden Centre in Cambridge on September 7.



Cops later charged Lundgren who is from Sawston in Cambs.

He pleaded guilty to the theft which was in breach of three suspended sentences.

He was sentenced to one year and 11 months in prison at Ipswich Magistrates’ Court on November 9.

PC Denzel Boachie said: “Lundgren is a prolific thief who has continued to offend despite being given previous opportunities by the courts.



“His repeated offending has now caught up with him and he will spend time behind bars.”

In October 2023, Lundgren was reportedly caught with a drill – which he stole from B&Q – down his trousers, according to Cambridgeshire Live.

Just a month later, he reportedly stole a box of Christmas lights.

A little over a week after that, he allegedly took washing powder, beer, steak, and coffee from a Co-op, according to the outlet.

It comes after a “bog bandit” was caught on CCTV allegedly raiding a pub toilet.



Footage shows a man with a backpack, who staff suspect to be the culprit, entering and leaving the premises without buying a drink.

Employees at the Ship Inn Pub in Ripley, Surrey said the reported bandit stole £35 worth of soap, toilet roll, hand towels, plants, lotion, and signs from the wall.

When the man had left the gents, pub staff found the urinals clogged with loo roll, and the toilet completely raided.

News.title: Moment two French guards collapse next to Macron during ceremonial welcome at Elysee Palace
News.content:
Next

THIS is the moment two French honour guards collapse next to Emmanuel Macron during a ceremonial welcome at the Elysee Palace.

Astonishing footage showed a sabre-wielding soldier stumbling over just seconds before another lost his footing off-camera.



The baffling ordeal unfolded as the French president welcomed his Slovakian counterpart Peter Pellegrini in Paris on Wednesday.

In the clip, one of the guards can be seen swaying off balance and lowering his sword before crashing backwards into a pillar.



He remains still on the floor while a group of officials hurry over to his aid.

The soldier is then seen being carried away by two security personnel.



Just moments later, a second guard fell over off-camera, according to Le Parisien.

Macron appeared gob-smacked as he escorted Pellegrini through the chaotic scene and into the palace.



A French presidential source said both men suffered from “fainting attacks”.

But they provided no additional details and insisted there were no issues.

They said: “Both of them were swiftly taken care of, and everything is fine.”



The dramatic clip marked the beginning of Pellegrini’s trip to the French capital, to discuss EU enlargement and Ukraine among other issues.

Pellegrini said on X: “We reaffirmed our shared commitment to taking the strategic partnership between Slovakia and France to an even higher level.”

He added: “At a time of profound global challenges, Europe needs strong partnerships, unity and determination.

“Slovakia and France stand ready to work hand in hand for a stronger, safer and more prosperous Europe.”

Macron visited Dublin following the summit, where he doubled down again on France‘s support for Ukraine.

News.title: Iranian hitman illegal immigrant convicted of spying after being promised up to £150k to carry out violence against UK
News.content:
DISSIDENTS TARGETED Iranian hitman illegal immigrant convicted of spying after being promised up to £150k to carry out violence against UK







Next

TWO Iranians who got into the UK illegally were yesterday convicted of spying.

Hitman Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, was recruited to target and attack two dissident journalists and a pro-Israel lawyer.



He was promised up to £150,000 by agents of the Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps to carry out acts of violence in Britain.

Asylum seeker Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, helped him with planning.



The pair, of West London, were found guilty at Woolwich crown court of assisting a foreign intelligence service. They will be sentenced on December 17. Another Iranian, Shapoor Noori, 57, of Ealing, was acquitted of the same charge.

Ex-gym owner Sepahvand was also found guilty of preparing to commit serious violence against a person in the UK.

He arrived in a lorry in 2016 and was granted temporary asylum on appeal after converting to Christianity. He was wanted for 32 robberies in Iran where in his absence he was jailed for 4½ years and sentenced to 70 lashes. He was believed to be claiming UK benefits while selling cars from his home.

IRGC officers sent Sepahvand files including images of targets, cars, work addresses, and names of pets. Jonathan Turner, of UK Lawyers for Israel, and two Iranian journalists were in his crosshairs.

Prosecutor Bill Emlyn Jones said the ultimate objective was at least one target “would be subjected to serious violence, no doubt as retribution for their criticism of the Iranian regime”. Sepahvand was paid only £5,000 but did have three months shaved off his robbery sentence in Iran.

Sepahvand and Manesh, who had arrived by small boat and claimed asylum in 2022, used ChatGPT for further research on targets — only the second time an AI tool has been used in a hostile state threat case.



And it is the first time Iranians in the UK have been accused of spying for the IRGC. Their plot was foiled in May last year — with the pair failing to find any targets — following an intelligence-led operation by counter-terror police and MI5.

Security Minister Dan Jarvis said: “Threats from Iran are grave and real. This case sends a clear message to those acting in their malign interests, that they will not succeed.”

News.title: Fury as Angela Rayner approves Piddington migrant camp for 1,200 asylum seekers near tiny village after vote to leave UK
News.content:
Next

ANGELA Rayner has triggered fury by approving plans to house 1,200 migrants next to an Oxfordshire village.

The Cabinet Minister gave the green light despite the residents of Piddington holding their own referendum opposing the scheme.



Fearful women in the area have resorted to self-defence lessons ahead of the influx of asylum seekers.

Converting the former military base MoD Bicester on the site is expected to cost an estimated £250 million, reports have suggested.. It was previously a military equipment storage facility.



Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has said that such bases are “the future for asylum accommodation”.

Tory MP Greg Smith said: “Disaster – the Labour Government have approved MOD Bicester Site A as an asylum camp.

“This is totally outrageous and proves this government don’t give two hoots about us here in Bucks.

“I will keep working to get this overturned.”



But Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said the decision was “sickening”.

He added: “Angela Rayner and the Labour government have betrayed the people of Piddington and Bicester by abusing their emergency powers in this way.

“I have met many women from the village who are scared for their safety but Angela Rayner doesn’t care.



“Instead of accommodating illegal immigrants, the government should leave the ECHR so illegal immigrants can be rapidly deported.”

A Home Office spokesperson said: “Planning permission allows us to continue to progress the use of MOD Bicester. However, a final decision to proceed is yet to be taken.

“The government is working on a fairer distribution of asylum accommodation across the country, with over £1 billion saved in costs since the election.”

In September, the quintennial English village voted for independence from the UK in a symbolic local referendum.

A whopping 285 villagers voted for “independence”, with just 26 against and one spoiled ballot on a turnout of almost 92 per cent.



Parish council vice chair Susannah Parden, who announced the result, said: “We are Piddington — the village that roars.”

The referendum was held in protest of the government’s proposal, reflecting local concerns about the impact of a significant influx of new residents.

Village officials previously estimated that male asylum migrants will outnumber women in Piddington by 10-1.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

After the independence vote, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he understood the “strength of feeling” displayed by residents.

Local mums told The Sun they would be too scared to take their children to the park if plans were approved — a fear that has now become reality.

News.title: How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions
News.content:
Colette Kress, who takes over for now, will be a familiar face internally and that must feel reassuring to some at Nvidia.

She's worked at the company for 13 years and for those who follow its considerable finances, she is often present on earnings calls. She is a billionaire in her own right and a high-flying tech executive.

But she's not an engineer and Nvidia's products are highly technical.

She will have to convince investors that it is business as usual for Nvidia, that the innovation for which it is renowned can continue at its existing pace, and that the top talent won't leave with Huang.

A wobbly Nvidia would be bad news for the entire AI industry because its ever-advancing chips drive the most powerful AI models, and it's also regarded as something of a central bank, loaning money to other firms.

As for Huang himself, we assume for now that the investigation into his relationship with the woman accused of being a Chinese spy will continue, and the results of that may well determine what he does next.

He probably won't be short of offers despite his conduct â and I expect Nvidia's rivals can't believe their luck that their formidable rival has taken himself out of the game. Elon Musk has already said it would be "an honour" to work with him at SpaceX.

It's important though to remember that even if Huang turns out not to have betrayed his company or his country, he still betrayed his wife of 41 years, Lori Huang.

And for her, it's not a story of tech, temptation and trillion-dollar-valuations.

It's a painfully personal matter.

News.title: Microsoft users report outages amid tech giant 'connectivity issues'
News.content:
Microsoft says it is working to tackle "connectivity problems" after users worldwide reported outages on Thursday.

Services including Teams, Outlook and Microsoft's AI software Copilot were affected.

The tech giant said a part of its infrastructure was experiencing "elevated load", which was likely contributing to connectivity errors.

While the issue was originally reported in the US, Microsoft said the connectivity problems could affect users "in any region".

At around 18:30 GMT on Thursday evening, monitoring website Downdetector showed a spike in UK users reporting issues with Microsoft products.

Similarly for the US, the monitoring site suggested there had been over 131,000 reports of Microsoft Outlook problems at 18:15 GMT.

"We determined the elevated load isn't driven by an increase in traffic, but by a number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable; straining the remaining infrastructure," Microsoft said in a statement.

In a further update issued at 19:50 GMT, Microsoft said it was "testing a configuration" to fix the problem, which was "causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable".

All affected servers had been restarted, it added.

News.title: Can Burnham avoid another Labour welfare rebellion?
News.content:
Andy Burnham has committed to bringing the welfare bill down, but he knows just how the high the political stakes are.

He saw how last year's welfare rebellion marked the beginning of the end for his predecessor in Downing Street.

Sir Keir Starmer's authority was shredded when 120 - more than a quarter - of his own MPs threatened to derail his reforms.

To defuse this, Sir Keir was compelled to guarantee that existing claimants of personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales, wouldn't lose out.

Even then, 49 of the 120 potential Labour rebels still voted against their own government.

Next week, a review from former New Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn has the capacity to create another internal row in Labour's ranks.

Milburn has spent a year grappling with how to reduce the nearly one million young people who are not in employment, education or training (Neets).

In an interview with the Times, he has now confirmed he is set to recommend cutting benefits for some 16-24 year olds who currently receive Pip, or the enhanced health-related payment of Universal Credit.

Taking benefit cuts to the Parliamentary Labour Party would usually have a similar effect to adding phosphorous to water.

But from my soundings, the deep waters of the Labour ranks are calmer than might be expected.

Why?

News.title: What we know about Brooklyn building collapse that killed eight people
News.content:
Eight people have died and 18 more were injured after a three-storey building collapsed in the Flatbush neighbourhood of Brooklyn, New York.

Witnesses described hearing a loud boom and seeing dust in the air as the building came down and fell into an adjacent construction pit where people were working on Wednesday.

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, described a harrowing scene, saying workers "who had only barely survived themselves turned back and dug victims out of the rubble".

The city's fire commissioner, Lillian Bonsignore, said firefighters were on the scene within minutes and called their actions "incredibly heroic".

Speaking on Thursday, she said fire crews "are still in a recovery phase".

Despite the hard rain and falling temperatures at the site, she said, their efforts would continue until every victim was located.

News.title: Military base asylum plans granted planning approval
News.content:
Planning permission to house asylum seekers at a former military site near the Oxfordshire village of Piddington has been granted by the government.

The Home Office's application to house up to 1,256 men at the MoD Bicester site was fast-tracked using an Urgent Crown Development application.

The nearby village of Piddington symbolically voted to leave the UK in opposition to the planned site, which has also been legally challenged by campaigners.

A Home Office spokesperson said the planning permission "allows us to continue to progress the use of MoD Bicester" but no final decision on the proposal had been taken.

A government report said the decision received 3,177 representations against, and one in support.

It also said Housing Secretary Angela Rayner ruled permission should be granted because "national demand for asylum accommodation remains high".

The permission allows for demolition of existing buildings, the erection of new modular accommodation, and provisions for health and welfare facilities.

Chris Philp MP, Shadow Home Secretary, said: "Angela Rayner and the Labour government have betrayed the people of Piddington by abusing their emergency powers in this way."

He continued: "Instead of accommodating illegal immigrants, the government should leave the ECHR so they can be rapidly deported."

News.title: 'We've got to run': Inside ruined Ukraine power plant under constant drone threat
News.content:
As peace talks between Ukraine and Russia continue, Ukrainians are facing a rolling schedule of planned power cuts because of intensified Russian attacks on their energy grid. Ukraine has responded by striking Russian oil refineries.

Officials are concerned that life will quickly become unsustainable for millions of Ukrainians if power supplies cannot be maintained for at least four hours per day. Some privately warn that's close already, as some families are living with outages of up to 20 hours in Kyiv.

Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson visits one of the country's power stations on the front lines of the war. Devastated by a direct ballistic missile strike, repair work is hampered by frequent air raids.

Read the BBC's dispatch from Ukraine.

News.title: Duran Duran drummer quits band due to tinnitus
News.content:
Duran Duran drummer Roger Taylor said he will leave the band due to his worsening tinnitus.

Taylor has been the chart-topping group's drummer since they formed in Birmingham in 1978, which he described as "the joy of my life", but said he had "reached the point where I must now listen to my body and my doctors".

The 66-year-old said his condition has been getting steadily worse, leading to him making one of his hardest decisions to quit the band.

The group, made up of Simon Le Bon, keyboardist Nick Rhodes and guitarist John Taylor, said his decision came after "careful consideration and medical advice", which said that "protecting his hearing and long-term health must now come first".

Taylor, who left the band in 1985 before returning in 2001, said: "Playing drums in this band has been the joy of my life, and I'll never be able to properly thank the fans for the love they've shown us over the years.

"But the truth is that my tinnitus has been getting steadily worse," he said.

News.title: Faisal Islam: Why the UK economy is surprisingly resilient
News.content:
The UK economy grew at its fastest rate for more than two years in the three months to September.

"Top gear" and "strikingly strong" were among the descriptions of the 0.7% growth offered by the economists who track every minor murmur of Britain's economy.

It is an upgrade on "solid" and "resilient", and in turn a world away from "hardest hit by the Iran War".

Against the backdrop of the world's biggest disruption to energy flows, rising market borrowing costs - and the cruel summers since the pandemic - it is impressive growth.

It should reset some of the swirl of self-reinforcing negativity.

The UK's economic growth has averaged less than 0.1% in the four Q3s [ie July to September] since the pandemic.

The average prediction just months ago for this July to September was just 0.1%.

Even the UK's official forecaster the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) effectively pencilled in 0.3% at the Budget just 3 weeks ago.

This figure has not been exceeded outside the pandemic since 2017. It puts the UK on course to be the second fastest growing economy after the US across the major G7 countries which also includes Canada, Japan, Germany, Italy and France.

It is tempting to think about what the economy would have done if the Iran War hadn't happened. If interest rates had been cut instead of their recent rise.

News.title: UK economy grows at fastest rate for more than two years
News.content:
ï»¿The UK economy grew at its fastest rate for more than two years in the three months to September.

Between July and September, the economy expanded by 0.7%, accelerating from the previous three months, official figures, external show.

The robust growth suggests a far more resilient economy than expected over the summer, despite the impact of higher energy prices from the Iran war.

Strong growth in the services sector - the largest part of the economy, which includes non-physical goods such as consultancy services and computer programming as well as hotels and restaurants - helped boost the numbers.

Within services, computer programming registered its fastest growth for the past three years, helped by cloud computing and AI-linked spending.

The boost from computer programming and consultancy services has been the biggest driver of growth so far this year.

Grant Fitzner, chief economist at the Office for National Statistics, said it was "possible growth could have been even stronger" if there hadn't been a war in the Middle East.

But he says households may still not feel better off, and that prices might soon start to rise more quickly than wages.

However, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the figures were "welcome news".

"Despite a year where events around the world have pushed up costs here at home, our economy is growing, bringing hope for the future," he said.

Chancellor John Healey told the BBC the figures showed a "remarkable resilience" in the face of global conflicts, and hopes they "bring back confidence in Britain".

Asked about how government decisions could be the reason for growth when AI investment has been a main driver, Healey said ministers can always "help or hinder" business confidence and investments.

News.title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say
News.content:
Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to under a radical overhaul of the welfare system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review.

As reported in the Times,, external Alan Milburn's year-long report, to be published on Tuesday, is expected to recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits.

Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 16 to 24 year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training - otherwise known as "Neet".

He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants.

His report is expected to say that under-25s should no longer be able to claim the health element of UK-wide universal credit - or personal independence payment (Pip), the main disability benefit in England and Wales.

Disabled people in Scotland can claim the devolved Adult Disability Payment.

Instead, under Milburn's plan, under-25s would receive an allowance on the same basic rate as universal credit.

Some could be eligible for a new "additional cost allowance" to cover day-to-day costs related to their conditions.

Some claimants would receive less under the plans - although the exact amounts will not be clear until early next year, when the government publishes legislation to implement the changes.

People can claim Pip to help them with the additional cost of being disabled or living with long-term physical or mental health conditions. It is available to those both in and out of work.

In his interim report,, external Milburn said survey data found that 19% of young people claiming disability or health benefits were in work.

Milburn, a Labour MP from 1992 to 2010, is also expected to recommend an investment of billions into more employment support for young people, including work placements, job subsidies and one-to-one personal advisers.

Those with more severe disabilities and unable to work would get a new benefit paid at a higher rate.

Milburn told the Times: "Candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system.

News.title: Some childhood offenders may no longer have to reveal convictions to employers
News.content:
Some job applicants in England and Wales would no longer need to declare criminal convictions they received as children under government proposals designed to improve the employment prospects of rehabilitated young people.

The changes would mean criminal records for people detained when they were under 18 years old would no longer show up for life during checks carried out by employers.

The Ministry of Justice has also launched a consultation on relaxing disclosure requirements for some specific drug-related and violent crimes committed by children.

Young people who have not re-offended as adults struggle to find work because of their past behaviour, the government says.

Many employers require applicants to undergo a background check, which in their most basic form require people to self-declare if they have a criminal record.

For more sensitive roles, such as working with children or joining the police, an employer can carry out a standard or enhanced check, which allows them to request information from the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS).

How long a criminal record must be volunteered for or will show up in those checks differs depending on the severity of the offence, the punishment received and how long ago the crime was committed - sometimes referred to as whether a conviction is 'spent'.

For example, a young person who was convicted and fined for an offence when they were under-18 will have that information show up in checks for five-and-a-half years. If they were given a custodial sentence, that will be disclosed for the rest of their lives.

The government wants to reduce the number of young people those disclosure rules apply to if an applicant has not continued to offend as an adult.

Five offences would be removed from a list of crimes which will show up in background for checks for life if committed by an adult. They are: affray, violent disorder, supplying a controlled drug to a child, robbery and assaults occasioning actual bodily harm.

Between March 2022 and March 2026, around 8,500 under-18s were convicted of those offences, according to Ministry of Justice data.

The government says that type of crime is often a result of peer pressure, exploitation and "adolescent impulsivity" by individuals who are still developing, as opposed to a broader propensity for crime and violence.

Under the new rules, they would cease to show up in checks after five-and-a-half years.

Lifelong disclosure would also be removed for offences which led to a detention period of less than two years, the maximum which can be handed out by a youth court, and replaced by a new 11-year disclosure period.

In cases where a child was given a sentence longer than two years - which can only happen if the severity of the crime meant they were dealt with by an adult crown court - the rules would stay the same.

The most serious offences - including severe violence, terrorism-related crimes and sexual offences - would be exempted from the reforms.

Other proposed changes include:

Cutting or removing altogether the disclosure period for offences which led to a fine, the majority of which are for driving-related crimes

Ending disclosure of offences which were dealt with via an out of court resolution, which have primarily been used to tackle knife possession and assault

Reforming how long earlier offences appear in checks for young people who committed more than one crime as a child

Announcing a consultation on proposals, justice minister Jake Richards said: "Many young people who offend do not go on to lead lives of crime.

"They take responsibility, turn their lives around and want to make something of themselves.

"When they do, we should recognise that progress and support them â not put unnecessary barriers in their way."

The proposals come as the government prepares to publish a long-awaited report authored by former Labour minister Alan Milburn on tackling the number of young people not in work or education.

In May, he warned the UK was at risk of a raising a "lost generation" as almost one in eight young people are not working or studying.

Richards pointed to that intervention as he announced the disclosure reforms, saying barriers to employment can be "particularly difficult to overcome" for people who committed crimes as children.

News.title: Teenage girl admits murder in row over boy
News.content:
A teenager has admitted murdering a 16-year-old girl who she stabbed to death in a pre-planned fight over a boy.

Leeds Crown Court heard that Chloe Watson Dransfield was attacked by 18-year-old Kayla Smith after going to Smith's home with her boyfriend Blake Dowling in the early hours of 28 March.

Smith had pleaded guilty to manslaughter but denied murder. She then changed her plea to guilty on the second day of her trial.

Dowling, 18, who took Chloe to the house in Kennerleigh Avenue in Leeds, and Archie Rycroft, 20, who followed Smith to the fight, are also charged with murder and manslaughter and their trial will continue. They both deny the charges against them.

The judge, Mr Justice Cavanagh KC, said he would sentence Smith once the trial was over.

He told her the only sentence he could give was life imprisonment, but that he would need to set the minimum term she must spend in custody.

The trial previously heard that Dowling had been in a relationship with both Chloe and Smith and "knew of the bad feeling between the two females".

Dowling's mother told the court that Smith was "jealous and obsessed" over her son's relationship with Chloe.

News.title: Poundland gets more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue
News.content:
Poundland has avoided immediate collapse after a deadline was extended to find a rescue deal.

A deadline to secure a buyer for the retail chain was set to expire at midnight, but a court has given Poundland an extra 10 days to find a buyer.

The discount chain, which has 11,000 employees, has been edging towards administration after being blocked by owners Gordon Brothers from accessing cash in its bank accounts.

A committee of MPs questioned Gordon Brothers following accusations that the investment firm hoped to profit from selling off Poundland's 600 shops and stock piecemeal.

Gordon Brothers - which bought the chain for just Â£1 last year - is accused of forcing that outcome by restricting Poundland's access to available cash needed to restock shops, and pay wages and rent, ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period.

The investment firm, which specialises in buying and restructuring distressed companies, has denied the claims.

However, pressure remains on Poundland's owners after a takeover bid was rejected. The decision prompted calls for answers from politicians, including Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

About Â£50m had been frozen by Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning Poundland bosses were unable to restock shelves across its 600 shops.

The BBC understands that Gordon Brothers agreed to release a further Â£11m today from Poundland's accounts, on top of Â£10m announced earlier, as the firm seeks to find a new buyer.

Gordon Brothers said it was in talks with three parties for a sale of the whole business, and it had received "several offers from established high street retailers for significant parts of the business".

News.title: Man jailed for 'appalling' catalogue of coercive control and abuse against partner
News.content:
Warning: This article contains details and references to suicide and abusive behaviour

A man subjected his partner to an "appalling" catalogue of abuse, including beating and abusive messages, which the judge said was "one of the worst" cases of coercive control the court had seen.

John Gizzi, 55, from St Asaph, Denbighshire, was jailed for four years and 11 months after pleading guilty to coercive and controlling behaviour towards Natasha Farah, 32, and for intentional strangulation of her sister.

There were shouts of "scumbag" and "rot in hell" from the public gallery towards Gizzi who appeared at the hearing via video link from prison.

Farah's mother said she would campaign in her daughter's name for sentences around coercive and controlling behaviour to be longer.

At Mold Crown Court, some people called out that the sentence was too short, until they were asked to be quiet by a court usher.

The court heard that a catalogue of physical and verbal abuse of Farah by Gizzi was unearthed after she made a suspected suicide attempt that left her with severe brain damage.

In his sentencing remarks, Judge Mills said Farah and her family and friends had faced an "appalling tragedy" and said the case of coercive control was one of the worst the court had seen, telling Gizzi he had subjected her to "appalling" behaviour.

Judge Mills said Gizzi had used "dreadful misogynistic language" towards Farah which was "part of the process of humiliation" and "destroying" her self worth.

Farah's mother, wearing a T-shirt saying Justice for Natasha, read a lengthy victim impact statement, saying she wanted to detail the "sheer devastating" impact Gizzi's behaviour had had and the "pain, grief, anger, torture" he had inflicted.

She described her daughter as "the most beautiful, funniest, kindest soul in the world" and told Gizzi, who was appearing by video link, that he was a "smiling devil monster".

Judge Mills said Natasha was often seen to have bruises, and was once assaulted by Gizzi with a dumbbell.

"You would accuse her of sleeping with other menâ¦ assaulted her frequentlyâ¦ sometimes in front of other peopleâ¦ you assaulted her in front of her child," he said.

The judge also said Gizzi had assaulted her on Valentine's Day and Mother's Day.

"She would plead with you to desist," he added.

News.title: Rolls-Royce gas leak prompts emergency response
News.content:
Emergency services have responded to a gas leak at a Rolls-Royce factory in Derby.

Derbyshire Fire and Rescue Service said it was called to the site in Raynesway at about 15:40 GMT on Thursday.

It said police, fire crews and ambulances responded to a "small chemical and gas leak", adding this was "not a nuclear incident", and that all employees were accounted for.

A 300m (985ft) cordon was put in place and locals were asked to remain indoors with windows and doors shut, however the guidance was lifted shortly before 22:00.

A BBC reporter at the scene was advised by police to stay in her car for her safety, and an alarm was heard coming from the building.

A number of roads were closed around the factory, including Royal Scot Way, Pride Park Way, from Derby Audi to the London Road roundabout, Harrow Street, and London Road, from the junction of Harrow Steet to Meadow Lane. They have all reopened, the fire service said.

In a statement, a fire service spokesperson added: "Emergency services and Rolls-Royce would like to thank local residents and businesses for their co-operation while the incident was resolved safely and as quickly as possible.

"The incident has now been handed over to Rolls-Royce."

News.title: Activist Daniel Thomas admits criminal damage after slashing migrant dinghy in Channel
News.content:
Anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas, also known as Danny Tommo, has admitted criminal damage after slashing a dinghy with a knife in the English Channel.

The 37-year-old changed his plea to the single charge when he appeared via video link from prison at Portsmouth Crown Court on Thursday.

A court previously heard he had taken a boat into the English Channel on 22 September and observed the migrant occupants of a dinghy being assisted by the RNLI, Border Force and the French Coastguard.

Thomas admitted using a knife on the dinghy, which had French personnel on board.

Prosecutor Kevin Lucie told Basingstoke Magistrates' Court in September the defendant instructed his vessel to be steered towards the empty rigid inflatable boat (RIB) that was adrift.

The court heard he then armed himself with a knife as rescue crews also approached the dinghy and a Frenchman boarded from a rescue vessel.

After slashing the boat with the knife, Thomas could be heard on a livestream saying: "This is what needs to happen to everyone in these boats.

"Right, you're on English territory, This is England, this is not France anymore.

"Get off the boat, you have time to get off the boat. This is not France. Take them back."

News.title: Russell Brand accused of sexual misconduct by six more women
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Russell Brand has been accused of sexual misconduct and predatory behaviour by six more women, according to a report.

The disgraced comedian this week began a 10-and-a-half-year prison sentence for raping a woman and sexually assaulting three others.

The new claims, published as part of an investigation by The Times and the Sunday Times, include allegations from one woman who claimed Brand had sex with her without her consent, then apologised.

The Times reported that the woman, who said she had an on-off relationship with Brand in the late 2000s after a professional meeting at his London home, said the comedian continued having sex with her despite her saying “No, stop”.

After the alleged incident, the woman said Brand apologised to her in person and by text message.

Russell Brand was jailed on Monday for 10-and-a-half years (James Manning/PA). ( PA Wire )

Another woman who encountered Brand when she was queuing to meet him with a friend in 2007 aged 19 says she told him during sex “It’s painful”.

She alleged Brand would not stop, adding: “And then it gets worse and it’s really painful. And I say ‘stop’ and he doesn’t stop.”

The woman claimed Brand said afterwards: “Tonight was consensual. Nobody did anything they didn’t want to do.”

The new allegations could not be reported until the criminal case against Brand was over to avoid prejudicing proceedings, but all of the women spoke to reporters before hearing the allegations in the trial.

Brand, 51, was found guilty last week of rape and sex assault following a four-week trial at Southwark Crown Court.

Half of the new accusers had been at his shows or gigs, where he used his fame to pick up women, The Times said.

The Times says Brand’s lawyer initially said he would consider “injunctive relief” and demanded further time to respond but a later agreed deadline passed with no response.

Brand has previously denied wrongdoing and claimed all his relationships were consensual.

News.title: Emotional Harry Kane reflects on ‘crazy few weeks’ after setting another England record
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Harry Kane reflected on a “crazy few weeks” after scoring the winning goal against Croatia on his record-breaking 126th appearance for England.

The England captain struck a record-extending 92nd international goal to seal a 2-1 win over Croatia at Wembley on Thursday night, a result that confirmed the team's progress into the quarter-finals of the Nations League.

The Ballon d'Or winner became England's most capped men's player of all-time in that match, having equalled the record held by Peter Shilton last month. Shilton was on hand to make a pre-match presentation to the star striker, along with the Prince of Wales.

England had beaten Slaven Bilic's side 7-0 in Croatia 40 days earlier, but this was a much more keenly contested affair. Kane was happy England got the job done, setting up a top-of-the-table shootout against Spain on Sunday.

“It’s been a crazy few weeks,” Kane told BBC Radio 5 Live. “Of course it takes a lot out of you emotionally, physically and mentally and all these things.

open image in gallery Kane was honoured with a tifo before kick-off ( PA )

“I'm very good at staying focused on the job and what needs to be done but it's a hard balance because you want to take it in. Breaking the record is a massive thing in the history of our game, seeing the tifo there, having my kids with me, and being presented by all the people was beyond dreams.

“Once the whistle goes and you're on the pitch, you just start focusing on what your job is, pressing and playing the ball, playing assists and goals and that just takes over. It's always been in me that I'm able to switch, and of course now I can enjoy it with my family on the pitch after this.

“I’ve always said all these big milestones that I’ve had, when you win the game it makes it 10 times better and I’ve been lucky enough to win all of them, especially here at Wembley so it’s nice to do it again.”

Spain defeated Czechia 2-0 in Prague on Thursday as the world champions extended their historic unbeaten streak to 43 matches. That run stretches back to March 2024.

Luis de la Fuente's side had to come from a goal behind to beat England 3-2 in the reverse fixture in September. Kane is looking forward to the return contest at Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium.

“After the first game when we lost here against them, we knew we left a bit out there, we knew we could have done a little bit better,” Kane added on ITV.

“We said to ourselves ‘let’s win every game from now until the next one and see what happens’. It’s the perfect opportunity now to try and prove ourselves.”

News.title: Darth Vader's light saber used in ‘I am your father’ duel sells for nearly $5 million
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A light saber used by Darth Vader in the “Star Wars” movies “The Empire Strikes Back” and ”Return of the Jedi" sold Thursday for nearly $5 million in an auction.

The light saber, which was used in the climactic duel in Cloud City where Vader tells Luke Skywalker “I am your father,” sold for $4.875 million at the Ultimate Star Wars Auction held by Heritage Auctions. The sale marks a world auction record for any “Star Wars” collectible, according to Heritage Auctions.

The sale also established a new auction record for a screen-used “Star Wars” prop, according to the auction organizer, shooting past their $3.75 million July auction sale of Skywalker’s light saber and severed hand-effects rig from “The Empire Strikes Back."

Heritage's Thursday auction also featured material from “Star Wars” Episodes I through IX and additional films and TV shows. In addition to Vader's light saber, 27 other “Star Wars” light sabers were assembled for public auction, according to Heritage Auctions.

News.title: Jack Grealish issues public apology to Everton fans after disciplinary breach
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Jack Grealish has apologised to Everton supporters after returning to action during a behind-closed-doors friendly with Derby.

The player has missed four matches and had not featured for the Toffees since 17 October following a breach of team discipline.

Boss David Moyes was reluctant to discuss any details, with the club only confirming the 31-year-old former England winger was "not match-fit" ahead of a trip to Newcastle on November 2. However, Grealish featuring at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday suggests a line has now been drawn under the issue.

"Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training," Grealish wrote on his Instagram story.

"I want to apologise to the fans and everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.

open image in gallery David Moyes did not pick Grealish in Everton's final four games before the international break ( Reuters )

"I love playing for this club and can’t wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt. See you all soon."

Grealish spent the first half of the 2025-26 season on loan at Everton before injury disrupted his spell, but he secured another temporary deal on transfer deadline day.

In his absence, Everton have won three of their last four matches to move up to sixth in the Premier League table, while also earning their spot in the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup.

Following a 2-0 loss to Arsenal, the Toffees picked up successive wins over Newcastle before beating Coventry in their final game before the international break.

Everton are due to return to action on 23 November when they travel to Brentford. Grealish could be set to make his first competitive appearance in over a month in that game as he looks to get his season back on track.

Grealish has earned 39 caps in his England career, but has not played for the Three Lions since October 2024.

News.title: Harry Kane marks historic 126th England cap with a little reminder of his greatness
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Harry Kane was asked this week to name the lowest moment of his 125 England caps, and his mind travelled back to that evening in Qatar when he sent a penalty over Hugo Lloris’s crossbar and up to the heavens. Kane being Kane, he would score the next 30 penalties of his career. “It made me improve,” he said. “A lot of the bad things have helped me get to where I am now.”

Perhaps it was apt, then, that on the night of his record-breaking 126th England cap, Kane scored his 92nd England goal from the penalty spot to settle this 2-1 win over Croatia and book a spot in the Nations League quarter-finals. It was a little display of his work ethic, a simple kick of the ball honed to a fine point through thousands of repetitions on the training ground.

Kane dinked his penalty down the middle and a diving Dominik Livakovic almost blocked the ball with his trail leg. The goalkeeper beat the ground in frustration as if to say, I knew you’d do that. But perhaps this is the point: since that World Cup miss against France, Kane has trained every penalty into his armoury – the stutter or the run, the blast or the dink, left or right or the space a goalkeeper leaves behind – and Livakovic couldn’t cover them all.

It came after a rare miss for Bayern Munich last month. “The next one is always important to bounce back,” Kane said. “I did my usual routine yesterday in training and looked at the goalkeeper. I haven’t gone down the middle with a penalty for maybe three or four years. With penalties, you have to keep things fresh, keep things moving. I thought it was a good time to do it, looking at his clips. Thankfully, it paid off today.”

open image in gallery Kane's penalty evades the leg of Croatia goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic ( PA )

What did we learn from this slightly underwhelming performance? England are better than Croatia, but then we saw that at the World Cup when England beat them 4-2, and more emphatically in Rijeka last month when England won 7-0. This was naturally a more cautious Croatia, against an altogether sloppier England who made a series of uncharacteristic errors all over the field.

Trent Alexander-Arnold gave the ball away on the edge of his own box, Lewis Hall played a fancy flick straight off the pitch and Jarell Quansah assisted Croatia’s equaliser with a deft, daft header inside his own six-yard box. Jude Bellingham showed frustration towards some of his teammates’ errors, yet his best game largely deserted him too.

The England fans who shivered through these 90 minutes might instead remember the few moments beforehand. The commemorations began with a giant Tifo behind one goal displaying England’s captain roaring into the night sky with the words “England’s finest” and “Kane 126” emblazoned top and bottom. Kane emerged from the tunnel with his four children as mascots, and then spent a couple of minutes waving around the Ballon d’Or before being presented with three gifts, like a scene from the nativity. The three wise men were played by Peter Shilton (gift one: a golden crest), Croatia captain Luka Modric (gift two: an old football), and Prince William (gift three: a framed shirt).

"It's been a crazy few weeks,” Kane said. “It takes a lot out of you emotionally, physically and mentally ... it’s a hard balance because you want to take it in. Breaking the record is a massive thing in the history of our game, seeing the tifo there, having my kids with me, and being presented by all the people was beyond dreams, so of course you have got to take it in. Once the whistle goes and you’re on the pitch, you just start focusing on what your job is.”

open image in gallery Kane poses with Prince Phillip and Peter Shilton ( Reuters )

England started haphazardly but began to get a grip midway through the first half and it was Kane who unlocked Croatia’s defence with a raking pass to Bellingham arriving at the far post. Bellingham’s first-time cross found Morgan Rogers, who managed to impart just enough energy to the ball to bounce it home from three yards.

Kane had to wait. His first big chance came early in the second half when he received a cutback in the box from Declan Rice and a half-empty goal prepared to bulge, but Josip Stanisic wasn’t feeling sentimental and he lunged in front to block Kane’s goalbound shot.

Croatia drew level a few minutes later when Quansah took the extraordinary step of attempting a header back to Jordan Pickford inside a crowded penalty area. Pickford understandably wasn’t expecting the pass, and he was beaten to the ball by Petar Sucic who knocked it into the roof of England’s goal.

But Quansah went some way to making amends when his run drew some suspicious shirt pulling from Ivan Smolcic. Danish referee Morten Krogh missed it at first look but VAR intervened, and when Kane placed the ball down on the spot, the rest felt inevitable.

open image in gallery Kane celebrates after scoring from the spot ( PA )

England now travel to Madrid to face Spain on Sunday, where victory would clinch top spot in the group. It would also serve as a sign of England’s standing in the game right now if they were to beat the world champions on their own turf, after a narrow but encouraging 3-2 defeat by Spain at Wembley in September.

Kane will earn cap number 127 and he is intent on gathering many more. Since winning the Ballon d’Or he has made his remaining career targets abundantly clear: scoring 100 England goals, winning the Champions League with Bayern Munich and winning a major trophy for England.

Whether the Nations League counts as “major” is debatable – Cristiano Ronaldo might say yes but just about everyone else says no – yet it presents an opportunity to end England’s 60-year wait for a men’s trophy. It would be fitting if Kane, now England’s greatest player by any measure, was the man to lift it.

News.title: Donald Trump Jr. exits Kalshi adviser role after firm invests in competitor Polymarket
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Donald Trump Jr. is no longer serving as a paid adviser for the prediction market company Kalshi, the platform announced on Thursday.

Kalshi described the outcome as a mutual commercial decision between the two parties that followed a decision by 1789 Capital, the investment firm tied to Trump Jr., to expand its financial stake in Kalshi's major market competitor, Polymarket.

The announcement arrives just one week after Democrats managed to take control of both the House and Senate following the midterm elections.

Democrats have previously stated that they intend to investigate the financial investments of the Trump family, with a specific focus on their ongoing business relationships with both prediction markets.

"We have mutually agreed to end Don’s advisory role after his firm’s significant investment in a competitor this past summer," said Dani Lever, a spokesperson for Kalshi.

"We are grateful for his contributions in helping us market Kalshi to more customers."

The president's eldest son stepped into his role as a paid "strategic adviser" for Kalshi shortly after President Trump was sworn into office for his second term in January 2025, having also maintained a stake as an investor in Polymarket since August 2025.

Ivanka Trump and Donald Trump Jr. arrive at their dad's inauguration ( AFP/Getty )

Both commercial platforms have seen their general popularity and usage jump significantly over the past two years.

During the same timeframe, both businesses received favorable regulatory treatment from the White House.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission has supported the industry's ongoing efforts to expand its financial products nationwide, including permitting customers to actively trade sports-related contracts.

Both companies have adamantly denied that the underlying financial relationship between Polymarket, Kalshi, and the Trumps played any role in how regulatory oversight was carried out under this administration.

1789 Capital expanded its financial investment in Polymarket this past August during Polymarket's latest capital fundraising round, an action that initiated the internal conversations that ultimately concluded Trump Jr.'s advisory role with Kalshi.

News.title: Trump’s DOJ tried to hide who on his staff worked on DC golf course. The judge wasn’t having it
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Donald Trump’s administration wanted to conceal a list of officials behind a multimillion-dollar, taxpayer-funded overhaul of a public golf course in Washington, D.C., after a federal judge opened an investigation into whether the government approved the plans in spite of her orders.

The administration wants to “preserve the anonymity” of Department of Interior employees who “drafted, edited, or provided input” on a plan for the East Potomac Golf Links that was sent to the National Capital Planning Commission, according to court filings.

“There are significant privacy concerns involved in this case and there is no need for public access to this information,” lawyers for the Department of Justice wrote Thursday.

“The case at hand is a highly publicized matter which has drawn national attention. With that attention, has sadly come outrage and death threats. These privacy concerns support sealing,” lawyers wrote. “Government employees are reasonably concerned that they will be subject to the same level of publicity, harassment, and potential harm.”

But U.S. District Judge Ana C Reyes wasn’t buying it.

open image in gallery A federal judge ordered the Trump administration to publicly disclose the names of government officials behind a plan to overhaul East Potomac Golf Links in Washington DC — but the government tried to keep that list secret ( Getty )

She ordered the government to publish the list of names by 5 p.m. Thursday.

“There is little possibility of prejudice from the disclosure of the names of government employees acting within the scope of their employment,” the judge said.

The government reluctantly supplied the list of names shortly before the judge’s 5 p.m. deadline — and accused the judge of violating the president’s constitutional rights.

Justice Department officials said that “ordering the production of such names is not a legitimate exercise” of judicial authority — and “an unconstitutional infringement on the Executive Branch’s right to conduct its own affairs.”

The Trump administration insisted for weeks that there were no imminent plans to close the park despite the president's Truth Social announcements outlining his vision for the project.

But the Department of Justice finally admitted in court filings last month that the president’s plans to close East Potomac Park on November 15 are, in fact, in the works.

The revelation stunned Judge Reyes, who appointed a former federal prosecutor to investigate the government’s conduct in the case and determine whether officials were lying or violated ethics rules.

open image in gallery Judge Ana Reyes has appointed a special master to investigate whether the government lied to her about plans that were in the works for the park despite her court orders ( AP )

She repeatedly erupted at government attorneys during a heated court hearing on October 30 before finding that Justice Department officials “intentionally” timed the abrupt removal of hundreds of trees at the park to evade judicial review — and may have been misleading the court about plans that have long been in the works.

The National Park Service submitted plans for what the administration is calling a “World Class, championship-level golf course that is capable of hosting major events” — and the park will close November 15, “consistent with the President’s directive,” according to filings from the Justice Department.

Last month, the president wrote on Truth Social that the Interior Department has “an absolute right” to “take a terrible and very unsafe golf course, and make it into a great, safe, and prestigious golf course.”

“The judge on the case is a crazed lunatic whose courthouse tapes will reveal, may be insane?” Trump wrote.

On October 26, Reyes issued a preliminary injunction to stop the removal of any trees at the golf course, stating that 10 days’ notice must be given before any “irreparable modification” is made to the site while a lawsuit filed by the D.C. Preservation League and two golfers remains active.

The legal battle escalates a fight over what could be Trump’s biggest D.C. makeover project yet, putting the future of the nearly 400-acre public park at risk.

News.title: Arsenal earn impressive Women’s Champions League draw at reigning champions Barcelona
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Frida Maanum scored as Arsenal held Women’s Champions League holders Barcelona to a creditable 1-1 draw at the Nou Camp.

The goal came against the run of play, with both Irene Paredes and Patri Guijarro having gone close for the hosts before half-time.

Caroline Graham Hansen then levelled for Barcelona in the 59th minute, but the points were ultimately shared after a more even second half

open image in gallery Frida Maanum scored for Arsenal as they secured a creditable draw ( Getty )

The result leaves Renee Slegers’ side on eight points after four matches in the league phase, and extends their unbeaten run to six matches in all competitions.

The fixture was a rematch of the 2025 final, in which Arsenal triumphed to claim a maiden European title, and Slegers’ side produced a similarly dogged defensive display on this occasion to leave with a point.

Arsenal could have gone in front after just four minutes when Caitlin Foord raced away down the right and had a shot deflected into the path of Alessia Russo but the England forward inexplicably headed wide with an open goal at her mercy.

That chance was immediately followed by wave after wave of Barcelona attack, with Misa Rodriguez forced to deny Graham Hansen and Sydney Schertenleib in quick succession.

open image in gallery Barcelona had wave after wave of attack in the first half ( Reuters )

After Rodriguez also thwarted Esmee Brugts, Arsenal made the breakthrough on 22 minutes. Russo did well down the left and crossed in for Foord, who was denied by Cata Coll. Maanum was first to the loose ball and fired under the Barcelona goalkeeper to make it 1-0.

Barcelona turned to three-time Ballon d’Or winner Aitana Bonmati early into the second half and equalised in the 59th minute. Brugts spotted the unmarked Graham Hansen, who controlled and cut inside before rifling into the corner.

Slegers reacted by introducing Ona Battle and Olivia Smith, which was followed by Russo sending an effort over. Schertenleib went close next, but Leah Williamson produced a timely block and it finished all square.

News.title: Kane bends game to his will on record-breaking night
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of England vs Croatia in the Nations League, with the hosts’ captain Harry Kane set to become the country’s most-capped player.

The 33-year-old has enjoyed a memorable few weeks, becoming the first English Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years and following it up with a new Bayern Munich contract, and an appearance at Wembley tonight will take him clear of Peter Shilton’s record of 125 England caps.

Kane scored twice in his record-equalling appearance against Czech Republic at Wembley last month, extending his international tally to 91 goals – a total that is unrivalled for England.

“It’s not about me – it’s about the team,” Kane said before tonight’s landmark moment. “I love coming to every England camp. I love playing every game and representing the country in the best way possible.”

The 3-0 home victory over Czech Republic left England on nine points after four Nations League group games, with a 2-0 win in the away contest and a 7-0 thumping of Croatia coming after a 3-2 defeat against world champions Spain.

Thomas Tuchel will be hoping that his side can inflict another heavy defeat on Croatia this evening, but a draw will be enough to book their place in the quarter-finals, with the group’s top two teams progressing.

While Kane will collect plaudits for his 126th cap, attention will also be on a potential first, with Jude Bellingham’s younger brother, Jobe, included in a senior England squad for the first time.

The two Bellinghams appearing together in a senior match would be a new experience for them, while it would be the first time that brothers have taken to the field together for England in 19 years.

“I can’t ignore it, but obviously with Jude being here too, it’s a great, great feeling for the family,” Jobe said on the Football Association’s England app. “It’s quite special, to be honest. It’s such a huge bonus on top of something that’s already so special and so great.”

News.title: Experts hail a “milestone” as TB deaths fall by more than a third in 10 years
News.content:
The number of people dying from tuberculosis has dropped by more than a third over the last 10 years but progress against the disease is still too slow, according to the World Health Organization.

Figures from WHO’s annual TB report showed that the lung disease took the lives of an estimated 1.13 million people in 2025, down from 1.7m in 2015, a drop of 35 per cent.

While WHO hailed this as a major milestone in achieving global targets - albeit five years too late - it said that progress in wiping out TB was still too slow.

Africa and Europe have made the greatest progress in reducing deaths, with numbers halving on both continents over the 10-year period. India and China - countries that have high burdens of the disease - also cut deaths by 35 per cent.

The report also showed that an estimated 10.6million people contracted the disease in 2025, a reduction of just 75,000 since 2024.

TB - still the world’s leading infectious disease killer - is preventable and curable, and is caused by the bacillus Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which is spread when infected people cough or sneeze.

The disease has been around for centuries, and has been described as the quintessential disease of poverty as it spreads in areas of low quality housing, among people with poor nutrition and immunity. It is a particular risk to people who are HIV positive.

Treatment requires a six-month long regimen of medication, and while treatments have become less toxic in recent years, they still take a heavy toll on patients and have a range of side effects, including at the most extreme deafness. Adherence to medication is also a problem.

News.title: Low-cost parenting app halves rates of sexual violence amongst teenagers in Tanzania
News.content:
A low cost parenting intervention has more than halved rates of sexual violence among teenage girls in Tanzania, a study has shown.

The ParentApp digital parenting programme for families is aimed at reducing rates of violence experienced by teenagers of both sexes.

Researchers found the programme helped bolster family relationships and enabled mothers and fathers to better communicate with their children at what is often a tricky stage of their development.

The programme, led by Oxford University and the University of Cape Town in partnership with the Tanzanian government, the World Health Organization and Unicef, combines in-person and mobile parenting support.

Parents have an introductory session with a facilitator and then undertake 12 weekly sessions online. They also join a WhatsApp group with other parents where they can discuss problems and support one another.

The randomized controlled trial, published in The Lancet, included 2,396 children aged 10–17 and 2,396 parents and carers across 80 urban and rural areas.

Families were randomly assigned to receive either ParentApp or a comparison app focused on safe water and hygiene. Researchers analysing the results did not know which app each family received.

At the 14-month follow-up, girls in families participating in the ParentApp initiative reported a 67% reduction in sexual violence; a 54% reduction in sexual exploitation and an improvement in parent-child relationships. The successes were less marked in boys, however.

Violence against children is widespread globally: Unicef data shows that around one in five girls and women and one in seven boys and men globally have experienced sexual violence as children.

Lucie Cluver, professor of child and family social work at Oxford University and one of the authors of the study, said the intervention was aimed at helping parents and children talk to one another and discuss situations before they arise.

In Tanzania, for example, teenage girls might get a motorbike taxi late at night, potentially putting them in a dangerous situation.

“What you’re doing is making plans and problem solving ahead of these risky situations that teenagers end up in. And you’re building trust and the relationship so you can have these difficult conversations,” said Prof Cluver.

She said she was surprised at how big an impact the intervention had on sexual violence: teenage girls reported that because the app helped improve communication with their parents and carers they did not feel the need to go out as much.

The programme cost around $6 per family but researchers calculated that it goes up to around $10 per family if 20% are given smartphones. A traditional in-person parenting intervention generally costs around $120 per family.

Engagement in the sessions was high - around 70 per cent of participants completed the course - and some parents kept in touch with one another after the programme.

However, the authors of the study stressed that while the app focused on families there remains a need to prevent violence against children in other settings, such as schools and religious institutions. There also needs to be a broader societal push to address the scourge.

“The app isn’t the answer to everything - it’s just one part of the puzzle,” said Prof Cluver.

Prof Cluver said she hoped future versions of the programme would include greater focus on digital harms and test whether parents could take the lead themselves.

The programme is being rolled out in other countries, including Mexico, Panama and South Africa, and is easily adaptable for different contexts.

“Tanzania only has 20% smartphone use and we thought if it works in one of the hardest places to do a digital intervention it could work anywhere,” she said.

She said the study showed how parenting was a universal experience, with the majority focused on what is best for their children.

“Parents feel powerless. We live in a world where our kids are facing risks and parents just want to help,” added Prof Cluver.
