News.title: AI fuels fastest economic growth in two years
News.content:
The Prime Minister and the Chancellor should not claim credit for the AI-fuelled expansion of Britain’s economy in the third quarter, a think tank said.

Julian Jessop, economics fellow at the Institute of Economic Affairs, said the 0.7pc expansion in the economy was “a tribute to the resilience of the private sector in the face of the energy shock and policy headwinds”.

He said: “This resilience is despite rather than because of anything the Government has done. In particular, the persistent weakens of the construction sector underlines the failure of flagship policies to boost housebuilding and infrastructure spending.

“The Government’s clumsy interventions are also continuing to add to labour and housing costs, including rents. Instead, the key driver of growth and business optimism has been the rollout of AI. This is an area that the Government has not got round to messing up, though that may yet be coming.

“In the meantime, the Government is still borrowing more than expected and the labour market remains weak.

“The full impact of higher inflation and higher interest rates has also yet to be felt. Early surveys for the fourth quarter already show that consumer confidence, retail spending, private sector hiring and housing market activity are all starting to slide again.

“2026 will still be a year when the economy performed much better than expected – at least in terms of GDP. But the new year will start with further increases in energy bills and high levels of job insecurity, which will matter far more to most people.”

News.title: Bird flu viruses gaining function through natural mixing, warn scientists
News.content:
The bird flu virus’ resurgence began with an 11-year-old. In February 2023, the schoolgirl was admitted to a hospital in Phnom Penh with severe pneumonia – within a day, she was dead.

Tests soon revealed that she had contracted avian influenza: Cambodia hadn’t reported a human case of bird flu since 2014, but the hiatus was over. Since then, 39 more people have been infected and 15 have died in the Southeast Asian country – a case fatality rate of roughly 40 per cent.

Researchers have been scratching their heads as to why, after nine years, this particular stain of H5N1 suddenly started jumping from birds to people again. The strain or clade called 2.3.2.1 had been circulating for almost a decade without spilling into humans. What changed?

Now, a paper in Emerging Infectious Diseases offers clues.

Scientists say the apparent rise in human cases has coincided with the virus gaining new genetic material and, potentially, new powers of infection, from a second flu virus via a process known as “reassortment”.

News.title: The country where diabetes is more feared than HIV
News.content:
Sikelela Mamba has had HIV for about 15 years, and it’s never really troubled him. The pills cost him nothing, and he’s never experienced any stigma or discrimination. “HIV is just like any other disease,” said the vegetable farmer from Eswatini, now in his 60s.

It’s Mr Mamba’s diabetes that terrifies him. For three or four months during a nationwide drug shortage, the local clinic had to ration his medicines, and he couldn’t afford to buy the rest. His blood sugar climbed dangerously high; he could do little but wait.

Mr Mamba knows HIV will not kill him. But he is less sure about diabetes.

Few places have been hit harder by HIV than Eswatini, a small landlocked country sandwiched between South Africa and Mozambique, the last absolute monarchy in Africa. Nearly a quarter of its population aged 15 to 49 has HIV - the highest in the world.

But with substantial international funding and government commitment, it has become one of the world’s leaders in diagnosing and treating the virus.

Since 2010, Aids-related deaths have fallen by 56 per cent in Eswatini, while non-communicable diseases (NCDs), like heart disease and diabetes, have surged, now accounting for almost half of all deaths.

This turnaround reflects a larger shift in global health: people with HIV are living long enough to die of something else. According to a recent report from the Lancet HIV Commission, nearly a third of people with HIV are 50 or older, and by 2040, half will be. Many low- and middle-income countries, however, are ill-prepared.

Decades of donor investment helped build health systems to fight infectious diseases - with far less attention to the chronic illnesses now threatening those who survived.

In Eswatini, that means people with HIV can get free testing, same-day treatment and easy access to care, while those with diabetes and other NCDs face higher costs, recurring medicine shortages and a scarcity of specialists.

News.title: Ebola could be raging in DRC for another year, expert warns
News.content:
The Ebola epidemic currently raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo could last at least another year, a leading UK epidemiologist has warned.

Experts have struggled to contain the current outbreak since the first cases of the rare Bundibugyo strain of the disease were reported in May.

There have so far been almost 11,000 cases including 5,000 deaths, making it the second largest outbreak in history, after the devastating West Africa epidemic of 2014-16. Cases have also been reported in Nigeria and Kenya, although transmission has not been widespread.

The outbreak is taking place across a vast area of DRC - North Kivu and Ituri - where conflict and widespread mistrust of authorities, including health workers, have hampered the response.

Neil Ferguson, professor of epidemiology at Imperial College, London, told a press briefing that at the current rate of disease spread that the epidemic could still be ongoing at the end of next year.

“Controlling Ebola outbreaks takes a long time so it is highly likely we’ll still be seeing transmission in a year’s time,” he said.

“We’re ticking over at about 70 confirmed cases a day at the moment and that’s almost certainly quite a significant underestimate of the true number of infections,” said Prof Ferguson, who rose to prominence at the beginning of the Covid pandemic when he advised government on the likely trajectory of the outbreak.

News.title: Many more cattle ranch workers infected with H5N1 than reported, says US farming union
News.content:
Far more US farm workers are infected with bird flu than officially reported, with some suffering “very severe” symptoms, according to the country’s largest farming union.

H5N1 is currently spreading rapidly across US cattle farms in dozens of US states.

Officially, just three people have been diagnosed with the virus in the past month, all following close contact with infected cows.

In total, 73 people in the US have been officially been recorded as infected with H5N1 since 2024, mostly dairy farm workers. Three have died.

But United Farm Workers (UFW), which represents thousands of workers across the US, said it was aware of many more farmers experiencing symptoms consistent with H5N1 who had not been tested.

“We have now connected with a number of workers and have confirmed that more workers are sick with avian flu symptoms who have not been tested,” the UFW wrote on X.

Symptoms range from “very mild to very severe”, the post added, including mild upper respiratory infections and conjunctivitis to severe flu-like symptoms, bone pain, persistent coughing and high fever.

The ongoing outbreak is worrying disease experts.

“H5N1 is not a virus to be casual about- or to let spread unchecked, given every mutation is like the virus buying a lottery ticket to acquire human-to-human transmission,” said Dr Devi Sridhar, a public health researcher at the University of Edinburgh.

Referring to the statement by the UFW, Professor Francois Balloux, director of the UCL Genetics Institute, added: “The most puzzling aspect to me is not even the incompetence and paralysis of the authorities but the resignation and fatalism. It feels like reading some chronicle by a mediaeval peasant.”

Of the roughly 1,000 people infected with H5N1 since the virus was first identified in the late 1990s, almost half have died. However, most historical cases have resulted from contact with wild birds, while the strain circulating in cattle, known as genotype B.12, is thought to cause much milder illness.

Concerns have nevertheless grown after an unidentified farm worker in Washington state died in late October from the cattle-derived H5N1 strain, raising questions about whether the virus may have mutated.

The Trump administration has been heavily criticised for allowing bird flu to run rampant through America’s wild and domestic animals, putting people at risk.

Deep cuts to the federal agencies responsible for managing human and animal health, the US Centers for Disease Control (CDC) and the Department of Agriculture (USDA), have resulted in the scaling down of surveillance and testing programmes amongst both livestock and farm workers.

Every infection, animal or human, raises the chance the virus could mutate and eventually gain the ability to spread between people – something which experts have long warned could trigger the next pandemic.

As flu season begins, experts are concerned a dairy worker infected with ordinary seasonal flu could catch H5N1 at the same time, and the two viruses could mix to create a new, more dangerous strain that could spread between people – a phenomenon known as “reassortment.”

“It is clear that workers are not being informed of the risks of handling sick cattle and infected milk. They are being given no information on flu shots or avian flu testing,” the UFW said.

Estimates suggest that over half of the 150,000-strong dairy workforce in the US are immigrant or undocumented workers, driven in part by high demand for intensive year-round labour and a lack of domestic applicants.

Many are reportedly worried about coming forward for testing over fears they will come into contact with US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the federal agency emboldened under Trump, which has been tasked with deporting one million immigrants every year.

Yakima Valley, the region of Washington State where the three recent H5N1 cases have been reported and where the virus is spreading through dozens of dairy herds, is in the midst of an ICE crackdown.

Sports.title: Max Dowman set to break Jude Bellingham’s incredible England record as Lee Carsley backs Arsenal whiz for superstardom

MAX DOWMAN will break Jude Bellingham’s record as the youngest-ever England U21s player if he plays against Portugal at Ashton Gate on Friday.

And Lee Carsley reckons the pair already share the same incredible mentality that can take them anywhere.



Carsley told SunSport: “I think players that get exposed early, what they generally have is that mentality.

“They’re not overwhelmed by anything, it’s just another challenge. Max definitely looks like he’s got those traits.



“Whatever he does, there’s always something more to come from him.”

Bellingham was just 17 years, two months and six days old when he debuted against Kosovo in 2020.

But Dowman, 16, can smash that record by almost FOUR MONTHS if he plays against Portugal or France during the international break.

Bellingham has gone on to earn 60 caps for the first team, play in four major tournaments and become one of the best players in the world since his U21s debut.

But Carsley reckons you can’t even put a ceiling on Dowman’s potential.

He added: “God knows where his ceiling is going to be. He’s a very, very high potential player who’s at the right club with Arsenal and getting pushed along at a nice speed.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“We’ve got a chance now to be part of that development. Try not to put too much pressure on him and let him just enjoy his football when he comes with us.”

Dowman has already played for England at youth level from Under-16s, but this is the first time he has been called up to the U21s.

Carsely has had a keen eye on Dowman throughout his development, but felt that now was the right time to give him the call-up.

The Young Lions chief reckons the pressure is off after his team have already qualified for next summer’s U21 European Championships, but felt that the games against Portugal and France would be the perfect test for Dowman.



He said: “I think there’s not as much pressure on the team now because we’ve qualified.

“So, it gives us a chance to look at him obviously in training also, which has been very good.

“He’s settled into the group very well, looks like he belongs here.

“It was a good chance for us now to get him some potential exposure against two really good teams.”

New teammate, Max Alleyne, has already been just as impressed by what he has seen by the teenager in training.



The Burnley centre-back told SunSport: “He’s sharp. So sharp One-v-One. Somehow he gets better when there’s more people around him. He just wriggles out of stuff.”

Alleyene, who is on loan from Arsenal’s title rivals Manchester City, can’t even remember what he was doing when he was Dowman’s age.

He added: “I think it’s tricky being that young. I can’t even remember what I was doing at 16 and I’m only 21.



“So, it must be tricky for him, but I think all the lads have been really good with him.

“Obviously, he knows a few of the lads from his club and things like that.

“But I think you can see there’s so much talent there. Even just watching the finishing drills and stuff like that, there’s so much talent there.

“He will be a massive player for us, I’m sure.”

He joked: “He’s lucky enough to not have a chance to attack against me yet because it would be embarrassing for him.”

Sports.title: On Harry Kane’s big night, Jude Bellingham proves he’s ready to shatter record.. but forced to wait to play with brother
Sports.content:

JUDE BELLINGHAM will have to wait a little longer before he shares the pitch with his brother Jobe.

It is 19 years since Neville and Phil Neville played their final game together for England.



Whether it is against Spain on Sunday, or in the Nations League quarter-finals in March – or even next summer – the Bellinghams will soon write their own piece of England history.

Yet to spend the last few days training with his younger sibling, while also walking out of the Wembley dressing room at the same time together, will have been an unbelievably special moment not just for the Real Madrid midfielder but the entire family.



There have been a few occasions under Thomas Tuchel, both during 2025 and even before the World Cup, when the relationship with Bellingham looked a bit broken but it has been salvaged.

So Bellingham has ended the year as we all hoped, a hugely important part of an England team and probably the next Englishman who will win the Ballon d’Or – unless Harry Kane does it again next season which is entirely possible.



While this night was all about Kane, we should remember Bellingham the elder was making his 61st senior appearance and he is still only 23.

So however many caps record-breaker Kane makes, and it will be 150 and beyond, Bellingham will be the player, if there is one, who races through and smashes that record before motoring towards 200 appearances.

Since the World Cup when he was England’s best player, Bellingham has been playing with a smile on his face.

So 2026 will be remembered as the year when Bellingham finally came of age in a Three Lions shirt and it is no coincidence that of his 14 England goals, eight have come since June.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Bellingham was not at his best against the Croatians although he took a whack on the foot in the first minute which he was not very happy about.

Equally, he was on a booking from the previous game – meaning another yellow would have seen him banned for the Spain match – and it did seem as though he was playing with a degree of caution.

Even so, he still had a hand in the opening goal, when Kane delivered an outstanding pass to the back post and Bellingham knocked the ball back across goal towards his West Midlands chum Morgan Rogers.

When you consider Bellingham has known Rogers since he was a kid – and went to his fifth birthday party in Halesowen – he already has an extremely strong emotional tie with one team-mate which in itself is unusual.



For that opening goal, it was Bellingham’s sixth assist for England in 2026, the most by a player for the national team in a calendar year since Raheem Sterling also chipped in with six in 2019.

Because Bellingham plays in an incredibly offensive position and as a fellow forward to Kane, he will also expect to score every time he plays.

At times, England’s formation is more like a 4-4-2 and when Kane drops deep to receive the ball, Bellingham is the highest player up the pitch.

And he will be desperate to make his mark when he heads to the home of Real’s arch rivals Atletico to face the world champions this weekend.



It will certainly be a tougher test than this one although England were certainly not at their best in a scruffy 2-1 win.

Tuchel will once again field a strong team against Spain and there will not be much experimenting.

However, if the pair do play together, there will not be a dry eye among the Bellingham family – and that will include the two lads out on the pitch.

Sports.title: England 2 Croatia 1: Harry Kane marks record Three Lions appearance with goal as Jude Bellingham equals 7-year feat
Sports.content:

NOT quite a Royal Command Performance to honour the cap King, even with a real-life Prince leading the accolades.

But a goal, of course, a penalty slotted with the minimum of fuss, now leaves him just eight short of the century he craves.



And while there was never going to be a repeat of the 7-0 thumping England inflicted last month, Harry Kane’s special night still saw Wembley applauding Captain Fantastic.

With Prince William among the crowd, the captain’s 126th England appearance, surpassing Peter Shilton’s tally, ended with him being the match-winner again.



Just minutes after Jarell Quansah’s horror moment, failing to guide a header back towards Jordan Pickford and presenting Petar Susic with a tap-in equaliser, the Leverkusen defender was sent tumbling at the other end.

The VAR check was only going to finish with Danish ref Morten Krogh pointing to the spot and on this of all evenings, Kane’s 27th spot kick conversion for his country was utterly nailed-on, sweeping home before that trademark celebration, his family up in the gods joining in.

It ensured another, not entirely comfortable win, after Morgan Rogers put England in front in the first half.

November evenings under the Arch against Croatia have not always been about the good things.

But nineteen years on from the sodden debacle that meant Steve McLaren was sacked before breakfast the next morning, it was very different for Thomas Tuchel and his players.

A night to celebrate England’s greatest marksman, most-capped player and – for many – the finest in the nation’s illustrious heritage, which began with his team-mates joining Wembley in paying tribute.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The golden colours on the front of a match programme that was almost entirely dedicated to his international career was designed in homage to the Golden Boy.

Kane is the symbol of English football, a giant among the Three Lions of history, his face adorning a huge “126” celebratory tifo that rose to the roof behind one goal.

His feats in that white shirt have taken him into the same pantheon as the other footballing knights – Moore, Charlton, Hurst and Beckham among them – he is surely set to join when he hangs up his boots.

Yet for now, there is no thought of that, just a quest for more – the first to score 100 England goals, the first to 150 caps, the first since Moore to lift a trophy into the skies.

That could come as early as the summer, even if the Nations League is barely the Carabao Cup of international football competitions.



This victory secured their place in the last eight and they could still top the group to secure home advantage for the quarter-final second leg in March with a win in Madrid on Sunday.

Injuries meant Kane was among just seven retained starters from the side that thrashed the Croats in Rijeka, with the defence most significantly changed, while Luka Modric was among five men missing from Slaven Bilic’s team.

Modric was still involved in the evening, presenting Kane with a special gift – a replica of the first ball brought to Croatia – before kick-off.

Not that Kane saw too much of the match balls being used as England made a sloppy start, with Jude Bellingham, Lewis Hall, Quansah and Elliot Anderson all initially uncomfortable.



Fortunately for Tuchel’s side, the Croats looked like a team whose thoughts were on damage limitation, before Kane’s glorious crossfield ball to the overlapping Hall got the home team going.

Anderson was just too high from 18 yards, Trent Alexander-Arnold’s strike was blocked, Rogers sneaked in round the back but could not find the skipper.

And on 24 minutes, Kane was involved as he picked out Bellingham’s run in behind the Croatian left wing-back with a perfect diagonal.

The Real Madrid ace played it back across goal to get his sixth international assist of 2026, equaling Raheem Sterling‘s record for the most recorded in a calendar year.



Josko Gvardiol made the sort of mistake that has plagued Manchester City in recent weeks, failing to deal with the ball, and Rogers forced over the line from a couple of yards.

Mateo Kovacic stung Pickford’s fingers from distance with England still playing in second gear.

In Dallas in the summer, England flew out of the blocks in the second half to blow the Croats away.

Had Kane not been blocked in front of goal by Josip Stanisic, after Rogers and Declan Rice had sliced up the visitors six minutes after the restart, there might have been a repeat. It was delaying, not denying.

Anthony Gordon went close before Quansah’s shocker after a scrappy corner allowed Susic to poke home the unlikely equaliser just before the hour.



Yet almost instantly, defender Ivan Smolcic needlessly dragged Quansah to the ground from Rice’s corner, giving Kane the chance he eagerly snapped up.

England were still vulnerable and hesitant defensively, Nikola Vlasic close after getting the wrong side of Dan Burn and there was a smattering of boos for Ben White when he replaced Alexander-Arnold – some grudges remain.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The flag, rightly raised against Bellingham, denied James Garner a first England goal late-on.

But this was an evening about one man above all. We are lucky to have him.

Sports.title: Arsenal star Ben White BOOED by England fans in first international appearance for eight months
Sports.content:
Next

BEN WHITE was BOOED by England fans after he was subbed on against Croatia.

The Arsenal star was making his first appearance for the Three Lions since March 31.



His last outing for England was against Japan before the World Cup just four days after scoring in the 1-1 draw against Uruguay.

White, 29, was recalled by Thomas Tuchel for the Nations League games against Croatia and Spain.



He was sent on in the second half of the match against Croatia at Wembley Stadium, replacing Trent Alexander-Arnold.

But the fans were divided in the stands with vocal boos being heard directed at him.



White was not picked by Tuchel for the World Cup with Reece James, Djed Spence and Jarrell Quansah being selected ahead of him.

He was booed in both friendly matches against Uruguay and Japan ahead of the tournament in the USA.

It followed on from his self-imposed exile from the previous World Cup in Qatar when he returned home midway through the tournament.

While there was a bust-up involving Steve Holland, it is understood there were other reasons the versatile defender – who had not featured in any of the matches – made the huge decision to leave the Middle East.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

White has since claimed that fans would not be booing him if they knew more about the situation.

He said: “It’s something I haven’t spoken about and I won’t go into detail about it but it’s a decision that I don’t want to talk about anyone in a negative way.

“It wasn’t an ideal situation but it’s probably one I would make again.

“Obviously, it’s amazing to be here in a fresh moment ahead of the two amazing games.



“There were loads of things that happened and communication wasn’t great. I don’t want to throw anyone under the bus.

“A lot of people tried to do that to me so it’s something I wouldn’t want to do myself.

“I don’t think I am looking to win anyone over or say anything that helps them get back on my side.

“It is what it is. There are reasons for it and I am just looking forward to playing for England and doing well and looking for success.”

White helped England see out the win over Croatia to set up a must-win game against Spain on Sunday.

Morgan Rogers opened the scoring in the first half but Petar Sucic levelled for the visitors after the break.

Harry Kane netted from the spot to restore the lead for the hosts and earn the win.

Sports.title: Kane the hero on historic night as England book Nations League QF spot
Sports.content:
Record-breaker Harry Kane scored from the spot to seal England's place in the Nations League quarter-finals with a 2-1 victory over Croatia, capping a memorable Wembley night as the captain became his country's most-capped player.

There was an inevitability about Kane hitting the net on his 126th appearance. There had been pre-match tributes and accolades as the Ballon d'Or holder passed the mark of legendary goalkeeper Peter Shilton and once again Kane was England's match winner with his second-half spot-kick. That's 92 goals now in England colours for the record scorer.

The win means England will now have the chance to win Nations League Group A3 and be seeded for the quarter-finals - but they will have to be far better than this if they are to beat table-toppers and world champions Spain in Madrid on Sunday.

When are the Nations League quarter-finals? The Nations League quarter-finals will take place in March, with the top two from each League A group going into the draw.



Teams which finish top of their group will be seeded and drawn against teams which have finished second for the two-leg ties which will determine who make it into the Nations League finals in June.

England thumped Croatia 7-0 last month but this was a performance far shy of that previous display, lacking intensity and final-third spark for long periods, and littered with jittery moments at the back.

Thankfully for Thomas Tuchel, he has Kane. The captain orchestrated the opener in his trademark style, dropping deep before clipping a fine pass for Jude Bellingham to cross for Morgan Rogers to bundle in when Josko Gvardiol failed to clear.

Image: England's Morgan Rogers scores a goal against Croatia

But moments after Kane's Bayern Munich team-mate Josip Stansic made a key block on the England skipper, Jarell Quansah's blunder gave Croatia a gift. His header back to Jordan Pickford was too casual and pounced on by Petar Sucic.

Quansah almost immediately made amends, being hauled down from an England corner by Ivan Smolcic for Kane to have his big moment.

But still England couldn't go up through the gears. James Garner's celebrations were cut short by an offside flag but the final stages were nervy for the hosts, with Nikola Vlasic wastefully clipping wide and Ante Budimir heading over.

On Kane's historic night, England were again indebted to their captain fantastic.

Image: Harry Kane scores a penalty against Croatia

Pre-match tributes for record-breaker Kane

Image: Harry Kane proudly shows off his Ballon d'Or to the Wembley crowd

Image: England fans showed off a Harry Kane tifo before kick-off

Image: Harry Kane poses with the Prince of Wales

Image: Harry Kane is presented with an award by Peter Shilton, whose record for England appearances he surpassed

Kane on 'incredible' night

England captain Harry Kane:

"It was incredible. Everything was amazing. Thank you to everyone who organised [the build-up], with the tifo and presentations. Thank you to Luka [Modric] and Croatia for their gift.

"I knew there would be something before the game. It's been a crazy few weeks with a lot happening, but it's an important moment in our history as a national team.

"But once the game started it was full focus. These occasions feel much better when you win and now I can take a breath and enjoy this."

As it happened at Wembley...

15: CLOSE! Elliot Anderson goes close to his first England goal with a decent snapshot from 20 yards.

18: BLOCK! A Bellingham cross is cleared as far as Trent Alexander-Arnold, who strikes it well but into the body of Josip Misic.

24: GOAL! Kane's fine pass into the box finds Bellingham to volley a cross for Rogers to bundle in.

48: WIDE! Anthony Gordon takes aim but doesn't get the bend on his shot he'd like and it flies well wide.

51: BIG BLOCK! Kane is denied a goal when his Bayern Munich team-mate Stanisic gets in the way as the England captain tries to turn in Declan Rice's cutback.

55: PENALTY APPEALS! But there's deemed to be no foul when Gordon is bundled over by Misic before Bellingham hits the target with a follow-up shot.

59: GOAL! Quansah tries to head the ball back to Jordan Pickford from a Croatia corner but Sucic is there to pounce and poke in. A bad mistake from the England centre-back!

63: PENALTY TO ENGLAND! After a VAR check referee Morten Krogh awards England a penalty for Quansah being pulled down from an England corner by Smolcic.

64: GOAL! Record-breaker Kane scores from the spot for England goal number 92.

82: BIG CHANCE! But Vlasic clips his shot wide when he looked set to equalise.

86: NO GOAL! Garner is denied his first England goal by the offside flag.

88: BLOCK! Quansah slides in to block Budimir's shot.

90+2: CHANCE! But Budimir heads over from a late corner.

Analysis: An historic night for Kane - but forgettable performance from England

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett at Wembley Stadium:

"As a game, it was instantly forgettable. As an occasion, it will live long in the memory. But that is all about what happened pre-match, rather than during the 90 minutes.

"Captain Kane being recognised as not only the best player in the world, but also as England's most capped player of all time, was a proper "I was there" moment. Inevitably, he scored to mark the occasion, with a coolly-slotted second-half penalty.

"But beyond that, England were disappointing. Flat. Lifeless, in the main. Lacking energy, spark and invention. The two full-backs, Alexander-Arnold and Hall, came out of it with some credit. And Elliot Anderson was as industrious and effective as ever. But that was about it.

"It was enough to ensure a victory - just about - and to set up a winner-takes-all Nations League group finale against the world champions Spain in Madrid on Sunday. Maybe England's players had that game in the back of their minds, and held back a bit. Let's hope that's what it was, anyway."

Sports.title: Kane makes history with record 126th England cap
Sports.content:
Harry Kane has broken the record for the most senior England caps by a single player in history.

The Three Lions captain led the line for Thursday's Nations League game against Croatia, making his 126th appearance for his country in the process.

He bypasses the record previously held by goalkeeper Peter Shilton, who earned 125 caps between 1970 and 1990.

Shilton made a presentation to the England skipper on the pitch ahead of kick-off at Wembley.

Sports.title: The trilingual son of Mr Universe makes homecoming - NFL Gameday Guide
Sports.content:
Amon-Ra St. Brown. The globe-trotting trilingual son of Mr Universe, named after an Egyptian god, returning for the most special of homecomings to his mother's native land. This time, as one of the stars of the NFL.

Some five years ago, St. Brown spoke to Sky Sports about the importance of his German heritage ahead of entering the NFL Draft. And now he gets to honour it by doing what he does best.

The Detroit Lions will play an international game for the first time since November 2015 this Sunday when they host the New England Patriots at Munich's Allianz Arena.

His mother Miriam hails from Leverkusen and predominantly spoke to the Lions wide receiver and his two brothers in German growing up, while also taking them back to Europe each summer to spend time with their grandparents and play soccer.

St Brown even represented the German national team alongside brother Osiris during his sophomore year of high school, and since landing in the NFL, has worn decals of the German flag on his helmet and returned to host football camps in the country.

St Brown sat his SATs in English, German and French, spent time in French academy Lycee International de Los Angeles, spent a semester in Paris and joined his mother in travelling across the world with trips to Spain, Italy, London, France, the Caribbean, his German home from home and beyond. It was his mother Miriam who revealed the Lions would be playing in Munich on a FaceTime call set up by the Lions back in February.

At long last, he gets to take centre stage overseas as the NFL reaches the final stop on its European tour with the eighth of a record nine international games in 2026.

St Brown brings one of the NFL's most fascinating backgrounds as a ready-made ambassador for the league's increasing global reach, which will be championed by way of its sixth regular-season matchup in Germany since 2022.

His own global connections travel as far as Egyptian nomenclature, after his father John - a three-time Mr World and two-time Mr Universe body-builder - named his son after Amun, the ancient Egyptian deity.

It is Germany the NFL can thank for one of its most gifted players, with St Brown's parents having met at a fitness trade show in Cologne in 1987.

His transatlantic ties have naturally forged a love of soccer as he pitches up in the home of Bayern Munich, where Ballon d'Or-winning England captain Harry Kane has often spoken of his own ambitions to step into the world of St. Brown - as an NFL kicker.

Has he got the leg to do it? Sure. Would it ever happen? Most would say no. Funnily enough, his age by the end of his football career - he is 33 now - is probably a primary reason above all as to why it wouldn't happen.

But will we take advantage of the opportunity to shoehorn Kane's name into a headline? Duh. Clicks pay for this writer's coffee (they don't).

"If I was going to do it, I would take it seriously. I would probably dedicate six months to a year to training," said Kane earlier this year. "Maybe if I am in the MLS in the future or somewhere like that it might be a thing where you could connect the two maybe with the seasons."

Regardless, the NFL's global ventures have often amounted to crossover collaboration between its travelling teams and the sporting giants hosting them; last week Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson caught up with Jude Bellingham ahead of their matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals at the Bernabeu, where the likes of Thibaut Courtois, Marc Cucurella and Raphael Varane were in attendance. As far as growing the game is concerned, it is a no-brainer of an easy win.

The Lions arrive 6-2 in a fiercely competitive NFC North, St. Brown continuing to be Jared Goff's prized weapon on the outside with a team-high 61 catches for 657 yards (10th most in the league) and five touchdowns within an offense ranked fifth in yards per game and fifth in scoring.

Detroit have won four straight games, including divisional victories over both the Minnesota Vikings and Green Bay Packers in the last three weeks. Running back Jahmyr Gibbs is also at the heart of their success with an NFL-high 1,132 yards and 11 touchdowns from scrimmage.

New England are 5-4 and coming off a 45-27 defeat to the Packers during which Drake Maye, struggling to live up to his MVP-contending heights of last season, threw three interceptions.

The Patriots are battling to swerve a Super Bowl hangover after February's one-sided defeat to the Seattle Seahawks and return to play in Germany for the second time after losing to the Indianapolis Colts in Frankfurt in 2023.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Week 9 matchup between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Atlanta Falcons during the 2026 NFL season.

Germany remains one of the NFL's largest fanbases outside of North America, with millions of listeners having previously tuned in to the Armed Forces Network radio station based in Frankfurt during World War II.

The first broadcast out of AFN Frankfurt was on July 15, 1945 from a confiscated house, after which thousands of US troops remained stationed in Germany.

There were later five preseason NFL games in Germany from 1990 to 1994, while the country was also represented by the Hamburg Sea Devils, Rhein Fire, Berlin Thunder, Cologne Centurions and Frankfurt Galaxy in the former World League of American Football/NFL Europe/NFL Europa between 1991 and 2007.

It is Germany's time once again.

5 things to watch live on Sky:

No 1 player in football?

Is there another player in football who reigns as his position's outright No 1 more so than Fred Warner? Arguably not.

The San Francisco 49ers stalwart has occupied top spot among inside linebackers for multiple years now, and remains an unrivalled difference-maker from his role within Raheem Morris' defense.

Warner has been electric in his first campaign back since suffering a season-ending injury in Week Six of 2025, racking up 77 total tackles, five forced fumbles, a fumble recovery, half a sack, 5.5 stuffs and three pass breakups. Few, if any, diagnose the game better than Warner, whose film study is as refined and as expertly-exercised as any player in football.

An incredible sequence against the Las Vegas Raiders last week saw him punch the ball from the hands of Brock Bowers, recover Michael Mayers' fumble in the end zone and deny Kirk Cousins on a quarterback sneak with an incredible leaping stop over center Tyler Linderbaum in the space of about 10 minutes.

Wonder why teams are scared to throw over the middle of the field against the 49ers? Fred Warner.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player There was confusion during a Bengals play as the lights went out at the Bernabeu!

Kirko chains is back

The Minnesota Vikings would be Super Bowl contenders if they could just figure things out at quarterback, and on Tuesday they rolled the dice once more by trading to bring back Kirk Cousins.

Any scenario in which Justin Jefferson isn't getting the ball thrown his way becomes a major concern; the Vikings had no choice. Kyler Murray could not get it done, the Vikings traded away J.J. McCarthy to the New York Giants and on Monday night Carson Wentz epitomised this hobbling offense, which has failed miserably in its bid to back up Brian Flores' defense.

Cousins may be 38 years old, but has been impressive for the Las Vegas Raiders this season and gives Minnesota a significantly better chance of reigniting Jefferson, who has been starved of production.

Cousins is 202 of 315, passing for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns, eight interceptions, and a passer rating of 97.1 as he re-joins the franchise he played for from 2018-2023. Would be quite the story, huh?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jeff Reinebold says the recent trade action from the Jacksonville Jaguars has the fingerprints of their executive vice president of football operations, Tony Boselli, on the franchise, and believes they’re all in on going for a Super Bowl.

Surging Love

Jordan Love is flying, and it feels as though the Green Bay Packers are gathering Super Bowl momentum by the week as their offense begins to takeover.

Love now leads the NFL in passing yards with 2,618 for 19 touchdowns to six interceptions as the league's most aggressive splash-play merchant.

He ranks first in intended air yards (3,251), intended air yards per attempt (9.5) and completed air yards (1,553) at the heart of the league's second-best passing attack, within which his receivers have notably dropped a league-high 23 passes.

They have become box office viewing, with two No 1 receivers emerging in Christian Watson - third in the league with 879 yards - and Matthew Golden - fourth in the league with 783 yards.

Matt LaFleur has typically built his offense around run game foundations that he can tee off from through the air, but even through the NFL's worst rushing attack he is finding success thanks to Love's arm.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Week 9 matchup between the Green Bay Packers and New England Patriots during the 2026 NFL season.

AFC North decider?

Sunday Night Football stages one of the biggest games of the weekend when the Cincinnati Bengals take on the Pittsburgh Steelers in a possible AFC North division decider.

Both sit 6-2 with the Steelers holding the head-to-head advantage after their 30-27 win in the reverse fixture back in September, Jaylen Warren starring out of the backfield on that occasion with 176 yards from scrimmage.

But the Bengals have hit their stride with a four-game winning streak over the last month, Joe Burrow rising to MVP contention while playing some of the best football of his NFL career within the league's most potent passing attack.

Across that four-game span, Burrow has completed 77 per cent of passes for 1,215 yards with 18 total touchdowns, three interceptions and a 132.0 passer rating.

Cincinnati look like legitimate Super Bowl contenders again, producing their best start through eight games since 2015.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A corgi gets loose during halftime and delays the start of the Carolina Panthers game against the Denver Broncos.

Where are Stafford's weapons?

The 'super-team' Los Angeles Rams are not looking so super, and there is growing reason to be concerned over their playoff chances this season.

Sean McVay's side were dealt another crushing blow this week when it was revealed Puka Nacua had suffered a right knee injury set to land him on injured reserve and miss at least a month of action, adding to an absentee list already featuring Davante Adams.

Rams General Manager Les Snead is typically one of football's most aggressive dealers, but on Tuesday neglected to add receiver help for Matthew Stafford as they enter Sunday's divisional clash against the Arizona Cardinals 5-4.

McVay is known for his multiple tight end sets, and will now need to lean on as much alongside Kyren Williams and Blake Corum in order to keep this offense afloat

Sports.title: Overeem vs Manuwa added to Jake Paul's Christmas Eve fight card
Sports.content:
Alistair Overeem will make his professional boxing debut against Britain's Jimi Manuwa as the MMA stars collide on Jake Paul's comeback show on Christmas Eve.

Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) have confirmed that Overeem, known as 'The Demolition Man', and 'Poster Boy' Manuwa will meet in a six-round professional heavyweight boxing bout on the undercard of Paul's cruiserweight clash with Cedric Doumbe in Dubai.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Jake Paul’s new opponent, Cedric Doumbe, leave Kylian Mbappe stunned with this nine-second knockout in the PFL

Former Strikeforce heavyweight champion and K-1 World Grand Prix winner Overeem said: "I've fought the best in the world, and I've been a world champion in multiple disciplines. Now I'm starting a new chapter in boxing, and I'm not here to make up the numbers.

"Jimi Manuwa is a dangerous man with serious knockout power, but I've built my career on taking the toughest challenges in combat sports"

Image: British knockout artist and former UFC light heavyweight contender Jimi Manuwa will go up against Overeem

Manuwa, who began his professional MMA career in 2008, won his first 14 professional fights before establishing himself among the UFC's most dangerous strikers.

He retired from MMA in 2019 with a 17-6 record, with 15 of his 17 victories coming by knockout or technical knockout. The 46-year-old returned to competition in August 2026, making a successful professional boxing debut with a second-round TKO victory over former UFC heavyweight Chase Sherman.

Manuwa said: "London is in everything I do. Where I come from, pressure makes you, and it makes me.

"I've watched Alistair since I was coming up, and I know exactly what he's capable of. That's why I wanted this fight.

"After my win in Orlando, I wasn't looking for an easy opponent. On Christmas Eve, one of us is going to sleep, and it's not going to be me."

Overeem vs Manuwa adds another explosive encounter to the card headlined by global superstar Paul, on his return to the ring a year on from suffering a broken jaw in a sixth-round stoppage loss to former two-time unified heavyweight world champion Anthony Joshua.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jake Paul and his opponent Cedric Doumbe face-off for the first time ahead of their boxing match on December 24

MVP chief executive Nakisa Bidarian said: "Netherlands' Alistair Overeem and the United Kingdom's Jimi Manuwa are two of the most recognisable names in combat sports, with decades of experience competing against the best in the world and a combined 40 knockouts in MMA.

"Bringing these two legends together in a professional boxing match adds another compelling matchup to an already massive Christmas Eve event.

"With Jake Paul facing Cedric Doumbe in the main event, we're assembling a card that brings together some of the biggest personalities and most dangerous strikers in combat sports for fans in Dubai and around the world."
