Sports.title: F1 2026 calendar update: Imola off the table, no plan B if Iran war escalates
Sports.content:
The Qatar and Abu Dhabi grands prix which will conclude Formula 1’s 2026 season are set to proceed as planned, provided there is no dramatic escalation of the Iran war.

The Middle Eastern conflict, which started in late February as the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, has destabilised the region. The calendars of many motorsport championships have been impacted – not least F1’s, whose Saudi Arabian race was cancelled while Bahrain’s round was postponed and hosted in Malaysia.

F1 has been monitoring the situation closely, with a chilly Imola as an alternative season finale on the first weekend of December if Qatar and Abu Dhabi were unable to host their respective events.

Lusail did run its MotoGP round without major issues last weekend, though both Yamaha teams withdrew from the competition due to the geopolitical situation.

10 November was F1’s deadline to provide Imola with a final answer as to whether the Italian track would have to prepare for a grand prix in the next three weeks; it will not.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Isack Hadjar, Racing Bulls Photo by: Zak Mauger / Motorsport Images

So the 2026 season will end with the planned Las Vegas-Qatar-Abu Dhabi triple-header, with travel insurance and governments’ travel advice currently allowing it.

However, there’s a caveat: F1 is aware it cannot guarantee the situation won’t change by early December and insists it will prioritise safety if the conflict escalates.

Team bosses have been maintaining a straightforward stance on the matter – they trust F1 and the FIA to make the right calls.

“I trust them to take the best decision for all of us,” Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur commented in Mexico. “Me, personally, I want to race. It doesn't matter where, but I want to race. Now, I will go where they will tell us to go.”

“Stefano and Mohammed have been pretty clear about the situation that Formula 1 follows what the international guidelines are, whether there are travel restrictions, airlines not flying, any warnings in the region, the kind of feedback that local governments are making,” his Mercedes counterpart Toto Wolff added in Friday’s press conference at Interlagos. “So not only the promoters, but what the local governments are making. And this is what you need to rely on, in my opinion, and I'm fully with that.

Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Mark Sutton / Formula 1 via Getty Images

“I think that if riders stand up, who know nothing geopolitically about what's going on, but have an audience that listens, I think that is something that creates media value. But I would have done the same as MotoGP management has done. You want to ride or drive, go. If you don't want to, don't go. It's as simple as that, and everybody can take their personal decisions on that, and I respect that.

“Of course, you've got to be wary of what's happening in the next few days, a few weeks, and Stefano has his finger on the pulse to monitor that. If things were to get more dangerous and we would get that feedback, then he's going to be the first one, together with Mohammed, to protect the people that were meant to travel. So that's why I'm following their guidance.

“From what I'm hearing internally, it hasn't been raised. It hasn't been a topic. But also there, if someone feels they don't feel comfortable, he or she doesn't feel comfortable travelling, then it's something that I would always respect. And maybe that's an opportunity to give somebody else a chance. It wouldn't change anything for the relationship. I've always respected that some people didn't want to go to certain grands prix, and that's how I see it at the moment.”

Additional reporting by Ronald Vording

Sports.title: FIA reveals ADUO results in final review of 2026 F1 season
Sports.content:
The FIA has announced its final Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) results for the 2026 Formula 1 season, with no changes granted for any of the power unit manufacturers.

From this season, the FIA installed a mechanism in the F1 regulations which allowed power unit manufacturers the ability to make updates, if they fell behind the leading engine, in the form of tokens permitted under a performance scale.

After the first period in 2026, which ran from the Australian Grand Prix to the Canadian GP, it was announced that Red Bull Ford Powertrains emerged as the benchmark, while Mercedes’ internal combustion engine trails by between 2-4%, which gave the German manufacturer to one additional upgrade this year and one more next season.

Ferrari, Audi and Honda fell into the category of being more than 4% behind on ICE power, which grants them two upgrades during the current campaign and two more in 2027.

Red Bull Ford Powertrains asked for a review of the ADUO analysis, which delayed the official publication of the first results, as it disputed the results and being considered the manufacturer with the strongest engine.

As agreed before the start of the season by the teams, the FIA only measures the internal combustion engine, but once a manufacturer qualifies for ADUO, it is also allowed to modify electrical components such as the battery and MGU-K.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Colin McMaster / LAT Images via Getty Images

So while Red Bull’s rivals have been able to install power unit upgrades across this season, the Milton Keynes-based effort has effectively faced an engine freeze.

In the third and final FIA analysis of ADUO – which took engine data from the Dutch GP up to and including the US GP – there has been no change and therefore no manufacturer will gain or lose its current concessions.

There was also no change in the second ADUO period over the summer.

“For the third period, the relative performance gaps to the leading ICE evolved, but these changes did not result in any additional homologations being granted to the Power Unit Manufacturers,” an FIA report stated.

Given the dispute over how ADUO is measured, the FIA is open to changes in the system in the future, subject to approval from the power unit manufacturers, while FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis is confident the concept is working as desired.

“The FIA has undertaken extensive analysis as part of the review of ADUO this year. Based on the quality of the data and the robustness of the assessment process, we are confident in our findings and the conclusions reached,” Tombazis said.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

“The first year of implementation has also reinforced our belief that the ADUO concept is the right one for Formula 1.

“However, it is important that the system continues to evolve to ensure it remains efficient, relevant and fit for purpose. To that end, we have been working closely with the power unit manufacturers and teams to explore refinements to the methodology that will support the continued effectiveness of ADUO in future seasons.”

The next ADUO period will start in 2027, covering the opening six races of the F1 season from the Bahrain GP to the Miami GP.

Sports.title: What's behind Piastri's split with Webber – and what it means for his F1 career
Sports.content:
On the Monday after the Formula 1 Brazilian Grand Prix, Oscar Piastri and Mark Webber announced in a joint statement that the latter and Ann Neal would no longer manage the 25-year-old McLaren driver. The timing may come as a surprise – now rather than at the end of the season – but the news itself had been on the cards for some time.

The clearest hint came from Piastri during pre-season testing in Bahrain. While this writer was mainly interested in his opinion of the 2026 cars – which immediately brought a telling smile to Piastri's face – an Australian colleague raised the subject of Webber's changing role.

Read Also: Formula 1 Piastri and Webber terminate management agreement

"There wasn't anything specific, we just made a decision for things to look a bit different," Piastri said on that unusually cold February evening in the Bahrain paddock. "Mark is still very much involved and I've been in contact with him a lot over the last few weeks. He just won't be trackside as much anymore. So that's really the extent of it. There was nothing specific that triggered it."

Although that last point is essentially true, it is clear that the 2025 season was intense on several fronts – including behind the scenes, at least from Webber’s perspective. That was naturally closely linked to the 'papaya rules' through which McLaren tried to treat both drivers as fairly as possible, but which also made life difficult for the team at certain moments, as Andrea Stella frankly admitted at the beginning of this year.

It is no secret that Webber was not always happy with how McLaren handled certain moments on track, nor with the explanation for Piastri's dip in form during the final quarter of the season, which ultimately cost him the world title. It is important to emphasise, however, that a manager's role is also to defend the interests of his own driver, even though there are multiple ways of doing so.

Webber naturally had the experiences from his own Red Bull years in mind and wanted to prevent Piastri from ever being labelled a number two driver in the F1 paddock. In a recent interview with Autosport, former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner even described this as a key part of Webber's mentality, a worldview that Horner believes he brought into the cockpit.

"I think probably the difficulty with Mark was, he motivated himself through adversity. He always drove better when he felt that the world was against him," Horner said. "He could see this talent emerging in Sebastian [Vettel], and he was using everything in his locker to try and destabilise that, or to cause any tension in a way that would then fall back in his favour. I think as a team we were learning how to handle these dynamics."

Watch: Christian Horner on Toto, Abu Dhabi 2021 and Life After Red Bull.

The differences between Red Bull back then and McLaren today are considerable, however. Red Bull was led at the time by Horner and Helmut Marko, two men who were certainly no strangers to the political side of F1, whereas McLaren is now much more engineering-led under Andrea Stella, who constantly emphasises the principles by which he wants to go racing – including fairness. This brings a different dynamic and also means that any attempts to avoid being pushed into a number two role are viewed in a completely different light.

It must be emphasised that McLaren has never formally asked Piastri to change his management, but Autosport understands that the driver himself, with some input from those around him, has formed his own view of what he needs going forward.

In any case, the decision had already been made at the beginning of this year for Webber to take a step back and operate primarily 'behind the scenes' rather than being in the spotlight during race weekends. With hindsight, that was a first step towards this split, which, according to the statement, has come about by mutual agreement. "Following our reduced trackside involvement this season, we have collectively agreed that now is an appropriate time to bring our management agreement to a close," Webber said.

Piastri's development and a new reality in the F1 driver market

Aside from all that, it must also be said that Piastri's situation is very different now from what it was at the beginning of his career. Consequently, what he needs from the people around him has changed as well. This applies in two areas: his experience as a driver and the current situation in the F1 driver market.

In his younger years, Piastri needed Webber's experience as a racing driver more than he does now. When the Australian made his F1 debut at the age of 21 – and was, as Toto Wolff tends to describe young drivers, still a "deer in the headlights" – it helped to have a trusted figure by his side who had already experienced it all. Someone outside the team who was concerned solely with his interests and could help him avoid potential pitfalls.

When Autosport spoke to Piastri in Barcelona during his debut season, that was precisely the added value he highlighted: "Mark’s advice was to not underestimate the challenge of F1 and how big of a step up it is, not just from the cars but from everything: the amount of people you need to interact with, the media commitments, and the sponsor commitments. It's all much higher than before. I think having him reminding me of that before the season started was nice, not to be shocked when I arrived. That's probably been the biggest thing.

Oscar Piastri, McLaren F1 Team, 2nd position, is congratulated by Mark Webber in Parc Ferme Photo by: Steven Tee / Motorsport Images

"But he's very helpful with small driving tips here and there as well, and sometimes thinking of questions for the engineers that don't even come to my head at the moment.

"He's still very sharp. He thinks like a racing driver still and is always trying to get the best out of me."

More than three years later, Piastri has experienced all of this himself and therefore needs that hands-on guidance as a driver less than he did during his rookie season. Logically, this means that a different type of management can now suffice, with different priorities in that respect as well.

Moreover, the situation in the driver market has changed. Piastri is committed to McLaren for the longer term, with a contract running until the end of 2028. Yes, an extraordinary amount has been said and written about Piastri's seat this summer, particularly in light of the Max Verstappen rumours, which have been blown considerably out of proportion by certain publications. In reality, however, the Dutchman indicated that he had come much closer to retiring from F1 than to moving to another team, meaning Piastri has not seriously been looking elsewhere either.

He did describe it as 'flattering' that his name was linked with Red Bull during the summer months, but the reality is that this route appears to be closed for the coming years. After all, Verstappen has extended his contract, meaning Red Bull – provided it gives him a competitive car – has its lead driver in place. And with talents such as Isack Hadjar, Arvid Lindblad and perhaps Nikola Tsolov in the longer term, Red Bull appears perfectly capable of filling its second seat from within its own talent pool.

Add to that the fact that Mercedes and Ferrari also still have long-term lead drivers in Kimi Antonelli and Charles Leclerc, and maintaining and further strengthening his relationship with McLaren seems far more important for Piastri than having contacts elsewhere, for example through Webber at Red Bull. These two factors may still make the timing surprising, but not so much the decision itself to end the partnership after Webber had already taken a step back.

Oscar Piastri, McLaren with Mark Webber Photo by: Getty Images

Finally, it must be said that Webber did play a key role in the early years of Piastri's career, one that should not be forgotten at a moment like this. Indeed, Piastri himself has not forgotten it either, as his quote in the joint statement demonstrates: "I'd like to thank Mark and Ann for all their support and advice over the years. Their guidance has been invaluable, particularly in navigating the beginning of my F1 career. I wish them all the best going forward."

The most important move, of course, was leaving Alpine for McLaren, including Piastri's now-famous tweet. That was a period in which Webber's 'us against the world' mentality, as Horner described it, proved particularly useful. The move also saved Piastri from the quicksand that Alpine was, especially at that time. It is a decision for which he remains grateful, but this phase of his career calls for something different, and that explains why the partnership between two of the four most recent Australian F1 drivers has come to an end.

Webber played an important role in getting Piastri to where he is today, and the current seventh-placed driver in the championship has not forgotten that. But he feels that something different is needed for the next phase of his career, ideally one of harmony within McLaren – and, given all of the above, that is understandable.

Sports.title: How the Racing Bulls pendulum is swinging back towards Lawson
Sports.content:
When job security is in short supply, there's one solution for an Formula 1 driver. Be so good they can't ignore you.

That's easier said than done, but it certainly seems to be what Liam Lawson has taken to heart as he battled for his future over the recent Americas triple-header. Having been an integral part of Racing Bulls' rise to fifth in the constructors' championship, which will be the Anglo-Italian team's best-ever result, Lawson took ninth in Austin before bagging a pair of seventh-place finishes in Mexico and Brazil.

Following his challenger Nikola Tsolov's strong FP1 debut in Mexico, and Lawson's unfortunate run-in with Red Bull's stalwart Max Verstappen, signs are now pointing towards the pendulum having swung back in Lawson's favour with a decision expected over the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend next week. A report from The Race, which Autosport understands is accurate, says Lawson is now set to stay put after all with Tsolov coming on board as a reserve in 2027. Sources have indicated a final decision is close but not signed off yet.

Driving for his future has been exhausting for Lawson, even if it's not a new situation for the 24-year-old. Ever since he arrived as a deputy for the injured Daniel Ricciardo in 2023, Lawson has effectively been fighting for his seat, first from the sidelines and then as Ricciardo's full-time replacement with little to no job security beyond the next race weekend.



It all came to a head over the past triple-header as Racing Bulls and the wider Red Bull organisation kept delaying a final call between Lawson and Tsolov.



If Racing Bulls had been a standalone team, the decision to retain Lawson and Arvid Lindblad would have been a no-brainer. Rookie Lindblad is still seen as potential Red Bull material in the future. And while that window appears to have come and gone for Lawson, he has amassed 89 points as the highest point scorer outside the top four teams.



With Racing Bulls tasked to train young drivers for the Red Bull senior team though, it is understood Red Bull's Austrian parent company is particularly excited by F2 frontrunner Tsolov's promise. However, a decision to keep Lawson wouldn't necessarily work against Racing Bull's objective, as having such a solid benchmark in the other car has been useful to gauge Lindblad's performances this year too. Meanwhile, 19-year-old Tsolov would still benefit from a full year as a reserve driver, which includes more FP1s, private testing and simulator work.

Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Guido De Bortoli / LAT Images via Getty Images

Racing Bulls qualifying head-to-head

Arvid Lindblad 7-14 (6-11 without sprints) Liam Lawson 9 (+1.253s in Q3) Australia 8 15 (+0.334s in SQ2) China (sprint) 13 15 (+0.019s in Q2) China 14 10 Japan 14 (+0.386s in Q2) 16 Miami (sprint) 17 (+0.171s in SQ1) 17 (+0.538s in Q1) Miami 12 9 Canada (sprint) DNS 9 Canada 12 (+0.349s in Q2) 15 (+0.777s in Q2) Monaco 10 11 (+0.255s in Q2) Barcelona 8 10 (+0.052s in Q3) Austria 9 10 (+0.440s in SQ3) Britain (sprint) 9 9 Britain 10 (+0.411s in Q3) 8 Belgium 11 (+0.491s in Q2) 9 Hungary 11 (+0.405s in Q2) 15 (+0.246s in Q2) Azerbaijan 12 16 (no time - grid penalty) Bahrain in Malaysia 11 17 (+0.281s in SQ1) Singapore (sprint) 8 10 (+0.412s in Q3) Singapore 9 9 United States 10 (No lap time in Q3) 9 (+0.088s in Q3) Mexico 8 14 (+4.638s in Q2 - rain) Brazil 5

Racing Bulls has also been explicitly asked by Austria to stand on its own feet both in terms of identity and performance, so that's why a dyed-in-the-wool F1 veteran like team principal Alan Permane would have been keen to maximise performance and stick with Lawson.



"The main factors are, as always, pace and speed. That's the very first thing we look for," Permane said when grilled on the topic on Friday in Sao Paulo. "But we're not just a team that exists solely to compete. We are here to bring young talent through, so we have to keep an eye on that. And that doesn't necessarily mean that we just keep churning young talent through the car. We need to maybe have some experience as well to measure that talent."

The clearest hint that a difference in opinion between the various stakeholders is what has really been holding up the decision came from Lawson himself. "I feel like Alan's been extremely supportive to me and I appreciate that a lot," he said. "I've enjoyed working closely with him and with the team this year. Obviously, it's a big organisation so..."



Permane recently inked a fresh deal until 2031 as Racing Bulls team principal and co-CEO, so it's obvious that his opinion carries plenty of weight. And it would stand to reason that Permane has wanted some assurances about his share in the decision-making before committing.

"Alan is doing a tremendous job, and the progress the team has made is a direct reflection of his experience, commitment and competitive mindset," said Permane's boss Oliver Mintzlaff, CEO Corporate Projects and Investments Red Bull. "He brings clarity, composure, and a deep understanding of what it takes to perform in Formula 1, while creating an environment where people can consistently deliver at their best."

Meanwhile, fans of Lawson and the team have been flooding the squad's social media channels urging it to re-sign the Kiwi. He said: "I appreciate all the support. I've seen it over the last few weeks. It's honestly really nice to see.

A treacherous Brazil weekend was one of Liam Lawson's finest. Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

"Obviously, I would love it if it was more from a team. But at the moment I'm just trying to enjoy driving the car because with everything else going on I don't really know what else I'm meant to do. I don't really know what else I'm meant to say to you guys. So, at the moment I'm just going to keep driving and see what happens."

When it mattered the most, Brazil was perhaps Lawson's finest weekend yet. In treacherous conditions, Lawson took fifth on the grid, starting from third after grid penalties for George Russell and Charles Leclerc.

In the rain, he picked off McLaren's Lando Norris for second at the start, only to fall back to his natural position once drivers got their intermediate tyres back in the right operating window. Lawson battled to claim eighth on the road, being promoted to seventh after Leclerc was penalised for barging his way past in the closing laps.



Permane was obviously appreciative of how tough the past few weeks and months have been on one of F1 2026's standout performers, but said the team is nearly there.



"I realise it's frustrating for our drivers," he added. "I realise it's frustrating for everyone else, but we want to get it right, and we will get it right. I'm sure when we announce it in the coming weeks, everyone will be happy..."

Sports.title: Court of Appeal to hear Audi’s case over Tsunoda decision on November 25th | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The International Court of Appeal has set a date to hear Audi’s appeal over the Italian Grand Prix stewards’ decision regarding Yuki Tsunoda.

Audi is challenging the decision not to penalise Tsunoda, who finished the race in 10th position, for triggering an extra formation lap before the start of the race.

The ICA will hear the case on November 25th at the FIA’s headquarters in Paris.

Tsunoda, who substituted for Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson at Monza, finished seven seconds ahead of Gabriel Bortoleto. Therefore the Audi driver could gain a point if Tsunoda is penalised.

Bortoleto previously said Audi’s case was “straightforward”.

F1’s sporting regulations state any driver who causes an extra formation lap must start the race from the pit lane and will receive a Stop-and-Go penalty if they fail to. As Tsunoda did not start from the pit lane, Audi believes he should receive a penalty.

The stewards ruled Tsunoda “was not the ’cause’ of the extra formation lap” and therefore did not have to start from the pit lane.

This is the second time this year the ICA has been asked to rule on a decision taken by the stewards at a grand prix. In September they reinstated two penalties which were originally issued to Pierre Gasly during the Monaco Grand Prix and later rescinded.

ICA hearing announcement

On 6th September 2026, at the end of the formation lap during the race restart following a red flag, the race director ordered an additional formation lap Following the race, the stewards investigated a potential breach of Article B5.9.4 of the 2026 FIA Formula 1 Sporting Regulations by Mr Yuki Tsunoda (driver of car number 22), which requires any driver who caused an extra formation lap to start from the end of the pit lane. Failure to do so, a Stop-and-Go penalty should be imposed on the driver. In decision number 69, the stewards decided to take no further action against Mr Yuki Tsunoda. On 9th September 2026, Audi Revolut F1 Team lodged an appeal against that decision, arguing that Mr Yuki Tsunoda had caused the extra formation lap and should therefore have received the prescribed Stop-and-Go penalty.

Sports.title: Racing Bulls keep Lawson and Lindblad as Tsolov gets Red Bull reserve role | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Racing Bulls has confirmed an unchanged driver line-up for the 2027 Formula 1 season.

Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad will continue to drive for the team next year.

The news ends speculation Red Bull’s second Formula 1 team would replace either of its drivers with Nikola Tsolov. The Red Bull junior driver lies second in the Formula 2 standings with four races remaining.

Shortly after Racing Bulls confirmed its driver line-up, Red Bull announced Tsolov as its reserve driver for 2027. Red Bull also announced Tsolov will be Racing Bulls’ reserve driver.

Racing Bulls is on course to score its best championship result under any of its identities, including its time competing as Minardi, before it was purchased by Red Bull at the end of 2005.

However Lawson’s future at the team came into doubt as Racing Bulls delayed its decision on its driver line-up for next year. Lawson made his F1 debut in 2023 and gained promotion to Red Bull in 2025 but the team dropped him after just two rounds. Lawson made a temporary return to Red Bull this year as a substitute for the injured Isack Hadjar.

During his time at Racing Bulls, Lawson has scored enough points to single-handedly put Racing Bulls fifth in the constructors’ championship. However he clashed with Red Bull driver Max Verstappen during a practice session in Mexico earlier this month, which his rival said was “not very smart behaviour” for a driver who was “fighting for [his] seat”. Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies denied his team would have any say in its junior squad’s driver line-up.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane said Lawson and his rookie team mate Lindblad form “the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition”.

“Together, we have a solid foundation to build on the progress made this year, continue pushing ourselves forward and take the next step towards achieving our ambitions in 2027.”

Tsolov said he hopes to make the step up to F1 after next year. “My ambition is clear: I want to become an F1 driver,” he said. “Having the opportunity to spend next year preparing for that next step is incredibly exciting.

“I’m confident that with the team’s support and experience, I’ll have the best possible preparation to make sure I’m fully ready to take the next step onto the F1 grid when the time comes.”

Mekies said Red Bull has been highly impressed by Tsolov. “Nikola is an exceptionally talented young driver, and we have been hugely impressed by his development and performances over the past few years,” he said.

“To fight for the championship in F3 and now challenge for the F2 title in his first full season says a great deal about his ability and determination. What has impressed us just as much is his maturity, his approach to racing and his willingness to keep learning and improving.

“We have enormous belief in Nikola’s potential and see him as a driver with a very exciting future in F1. This appointment reflects our confidence in him and our commitment to his continued development. Our focus in 2027 will be on giving him the experience, tools and support he needs to be ready to race in F1 next.”

Sports.title: Stats: Verstappen claims second place from lowest grid position since 1983 | 2026 Brazilian Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
In 2024 Lando Norris’s championship hopes suffered a fatal blow when he failed to win from pole position at Interlagos.

Max Verstappen claimed an unlikely victory in a rain-hit race from 17th on the grid, putting him on course to retain his championship crown.

Norris has made amends since then, however, winning the next two grands prix at Interlagos from pole position. Both times he prevented Verstappen from completing another impressive back-to-front charge: the Red Bull driver finished second on Sunday from the penultimate place on the grid, just as he did 12 months earlier.

However as there are two more cars in the field this year, Verstappen’s charge to second place came from 21st position on the grid (he was actually the 20th car on the grid as Valtteri Bottas’s Cadillac was pushed into the pit lane). This is the lowest starting position anyone has taken second place from since the 1983 Long Beach Grand Prix, when Niki Lauda charged there from 23rd.

Lauda started one place behind his team mate John Watson, who led him home in a McLaren one-two, setting the record for the lowest grid position from which a grand prix has been won.

McLaren may not have managed a one-two last weekend but Norris took his 14th grand prix victory, giving him as many as a trio of multiple world champions: Jack Brabham, Graham Hill and Emerson Fittipaldi. This was also his 20th pole position, the latter giving him as many as Damon Hill and Valtteri Bottas.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Norris reached the podium for the 50th time in his career. Verstappen, meanwhile, took his eighth podium finish in a row, which is the longest streak any driver has managed this year.

Isack Hadjar equalled his best finish with another third place – this was his fourth. Although he briefly hit the front of the field after Norris pitted on lap 49 he did not officially lead a lap, as he pitted the next time by and Andrea Kimi Antonelli crossed the line in front.

Liam Lawson finished seventh for the second race in a row. He has now scored enough points for Racing Bulls to single-handedly put them fifth in the constructors’ championship.

Lewis Hamilton became the second driver in Formula 1 history to record his 400th grand prix start. He joins Fernando Alonso, who reached 400 two years ago:

Lewis Hamilton Fernando Alonso Start Team Race Result Team Race Result 100th McLaren 2012 German Grand Prix, Hockenheim DNF (puncture) McLaren 2007 Belgian Grand Prix, Spa-Francorchamps 3rd 200th Mercedes 2017 Belgian Grand Prix, Spa-Francorchamps 1st Ferrari 2013 Bahrain Grand Prix, Bahrain 8th 300th Mercedes 2022 French Grand Prix, Paul Ricard 2nd McLaren 2018 British Grand Prix, Silverstone 8th 400th Ferrari 2026 Brazilian Grand Prix, Interlagos 9th Aston Martin 2024 Qatar Grand Prix, Losail 7th

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

For the second race in a row, Haas ran a new driver, but this time their rookie did not manage to bag a point. Rafael Camara made his debut in his home race, becoming the first driver to do so since Germany’s Markus Winkelhock in the 2007 European Grand Prix, held at the Nurburgring.

Camara raced with number 51 which last appeared in a grand prix at Abu Dhabi in 2020. It was also used on that occasion by another Brazilian driving for Haas: Pietro Fittipaldi.

Lance Stroll’s race ended in retirement yet again. That was the 14th time this year he has not been classified – failing to complete 90% of the race distance – equalling the all-time record which has been set on five other occasions by four drivers.

These are Andrea de Cesaris twice (in 1986 with Minardi and 1987 with Brabham), Piercarlo Ghinzani (in 1986 with Osella), Ivan Capelli (in 1989 with Leyton House) and Rubens Barrichello (in 1997 with Stewart).

It remains possible for Stroll to match or even exceed the record for most retirements in a season. De Cesaris set this in 1987 when he started but was not running at the end of all 16 rounds. In addition to his 14 non-classifications he ran out of fuel before completing the final lap at Spa (but was classified third) and spun out with four laps to go in the final race at Adelaide, taking eighth place.

Sports.title: Social media: Russell launches GR63 Academy to find 25 future racers | Brief
Sports.content:
George Russell has launched a karting academy to help unearth the next generation of new motorsport stars

The GR63 Academy will feature 25 racers next year. They will be chosen following a shoot-out involving 80 potential competitors at Silverstone. The competition is open to children aged eight to nine and the winner will receive a “fully funded karting season in 2028”.

“So proud to introduce you all to the GR63 Academy,” he wrote. “Karting is where it all started for me and has played a crucial role in my career.

“I also know how hard it is for talented young drivers to get that first opportunity, especially when budgets are tight. With the GR63 Academy, I want to give something back to my sport by finding those hidden stars and giving them the support and guidance they need to reach their potential.

“Following the first two rounds at Silverstone, I’ll identify 25 kids to take part in the GR63 Academy in 2027. Thank you to Silverstone and the BRDC for helping make this happen.”

Sports.title: On This Day: Bourdais wins in final bow for Champ Car’s Lola in Mexico City | Brief
Sports.content:
20 years ago today Sebastien Bourdais won the 14th and final race of the 2006 Champ Car series. It was the final race for the Lola B2/00 chassis before it was replaced by a new designed built by Panoz.

The race was held at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, prior to its remodelling for F1’s return in 2015. Most of the corners were wider and quicker.

In previous years the cars ran through the Foro Sol stadium, much as F1 does today. However for 2006 the original, 180-degree Peraltada was restored, but with a tight chicane before it.

Sports.content:
Formula One Management has decided to press ahead with its plans to hold its final two races in the Middle East despite the potential threat posed by America’s war with Iran.

Moto GP raced in Qatar last weekend but one manufacturer stayed away due to concerns over travelling to the area.

One RaceFans reader in the region, however, welcome the news F1 intends to visit as planned:

I am glad these events are going ahead. I live in the UAE, this conflict which the US started by choice and which it has let spiral out of all control has been a strain on the region and everyone living here. Being able to go to the final race of the year will be a nice way to see out what has been a very tough year. The UAE has handled the situation remarkably well, and we have not had any alerts or strikes for several months, so I expect the race will go off without a hitch.

Sports.title: On This Day: F1’s first female racer, Maria Teresa de Filiipis, born 100 years ago | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Maria Theresa de Filippis, the first woman to start a round of the Formula 1 world championship, was born 100 years ago to this day.

She started 19th on the grid for the Belgian Grand Prix in 1958 (above) in a privately-entered Maserati 250F. She took the chequered flag in 10th place, but unlike today, only the top five finishers scored points.

De Filippis started two other races that year, but retired from both with engine trouble, and made two unsuccessful attempts to qualify for the Monaco Grand Prix. She died 10 years ago.

Sports.title: Lawson made sure Red Bull saw he helped Verstappen in Brazil after Mexico incident | Formula 1
Sports.content:
“When you’re fighting for your seat, it’s not very smart behaviour,” remarked Max Verstappen after Liam Lawson refused to get out of his way during practice in Mexico last week.

A week later during the grand prix at Interlagos, Lawson was far more obliging. He dived out of Verstappen’s way when the Red Bull driver appeared in his mirrors. Lawson then made sure his Racing Bulls team – and perhaps more importantly its senior sibling Red Bull – did not overlook how helpful he’d been.

It’s not uncommon to see drivers make way for their team mates when ordered to on the radio. In the same race Isack Hadjar slowed significantly to let Verstappen in the other Red Bull past.

Lawson, in theory at least, drives for a rival team and has no need to be helpful at all. But while a midfield team driver such as Lawson would likely see no benefit from wasting time and tyre life fighting one of the front-running cars, nor would they be expected to cost themselves time by slowing down. “Don’t lose time with him” is typical advice from race engineers.

Yet that is precisely what Lawson did. Racing Bulls made sure he was aware how quickly Verstappen was gaining on him. Then Lawson dived out of the way on the Reta Oposta back straight, slowing so sharply he dropped down two gears and lost over one-and-a-half seconds.

Job done, he pointed out to race engineer Alexandre Iliopoulos he had not cost Verstappen any time:

Lap: 9/71 LAW: 1’28.088 Iliopoulos Copy. The car behind is now Max. Iliopoulos Some cars around are struggling with tyres. Iliopoulos Car behind is Max, two seconds. Iliopoulos Feedback on balance when you can Lawson Well, it’s just graining, so I have no fronts, and the traction is really, really bad. Do you want me to try clear it? Lap: 10/71 LAW: 1’27.900 Iliopoulos Yes. Yes, we think that’s the best option. Iliopoulos Engine braking eight if you want. Engine nine position three. Lap: 11/71 LAW: 1’29.516 Iliopoulos Push toggle last corner if you want. Iliopoulos Lawson pulls over, slows down and lets Verstappen pass him

Car behind, Piastri, one second, and Hulkenberg is six behind you. Lawson Yep, I let him go. Iliopoulos Copy.

Lawson is still waiting to learn if he will remain at Red Bull’s junior team next year. He clearly wanted to demonstrate he is ready to help Racing Bulls’ sister team.

He was much more prepared to fight his corner in Miami earlier this year, when he challenged Racing Bulls’ order that he let Verstappen past.

But Lawson’s eagerness to show his worth to Red Bull also highlights how unusual their arrangement with their junior team is. One driver pulling over and slowing down so blatantly to let a driver from a rival team overtake him – and then drawing attention to it – would be astonishing if it involved any other pair of teams on the grid.

Sports.title: Josh Kelly Vows to Be ‘Bad for Business’ Against Boots
Sports.content:
Josh Kelly suspects promoter Eddie Hearn would rather see Jaron “Boots” Ennis win their February 27 unification fight in Atlanta. Kelly’s response to that reality is simple: he plans to be “bad for business that night.”

The subject came up during a joint appearance on Inside the Ring, where Devin Haney pressed Kelly on the politics of the matchup while Hearn sat right beside them. Thinking back to when Matchroom promoted both him and Regis Prograis, Haney recalled feeling that Hearn genuinely had his best interests at heart. He wanted to know if Kelly felt that same backing with Matchroom representing both corners.

“I know Eddie’s favorite probably Boots. He’s good for business in the U.S.,” Kelly said to Ring Magazine. “I’m going to be bad for business that night for the U.S.”

Hearn pointed to his long history with Kelly and claimed he hates matching two of his own fighters together because he can’t cheer for either side. He also insisted that Ennis and his father and trainer, Bozy, know how good Kelly is, even as talk about Boots becoming the pound-for-pound king has fans treating this like a showcase.

If Hearn does favor Ennis, it makes total sense. Ennis is a major, fan-friendly talent who closes the show, whereas Kelly’s recent run has been built on survival and generous scorecards. Kelly looked poor in his outing against Caoimhin Agyarko. Before that, he walked away with a questionable decision over IBF champion Bakhram Murtazaliev in a fight where he spent practically the entire night on his back foot.

Their shared history against David Avanesyan tells the whole story. Avanesyan stopped Kelly in six rounds; Ennis blew Avanesyan away in five.

Haney suggested on the show that a fighter who can change range, turn Ennis, and tie him up can force Boots to take his time and think his way into the fight. The problem is that Kelly’s game doesn’t center on breaking opponents down with smart boxing.

Lately, it has revolved around running around the ring and trying to steal rounds in the final ten seconds. Hearn can still steer the winner into a potential undisputed clash with Sebastian Fundora, and unless Kelly brings a completely different style to Atlanta, Matchroom’s U.S. business plans aren’t in much danger.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Won’t Touch Britain’s Harder-Hitting Shakur Stevenson
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is already trying to steer Devin Haney into an in-house unification trap with Jack Catterall, hoping the matchup will eventually set up an undisputed welterweight clash with Ryan Garcia.

For Hearn’s convenient blueprint to work, he is banking on Teofimo Lopez vacating his WBA title rather than fighting Catterall, his mandatory challenger. Sitting right beside Haney on Inside the Ring, Hearn laid out his preferred path: beat Liam Paro in December, face Catterall for the vacant WBA belt, and save Garcia for all four straps.

“Fight Liam Paro, fight Jack Catterall, who I believe will be the WBA world champion because Teo will vacate now,” Hearn said to Ring Magazine. “That’s been ordered. They’ve got 10 days to make a deal.”

Hearn’s In-House Matchmaking Hits a Wall

This is classic promotional maneuvering from Hearn, who has promoted Paro and represents Catterall. Trying to slip Catterall into a vacant title spot and feed him directly into a Haney unification bout keeps all the belts and business under the Matchroom umbrella, regardless of whether fans actually want to see it. The problem for Hearn is that the fight makes zero sense for Haney.

Haney is not going to take that kind of risk for a fraction of the money he would make fighting Garcia. Catterall is essentially Britain’s version of Shakur Stevenson, able to do everything Stevenson does in the ring while carrying more pop in his punches. Asking Haney to take on a slick, heavy-handed southpaw technician with virtually no commercial pull in the United States is a terrible business move when a massive rematch is within reach.

On paper, Lopez dropping the belt to chase Garcia opens the door for Catterall, who earned his mandatory spot by beating Shakhram Giyasov after Lopez inherited the obligation from his win over Rolly Romero. If Catterall picks up the vacant strap, he could bring a third title into the ring against Haney, assuming Haney gets past Paro first.

Haney defends his WBO belt against IBF titleholder Paro on December 19 at San Francisco’s Chase Center. Hearn naturally talked up Paro as underrated, pointing to his road win over Subriel Matias in Puerto Rico before picking Haney to unify. Hearn claimed Paro lacks the power to stop Haney or the skills to outbox him. Haney sounded even more dismissive, stating Paro looks the exact same in his recent fights as he did during their past sparring sessions.

Teofimo’s Choice Could Ruin Hearn’s Plans

Even if Haney gets through Paro, signing up for Catterall next means taking back-to-back southpaws who do nothing at the American box office while stalling the Garcia rematch. Hearn’s entire four-belt pitch also assumes Garcia holds onto his WBC title, which is far from guaranteed. Insider Mike Coppinger reported during the broadcast that Garcia and Lopez are trying to finalize a February 6 bout.

If Garcia and Lopez fight and Lopez wins, Lopez walks away with the WBC belt and instantly becomes the target Haney actually wants, leaving Catterall completely out in the cold. Haney made it clear he still wants to settle the score with Garcia alongside his goal of becoming a two-division undisputed champion.

Right now, Lopez holds all the leverage. Defending against Catterall lets him carry the WBA belt into a Garcia fight, while vacating clears his path to Garcia sooner. Hearn is clearly hoping Lopez drops the title so he can manufacture an in-house unification bout, but expecting Haney to willingly walk into an ambush against a sharper, harder-hitting version of Stevenson is pure wishful thinking.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Keeps Lester Martinez Waiting as Contenders Circle
Sports.content:
Lester Martínez traveled to Acapulco hoping the WBC would mandate a clash with Canelo Álvarez. Instead, he left facing the possibility of yet another interim title defense, with zero assurance that a win would actually earn him a crack at the undisputed super middleweight champion.

During Wednesday’s convention, the sanctioning body opted to put off making a ruling. Martínez contended that holding the interim strap gives him the right to challenge Álvarez, who recaptured the WBC crown by defeating Christian Mbilli in Riyadh on October 31. Rather than ordering the bout, WBC president Mauricio Sulaimán floated the idea of Martínez making another interim defense while Canelo weighs his future options.

“I’m here to exercise the right the WBC gave the interim champion to face the full champion,” Martínez stated in Acapulco, according to translated remarks.

Martínez already has one successful interim defense under his belt, having stopped Luka Plantic in the tenth round this past August. Prior to that, he battled Mbilli to a draw last year. If the WBC needed proof that Martínez belongs at the elite level, he already proved it across ten grueling rounds against the very fighter Canelo just defeated to reclaim the title.

Sulaimán noted that Canelo is open to facing Martínez and wants the matchup to happen on the grandest stage possible. According to the WBC’s convention summary, Álvarez still has one bout left on his current four-fight deal. This leaves Canelo plenty of breathing room to explore all his alternatives, forcing Martínez to choose between sitting on the sidelines or gambling his belt once more.

Sulaimán suggested a bout in Guatemala, which would offer Martínez a hometown showcase while keeping him sharp, though his camp admitted they had no plans in place when the idea was brought up. Accepting another defense means putting his status on the line a second time without a locked-in date against Canelo. While another victory might bolster his resume, Martínez already brought a championship belt to Acapulco to prove he deserves the shot right now.

Lester is in a classic boxing catch-22. Holding the interim belt is supposed to make him the mandatory next in line, yet if Canelo chooses to use the final fight of his contract elsewhere, he is stuck either sitting on the shelf or taking high-risk fights to stay active while everyone else hunts for a shortcut to a title shot.

The real danger for Martínez is taking on a dangerous spoiler like Kevin Lele Sadjo or Diego Pacheco for a fraction of the Canelo purse, only for Canelo to vacate the belt or retire after his next fight anyway. At that point, Martínez would have risked everything just to end up fighting for a vacant title he could have claimed without taking the extra damage.

Sports.title: Pat Brown vs. Chev Clarke: Is 7-0 Too Soon?
Sports.content:
Pat Brown has stopped every single one of his seven professional opponents. Now, Eddie Hearn’s undefeated cruiserweight prospect has been ordered to defend his British title against Chev Clarke, who is coming off a huge stoppage win over former world champion Chris Billam-Smith. The British Boxing Board of Control has set purse bids for December 9.

Brown claimed the vacant British and Commonwealth belts by knocking out John Hedges back in September. Clarke, a former British champion himself, earned a seventh-round stoppage against Billam-Smith on November 7. That kind of victory makes him a serious threat for a fighter with just seven pro bouts, even for a heavy-handed Olympian like Brown.

Matchroom locked Brown into a long-term deal in November 2024 following the Paris Olympics and has guided his entire pro run. Managed by Sam Jones and trained by Jamie Moore and Nigel Travis, Brown already holds two domestic straps. Now, defending that British title puts him directly in the path of a contender who just took out a proven world-level operator.

The real test for Brown is finding out what happens if Clarke absorbs his best shots and keeps walking forward. Brown’s power has ended every fight early so far. If Clarke survives those opening rounds, Brown will have to lean on his jab, choose his moments carefully, and pace himself against a challenger who still carried plenty of danger into the seventh round against Billam-Smith. Clarke’s recent win gives him all the confidence in the world that his odds improve the deeper the fight goes.

Getting past Clarke would give Hearn a massive reason to graduate Brown beyond the domestic scene. Clarke has already worn the belt Brown is putting on the line, and his last outing proved he can take down a former world champion. Beating him would reveal way more about Brown’s ceiling than simply padding his record with another quick knockout over lesser competition.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Rages After Dana White’s Heavyweight Phenom Steals Joe Cordina’s Fury vs. Joshua Spot
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is furious that Dana White’s 21-year-old heavyweight prospect Da’Mazion Vanhouter landed the main card spot on Fury vs. Joshua instead of Joe Cordina. Hearn claims he already had terms agreed for Cordina to face 47-year-old Manny Pacquiao in Cardiff on December 11, yet putting a fresh American knockout artist on Netflix makes infinitely more sense than trotting out another nostalgia act.

“What about Joe Cordina? What about a two-time world champion from Wales?” Hearn complained to iFL TV. Let’s be honest: if Hearn wasn’t Cordina’s promoter, he wouldn’t even mention his name for this card.

Cordina’s hometown appeal and past titles give him a thin excuse for a spot, yet the 34-year-old has been largely invisible since Anthony Cacace stopped him. The two low-profile fights he has taken since barely registered with the boxing public because of the weak opposition. Among the fans who know him, he is not a popular attraction, and American viewers tuning in for the main event have zero interest in watching him.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are already carrying the promotion based on what they did at their best, while 41-year-old Deontay Wilder brings another aging veteran to the co-feature against Jai Opetaia. Fury is 38 and looks more and more like his 61-year-old father, John Fury. Loading the card with older fighters is a disaster when you are trying to reach younger fans on Netflix who cannot connect to a lineup of relics.

Throwing Cordina into the ring with a 47-year-old Pacquiao would have been pure poison for the broadcast. From Turki Alalshikh’s perspective, there is no value in burning a prime slot on a cash-grab sideshow when the sport desperately needs new blood.

The American market makes the decision even easier. Fury and Joshua easily hook British viewers, whereas Vanhouter (14-0, 11 KOs) gives the U.S. broadcast an exciting domestic heavyweight prospect to get behind. The real payoff for featuring Vanhouter comes down the road, when younger viewers remember his explosive style and tune in for his next fight.

Questions remain about whether Vanhouter is the real deal. He turned pro at 17 in the middleweight ranks before growing into a 6’3½”, 231-pound heavyweight, giving him the footwork, loose mechanics, and compact uppercut of a smaller fighter. Still, he has only logged 27 total pro rounds, meaning his stamina against a durable opponent who can take his early power is completely untested.

Facing Michael Essomba on December 11 leaves room for doubt about the quality of the matchup, and Hearn has tried to attack the competitiveness of the fight to distract from Cordina getting left off. Even with those unknowns, a 21-year-old heavyweight on the rise belongs on this stage far more than a 34-year-old former champion trying to cash out against an aging legend.

Sports.title: The Pride Problem Blocking Devin Haney’s Ryan Garcia Rematch
Sports.content:
Devin Haney isn’t even trying to hide his self-interest anymore. He is openly rooting for Ryan Garcia to beat Teofimo Lopez so he can avenge his embarrassing beatdown from two years ago while simultaneously fighting for the undisputed welterweight championship.

By obsessing over a Garcia rematch, Haney is looking right past Liam Paro on December 19. That bitterness has overridden reason, leaving him mentally stuck on 2024 instead of focusing on the dangerous task directly in front of him.

Even if Haney manages to stay locked in enough to get past Paro at the Chase Center in San Francisco, his dream scenario hits a massive snag on both the title front and the financial side.

“First, there is the belt issue. The WBA just reaffirmed its order for Lopez to defend his title against mandatory challenger Jack Catterall, giving them 10 days to strike a deal. Lopez is almost certainly going to drop that WBA belt rather than take a high-risk, low-reward fight against an awkward southpaw like Catterall. That means even if Garcia beats Lopez in their targeted February 6 clash, he likely walks into a Haney rematch holding only his WBC strap, leaving Haney to chase the missing WBA title elsewhere if he still wants to become undisputed.”

More importantly, Haney is ignoring the harsh reality of the negotiating table. Whether Garcia holds two belts or just one, Haney is going to have to swallow his pride and accept a much smaller slice of the financial pie to get that rematch.

Titles have nothing to do with it. Ryan is simply a far bigger star and box office draw than Haney, and he holds all the commercial leverage. If Haney gets past Paro on December 19, he will hold the WBO and IBF titles, yet he will still be the B-side when it comes time to split the money.

Haney will need to agree to the smaller purse if he truly wants his shot at redemption. That is the reality of the business. Will he actually do it? There are serious doubts. The pride in Haney is strong, and accepting B-side money against a guy who already dropped him three times might be a pill he refuses to swallow.

For now, Haney is acting like the rematch is already signed, sealed, and for all four belts.

“The Ryan Garcia fight is the fight that I want the most,” Haney said to Fighthype. “I would take either or for undisputed. But obviously, I want Ryan Garcia to win so that I could right that wrong.”

Beating Garcia gives Haney a chance to erase the memory of their first meeting. Even though the official result was overturned to a no contest, those knockdowns are all boxing fans remember. A Lopez victory over Garcia ruins that setup completely. While Haney could still fight Lopez for whatever belts remain on the table, a Garcia loss sucks the air out of their rematch. Garcia would have to rebuild with a meaningful win or two before fans care again, and a unified champion defending against a challenger coming off a defeat is a much harder sell.

Haney also mentioned he is open to running it back with Brian Norman Jr., whom he previously beat for the WBO title. While a Norman rematch puts him in with a recognizable name, it does nothing to help him collect the remaining hardware at 147 pounds. Facing Garcia delivers the exact redemption Haney has been fixated on since 2024, assuming he gets past Paro and his ego lets him sign the contract.

Sports.title: Roy Jones Jr. Backs Vasily Lomachenko but Warns About Foster
Sports.content:
Roy Jones Jr. believes Vasiliy Lomachenko can still be competitive at 38, provided he drops down to 130 pounds and adjusts his approach following a layoff of over two years. Even with those changes, Jones views unified champion O’Shaquie Foster as a dangerous test for Lomachenko right now.

“I think that break gave him a chance to re-evaluate the whole situation and see that he should be fighting 130, which is true. And now he can go out the way he wants to go out,” Jones said on Hall of Game. Citing the Devin Haney bout as evidence, Jones explained that lightweight was simply too big for Lomachenko. He also noted that the extended hiatus likely gave the two-time Olympic gold medalist a much-needed mental reset after a grueling career.

Before Lomachenko even considers a title shot against Foster, he is expected to return against Charly Suarez, a tough super featherweight contender who gave Emanuel Navarrete major problems in their clash.

Taking on a high-motor opponent like Suarez right out of a two-year absence carries obvious risk, leaving Lomachenko little room to shake off ring rust. Still, Jones believes Lomachenko remains more skilled than 75% of the active boxers in the sport. Doubting a two-time Olympic gold medalist overlooks the fact that elite fundamentals and ring IQ do not simply vanish after two years away.

The real test against a relentless pressure fighter like Suarez, or a master technician like Foster, will be how frequently Lomachenko can still dart to his opponent’s blind side and fire before they have time to turn. While he might pull that off in short bursts, surviving twelve rounds means finding ways to score from a stationary position. That becomes critical against an opponent who uses a stiff jab to dictate range and force him to reset.

“To me, O’Shaquie is peaking right now. So that’s the wrong time to really mess with him,” Jones added. Foster proved that point against Emanuel Navarrete by controlling distance, clinching effectively on the inside, and maintaining enough power to score a knockdown in the twelfth round. Lomachenko would need to bait Foster into overextending before creating his signature angles, though Foster possesses the discipline to force Lomachenko to initiate the action.

Ultimately, Jones thinks Lomachenko’s deep amateur pedigree gives him the tools to trouble Foster if he evolves his game. The main thing to watch at super featherweight is whether Lomachenko can bait reactions with his jab and feints. If he can pull a younger opponent out of stance first, his footwork will only need to do half the work.

Sports.title: Dan Rafael Not Buying February 6 Ryan Garcia vs. Floyd Mayweather Talk
Sports.content:
Dan Rafael isn’t buying Ryan Garcia’s claim that he’ll face Floyd Mayweather on February 6. While Garcia threw that date out during an appearance on N3on’s stream, Rafael notes that Garcia’s team is already deep into negotiations for a February matchup against Teofimo Lopez.

“I don’t believe it,” Rafael said regarding the February 6 date. “They’re far, far down the road, his team with Teofimo’s team, about making the match for February.”

That doesn’t mean Rafael rules out a Garcia vs. Mayweather bout entirely for down the road. The financial upside is massive, and it would pit Garcia against a 49-year-old who hasn’t had an official professional bout since stopping Conor McGregor in 2017. Mayweather has stayed busy with exhibitions in the years since, though stepping into the ring with a reigning welterweight champion is a completely different test.

The idea of Mayweather fighting for Garcia’s title isn’t completely out of left field, especially since the WBC appears open to sanctioning it. Rafael pointed out that the organization could grant an exception given Mayweather’s long history in WBC championship fights, which explains how he could land a title shot after nearly ten years out of official competition. Even so, it remains tough to see why Garcia would lock in February 6 against Mayweather when his camp is so close to finalizing things with Lopez.

As for Lopez’s side of the equation, Rafael expects him to vacate his WBA title if forced to choose between a mandatory defense against Jack Catterall or the Garcia fight. Rafael shared that take prior to the WBA’s ruling while acknowledging Lopez could always have a change of heart. Still, the math is easy to understand. Facing Garcia brings in far more money, even if dropping the belt means losing the marketing angle of a unification bout.

Dropping Mayweather’s name certainly succeeded in generating buzz around February 6. However, the real story is the serious progress Garcia’s camp has already made toward locking in a different opponent for that exact same month.

Ghana News.title: Minority caucus questions women’s bank pledge, alleges silence in 2027 Budget
Ghana News.content:
The Minority in Parliament has questioned the government’s commitment to establishing a women’s bank, alleging that the 2027 Budget failed to address a promise repeated in the previous two budgets.

Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin raised the concern at a press conference on Thursday after Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson presented the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy to Parliament.

He accused the government of failing to honour its pledge to give women, particularly traders, access to loans through the proposed bank.

“Meanwhile, in the 2025 budget, they said they were going to establish a new women's bank. 2026, they said the same thing. But in 2027, they were quiet. The minister was silent.”

Afenyo-Markin argued that the alleged omission raised questions about the government’s delivery on its campaign commitments.

“It is clear that the NDC could not fulfil its own promises to the women, the traders of this country,” he said.

The criticism formed part of the caucus’s preliminary response to the budget. The Minority Leader said members would examine the statement in detail and present a fuller assessment after the budget workshop.

He linked the women’s bank pledge to broader concerns about employment, business support and the cost of living.

According to him, high food prices continued to put pressure on households and traders across markets in Techiman, Tamale, Kumasi, Winneba and Accra.

He argued that the government’s economic claims had not brought sufficient relief to ordinary Ghanaians.

“Stability on paper, hardship in our pockets.”

Afenyo-Markin also challenged the government to state how many jobs it had created. He questioned the Finance Minister’s appeal for patience, saying Ghanaians expected employment opportunities after two years in office.

“Ghanaians want jobs, jobs, jobs.”

The Minority Leader further demanded clarity on the relationship between the New Economy Programme and the government’s 24-hour economy policy.

He said the budget did not provide enough detail on how much of the proposed US$10 billion for the New Economy would be available in 2027 or which projects it would finance.

The caucus also questioned the government’s support for private businesses. Afenyo-Markin criticised what he described as limited incentives for machinery imports and argued that businesses needed a stronger enabling environment to expand and employ people.

“Without the private sector, the economy cannot grow.”

While welcoming the government’s stated ability to meet deferred payments under the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme, he asked why funding remained a concern for public-sector workers and recruitment.

For the Minority, he maintained, the budget's test would be its ability to deliver jobs, support businesses, and ease household hardship.

Ghana News.title: 2027 Budget offers figures, not relief for struggling Ghanaians – Minority caucus
Ghana News.content:
The Minority in Parliament says the 2027 Budget fails to address the hardship facing Ghanaians, arguing that the government’s economic figures offer little comfort to people struggling with food prices and unemployment.

Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin delivered the caucus’s preliminary assessment at a press conference on Thursday. This followed Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson’s presentation of the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy to Parliament.

“Stability on paper, hardship in our pockets,” he said.

Afenyo-Markin argued that the government’s claims of progress were not translating into affordable food or employment. He cited markets in Techiman, Tamale, Kumasi, Winneba, and Accra, where he said food prices remained out of reach for many households.

He also accused the government of failing to support farmers, saying locally produced staples had become increasingly expensive.

“Our farmers are suffering; they are not getting any support from the government.”

The Minority Leader questioned the Finance Minister’s appeal for patience. He argued that the government had already had two years to show it could improve living conditions.

“The NDC cannot rebrand unemployment. They cannot slogan away the cost of living.”

He said the budget did not adequately explain how the proposed New Economy Programme would deliver jobs. He questioned how it related to the government’s 24-hour economy policy.

According to him, the presentation lacked clarity on how much of the programme’s proposed US$10 billion would be available in 2027 and which projects it would finance.

He also questioned a development plan running from 2027 to 2030, saying it extended beyond the government’s current term.

Afenyo-Markin welcomed the government’s stated ability to meet obligations under the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme. However, he asked why similar resources were not available for public-sector workers and recruitment.

“But the question is that where is the money to pay JUSAG, the money to pay teachers, the money to pay nurses, and the money to recruit?”

He argued that employment and household welfare should test economic performance.

“It is not data that Ghanaians are going to consume. Ghanaians want jobs, jobs, jobs.”

The Minority Leader also questioned progress on the promised women’s bank. He said the Finance Minister had not addressed it in the presentation, despite commitments in previous budgets.

He criticised electricity tariff increases and argued that the proposed incentives for machinery imports were insufficient to stimulate private investment.

“Without the private sector, the economy cannot grow.”

Afenyo-Markin said the caucus would examine the budget in detail and present a fuller assessment after the budget workshop.

The Minority in Parliament has criticised the 2027 Budget, arguing that the government’s claims of economic stability have not translated into affordable food, jobs or relief for businesses.

Addressing journalists on Thursday after Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson presented the budget to Parliament, Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin accused the government of offering slogans instead of solutions.

“Stability on paper, hardship in our pockets.”

He said food prices remained high in markets across the country, including Techiman, Tamale, Kumasi Asafo, Winneba Central and Makola.

Afenyo-Markin argued that farmers lacked adequate support, while locally produced staples remained expensive. He also questioned the government’s support for cocoa farmers, saying the farmgate price had fallen despite promises made in opposition.

He rejected the Finance Minister’s appeal for patience, arguing that Ghanaians expected employment and improvements in living conditions after two years.

“The NDC cannot rebrand unemployment. They cannot slogan away the cost of living.”

The Minority Leader also challenged the government to explain how its New Economy Programme relates to the 24-hour economy policy.

He questioned the proposed 2027–2030 development timetable and demanded clearer information on financing and implementation.

According to him, the government had not adequately explained how much of the US$10 billion earmarked for the New Economy would be available in 2027. He also wanted specific projects identified to enable scrutiny.

“They also failed to tell us how much will be expended in 2027 and the specific projects this will finance for proper tracking,” he said.

Afenyo-Markin welcomed the government’s stated ability to meet obligations under the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme. However, he questioned why funding was not available for public sector workers and recruitment.

“But the question is that where is the money to pay JUSAG, the money to pay teachers, the money to pay nurses, and the money to recruit?”

He said the government had failed to state how many jobs it had created.

“It is not data that Ghanaians are going to consume. Ghanaians want jobs, jobs, jobs.”

The Minority Leader also questioned progress on the promised women’s bank. He said it had appeared in previous budgets but was not mentioned in the latest presentation.

On business growth, he argued that electricity costs and limited incentives would undermine private investment. He contrasted the proposed machinery exemptions with incentives offered under the previous NPP administration.

“Without the private sector, the economy cannot grow.”

Afenyo-Markin said the caucus would examine the budget further and issue a comprehensive assessment after the budget workshop.

Ghana News.title: Fourteen dead after truck loses control in 23-vehicle crash in UAE
Ghana News.content:
A night time general view of Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates (UAE)

Fourteen people have been killed and dozens injured after a truck driver lost control and hit several vehicles in Fujairah, in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), the interior ministry has said.

The accident involved 23 vehicles, including five trucks, and happened at the entrance of the eastern emirate in "slow-moving traffic" just before midnight, the ministry added in a statement.

The impact caused "the truck to catch fire and the blaze to spread to several other vehicles, resulting in a heavy loss of life", it said.

Thirty people were injured and taken to hospital, Fujairah Police said, adding that DNA tests are being used to identify the bodies of the victims.

Some of them were Emirati nationals, the police added.

The Indian consulate in the UAE said its citizens were also among the deceased, and said it has reached out to "bereaved families" and is working with the local authorities to provide assistance and support.

Officials said the truck collided with another vehicle before overturning and striking others who had stopped on the street due to "slow-moving traffic".

Emergency services, including the police, paramedics and civil defence teams, rushed to the scene to extinguish the fire, transfer the injured to hospitals and secure the site, where specialist teams remain.

Both the Interior Ministry and police expressed their deepest condolences and heartfelt sympathy to the families of the deceased, and wished a speedy recovery to those injured.

Half of the injured were discharged after receiving treatment, while the rest remain under medical care.

Authorities said the injured are Emirati, Omani, Indian, Brazilian, Pakistani, Jordanian, and Egyptian.

Ghana News.title: Government sets 2027 deadline for local refining of 70% of small-scale gold
Ghana News.content:
The government is targeting local refining of at least 70 per cent of Ghana’s artisanal and small-scale mining gold by December 2027, as part of efforts to retain more value from the country’s mineral resources.

Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson announced the target while presenting the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy to Parliament on Thursday, November 12.

He said government would expand local mineral processing and refining to reduce the export of raw resources and create opportunities for employment, technology transfer and industrial development.

“At least 70 per cent of artisanal and small-scale gold will be refined locally by December 2027,” he told Parliament.

Dr Forson said the government intended to achieve 100 per cent local refining by December 2028, when exports of raw artisanal and small-scale gold would be prohibited.

The initiative forms part of a broader US$1.5 billion investment under Pillar Four of the government's economic programme to develop an industrial minerals economy around manganese, bauxite, lithium and gold.

He said the investment would be assessed based on the value retained in Ghana, export earnings per tonne, skilled jobs created, participation of Ghanaian suppliers, technology transferred and environmental performance.

The government is also targeting local processing of at least 50 per cent of Ghana’s manganese and bauxite by the end of 2028.

“By the end of 2030, Ghana will process all its manganese and bauxite locally and prohibit raw manganese and bauxite exports,” Dr Forson said.

He added that bauxite processing would support the development of alumina refining and aluminium smelting.

For lithium, the government plans to begin with local refining before progressing into the production of battery-grade chemicals, components and cells.

Dr Forson also announced plans to establish a 24-hour critical minerals processing enclave in the Western Region.

The proposed enclave is expected to support the government's broader strategy of expanding domestic mineral processing and strengthening Ghana's position in the minerals value chain.

Ghana News.title: Two remanded over murder of woman who travelled to recover GH¢19,000 debt
Ghana News.content:
Two persons have been remanded into prison custody by the Dambai Magistrate Court for their alleged involvement in the murder of a 39-year-old woman, Rejoice Sena Akpaku, whose body was discovered in a bush near Adumadum in the Oti Region.

The suspects, identified as 36-year-old Isaac Sekyi and 45-year-old Reindolf Sekeni, alias Okeley, were arraigned on Thursday, November 12, 2026, and are expected to reappear in court on December 2, 2026.

According to the Ghana Police Service, the deceased travelled from Somanya in the Eastern Region to Dormabin on October 28, 2026, to recover GH¢19,000 allegedly owed to her by Sekyi.

However, she failed to return after the trip, prompting investigations into her disappearance.

Police said Sekyi was arrested on November 10, 2026, following which investigations traced the deceased’s Infinix Smart 8 mobile phone to his girlfriend, Seraphine Aku Koumah.

Koumah reportedly told investigators that Sekyi had given her the phone before she handed it over to his brother, Frank Sekyi.

The device was subsequently retrieved and found to have been flashed, with its SIM card removed.

A mobile phone technician, Mohammed Ali, was also arrested in connection with the incident.

The Police said that on November 11, Sekyi confessed to the murder and implicated Sekeni as an accomplice.

He subsequently led investigators to the location where the body had been abandoned. The deceased was identified by one of her siblings.

A stick allegedly used in the attack was also recovered by the Police as an exhibit.

While Sekyi and Sekeni have been remanded into prison custody, the other three persons arrested in connection with the investigation have been granted Police enquiry bail to assist with further investigations.

The Ghana Police Service has assured the public that investigations will be conducted professionally and in accordance with due process.
