He explained that the organisation works to protect people affected by hostilities, including detainees, displaced persons and people separated from their families.

The ICRC also visits places of detention, particularly in north-eastern Nigeria, to monitor the treatment of detainees and help them maintain contact with their families.

Mr Kundili said the organisation’s neutrality is essential to gaining the trust of parties involved in conflicts and securing access to people in need of assistance.

“Neutrality is what allows us, in fact, to be able to carry out this mandate given to us by all countries, including Nigeria. Our goal is to reach people who need aid, and to do that, we need to talk to both sides,” he said.

He explained that neutrality does not mean indifference to suffering or support for armed groups but enables the ICRC to engage different parties and negotiate humanitarian access.

ICRC’s operations in the north-west

Mr Dawobe said the organisation is providing humanitarian assistance to internally displaced persons and communities affected by prolonged insecurity in north-eastern and north-western Nigeria.

Its interventions include distributing essential and non-food items, promoting hygiene and supporting access to water and other basic services.

He said assistance was not restricted to people living in displacement camps, as the organisation also supported displaced persons living within host communities.

He cited interventions at the Ramunkura camp in Sokoto State, where the ICRC provides non-food items, hygiene promotion services and access to water.

Mr Dawobe said the organisation is expanding its operations in Sokoto and other locations in response to growing humanitarian needs.

He also addressed concerns that humanitarian supplies sometimes find their way into the hands of armed groups, prompting accusations against aid organisations.

He explained that the ICRC engages state and non-state armed actors to promote respect for international humanitarian law, including protecting captured combatants and their fundamental rights.

Mr Dawobe also commended PREMIUM TIMES for its fact-checking reports and efforts to combat misinformation.

“PREMIUM TIMES is one of the leading organisations in fact-checking. We appreciate all your reports and the efforts you put into combating misinformation,” he said.

Promoting transparency

Responding to the proposed partnership, Mr Akinbajo welcomed the planned collaboration, saying the engagement provided useful clarification about the distinct mandates of the ICRC, the Nigerian Red Cross Society and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

He said the newspaper is open to working with organisations committed to promoting transparency, accountability and a better society.

“Our goal at all times is to ensure that we use the tools to make Nigeria more open, more transparent, and a better country for the majority of the citizens,” he said.

He said PREMIUM TIMES wanted the ICRC to support journalists’ access to conflict-affected communities and internally displaced persons’ camps to obtain first-hand information about humanitarian conditions.

The ICRC delegation said an international humanitarian reporting workshop is scheduled for Abuja from 1 to 3 December, with editors and journalists expected to participate.

World.title: Lee Group’s $1.8b industrial park to create 15,000 jobs, boost Ogun’s manufacturing base — Abiodun
World.content:
Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, has said the $1.8 billion Lee Group First Industrial Park will create about 15,000 direct and indirect jobs, accommodate 29 manufacturing companies and further strengthen the state’s position as Nigeria’s leading industrial destination.

Abiodun stated this on Thursday at the groundbreaking ceremony of the 450-hectare industrial park, describing the investment as a major boost to Ogun’s industrialisation drive and a strong endorsement of the state’s business-friendly environment.

The governor said the project would significantly expand manufacturing activities, stimulate economic growth and create opportunities for thousands of people, particularly young Nigerians.

He noted that the decision by Lee Group to locate its first industrial park in Ogun reflected growing investor confidence in the state’s economic potential, strategic location and expanding infrastructure.

“Your decision to establish this first industrial park in our dear state is a clear demonstration of confidence in our economic potential, our industrial climate and the enormous opportunities that Ogun State offers,” he said.

Abiodun explained that the project’s economic benefits would extend beyond the 29 factories planned for its first phase, creating opportunities for small and medium-scale enterprises involved in logistics, transportation, warehousing, packaging, equipment maintenance, catering, security and construction.

He added that increased industrial activities would stimulate demand for housing, retail businesses, transportation and other essential services, with surrounding communities also benefiting from the investment.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, Ogun’s proximity to Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial and financial hub, coupled with access to major domestic and international markets, gives the state a competitive advantage as an investment destination.

“The choice of Ogun State for this investment is neither accidental nor surprising. Our state occupies a strategic position in Nigeria’s economic geography. We share a significant boundary with Lagos, the financial capital of Nigeria, and enjoy close proximity to a major domestic and international market,” he said.

The governor reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to providing the infrastructure, policies and business environment required to sustain investments and support industrial expansion.

“Our focus is not simply to attract industries to Ogun State, but to build an interconnected industrial ecosystem where large manufacturers, SMEs, service providers and communities can all benefit from increased economic activities,” he said.

He expressed confidence that the project would attract additional local and foreign investments and consolidate Ogun’s growing reputation as a major manufacturing hub.

In his remarks, the Minister of State for Industry, Trade and Investment, John Enoh, said the Federal Government’s Nigerian Investment Policy was designed to attract domestic and foreign capital, diversify the economy and encourage the development of industrial parks.

He disclosed that the Federal Government would, within the next month, undertake another groundbreaking ceremony in Niger State for a 17,000-hectare integrated sugar farm.

Enoh said investments such as the Lee Group industrial park would help Nigeria move beyond exporting raw materials to producing and exporting finished goods.

“With organisations like the Lee Group, Nigeria will move away from exporting raw materials to producing and exporting finished goods, thereby creating and sustaining millions of jobs,” he said.

He commended Abiodun for creating an environment conducive to investment, describing Ogun as the industrial hub of the country.

Earlier, Chairman of Lee Group of Companies, Sheau Fung Lee, said the project represented another significant milestone in the company’s investment journey in Nigeria, which began in 1962 with the establishment of an enamelware factory in Port Harcourt.

He disclosed that the group, which currently employs approximately 26,000 people, had expanded its operations across several sectors of the economy.

Lee said the new industrial park, valued at $1.8 billion, would occupy 450 hectares and accommodate 29 manufacturing companies, generating approximately 15,000 direct and indirect jobs.

He listed food and beverages, industrial support products, footwear, personal care products, automation and plastics recycling among the sectors expected to operate within the park.

The chairman attributed the investment to the group’s confidence in Nigeria’s market size, population and economic potential, while commending Governor Abiodun for facilitating the project and former President Olusegun Obasanjo for his encouragement and support.

Also speaking, the Akarigbo and Paramount Ruler of Remoland, Oba Babatunde Ajayi, commended the company for choosing Remoland for the investment and assured it of the support of the traditional institution and host communities.

The monarch, however, urged the company to ensure that the host communities enjoyed tangible benefits through employment opportunities, local contracts and corporate social responsibility programmes.

World.title: PREMIUM TIMES journalist, others shine at Global AMR Awards
World.content:
PREMIUM TIMES journalist Mariam Ileyemi has emerged as the third-prize winner in the Nigeria AMR Media Awards (NAMA), recognising her reporting on antimicrobial resistance (AMR).

The NAMA is a national category of the 2026 Global AMR Media Awards (GAMA), which recognises journalists and other media professionals whose work raises awareness of drug-resistant infections and promotes action against the growing public health threat.

The 2026 awards received 382 entries from four global regions, with Africa accounting for 193 submissions. Asia-Pacific followed with 134 entries, while Europe and the Americas recorded 28 and 27 entries, respectively. Nigeria submitted 96 entries for the global and national competitions, representing about a quarter of the total submissions.

Ms Ileyemi was recognised for her report examining the gender dimensions of AMR, including how gender-based violence, social inequalities and barriers to healthcare affect women’s exposure to drug-resistant infections and access to treatment.

In the report, published in March 2026, she highlighted calls by health experts for gender-responsive policies to address antimicrobial resistance.

The recognition adds to her reporting on AMR. In November 2024, she collaborated with Nike Adebowale-Tambe, the PREMIUM TIMES Head of Health and Development Desk, on a special investigation examining the experiences of Nigerians affected by drug-resistant infections and the challenges they face when medicines fail.

In the NAMA category, Kazeem Biriowo of Nigerian Tribune won first prize, while Julian Adetinuyo of News Scope Africa came second.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Seven other journalists received special mentions: Folashade Akpan of the News Agency of Nigeria, Chioma Obinna of Vanguard, Helen Oji Emmanuel of Blueprint, Fatima Saka of DistinctNews, Chinyere Okorafor of Nigeria Health Times, Laide Akinboade of Daily Asset and Odimmegwa John Peter of New Africa Horizon.

The winners in the Nigerian category will receive certificates and cash prizes supported by the Art for Health Initiative, a non-profit organisation.

The awards were announced on 11 November during the Sixth Global Media Forum on AMR, ahead of World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week, observed annually from 18 to 24 November.

Nigeria is scheduled to host the Fifth Global High-Level Ministerial Conference on AMR in Abuja from 6 to 8 December 2026. The conference, the first of its kind to be held on African soil, is expected to bring together government representatives and other stakeholders to strengthen global action against antimicrobial resistance.

Other Nigerian winners

Other Nigerian journalists also received recognition in the global award categories.

In the category for reporting on the Fifth High-Level Ministerial Conference on AMR, Annabel Nwachukwu of the Federal Radio Corporation of Nigeria won first prize, followed by Edward Samuel Ikpete of Voice of Nigeria in second place and Doris Obinna of The Sun in third. Alice Etuka of The Fact Daily received a special mention.

In the People’s Reporting category, Isioma Appiah-Yeboah of Clean Beat Radio won first prize, Racheal Abujah of NAN won second, and Helen Shikanda, a Kenyan, came third. Princess Ekwi-Ajide of the Anambra Broadcasting Service, Smith Nwokocha of Port Harcourt Wakawaka Blog and Chioma Vivian James of True Verdict received special mentions.

Patience Ihejirika of Leadership Newspaper and Benedict Ifeanyi Chukwu of Kaftan TV also received special mentions in the Africa category.

The Global AMR Media Awards are organised by the Global AMR Media Alliance, a network of media professionals working to raise awareness of antimicrobial resistance and promote its visibility within global health security and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

Media coverage of AMR

Speaking after the announcement, Shobha Shukla, chairperson of the Global AMR Media Alliance, congratulated Nigerian journalists and commended Ojoma Akor, founding chairperson of the Nigeria AMR Media Alliance, for highlighting the effects of AMR and strengthening media efforts to address the problem.

Ms Shukla said AMR was not merely a medical or scientific issue but also a societal and development challenge that required action beyond laboratories and hospitals.

“We need an informed public, accountable governments, and responsible practices across human, animal, and environmental health,” she said.

She said the media has the power to connect these issues, amplify the experiences of affected communities and turn public awareness into action.

Ms Shukla urged journalists to move beyond reporting AMR solely as a health news issue and help build public support for responsible antimicrobial use and stronger health systems.

Ms Akor, in her comments, described the inaugural NAMA awards as an important milestone for health and science journalism in Nigeria, noting that AMR had received insufficient attention in newsrooms despite its implications for public health, healthcare delivery, food security and national development.

She said the awards recognised journalism’s role in making an often-unseen public health threat visible, translating complex scientific evidence into accessible information, amplifying the experiences of affected communities and holding institutions accountable.

“As an alliance, we remain committed to building the capacity of journalists, encouraging investigative and solutions-oriented reporting, and ensuring that AMR receives the sustained attention it deserves,” she said.

Chidera Rosecamille Aneke, founder of the Art for Health Initiative, said AMR is one of the organisation’s focal areas and explained that its support for the NAMA awards was intended to encourage innovative storytelling.

“AMR is one of our organisation’s focal areas, and we are glad to support the NAMA awards to push innovative storytelling to communicate AMR in ways the audience can understand,” she said.

She said the initiative works at the intersection of storytelling, media and the arts to promote public understanding and action on critical health issues.

Understanding antimicrobial resistance

Antimicrobial resistance occurs when bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites change over time and no longer respond effectively to medicines used to treat infections. This makes infections harder to treat and increases the risk of severe illness and death.

The problem affects human and animal health, food production and the environment, making it a One Health concern.

Nigeria’s National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance 2024–2028 cites estimates that 64,500 deaths in the country were directly attributable to AMR in 2019, while 263,400 deaths were associated with it. The country has also acknowledged surveillance gaps that make it difficult to establish the full scale of drug-resistant infections.

About Mariam Ileyemi

Mariam Ileyemi is a Nigerian journalist on the Health and Development Desk at PREMIUM TIMES. Her reporting covers antimicrobial resistance, disease prevention, and primary healthcare.

She was named PREMIUM TIMES Reporter of the Year 2025 and is a fellow of the Africa Health Communications Fellowship and Media-EIS Fellowship, among others.

She was recently nominated for the Outstanding Health Investigation Award at the Private Sector Health Alliance of Nigeria (PSHAN) Annual Awards. She is also a recipient of the Mamman Marshall Scholarship for Women in Journalism.

World.title: AHF launches comic book to tackle menstrual stigma among Nigerian girls
World.content:
The AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF) Nigeria has launched a 26-page comic magazine titled ‘Amina’s First Flow’ to improve menstrual health education among adolescent girls and address the stigma surrounding menstruation in Nigeria.

The magazine, unveiled on Thursday in Abuja, uses illustrations and relatable stories to explain menstrual hygiene, correct misconceptions, and encourage open conversations about menstruation.

Speaking at the launch, AHF Nigeria’s Senior Advocacy and Marketing Manager, Steve Aborisade, said the initiative was designed to make menstrual health information more accessible and appealing to adolescents and young women.

Mr Aborisade said the stigma associated with menstruation remained a major challenge to menstrual health education, particularly in communities where cultural beliefs discourage open discussions about periods.

“We reckon that the target audience for the comic magazine would find the message in it interesting and easily embrace it for their benefit, and they too can help share the message accordingly,” he said.

Addressing menstrual stigma

Amina’s First Flow highlights some of the challenges girls face in managing menstruation, including limited access to accurate information, harmful cultural beliefs and misconceptions about menstrual health.

It also provides practical guidance on maintaining personal hygiene during menstruation and encourages boys and men to support menstrual health education.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to AHF, menstrual health education is important in addressing the shame and discrimination experienced by girls and young women.

The organisation noted that cultural taboos in some communities prevent girls from discussing menstruation openly, accessing reliable reproductive health information or seeking appropriate care.

It said the comic format was intended to make the information easier for young readers to understand and share with their peers.

Globally, nearly two billion people menstruate, while an estimated 500 million experience period poverty.

Period poverty refers to inadequate access to menstrual products, sanitation facilities, and information needed to manage menstruation safely and with dignity.

Plans for local language versions

The AHF Nigeria Country Programme Director, Echey Ijezie, said the organisation planned to translate the magazine into several Nigerian languages to reach more girls, particularly those who may have difficulty accessing menstrual health information in English.

Mr Ijezie said AHF would also explore collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Education to distribute the publication through educational and community outreach programmes.

“It is imperative to ensure that our target audience is reached in the near future. We would work with the Federal Ministry of Education and explore the outreaches to use them as education and awareness tools,” he said.

He explained that producing the magazine in local languages would help broaden its reach and make the information more accessible to its intended audience.

Government pledges support

Also speaking, the Minister of Women Affairs, Imaan Suleiman-Ibrahim, said the ministry would support AHF’s efforts to improve girls’ welfare and development in Nigeria.

READ ALSO: Experts call for wider adoption of proven health innovations in Nigeria

Mrs Suleiman-Ibrahim, who was represented by Osaro Osa-Jarikre of the Child Development Department, said the ministry intended to incorporate AHF’s programmes into a forthcoming policy initiative.

“Our ministry has resolved to carry the AHF along in the various programmes we have designed for the girl child in Nigeria, and we are also ready to offer needed support to the foundation in its quest to upgrade the Nigerian young generation,” she said.

She described the foundation as an important partner in advancing programmes aimed at improving girls’ wellbeing.

The launch was attended by representatives of civil society organisations, health professionals and youth-focused groups.

Among those present were AHF Nursing Manager Charity Awunor; AHF State Clinical Coordinator Ugochi Ajaero; Binta Suleiman Jalo of the Kids & Teens Resource Centre, Abuja; and Taiwo Ajani of Lawyers Alert.

World.title: EFCC arraigns businessman over alleged £122,000 investment fraud
World.content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has arraigned a businessman, Ashley Oshin, over allegations that he obtained £122,000 from two investors under the guise of investing the money in a fund.

Mr Oshin was arraigned on Thursday before the Lagos State High Court in Ikeja on one count of obtaining money by false pretence.

The EFCC alleged that he collected the money from Oluwafemi Fajana and Abiodun Adeogun between 2009 and 2010, promising to invest it in a debenture fund operated by Oschards Limited.

The alleged offence contravenes Section 1(3) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, 2006.

Mr Oshin pleaded not guilty when the charge was read to him before Justice Ismail Ijelu.According to the charge, he promised the investors an annual return of 40 per cent, although he allegedly knew the representation was false.

Prosecution lawyer, M.S. Owede, told the court that the charge was filed on 29 June and requested a date for trial.

He also asked the court to remand the defendant in a correctional centre, explaining that the EFCC detention facility was full and had no available space.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Owede further sought time to respond to the bail application filed by the defence.

Defence lawyer, Samuel Umoren, said he had filed a bail application dated 10 November 2026, which had been served on the prosecution. He urged the court to hear the application and sought an early date.

Mr Umoren also asked the court to remand his client in EFCC custody.

Mr Ijelu adjourned the case until 18 November for trial and hearing of the bail application.

The judge ordered that Mr Oshin be remanded in a correctional centre pending further proceedings.

The alleged 40 per cent annual return is also relevant to warnings issued by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) about investment schemes promising unusually high returns.

In a November 2023 advisory, the commission urged investors to be wary of schemes offering returns above 20 per cent annually and to verify whether investment operators are registered.

Under Section 1(3) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, 2006, a person convicted of the offence faces between seven and 20 years’ imprisonment.

World.title: Italy stun France 3-1 to hand Zidane first defeat as Les Bleus coach
World.content:
France’s midfielder #14 Adrien Rabiot fights for the ball with Italy’s defender #05 Riccardo Calafiori during the UEFA Nations League – League A day 5 group 1 – football match between Italy and France, at San Siro Stadium in Milan on November 12, 2026. (Photo by Alberto PIZZOLI / AFP)

Italy came from behind to beat France 3-1 in Milan and hand Zidane his first defeat since taking charge of Les Bleus.

France were without Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele due to injury but Michael Olise pounced on a loose pass from Gianluigi Donnarumma to fire them ahead on 10 minutes.

Francesco Pio Esposito steered in Nicolo Cambiaghi’s pass to bring Italy level before France twice hit the post through Bradley Barcola and Rayan Cherki.

Sebastiano Esposito blazed a second-half penalty wide for Italy, but Roberto Mancini’s side did not rue that miss as Davide Frattesi powered home Federico Dimarco’s cut-back.

Francesco Pio Esposito then doubled his tally for the night, succeeding where his older brother had failed by converting a penalty after Dayot Upamecano fouled substitute Antonio Vergara.

Italy climbed above France at the top of Group A1 on head-to-head record. Both teams have 10 points going into the final round of games, with Belgium just one point adrift.

Belgium host Italy on Sunday and France are at home to Turkey.

Turkey slid to a fifth straight loss as they went down 2-1 to Belgium in Izmir.

Arda Guler’s magnificent free-kick put Turkey ahead under new coach and former midfielder Sergen Yalcin, but Belgium struck twice in quick succession with goals from Kevin De Bruyne and Charles De Ketelaere to come away with victory.

World.title: Spain beat Czech Republic to retain perfect Nations League record
World.content:
Spain’s defender #02 Marc Pubill (2L) celebrates after scoring his team’s second goal with team-mates during the UEFA Nations League Group A3 football match between Czech Republic and Spain in Prague on November 12, 2026. Spain won the match 2-0. (Photo by Michal Cizek / AFP)

Alex Baena scored from the spot and Marc Pubill added another seconds from time as Spain beat ten-men Czech Republic 2-0 in the Nations League in Prague on Thursday.

The win leaves Spain unbeaten in 44 competitive games in a row, including five wins in as many Nations League games this season.

Spain, who already secured a quarter-final berth before travelling to Prague, will face England in Madrid on Sunday in their final Group A3 game.

Baena scored on 39 minutes after a VAR check revealed Czech midfielder Lukas Ambros had handled the ball inside the box.

The Atletico Madrid winger blasted his spot kick past Matej Kovar who touched the ball but failed to clear it.

Czech captain Ladislav Krejci was sent off in the 69th minute after bringing down second-half substitute Roberto Fernandez on a counter-attack.

It was a deja-vu for the Wolverhampton defender who also got a red card at the end of Spain’s 3-1 home win over the Czechs last month.

Pubill, another substitute, beat Kovar with a low shot deep into stoppage time after the Czech back four left him alone facing the Eindhoven goalkeeper.

Luis de la Fuentes missed Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo, Rodri and Eric Garcia over injuries while Mikel Oyarzabal was sidelined with flu for the Prague game.

Spain got off to a slow start on the chilly evening but never really let the hosts get close throughout the first half.

They gradually stepped up their pressure, often confining the Czechs to their box and looking for chances.

Fabian Ruiz hit the post with a curling right-footer three minutes from halftime, while Dean Huijsen’s header found Kovar’s arms.

Yeremy Pino, replacing Yamal on the right flank, saw his goal overturned by VAR for offside just two minutes into the second half.

The Czechs showed higher spirits after the break, but David Zima tipped the ball over the bar from close range on 50 minutes and Adam Hlozek’s glancing header landed on the top of the crossbar.

The Czechs lost momentum after the red card, but Baena had two efforts cleared by Kovar who also denied Fernandez from close range.

The hosts, led by de la Fuente’s long-time collaborator Santi Denia, have lost all their Nations League games this season.

They are next travelling to Croatia for a game they need to win to stay in the top tier of the competititon for the next edition.

World.title: Record-breaking Kane fires England into Nations League knockouts
World.content:
Croatia’s midfielder #17 Petar Sucic scores the equalising goal during the UEFA Nations League, League A – Group 3 football match between England and Croatia at Wembley Stadium in London on November 12, 2026. (Photo by Ben Stansall / AFP) / NOT FOR MARKETING OR ADVERTISING USE / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE

Harry Kane celebrated his record-breaking 126th England appearance with a goal from the penalty spot as England beat Croatia 2-1 on Thursday to book a place in the Nations League quarter-finals.

Slaven Bilic’s team were determined to avoid the embarrassment of their 7-0 mauling by England in Rijeka last month and looked much more solid from the kick-off.

But goals from Morgan Rogers and captain Kane kept England second in their group, confirming their place in the Nations League last eight in March.

Neither side got out of second gear in the opening stages of the match at Wembley.

Elliot Anderson fired over in the 16th minute and Croatia’s Josip Misic flashed a shot wide midway through the first half.

Chelsea forward Rogers broke the deadlock in the 24th minute in slightly fortuitous fashion following a neat move by the home side.

Kane floated a ball to Jude Bellingham on the right of the penalty area and the Real Madrid man cushioned the ball first time across the area towards Rogers.

Manchester City’s Josko Gvardiol had a chance to clear but got in a tangle and Chelsea’s Rogers poked the ball past goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic.

England started to find some rhythm as they went in search of a second goal but failed to add to their tally before half-time.

Thomas Tuchel’s men were again the more potent team at the beginning of the second period.

But the visitors levelled against the run of play just before the hour mark after a glaring error by England defender Jarell Quansah, who misdirected a header from close range towards Jordan Pickford following a Croatia corner.

The ball fell to Petar Sucic, who stabbed home.

Minutes later England were back in front, with Bayer Leverkusen defender Quansah again at the heart of the action after his shirt was tugged in the penalty area.

Referee Morten Krogh initially did not award a penalty but he was sent to the monitor by the VAR and pointed to the spot.

Kane made no mistake, drilling home for record-extending 92nd England goal.

Nikola Vlasic gave England a scare, firing just wide of Jordan Pickford’s goal as Croatia showed they were still alive.

James Garner thought he had scored a third for England after a Bellingham cut-back but Bellingham was in an off-side position when he received the ball.

Ballon d’Or winner Kane won his 126th cap when the game kicked off — taking him clear of his tie with former goalkeeper Peter Shilton.

A giant banner was raised before kick-off with a picture of the 33-year-old and the words “England’s Finest”.

Shilton was part of a pre-match presentation to honour the Three Lions skipper, along with Football Association patron Prince William.

England remain second in Nations League Group A3, after leaders Spain beat the Czech Republic 2-0 but are now assured of a place in the quarter-finals.

Spain and England face each other in Madrid on Sunday.

World.title: Online safety concerns are reshaping how people meet strangers
World.content:
It’s hard to ignore how meeting new people online has changed in the past decade. With so many platforms connecting millions, the possibilities feel endless, but the risks have become more visible too.

Stories about scams, harassment, and data breaches are everywhere, and they’ve made people think twice before reaching out to someone they don’t know. Safety concerns aren’t just in the background anymore—they’re shaping the way we start conversations, choose platforms, and decide how much to share.

As awareness grows, so do new habits and expectations for digital introductions. This shift doesn’t just affect individuals; it’s influencing whole communities as we all adapt to a more cautious, connected world.

Changing first steps: why some users now engage with strangers differently online

That growing caution is easy to spot in the way people now approach first interactions with strangers online.

Instead of jumping right into open conversations, many start by looking for platforms that let them control who they talk to, or give them the option to remain anonymous until they feel comfortable.

Features like one-click exit buttons, video previews, or private chat rooms have become popular for exactly this reason.

Women, in particular, are leading this change. They’re more likely to say safety is a top concern, which shows up in everything from avoiding certain apps to using aliases or insisting on in-app messaging only.

The choice of platform matters too. Video chat sites, for example, offer a sense of control because users can see and hear who they’re talking to—and can leave the conversation instantly if something doesn’t feel right.

For many, getting to know LuckyCrush and similar services is part of this shift toward safer, more controlled first steps when meeting someone new.

It’s a sign that concerns are not stopping people from connecting, but are changing the rules for how those first moments happen.

a shift in trust: navigating caution in the age of digital introductions

That change in first steps is really about trust—how it’s built, how it’s lost, and why it matters so much now. People aren’t just jumping into conversations and sharing details the way they might have a decade ago.

Instead, there’s this sense of needing to pause and check for warning signs. With more stories surfacing about online fraud and harassment, it feels riskier to let your guard down. A lot of users now watch for inconsistent stories, pressure to move chats off-platform, or requests for private information as red flags that something isn’t right.

Some of the ways people protect themselves include sticking to messaging within the app, looking for verification badges, or even googling someone before agreeing to meet. These habits are becoming more common, especially as platforms roll out tools designed for safer interactions.

The numbers back up this shift in attitude. In 2023, just under half of U.S. adults said they felt online dating was safe, down from a few years before. Women, in particular, tend to feel more uneasy about sharing personal details, which lines up with reports of higher rates of harassment.

For anyone wanting to understand why trust is changing, the Pew Research on online dating safety is a helpful resource. It highlights how both optimism and skepticism shape the way people meet and interact online now.

Safety in practice: behaviors and community responses on Nigerian social platforms

That skepticism and caution show up in everyday choices for users in Nigeria too. The reality of scams and harmful encounters is hard to ignore, so both individuals and communities have started to change how they approach online connections.

People are much more likely to double-check who they’re chatting with, sometimes even asking for proof of identity before sharing anything personal. It’s now common for users to avoid giving out phone numbers or addresses until they’ve built enough trust within the platform’s chat feature.

Platforms play a role by offering safety tools, but users often take things further by joining moderated groups or relying on word-of-mouth warnings. These groups work together to flag suspicious behavior and alert others, building a sense of collective vigilance that can help everyone feel a little safer.

Community-driven warnings have become especially important after a series of incidents have made headlines. Stories like Rivers Police nab kidnappers serve as stark reminders that online risks have real-life consequences, motivating even more caution among regular users.

The combination of individual caution and group action is changing the culture of meeting strangers online in Nigeria. People are still eager to connect, but staying safe is now a shared priority, not just a personal one.

Looking ahead: the enduring tension between connection and caution

This shift toward community vigilance hasn’t erased the basic human urge to connect online. People still want to meet, form friendships, and build relationships across digital spaces, even as they weigh the risks involved.

The real challenge now is finding a balance between openness and caution. Many users are adapting by taking advantage of improved verification processes, using reporting tools, and staying informed about possible threats. These steps aren’t just about individual safety—they’re shaping the culture of online interaction overall.

Platforms are also responding to these pressures. High-profile actions like WhatsApp bans scam accounts show that companies are working to remove bad actors and create safer environments. These crackdowns send a message that security isn’t optional, but a shared responsibility between users and service providers.

Even with new tools and policies, the tension between wanting to connect and needing to protect yourself is likely to stay. Ongoing education, clear safety features, and active moderation will remain important as the way we meet strangers online continues to evolve.

World.title: UNN Deaths: Gov Mbah mourns, orders investigation
World.content:
Governor of Enugu State, Dr Peter Mbah, has expressed deep grief over the deaths of four students of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, UNN, who reportedly died during an off-campus sign-out party organised for one of their friends, describing the incident as a heartbreaking loss.



Mbah described the deaths as a grievous loss, not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to Enugu State as a whole.

He called for a ban on sign-out parties among undergraduates, noting that the practice had brought too much sorrow to families and tertiary institutions across the country.



This was contained in a press statement issued by the governor’s media aide, Mazi Uche Anichukwu, on Thursday.



“I received with rude shock and deep sense of loss the news of the off-campus sign-out party leading to the death of four students of the University of Nigeria Nsukka, and hospitalisation of six others.



“This is a grievous loss not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to us as a state. Losing them in their prime and along with their promising future cuts as deeply as a sharp knife. We, therefore share in this grief and pray God to grant their families, friends, and the UNN community the equanimity to bear the heartbreaking loss.



“Our hearts go out to their parents in particular, who sacrificed personal comforts to sponsor their children through the university, but only to face this sad turn of events.



“As a government, we have ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding their deaths and will work closely with the university authorities and security agencies to get to the roots of the sad development and forestall a recurrence.



“In the meantime, I have suspended my scheduled town hall meeting with the UNN community on Friday, November 13, 2026, as we join the university in mourning the dead.



“Going forward, we will work with the authorities of tertiary institutions to enforce a full ban on sign-out parties and other excessive celebrations, a trend that has cost more lives and brought more sorrows than joy to families and higher institutions of learning,” the governor stated.



Mbah also called for increased public enlightenment campaigns by relevant agencies and institutions on the consequences of drug use and abuse.



He prayed for the peaceful repose of the souls of the deceased.

World.title: 2027: ‘Arrest perpetrators’, Senate condemns political violence nationwide
World.content:
Senate

By Henry Umoru

AHEAD of 2027 Presidential and general elections, the Senate has condemned in very strong terms, cases of political violence, attacks and disruption of political activities across the country.

The Senate has thus taken a swipe at acts of violence, intimidation, assault and destruction of property associated with political rallies, meetings, processions and other lawful political activities, irrespective of the political parties or individuals affected.

The Senate has urged the security agents to as a matter of urgency apprehend whoever is culpable in such heinous act in order to serve as deterrent to others.

The Upper Chamber has called on all political parties, candidates and their supporters to reject inflammatory rhetoric, discourage violence and cooperate with security agencies in maintaining public peace.

Speaking with Vanguard yesterday, Chairman of the Senate Committee on Media and Public Affairs, Senator Yemi Adaramodu, APC, Ekiti South, said, “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is preaching peace and national harmony, the National Assembly is in support of Mr President on this.

“We thus condemn in totality any act of political violence and urge the security agents to apprehend whoever is culpable in such heinous act.”
