World.title: NSIB: Aircraft door that fell off Abuja-Lagos flight had all locks open
World.content:
By Folarin Kehinde

The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) has disclosed that all locking mechanisms of the passenger-cabin door that detached from a Bombardier Challenger 604 aircraft mid-air during an Abuja-Lagos flight were found in the open position after the incident.

The Bureau also disclosed on its website that the aircraft’s door indicator displayed an ‘UNLOCKED/RED’ warning, while both the internal and external door handles were found in the open position.

These findings were contained in the preliminary investigation report released by the NSIB on November 11, following the October 15 incident involving an aircraft operated by Triton Aviation Limited.

The aircraft, with registration number T7-SEI and operating as flight DWC052, was carrying nine persons, comprising two pilots, one cabin crew member and six passengers, when its passenger-crew door detached during initial climb after take-off from the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja.

Interestingly, the flight crew told investigators that they did not receive any aural or visual door warning before the door separated from the aircraft.

The bureau further disclosed that no door-related faults or warnings were recorded in the aircraft’s downloaded Maintenance Diagnostic Computer (MDC) data.

According to the report, the incident occurred at approximately 5:19 p.m. when the flight crew observed an abnormal increase in cabin altitude and suspected a pressurisation problem.

The captain subsequently instructed the cabin crew to double-check the main cabin door by pushing and pulling it.

However, the cabin crew member told investigators that as she approached the passenger-crew door, it opened without her touching it.

Some passengers also reportedly said they could not recall seeing the cabin crew member touch the door.

The door subsequently detached from the aircraft and struck its lower fuselage, damaging a VHF antenna.

Following the occurrence, the captain took over control of the aircraft while the first officer assumed pilot-monitoring duties.

The pilots declared an emergency and coordinated with Abuja Air Traffic Control for an immediate return to the airport.

The aircraft eventually landed safely on Runway 22 at approximately 5:34 p.m., with all nine occupants disembarking without injuries.

The report also revealed that during the final approach, the pilot monitoring unfastened his seat belt and attempted to close the passenger-crew door by pressing the DOOR CLOSE button.

The detached door was subsequently recovered from a cornfield in Gui Village, Abuja Municipal Area Council, approximately five miles southwest of the airport.

Meanwhile, the NSIB said further investigations would focus on determining whether structural or mechanical failure contributed to the door separation.

It listed metallurgical testing and detailed examination of the detached door, its associated assemblies and locking mechanisms among the next investigative steps.

Investigators will also conduct detailed analysis of the Flight Data Recorder (FDR), particularly the passenger-crew door warning and indication parameters.

The Bureau said the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) would also undergo further analysis, including spectral examination of a recorded mechanical clicking sound to establish its source.

Other areas of investigation include examination of the door-warning and indication system, associated electrical circuits and their functionality at the time of the occurrence.

The NSIB, however, cautioned that the preliminary report contains factual information and initial findings only, stressing that it does not establish the causes or contributing factors responsible for the incident.

It said the final report, containing the investigation’s analysis, conclusions and further safety recommendations, would be published upon completion of the investigation in accordance with Annex 13 of the Convention on International Civil Aviation.

World.title: AFCONQ: Why I didn’t invite Maduka Okoye – Chelle
World.content:
Super Eagles coach, Chelle

Super Eagles head coach Eric Chelle has explained his decision to leave goalkeeper Maduka Okoye out of Nigeria’s squad for their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying matches.

Chelle, who is preparing the Super Eagles for their double-header against Tanzania, said his selection decisions were based on considerations both on and off the pitch.

The Franco-Malian tactician insisted that the national team was not obligated to any particular player, stressing that his choices were guided by his assessment of what was best for the squad.

“The national team is not close to him or anyone. I made my choice and when I made my choice I made it around the pitch and outside it,” Chelle said.

Okoye, who plays for Italian club Udinese, has been absent from recent Super Eagles selections, with Stanley Nwabali, Francis Uzoho and Arthur Okonkwo among the goalkeepers considered by the coach.

Chelle’s latest comments underline his position that selection for the national team is based on his technical and other considerations rather than a player’s reputation or status.

The Super Eagles are seeking to strengthen their position in the AFCON 2027 qualifying campaign as they prepare to face Tanzania in two crucial Group L encounters.

Vanguard News

World.title: Cross-border Payments Must Follow Trade, Says FMDQ MD
World.content:
Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of FMDQ Group Plc, Zeal Akaraiwe, has said that the full benefits of Africa’s growing cross-border payment infrastructure depend on goods and services moving as freely across the continent’s borders.

Akaraiwe took the helm at FMDQ in June after more than two decades in financial markets, derivatives and risk advisory across Nigeria, Zambia and the United Kingdom.

Akaraiwe spoke at the S&P Global Africa Summit 2026 in a two-day gathering in Lagos themed, ‘Turning West Africa’s Potential into Reality.’

His panel, ‘Beyond Banking: Fintech, Digital Assets and the Future of Capital Flows in Africa,’ was moderated by Luigi Motti, Head of Financial Institutions Ratings, EMEA, at S&P Global Ratings.

The other panellists were Serah Makka, Executive Director for Africa at ONE Campaign; Muyiwa Oni, Head of Equity Research at Stanbic IBTC; Ugo Nwaghodoh, Executive Director at United Bank for Africa; Niyi Toluwalope, Chief Executive Officer of eTranzact; and Jay Alabraba, Co-founder and Director of Business Development at Paga.

On digital assets, Akaraiwe described a question that has largely been settled. “Virtual assets,” he said, “are here to stay. What remains is how to integrate them.”

Virtual assets, he said, now need to be brought “deeply into the system” so that they thrive “alongside the traditional mechanisms”. FMDQ Group operates exchange, clearing and depository infrastructure across Nigeria’s debt capital, foreign exchange, derivatives and equity markets.

Turning to exchange controls, Akaraiwe pointed to exchange controls as one that does essential work. In his words, the regime “protects our economic environment from certain types of abuses that we cannot afford to have”.

He nonetheless saw room for change. Across the continent, he observed, countries are beginning to accept that these regimes could be eased, a shift that would allow capital to flow “slightly more freely”.

Freer capital, however, is only part of the picture. For the region, Akaraiwe argued, the movement of goods and services matters more.

“Much more important than the flow of capital is the actual flow of goods and services,” he said. “Because there is no point in having a very sophisticated payment infrastructure cross-border when the actual goods cannot cross the border.”

The greatest opportunity, in his view, lies in pairing these shifts with investment in processing Africa’s raw materials on the continent.

“If those things are combined with the building of processing capacity for raw materials in Africa, that’s going to be a massive game changer,” he said.

World.title: AfSNET 2026: Can Cross River Turn Investment Into Jobs?
World.content:
By Edem Darlington

As Calabar prepares to host the sixth African Sub-Sovereign Governments Network (AfSNET) Investment Conference from November 12 to 14, Cross River State faces a critical test: converting international investment interest into productive industries, sustainable jobs and improved living conditions.

Convened by Afreximbank, the Cross River Government, Nigeria Governors’ Forum and Forum of State Investment Promotion Agencies in Nigeria, the conference will hold at the Calabar International Convention Centre.

The theme is “The Role of Sub-Sovereigns in Catalysing Development Through Trade and Investment.” The programme includes project preparation, investment showcases, Special Economic Zones discussions and business-to-government deal rooms, with emphasis on bankable projects, industrialisation and intra-African trade.

For Cross River, the event must go beyond visibility and help confront poverty, limited processing, weak market access and unemployment.

The NGF Public Finance Database puts the state’s projected 2025 population at 4.69 million across 18 local government areas. Despite priorities including agriculture, tourism, infrastructure and revenue growth, residents face deprivation in education, healthcare, housing and basic services.

The National Bureau of Statistics’ 2022 Multidimensional Poverty Index estimated that 75.4 per cent of residents were multidimensionally poor. Though predating Otu’s administration, the figure underscores the challenge.

Farmers struggle to secure markets, fishers face post-harvest losses, and young people often lack finance, equipment and stable employment. AfSNET could attract investment to address these problems, but projects must respond to local needs rather than generate announcements.

Agriculture offers major opportunities. The state’s investment promotion agency identifies oil palm, cocoa, cassava, rice, yam and plantain as commercial prospects, estimating that agriculture accounts for more than 42 per cent of the economy.

The priority is value addition. Cocoa processing could connect farmers to higher-value markets; cassava plants could produce starch and flour, while oil palm investment could support edible oil and packaging. Such businesses could create jobs across farming, processing and distribution.

ValueFronteira Ltd. has committed more than $20 million to a 4,000-hectare oil palm plantation in Yala Local Government Area over five years. Its wider benefits will depend on implementation and links with local suppliers.

The government should connect producers with processors, financiers and buyers, encourage outgrower schemes and support extension services, storage and transport. Otherwise, factories may lack supplies while farmers remain excluded from expanding markets.

The coast also offers opportunities in fisheries, seafood processing, maritime transport and logistics. Ice plants, cold storage and refrigerated transport could reduce losses and improve fishers’ earnings. Women and small businesses in processing and trading could benefit from better facilities and wider markets.

A major prospect is the proposed $3.5 billion Bakassi Deep Seaport, for which Afreximbank is financial adviser. It could strengthen maritime connectivity and create opportunities in shipping, warehousing, manufacturing and export processing.

But the proposed cost is not secured financing. The project requires feasibility studies, funding, road connections, reliable electricity, security and sufficient cargo. AfSNET could connect financiers and potential users, but cannot replace detailed planning and implementation.

Coastal communities must benefit, while development safeguards fisheries, mangroves and other resources on which livelihoods depend.

Tourism offers another route to employment. Calabar’s heritage, annual Carnival, Obudu Mountain Resort and biodiversity create opportunities in hospitality, transport and nature-based tourism. Local guides, performers, artists, food vendors and small businesses must be included in the value chain.

Renewable energy, sustainable forestry, waste management and climate-resilient agriculture offer green-economy prospects. Investment must combine commercial returns with environmental safeguards and fair benefit-sharing.

Otu described the conference as an opportunity to attract investors and build partnerships for sustainable development.

“Hosting the sixth AfSNET Investment Conference provides Cross River State with an important opportunity to engage African and international investors, demonstrate the breadth of investment opportunities within the State and build partnerships that can support sustainable economic development,” he said.

Afreximbank’s Executive Vice-President for Intra-African Trade and Export Development, Mrs Kanayo Awani, said sub-national governments were central to Africa’s economic transformation because investment and production take place within local economies.

“Through AfSNET, we are creating a practical platform through which states, provinces and counties can strengthen project preparation, connect viable opportunities with capital and build the productive capacity needed to expand intra-African trade,” Awani said.

Afreximbank says AfSNET has convened more than 1,400 delegates from 21 African countries across five editions and facilitated more than $3.2 billion in investment opportunities and transactions. These figures relate to previous editions and do not guarantee investment for Cross River.

Otu has also sought collaboration with the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) to improve flight efficiency, airport facilities and passenger experience ahead of the conference.

“We are expecting people from about 19 African countries, and we are looking at almost 2,000 people coming into Cross River State,” Otu said.

FAAN Chairman, Dr Umar Abdullahi Ganduje, assured Otu of collaboration. Airport operations, customs, port regulation and major infrastructure decisions involve federal institutions, making federal-state cooperation essential.

AfSNET’s test will be whether it creates opportunities for residents. Government should prioritise local jobs, skills, small-business participation and community benefits. Training could prepare young people for agro-processing, hospitality, logistics and renewable energy, while small firms need help meeting investors’ standards.

The state should publish a post-conference register of projects, investors, financing needs, commitments and next steps, protecting commercial confidentiality. Updates should track financing, projects and jobs. A one-year review would establish whether lasting benefits followed.

For Nigeria, success could demonstrate how sub-national governments support diversification, industrialisation and trade under the African Continental Free Trade Area. For Cross River, the stakes are better markets, higher earnings, jobs, stronger businesses and a broader revenue base.

Calabar will not be transformed simply by hosting an investment conference. Progress will depend on what is financed, built and produced, and how widely the benefits are shared. That is the standard against which AfSNET 2026 should be judged.

*Darlington writes from

World.title: Four UNN Students Die At Off-Campus Party, Varsity Declares Three Days of Mourning
World.content:
Gideon Arinze in Enugu

The University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), has declared three days of mourning following the death of four students at an off-campus party in Nsukka, Enugu State.

The university also dismissed reports that seven students died in the incident, clarifying that four students were confirmed dead, while six others were receiving medical attention at different hospitals.

The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Simon Ortuanya, disclosed this while addressing journalists on the incident, which occurred on Wednesday, November 11, 2026.

He said 10 students were involved in the gathering organised to celebrate one of their friends who had completed his final-year examinations.

According to him, the students reportedly consumed substances suspected to be alcohol and drugs, after which four of them died. The six survivors are currently at various stages of recuperation in hospital.

Describing the incident as “a death too many”, Ortuanya announced three days of mourning, during which all social and academic activities in the university would be suspended.

“Within these three days, all social and academic activities will be suspended in the university,” he said.

The vice-chancellor also announced the suspension of a town hall meeting earlier scheduled between the university community and the Enugu State Governor, thanking the governor for his understanding.

He expressed condolences to the families, friends and colleagues of the deceased students, saying the university community shared in their grief.

Ortuanya also dismissed reports that all the students involved in the incident were from the Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences, clarifying that they came from different departments.

He reiterated the university’s ban on sign-out celebrations, warning students against activities that could endanger their lives.

He said graduation should be a period of reflection rather than an occasion for reckless celebrations.

The vice-chancellor added that the university was cooperating with security agencies to establish the actual circumstances surrounding the deaths.

World.title: Kwara PDP Guber Candidate, Kawu, Unveils 3-Point Vision, Promises to Establish N100bn Security Fund
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

Kwara State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) for the 2027 general election, Mr Sulaimon Bolakale Kawu, has unveiled a three-point vision to refix the state for economic prosperity and good governance.

He pledged to establish a N100 billion Security Trust Fund to tackle insecurity, alongside a series of economic interventions aimed at improving the living conditions of residents if elected governor in 2027.

Kawu made the pledge in Ilorin Thursday while unveiling his three-point vision of secure, productive and prosperity titled, ‘My Covenant with Kwara’ manifesto.

He also promised a 13th-month salary for civil servants and N4 billion monthly hardship allowance scheme for teachers serving in underserved, rural and hard-to-reach communities.

He said his proposed security fund would support intelligence-led operations, strengthen community partnerships, provide better equipment for security agencies and establish a coordinated system for identifying and responding promptly to security threats.

He described security as the foundation of development, lamenting the devastating impact of insecurity on communities, particularly in Kwara North and South Senatorial Districts.

Recalling his recent visits to rural communities, Kawu said the experience had strengthened his resolve to seek the governorship and address the challenges confronting residents.

“My recent visits to rural communities in the state geared me to more actions because at Kaiama, I saw despair written all over Kwarans. These are the people who lost their loved ones to insecurity,” he said.

He explained that his ambition was driven by the need to provide purposeful leadership rather than personal political considerations.

He added that his experience as a retired senior civil servant and former Director of the Rural Electrification Agency had prepared him for the task of governance.

He stated that the manifesto represents a comprehensive development blueprint designed to ensure that government policies translate into tangible benefits for residents across the state.

“This manifesto is about what government must do, how it must do it and, most importantly, who must benefit from it. It demonstrates that, as governor, I will hit the ground running from day one.

“I assure you that I do not seek to enter government with an empty head or mind, as we have seen in recent times,” he said.

Kawu, who described the document as a covenant with the people, said his proposed administration would be anchored on security, economic productivity and infrastructure development.

On economic empowerment, he promised to establish a N9.6 billion revolving loan scheme for traders and another N9.6 billion single-digit interest loan facility for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).

He said the initiative would provide businesses with access to affordable financing, stimulate economic activities, create employment opportunities and strengthen the capacity of local entrepreneurs.

On infrastructure, the PDP candidate pledged to prioritise projects capable of supporting businesses, attracting investments, creating jobs and improving the livelihoods of residents.

He also promised to give qualified and competent indigenous contractors consideration in the award and execution of government projects, provided they meet the required standards.

“This policy will help retain government investments within Kwara, strengthen local businesses, create jobs, develop local capacity and ensure that our people directly benefit from the economic activities generated by government projects,” he said.

In the education sector, Kawu promised to rehabilitate dilapidated schools, improve learning environments, provide teaching and learning materials and strengthen teachers’ welfare.

He said rural schools and communities would receive special attention to address the additional challenges confronting children in underserved areas.

“Every child deserves access to quality education irrespective of where they are born or the economic circumstances of their parents,” he stated.

The former REA director maintained that his proposed government would focus on ensuring equal opportunities for residents, regardless of their locations or economic circumstances.

He said the manifesto was informed by his conviction that Kwara could achieve more through strategic planning, competent administration, transparency and people-oriented policies.

Kawu added that his years of experience in public service, particularly in project conception, design, implementation and monitoring would guide his approach to governance.

The PDP gubernatorial candidate expressed confidence that the proposed blueprint would prevent a situation where an incoming administration assumes office without a clear development plan, insisting that every sector and community in the state had been considered in the document.

Also speaking, the Director General of the PDP Campaign Council, Prince Omar Bolaji Gambari, said: “Today is not just the unveiling of a document. It is the day that will be remembered as a full declaration of intent and the day when our candidate laid out his vision, his plan, his policies and programmes that will benefit every Kwara.

“This manifesto is not a document

of empty promises. It is a solemn compact. It is a blueprint forged from thousands of hours of listening to the citizens, the workers, the students, opinion leaders, community associations, traders, market women, entrepreneurs and many others, all over Kwara.

“Engineer Kawu’s manifesto embodies the hopes and aspirations of our people, as well as the struggles we refuse to accept any longer.

“Across every corner of this great state, the message has been clear. Our people are saying no to insecurity, no to banditry, no to unemployment, and no to.despair”

Gambari therefore urged the people of the state to rally round the party’s governorship candidate and other candidates so as to enable the party implement the manifesto for the overall development of the state come 2027.

World.title: COP31: Nigerian Bank of Agriculture Seeks Climate Funding to Support Agricultural Adaptation Projects
World.content:
Chiemelie Eze in Antalya, Türkiye

The Bank of Agriculture (BOA) has called for increased climate financing from developed countries to support agricultural adaptation projects in Nigeria and across Africa, while unveiling plans to deploy electric cargo tricycles and solar-powered irrigation systems to improve farmers’ productivity.

The BOA Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Ayo Sotinrin, made the call yesterday at the ongoing COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye, where he said Nigeria and other African countries needed more financial support to address the effects of climate change on agriculture.

Sotinrin said the bank was exploring partnerships and financing arrangements to introduce practical climate adaptation solutions, particularly in agricultural transportation and irrigation.

He disclosed that the bank was exploring the introduction of electric cargo tricycles capable of transporting 2,000kg of agricultural produce from farms to farm gates in one trip, compared with fossil-fuel-powered two-wheelers that carry about 50kg.

He said, “We are introducing electric cargo tricycles that can actually move 2,000kg from farms to the farm gate at once, rather than the fossil-fuel-powered two-wheelers that move only 50kg.”

He also said the bank was looking to expand solar-powered irrigation through one-to-five-horsepower pumps and subsurface pumps to enable farmers cultivate their land at least three times annually.

“We’ve also looked at how we increase the adoption of solar irrigation across board, using one-to-five-horsepower pumps or subsurface pumps to ensure that farmers can actually farm three times a year at the minimum.

“This would further increase our productivity by at least 300 per cent,” he said.

According to him, the initiatives would help transform agricultural production and mitigate some of the challenges posed by climate change.

On the outcomes expected from COP31, he called for renewed commitments by world leaders, expressing concern that previous climate financing promises had not been fulfilled.

He said existing commitments were insufficient to keep global warming below 2.5 degrees Celsius, let alone achieve the 2-degree and 1.5-degree targets.

“My takeaway from COP is refreshed commitments from world leaders. Also, the fact that we are all coming to a realisation that all the promises that were made were not kept.

“We are talking about those commitments that were made; they will not even get us below 2.5 degrees, let alone getting to 2 degrees or below 2 degrees, which is 1.5 degrees, where we want to be,” he said.

He called for increased funding from the Global North to Africa through blended financing instruments, including grants, commercial capital and development finance, to support climate adaptation projects.

“We need more capital. The capital stack needs to be explored, especially from the Global North to Africa, where we have different types of blended instruments, including grants, commercial and developmental capital going into adaptation solutions in Nigeria and Africa at large.

“So those are the sorts of things that we are happy have been discussed at COP31 today,” he said.

On access to agricultural financing, Sotinrin said the bank had digitised many of its processes and systems to make funding more accessible to farmers.

He, however, explained that the bank had moved away from providing microcredit directly to individual farmers, preferring to channel loans through cooperatives, farmer aggregation companies, microfinance banks and commercial banks.

He said, “We’ve stopped giving microcredits to individual farmers unless they come under an umbrella of a medium cooperative or a smaller cooperative, or a farmer aggregation company, or even through asset-based financial institutions such as microfinance banks and commercial banks that we blend capital with.”

He explained that the approach was necessary to ensure effective loan recovery, noting that the bank’s 110 branches could not independently manage lending to two million individual farmers.

“If you tell me to finance individual farmers, it’s very difficult because one of the things that scale, and there’s no way the Bank of Agriculture, with 110 branches, can actually finance two million farmers individually and be able to recover those monies.

“And if we don’t recover those monies, we erode our shareholder capital and we’re back to square one,” he said.

World.title: Praises as Abiodun Breaks Ground for 450 Hectares Industrial Park
World.content:
James Sowole in Abeokuta

Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, yesterday performed the groundbreaking of 450 hectares First Lee Group Industrial Park located near Sagamu Interchange on Lagos-Ibadan Expressway.

The governor was joined at the ceremony by the Minister of State for Trade for Industry Trade and Investment, Senator John Enoh, Commissioner for Finance and Chied Economic Adviser to the Ogun State, Hon Dapo Okubadejo, traditional rulers, Ambassador Plenipotentiary of the Peoples Republic of China Yu Dunhai, community leaders and other stakeholders.

Speaking at the ceremony, Abiodun said the industrial park would create opportunities for small and medium-scale enterprises to support the operations of the factory and other factories, with its proposed manufacturing components ranging from personal and home care products to footwear, leather processing, food processing, bakery production, and recycling, demonstrating the breadth of opportunities the project presents.

According to the governor, the establishment of the Aspira flagship factory, the S.F.M. footwear, and all other products in the park, would promote the utilization of locally available raw materials.

Abiodun said he is particularly encouraged by the project’s emphasis on value addition, backward integration, and environmental sustainability, while the proposed integration of leather and footwear accessory production will strengthen local manufacturing linkages.

The governor said beyond the factories and physical infrastructure, the greatest value of the investment will ultimately be measured by its impact on the people.

He noted that the project’s blueprint projects the generation of up to 15,000 direct and indirect employment opportunities upon completion and operation, which is very significant for young people, skilled professionals, artisans, technicians, and the surrounding community.

He said the project is expected to prioritize local employment, deliberate skills development, technology transfer, and the nurturing of home-grown managerial and technical talents.

He noted that people must not merely live around the industrial development but must participate meaningfully in its opportunities and benefits, and assured the leadership of the Lee Group that the Ogun State government remains committed to providing the necessary institutional support and investor-friendly environment for the project to succeed.

Abiodun urged local entrepreneurs, small and medium-scale enterprises, suppliers, and service providers to position themselves to benefit from the extensive business opportunities the project will create, saying Ogun State remains steadfast in its determination to consolidate its position as a leading destination for industrial investment.

He noted that with his administration about six months away from exiting, the Lee Group’s industrial park is a significant vote of confidence and a strong affirmation of the confidence investors continue to repose in the state, as well as a testament to the success of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope economic transformation agenda.

In his remark, the Chairman, Lee Group of Companies, Sheau Fung Lee, said the groundbreaking of the group’s industrial park continues a commitment to Nigeria that began in 1962, when his grandfather established an enamelware factory in Port Harcourt.

He said the firm has grown from that modest beginning into a multi-sector conglomerate that now employs approximately 26,000 workers in Nigeria, with footwear production of around 2 million pairs a day, a tannery in Kano, packaging, bread, bottled water, laundry detergents and personal care products.

He said more than six decades and three generations of leadership, the group has shared in Nigeria’s good times and difficult years, noting that the journey has not been easy but they continue to believe in Nigeria’s future and to invest in its economy.

In his remark, the Minister of State for Industry, Trade and Investment, Sen. John Enoh, commended the Abiodun for his vision and outstanding leadership, which have turned Ogun State into the industrial capital of Nigeria.

Enoh, who said investors is now trooping to Ogun State noted that if there was no good leadership and suitable environment, investors wouldn’t have come to invest in the state.

Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony of

The minister recalled that a project of such nature had been stalled for several years, but it took Abiodun to get it to where it is today.

He also noted that the governor still embarked on laudable projects in spite of just a few months to the end of governor his administration.

He said, “I think that the judgment of history will be fair to this man. It will be fair to him. That’s what leadership is about. Leadership is not about the end of a tenure, not about the next election, it’s about the future generation. Let me thank you, sir. Let me thank you for your leadership.”

He thanked the Lee Group for believing in Nigeria and for the confidence reposed in the country, noting that the group has spent several years in the country and stayed on through tough moments when other companies left the shores of the country.

He appealed to royal fathers and community leaders, who he described as custodians of the project, to give it all the support it requires, stressing that they are ultimately the greatest beneficiaries.

He expressed hope that as the Lee Group and the industrial park grow in leaps and bounds, the fortunes and circumstances of the community will also grow in leaps and bounds.

World.title: Glo Magic Bundles: When Data Becomes A Gift And Connectivity A Reward
World.content:
By Onyema Ohaegbu

What if purchasing data ceased to be a straightforward commercial transaction and became an experience in which certainty meets pleasant surprise, guaranteed value encounters unexpected generosity, and connectivity yields more than the customer originally bargained for? What if every subscription carried within it the possibility of an additional reward, transforming the familiar business of buying data into an invitation to enjoy more, achieve more and experience more?

This is the refreshing proposition behind Globacom’s Magic Data Bundles, an innovative offering that is redefining the conversation around affordability, customer value and digital inclusion in Nigeria’s telecommunications landscape.

At a time when data has become the indispensable currency of contemporary civilisation, powering conversations, commerce, education, entertainment, healthcare, governance and virtually every expression of human enterprise, the importance of affordable and dependable internet access cannot be overstated. Data is no longer merely a technological commodity; it is the invisible infrastructure upon which modern society conducts its business, exchanges knowledge, creates opportunities and sustains relationships.

Globacom’s Magic Bundles recognise this changing reality and respond with a proposition whose central philosophy is beautifully uncomplicated: customers should receive what they pay for, and enjoy something extra.

The ingenuity of the offering resides in its distinctive two-component architecture: a guaranteed main data allocation, complemented by an additional Magic Bonus, automatically credited following a successful subscription.

Available at two accessible price points, ₦1,600 and ₦3,500, the proposition introduces an appealing dimension of reward into the customer’s data experience.

At ₦1,600, subscribers receive a guaranteed 2.5GB main data allocation, alongside a Magic Bonus ranging from 500MB to 7.5GB, bringing the potential total allocation to between 3GB and 10GB. At ₦3,500, customers are assured of 8GB, with an additional bonus ranging from 1GB to 12GB, potentially raising their total data entitlement to between 9GB and 20GB.

Herein lies the magic: the guaranteed allocation remains sacrosanct, while the additional reward introduces an element of delightful anticipation. The bonus is automatically assigned by Globacom’s system, meaning that customers may receive different additional allocations on different subscriptions. The maximum reward is not guaranteed, but an additional bonus accompanies every qualifying purchase.

It is an ingenious marriage of commercial assurance and rewarding spontaneity.

Beyond the attractive numbers, the strategic significance of Magic Bundles becomes even more compelling when examined against the diverse demands of Nigeria’s increasingly data-dependent population.

For entrepreneurs, small businesses, retailers and corporate organisations, data is the oxygen of commercial productivity. It facilitates digital marketing, electronic payments, customer engagement, virtual meetings, inventory management and the expanding universe of online commerce.

Additional data can translate into more opportunities to transact, communicate and serve customers without immediately returning to the marketplace for another subscription.

For students, researchers, lecturers and educational institutions, connectivity is a gateway to intellectual discovery. Online libraries, virtual classrooms, academic journals, educational videos and collaborative learning platforms have made internet access indispensable to contemporary education. More data means greater latitude to explore knowledge and participate in the expanding global classroom.

In healthcare, connectivity strengthens the possibilities of teleconsultation, medical research, professional collaboration, digital health records and public-health communication. Government institutions equally depend on data for administrative efficiency, citizen engagement, electronic services, policy communication and the expanding architecture of digital governance.

Within Nigerian homes, the benefits assume an altogether intimate character. Parents connect with children, families maintain relationships across geographical distances, young people explore opportunities, and households access entertainment, information and digital services.

From video streaming and social networking to online banking and professional development, Magic Bundles offer additional breathing space for everyday digital living.

Another attractive dimension is the flexibility of the proposition. Customers can purchase through the Glo Café application or by dialling *312#. The bundles are also shareable and giftable, subject to applicable conditions, while rollover provisions apply under Globacom’s prevailing policies.

Customers can monitor their main and bonus balances through Glo Café, the web self-service platform or *323#.

Viewed against competing industry propositions, Glo’s offering deserves particular attention.

Other operators provide daily, weekly and monthly subscriptions, promotional bonuses and specialised data packages. However, Magic Bundles distinguish themselves through the deliberate combination of a guaranteed allocation and an automatically awarded additional data reward within one subscription proposition.

This differentiation, rather than any sweeping dismissal of competitors’ offerings, constitutes the product’s strongest competitive argument.

The television commercial currently running on Arise TV provides an important communications platform for this proposition. Its significance extends beyond announcing another data package.

It places the product within a broader conversation about value, aspiration and the changing expectations of Nigerian telecommunications consumers. Arise TV’s national visibility and business-oriented audience offer a useful environment for communicating the proposition to decision-makers, professionals, entrepreneurs and ordinary subscribers alike.

Ultimately, Glo Magic Bundles embodies an attractive commercial philosophy: connectivity should empower, affordability should deliver substance, and customer loyalty should encounter tangible rewards.

In an industry where operators compete for attention, subscription and market share, Globacom is making a persuasive statement by placing additional customer value at the centre of its proposition.

It is a philosophy that resonates naturally with the company’s overarching campaign declaration, Never Settle for Less. Indeed, why should customers settle for the ordinary when their subscriptions can deliver something extra?

With Magic Bundles, Globacom is inviting Nigerians to experience data differently: not simply as megabytes purchased, but as opportunities multiplied, possibilities enlarged and everyday digital experiences enriched.

Because when connectivity comes with a little more magic, the possibilities become considerably greater.

*Pastor Onyema Ohaegbu, Telecoms Enthusiast, writes in from Abuja

World.title: World Toilet Day: Nasarawa to Provide Massive Mobile Toilets
World.content:
Igbawase Ukumba in lafia

The Nasarawa State Government has said it is providing massive mobile toilets in public facilities in its renewed effort to end open defecation in the state.

The state Commissioner for Environment, Solid Minerals and Mining, Princess Margaret Elayo, disclosed this on Thursday in Lafia while briefing journalists at an event to commemorate the 2026 World Toilet Day.

THISDAY reports that November 19 is set aside every year to celebrate World Toilet Day.

According to her, “The state government has keyed into the plans of the Federal Government to end open defecation by 2030.

​”The word toilet sounds simple and funny to some people, but a toilet is life. A toilet is dignity. A toilet is health. A toilet is safety. A toilet is a peaceful space.

​”Imagine a child who cannot go to school because there is no toilet in the school. Imagine a woman who must wait until nightfall, risking her safety, just to ease herself in a bush.

“Imagine a community where human waste flows in the same water they drink, cook with, and bathe with.

“That is the reality for millions of people across the globe, even here in Nigeria, and Nasarawa State,” she said.

Elayo noted that the Governor Abdullahi Sule-led administration in the state is committed to ending open defecation, providing clean and accessible toilets for all and protecting the environment and water from contamination.

She said that the mobile toilets would be deployed in high-traffic areas including markets, motor parks, schools, and other public places where residents often lack access to toilet facilities.

The commissioner said the initiative is not only about providing toilets, but also about protecting public health, preventing diseases like cholera, typhoid and diarrhoea, and restoring dignity to residents.

Elayo further warned that the state government would no longer tolerate open defecation, noting that the state sanitation law makes it mandatory for every household to have a functional toilet.

The commissioner further disclosed that the government would immediately construct modern toilets at Shinge cattle market and On the Move Park in Lafia due to a recent discovery that those important places do not have toilet facilities.

She, therefore, called on members of the public to make use of the facilities when provided, keep them clean, and support the government’s effort to make Nasarawa open defecation-free.

World.title: Ex-Sundowns star signs with agency as he steps into coaching
World.content:
Former Mamelodi Sundowns star midfielder Surprise Ralani has signed a contract with prominent sports agency ProSport International.

Ralani, who enjoyed a long playing career, ventured into coaching in November 2025, and he joined his home town club Gaza United.

Gaza United are competing in the ABC Motsepe League, and Ralani took up the role in order to gain coaching experienced.



Now, the aim with this new deal is to help Ralani move up the ladder in the coaching ranks, and perhaps in the Motsepe Foundation Championship or the Betway Premiership.

ProSport International took to their social media platforms on Thursday to announce the acquisition of Ralani as their client.

Ex-sundowns star signs new deal with prominent agency

Ralani’s playing career…

Ralani, 39, spent almost a decade in Europe playing for a number clubs between 2009 and 2017.



He then returned to South Africa to join Cape Town City in 2018 where he spent four years before moving to Sundowns in 2022.

Ralani would spend just over a season with the Brazilians as game proved hard to come by, and he joined Cape Town Spurs in 2023.

He was also on the books on the likes of Hungry Lions and Orbit College before retiring from professional football.

World.title: Where is John Steenhuisen?
World.content:
John Steenhuisen has kept a low profile after he was effectively demoted from his position as Minister of Agriculture during a cabinet reshuffle in June.

Just two months earlier, the politician – who made headlines for allegedly splurging his party credit card on Uber Eats orders – handed over the reins of the Democratic Alliance to current leader Geordin Hill-Lewis.

WHERE IS JOHN STEENHUISEN?

In June, John Steenhuisen was removed from his post as Minister of Agriculture and seemingly demoted to Deputy Minister of Trade and Industry by DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis during a cabinet reshuffle.



In the months leading up to this, John had stepped down as president of the DA to focus his attention on agricultural issues, such as the rampant spread of foot-and-mouth disease.

He was replaced by Willie Aucamp as the new minister.

John Steenhuisen was sworn in to his new post on 1 July.

Since his move, John has gone completely silent on his social media platforms, prompting many South Africans to question where he is.

What happened to John Steenhuisen? 🤔 — Penuel The Black Pen (@penuelist_) November 11, 2026

However, he continues to perform his public duties.



In recent months, the 50-year-old has been active in various sectors within his department, including campaigning for local job creation in the automotive industry, encouraging European trade and investment and commenting on US-SA trade relations after SA’s exit from AGOA.

The Deputy Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition, Mr John Steenhuisen, is in Pietermaritzburg today as a guest of KwaZulu-Natal Member of Executive Council (MEC) for @KZNPublicWorks Mr Martin Meyer for the launch of the province's Government Property Finder Portal. pic.twitter.com/jvZckjznBC — the dtic (@the_dtic) October 7, 2026

Africa's blue economy is not merely a future opportunity; it is a present investment opportunity. This was the message from Deputy Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition, Mr John Steenhuisen, during his keynote address at #BlueInvestAfrica2026 in Cape Town today. pic.twitter.com/6oLIT6StSc — the dtic (@the_dtic) November 2, 2026

Deputy Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition, John Steenhuisen visited the Denel stand today at AAD where he was taken through our capabilities, projects and the people behind the work. pic.twitter.com/c3DI3xa36V — Denel (@DenelSOC) September 18, 2026

FALLOUT WITH DA STALWARTS

In recent months, John Steenhuisen is believed to have fallen out with former DA federal finance chair and environment minister Dion George, who was accused of misusing his party-issued credit card for personal expenses, including household and Uber Eats food delivery.

John – who accused the party of “betraying” him – was cleared of these allegations in an internal investigation.

He also accused ex-party leader Tony Leon of using his political connections to aid his PR company, Resolve Communications – a claim the latter denied.

World.title: Starlink’s South African future faces new court challenge over BEE rules
World.content:
The prospect of Starlink in South Africa has entered a new legal phase after business organisation Sakeliga challenged the telecommunications regulator’s interpretation of black economic empowerment (BEE) ownership rules.

Sakeliga filed papers in the Pretoria High Court on 9 November 2026, contesting the Independent Communications Authority of South Africa’s (ICASA) insistence on a 30% ownership requirement for companies seeking individual telecommunications licences.

The application adds a legal dimension to a dispute that has delayed the satellite internet provider’s local launch, despite government efforts to find a solution.



Why Sakeliga is challenging ICASA

The dispute centres on section 9(2)(b) of the Electronic Communications Act, which refers to a minimum 30% ownership by historically disadvantaged groups, alongside wording allowing “such other conditions”.

Sakeliga argues that the wording permits ICASA to recognise other ways of meeting empowerment requirements, rather than treating the ownership threshold as compulsory in every case.

In a statement released on 11 November, the organisation said its application seeks to set aside ICASA’s decision of 13 May 2026. Alternatively, it wants the relevant provision declared unconstitutional if the court accepts the regulator’s interpretation.

What the regulator and minister say

Communications and Digital Technologies Minister Solly Malatsi issued a policy direction in December 2025 calling on ICASA to consider aligning its licensing rules with the ICT Sector Code.

That could create a route for equity-equivalent investment programmes, allowing qualifying multinationals to contribute through approved investment and development initiatives instead of transferring local shareholding.

However, in its 13 May statement, ICASA maintained that the existing law requires at least 30% ownership by historically disadvantaged groups. It said fully recognising equity-equivalent programmes would require Parliament to amend the Act.



The disagreement follows an extended debate over changes to BEE requirements, with supporters of alternative arrangements arguing they could attract investment without abandoning transformation objectives.

Does the case mean Starlink can launch?

No. Starlink has not secured the South African licences required to sell its satellite internet service directly to local consumers. The latest court application does not grant permission to operate.

Even a ruling that ICASA has authority to consider equity-equivalent arrangements would not automatically compel the regulator to approve them or award Starlink a licence. The operator would still have to meet the applicable licensing requirements.

The dispute also reaches beyond Starlink. Its outcome could affect how domestic and international network operators meet empowerment conditions when applying for, renewing or transferring individual licences.

What happens next?

The court must first consider Sakeliga’s application and the respondents’ positions. No ruling or confirmed hearing date has been established in the sources reviewed as of 12 November 2026.

Until the legal and regulatory questions are settled, Starlink’s route into the South African market remains uncertain.

Should alternative empowerment investments count towards South Africa’s telecoms licensing rules?

World.title: SA-born rugby player Pierre Schoeman: ‘I choose Scotland’
World.content:
Pierre Schoeman has reflected on his decision to represent Scotland. Images via IG

South African-born rugby player Pierre Schoeman has defended his decision to play for Scotland’s national team.

The former Bulls player, who moved abroad in 2018, also recently celebrated earning his citizenship alongside his wife, Charissa.

PIERRE SCHOEMAN ON PLAYING FOR SCOTLAND

In a snippet from his interview on Origin Story, Pierre Schoeman opened up about leaving South Africa not only to play club rugby in Scotland, but also to represent his adoptive country on its national team.



The 33-year-old revealed that he had initially “manifested” owning a Springbok jersey, as his own. But as fate would have it, he ended up owning several – after trading it with his opponents whilst playing for Scotland’s national team.

He told host David McIntosh Junior: “God’s dreams for you are much bigger than your own dreams. The way was a much different route. And I would not change it for the world”

Pierre Schoeman shared that he had packed up his life in South Africa, sold his house and gave away his belongings to move to Scotland with his wife, Charissa, with just two suitcases. The couple vowed to “not look back”

Pierre stated that he had endured intense media scrutiny over his decision to represent his adoptive country.

He added: “Even if I’m good enough to play for South Africa, I chose Scotland. That’s my answer, and it still is. And it will forever be”.

FROM NELSPRUIT TO EDINBURGH

Before his big move to Scotland, Pierre Schoeman – who was born in Nelspruit- attended the Afrikaanse Hoër Seunskool in Pretoria. He also studied Business Studies at the University of Pretoria and represented the Blue Bulls.

Interestingly, Pierre represented South Africa at under-18 and under-20 levels.

In 2018, Schoeman signed a deal with Edinburgh Rugby. In 2021, he made the Scotland national training squad after he qualified to play for the country through residency.

Fast forward to 2026, and both Pierre and his wife, Charissa, officially received their Scottish citizenship. He has now earned 53 test caps for the national team.

Pierre and fellow South African rugby player Duhan van der Merwe, who, like him, plays for Edinburgh and for the Scotland national team, are also business partners in the whisky company called Against the Grain.

World.title: What Zimbabwe’s latest result means for AFCON 2027 hopes
World.content:
Zimbabwe's Warriors shared the points with Equatorial Guinea in their AFCON 2027 qualifier. Image: ZIFA

Zimbabwe’s Warriors remain in contention for a place at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) after playing out a goalless draw against Equatorial Guinea on Thursday, 12 November 2026.

The two nations shared the points in their Group E Matchday 3 encounter at Stade Ahmadou Ahidjo in Yaoundé, Cameroon.

The result means Zimbabwe have moved to four points from three qualifying matches, keeping them ahead of Equatorial Guinea in the race for a place at next year’s continental tournament.



But with another meeting between the two nations scheduled for Monday, the Warriors will have little time to reflect on Thursday’s result.

Zimbabwe remain ahead of Equatorial Guinea in Group E

Before Thursday’s encounter, Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea were level on three points after winning one and losing one of their opening two matches.

The Warriors started their campaign with a 3-2 comeback victory over Sierra Leone before suffering a 2-1 defeat against Group E leaders DR Congo.



Equatorial Guinea, meanwhile, lost 2-0 to DR Congo before recovering with a 1-0 victory over Sierra Leone.

The 0-0 result means both teams now have four points.

Zimbabwe retain the advantage on goal difference, having scored four goals and conceded four in their opening three matches.



Equatorial Guinea have scored one goal and conceded two in their first three qualifying fixtures.

In the other Group E encounter, DR Congo defeated Sierra Leone 3-1 to maintain their position at the top of the standings.

The top two teams in Group E will qualify for the 2027 AFCON finals, which will be jointly hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.



Warriors have another opportunity to collect maximum points

Zimbabwe will not have to wait long for another opportunity to strengthen their qualification hopes.

The Warriors are scheduled to host Equatorial Guinea at the National Sports Stadium in Harare on Monday, 16 November.

The return fixture presents an opportunity for Ramon Catala’s men to collect three points against a direct qualification rival.



A victory would take Zimbabwe to seven points and give them an advantage over Equatorial Guinea with two qualifying matches remaining in March 2027.

The two teams will also be monitoring the other Group E encounter between DR Congo and Sierra Leone.

DR Congo started the November international break with six points from two matches after defeating both Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea in September. Confédération Africaine de Football+2



Zimbabwe still have work to do

Although Thursday’s draw keeps Zimbabwe ahead of Equatorial Guinea, the Warriors cannot afford to become complacent.

Their remaining fixtures, including Monday’s return encounter, could prove decisive in determining which two nations progress from Group E.

With qualification still within reach, Zimbabwe will be hoping to make home advantage count when they welcome Equatorial Guinea to Harare.

World.title: Number Of The Day | $2.1 trillion | 12 November 2026
World.content:
The $2.1 Trillion Question: Has The World Put Too Much Faith In Big Tech?

The staggering fall in Nvidia's market value exposes an uncomfortable contradiction between financial wealth and the economic reality on which it depends.

It is difficult to comprehend $2.1 trillion. It is harder still to understand how that much market value can disappear from a single company while the factories, technology and customers underpinning its business remain largely intact.

Nvidia's extraordinary decline from its October valuation peak is a reminder that modern financial markets are increasingly shaped by expectations of tomorrow rather than the realities of today. Artificial intelligence has become one of the most powerful investment narratives in the world, and enormous financial wealth has accumulated around companies expected to lead its development.

The danger begins when confidence in that future becomes so concentrated that a change in sentiment can unsettle the wider market.

The concentration problem

The extraordinary rise of technology companies has created a peculiar contradiction. Investors seek diversification to protect themselves against risk, yet many widely

held global equity investments are increasingly influenced by the performance of the same small group of businesses.

A retirement fund may own shares across numerous industries and countries while remaining significantly exposed to the fortunes of America's largest technology companies. When those companies stumble, the consequences can travel through investment portfolios far removed from Silicon Valley.

For South Africa, where retirement savings and institutional investments often include international equities, global market concentration deserves closer attention. Offshore exposure can provide important diversification, but geographic distance does not automatically mean independence from the same underlying risks.

The question is whether investors are buying genuinely different opportunities or repeatedly investing in variations of the same expectation.

When optimism becomes an economic liability

The artificial intelligence boom has generated enormous enthusiasm about productivity, innovation and new commercial opportunities. Some of that optimism may prove justified. However, technological transformation does not guarantee that every investment made in anticipation of it will produce an attractive return.

History offers a useful warning. During the dot-com boom, investors correctly recognised that the internet would transform commerce and communication. Many nevertheless paid valuations that the businesses concerned could not sustain. The technology succeeded, but investors who overpaid did not necessarily share in that success.

Today's AI investment cycle faces a similar test of expectations, even if its leading companies have substantially more established businesses and earnings than many speculative internet ventures of the late 1990s.

The crucial issue is not whether artificial intelligence will matter. It is whether the financial promises attached to its development can be delivered at the scale investors anticipate.

The price of collective belief

A company worth trillions can lose an extraordinary amount of market value without an equivalent amount of cash disappearing from the economy. Yet the consequences of a major repricing are still real. Falling asset values can influence investment decisions, risk appetite and confidence across financial markets.

Nvidia's turmoil demonstrates how quickly questions about leadership, governance and future profitability can collide when expectations are exceptionally high.

For South Africa, the sheer scale of the decline invites a broader reflection about where economic value is created and where financial value accumulates. One company's shifting market valuation can dwarf the annual output of an entire developing economy, despite the enormous difference between financial ownership and productive activity.

That imbalance should encourage greater scrutiny of the assumptions driving investment decisions, rather than admiration for the size of the numbers alone.

The world may be entering an extraordinary technological age. But the financial markets financing that future are still vulnerable to one of humanity's oldest weaknesses: believing that yesterday's extraordinary success makes tomorrow's success inevitable.

· The Wall Street Journal. "Nvidia's Market Cap Continues to Slide." 12 November 2026.

· Reuters. "Drama at Nvidia." 12 November 2026.

· Encyclopaedia Britannica. "Dot-com bubble." Historical background.

Mpofu's comments come as the Jacob Zuma-led party confirmed its intention to meet with the ANC over coalition talks.

Mpofu said those conversations would be critical and direct.

“We're not going to be in some slanging match; we are going to appeal to the ANC to do the right thing, so that it avoids its own death... So, we really hope that whatever is happening on the other side of this place, called Birchwood, that sanity will prevail, that cool heads will prevail, and that people and egos must be put aside.”

World.title: Madlanga Commission | Questions raised over 'Cat' Matlala's silence
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Over the last three days, Vusimuzi 'Cat' Matlala faced tough questions at the Madlanga Commission.

But throughout his testimony, the alleged underworld boss refused to answer some questions, citing his right against self-incrimination.

A crime expert, Professor Dee Khosa, says there must be a balance between his rights and attempts to get satisfactory answers.

"The right is important and it must be respected, especially because he's facing criminal charges. But it's a shield, not a menu where he picks the questions that he likes. “It really becomes a problem when he points fingers at others, but goes quiet about his own role and the role that he has played in the entire scenario. Because then the commission only gets half of the story.”

Khosa said the commission must check that each refusal is genuine and not just convenient.
