El presidente se ha llevado a Janones, el general del Ejército de WhatsApp, en su viaje a Turquía y a Filipinas. Ambos han protagonizado este jueves un directo desde la cumbre del clima, donde Lula ha instado al mundo a no relegar la lucha contra el cambio climático.

Lula hace, pues, una parada en España con la intención indisimulada de participar en la campaña española y empujar a Sánchez en un momento de especial dificultad, cuando los sondeos apuntan a una recuperación del PSOE, pero no suficiente para gobernar y evitar que la derecha y la ultraderecha sumen una mayoría absoluta. En La Moncloa confían en que este acto de Lula pueda suponer el principio de una remontada que, según insisten sus sondeos internos, ya detectan, en línea con lo que plantea el CIS, aunque las demás encuestas, incluida la de 40dB. para EL PAÍS y la Cadena SER, apuntan que el PSOE sube casi dos puntos, pero la debilidad de Frente Amplio permite al PP y Vox sumar una cómoda mayoría absoluta por encima de los 190 escaños.

Lula no acudió a la cumbre Iberoamericana de Madrid porque, tras la campaña electoral, una de las más duras de su vida, necesitó de unos días para recuperar la voz y descansar tras los intensos comicios a doble vuelta. La primera semana tras su heroica victoria no tuvo más agenda pública que soplar las velas de su 81 cumpleaños, dos días después de los comicios que ganó contra pronóstico. Y ahora está embarcado en un largo viaje internacional que le lleva al otro lado del mundo.

Tras concluir su participación en la COP31 en Antalya (Turquía), la cumbre del clima que organiza anualmente la ONU, viajará a Manila para una visita de Estado a Filipinas y para participar después en la cumbre de la Asean, el organismo que aglutina a los países del sudeste asiático, con la vista puesta en la diversificación comercial.

World.title: Creado el mayor mapa del área cerebral clave en párkinson, alzhéimer, esquizofrenia y autismo
World.content:
Si está leyendo este artículo es porque sus ganglios basales le han dejado hacerlo. Estas pequeñas estructuras situadas en el centro del cerebro humano no son en conjunto más grandes que dos uvas, pero resultan esenciales para el movimiento voluntario, tomar decisiones, crear hábitos de conducta y generar sentimientos. Este pequeño centro de control está además relacionado con muchas enfermedades del cerebro, desde el párkinson y el alzhéimer al autismo y la esquizofrenia pasando por las adicciones. Es el lugar perfecto para comenzar a mapear el cerebro humano con una profundidad sin precedentes, y eso es exactamente lo que un gran consorcio de científicos de nueve países publica este jueves: el primer atlas célula a célula de los ganglios basales humanos, junto al de otros tres mamíferos, los macacos, los monos titís y los ratones. Este es el mayor mapa multiespecie que se haya publicado de esta región cerebral, y sus creadores esperan que ayude a entender tanto el funcionamiento normal del cerebro, como las múltiples dolencias que lo azotan.

Una de las mayores esperanzas de la neurología es entender mejor las enfermedades mentales identificando qué células en qué áreas del cerebro intervienen en cada una. Este nuevo atlas es el mayor catálogo de tipos celulares de los ganglios basales, e inaugura el camino hacia un futuro mapa global con todos los tipos de células que hay en el cerebro humano, un universo con más de 85.000 millones de neuronas y billones de conexiones entre ellas.

“Un diagnóstico de esquizofrenia o trastorno bipolar continúa siendo una condena devastadora para toda la vida; las personas con enfermedades neurodegenerativas también sufren enormemente y, por desgracia, mueren de forma prematura a causa de ellas”, afirma Evan Macosko, profesor asociado de Psiquiatría y Neurobiología en la Facultad de Medicina de Harvard, y coautor del nuevo mapa. “Esta región del cerebro es la gran estación central de las enfermedades cerebrales de ambos ámbitos”, añade.

Los investigadores han caracterizado 25,5 millones de células procedentes de cerebros humanos — 21 millones— , macacos cangrejeros — tres millones—, y titíes — 1,5 millones— . Los resultados se han publicado hoy en un conjunto de 26 estudios en distintas revistas del grupo Cell.

Este nuevo atlas se suma a otros anteriores de la corteza cerebral humana y a un primer bosquejo completo del encéfalo humano, con la importante novedad de que en este caso se analiza no solo qué genes están activos en cada célula, sino también los mecanismos epigenéticos que los regulan, la morfología, sus coordenadas espaciales exactas dentro del cerebro y su actividad eléctrica.

El atlas es la última entrega del megaproyecto Brain, que se creó en Estados Unidos en 2014 y en el que hasta ahora se han invertido unos 750 millones de dólares, y cuyo objetivo final es crear una lista completa de todos los tipos celulares del cerebro humano. “Para entender lo que ocurre realmente en el cerebro necesitamos una lista precisa de los tipos de células y estudiar la expresión de los genes en cada uno de ellos”, explica Hongkui Zeng, vicepresidenta ejecutiva y directora de Neurociencia del Instituto Allen, una de las principales entidades responsables del proyecto, en una nota de prensa. En el nuevo atlas han participado cientos de científicos de nueve países y 50 instituciones académicas.

Los investigadores han descubierto un nuevo tipo de célula cerebral relacionado con la esquizofrenia y el trastorno bipolar. El trabajo resalta la importancia de este nuevo tipo de neurona poco abundante que expresa el receptor de serotonina HTR7, y que está asociada a un mayor riesgo de padecer esquizofrenia. El estudio permite rastrear las señales genéticas de la dolencia hasta las células implicadas, lo que puede mejorar su estudio, e incluso tratarlas de forma selectiva en un futuro.

Otro de los trabajos describe una nueva versión de una terapia génica ya existente que reduce los temblores característicos de la enfermedad de Parkinson. El nuevo método ha resultado más eficaz en modelos animales y menos invasivo que los tratamientos que se administran actualmente a las personas.

Una muestra de un cerebro donado para el estudio. Instituto Allen/ Jenny Burns

Un estudio dirigido por investigadores de la Universidad de California en San Francisco ha identificado cambios genéticos importantes en determinados tipos celulares de los ganglios basales que podrían intervenir en el autismo. Este nuevo conocimiento podría conducir al desarrollo de tratamientos y a una comprensión más profunda de este trastorno neurológico.

Varios trabajos se centran en los cambios en el cerebro con la edad, y cómo usarlos para medir el envejecimiento del órgano. Científicos del Instituto Broad han descubierto cambios generalizados en la expresión génica asociados al envejecimiento que afectan de manera específica a distintos tipos celulares. El hallazgo permite predecir la edad de una persona a partir de los patrones de expresión génica de varios tipos de células cerebrales.

Otro trabajo demuestra que las proporciones de los distintos tipos celulares del cuerpo estriado, la mayor estructura de los ganglios basales, varían considerablemente de una persona a otra. Los investigadores realizaron una secuenciación de ARN de núcleo único en cuatro millones de células del cuerpo estriado y de la corteza prefrontal procedentes de cerca de 200 cerebros de adultos fallecidos. Los resultados muestran que, aunque la proporción de los distintos tipos celulares se mantiene relativamente constante entre los diferentes tejidos cerebrales de una misma persona, la composición celular varía significativamente de un individuo a otro. Estas diferencias eran especialmente acusadas en las células no neuronales, como los astrocitos y la microglía. También detectaron cambios asociados a la edad en todas las regiones cerebrales estudiadas. Por ejemplo, la abundancia de un tipo celular conocido como células progenitoras de oligodendrocitos disminuye un 40% entre los 30 y los 80 años.

El neurobiólogo español Rafael Yuste, investigador de la Universidad de Columbia, en Nueva York, fue uno de los ideólogos del proyecto Brain. El científico destaca que si bien se han publicado otros atlas cerebrales con anterioridad dentro de esta iniciativa, este es “el más exhaustivo, y el consorcio responsable es mayor que en otras ocasiones”. El investigador resalta la importancia de identificar todos los tipos cerebrales del cerebro humano, algo que “fue el sueño de Santiago Ramón y Cajal”. El médico español ganó el Nobel de Medicina en 1906 por descubrir la estructura del cerebro humano y el resto del sistema nervioso, sustentada por distintos tipos de neuronas. Parte de sus descubrimientos se centraron en el estriado, la mayor estructura de los ganglios basales. “Los ganglios basales son una parte compleja del cerebro, con un circuitaje neuronal endemoniado y que todavía se entienden poco”, reconoce Yuste por correo electrónico. “ A pesar de esto tienen una importancia vital en nuestro comportamiento, posiblemente escogiendo las acciones que queremos realizar y suprimiendo otras, e inyectando dopamina en otras partes del cerebro para mediar cambios conductuales”, dice.

La bióloga Ana Belén Muñoz Manchado, de la Universidad de Cádiz, destaca que los ganglios basales son “una de esas estructuras donde la neurología y la psiquiatría, que solemos tratar como campos separados, resultan estar mirando el mismo circuito”. La científica asegura que “lo valioso de este atlas no es solo el censo celular, que también, sino la infraestructura”. Hasta ahora, explica, cada laboratorio nombraba los tipos celulares a su manera, y comparar dos estudios era muy complicado. Este atlas establece un lenguaje común: un mismo tipo celular se llama igual en humano, macaco, tití y ratón, y además ofrece distintas capas de conocimiento de cada uno de estos tipos celulares, lo que facilita su identificación por otros laboratorios. ‘Estamos en un momento en el que, por primera vez, tenemos tecnología y herramientas capaces de responder preguntas sobre el sistema nervioso que llevaban décadas sin respuesta”, concluye.

World.title: Coalition in crisis as tax plan passes without VVD support
World.content:
The cabinet’s 2027 tax plan passed parliament by 76 votes to 74 on Thursday evening, despite the right-wing liberal VVD voting against it after its coalition partners backed a wealth tax amendment drawn up by left-wing opposition parties.

The VVD says the amendment breaches the coalition agreement, and warned it would vote against the whole plan if it was adopted. The party has not said whether it will stay in the coalition, meaning a cabinet collapse is still on the cards.

“I’m not going to make a decision two minutes after the votes,” parliamentary leader Ruben Brekelmans said as he left the chamber, calling the day’s events “appalling”, according to broadcaster NOS.

Prime minister Rob Jetten said he would meet his deputy prime ministers, VVD leader Dilan Yesilgöz and the CDA’s Bart van den Brink, on Friday morning, according to ANP.

Millionaires’ tax

The amendment was tabled by left-wing Pro and pan-European progressive party Volt, and is a scaled-down version of what the two parties call their “millionaires’ tax”. Their original plan aimed to raise €1.5 billion; the version adopted raises around €1 billion.

It uses nearly €900 million to reduce a planned rise in the lowest income tax rate. To pay for it, the tax on savings and investments (box 3) is split into two rates: 35.5% on returns up to €60,000 a year, and 38.5% above that.

It also clamps down on “paper gifts”, an arrangement where parents promise money to their children on paper to reduce gift and inheritance tax. About €400 million still has to be found from taxes on wealth from 2028.

Majority on the left

D66 and the CDA won the final vote with Pro, Volt, pensioners’ party 50PLUS, Christian-social ChristenUnie, left-wing multicultural party Denk, and the animal rights party PvdD.

The PvdD had said on Wednesday that it would vote against. It changed its position shortly before the vote, after D66 and the CDA agreed to raise the tax on private jets and drop a planned increase in train fares.

A motion of no confidence in the cabinet, tabled by the anti-immigration PVV, was defeated by 116 votes to 34. The tax plan now goes to the senate, where the coalition does not have a majority.

Pro leader Jesse Klaver said that by passing the plan, “a centre-left majority in parliament is taking responsibility for governing the country. That way we prevent chaos.”

World.title: Leiden bars extreme right student group from recruitment events
World.content:
Leiden University has banned the extreme right-wing student association GNSV from advertising club membership to new students during introduction weeks, following years of complaints and an investigation by the national security services.

The intelligence security body AIVD released a report detailing how the group hides behind moderate rhetoric to draw students in, while spreading far-right political agendas privately. Some members have been inspired to plot terror attacks.

Last year, one of its members was arrested for possession of firearms after a raid on his home in Erp in Bradant. The police were tipped off that he was planning a terror attack.

The GNSV, or Greater Netherlands Student Association, is known for spreading conspiracy theories like the Great Replacement, and advocating for remigration. The security services’ report said its members privately hold “deeply racist” views.

Dutch News spoke to its members at Leiden in 2024, where one of the group’s members discussed the idea that Flanders and the Netherlands should reunite and that too many immigrants were coming to the country.

The ban will take effect from next summer, the Volkskrant reported on Thursday. It follows three years of protests against the group’s presence at the event, which is aimed at new students.

“We do not want to offer space for that at our introduction market,” Leiden’s rector magnificus, Sarah de Rijcke, wrote on the university website.

Radboud University in Nijmegen barred the GNSV from its own introduction market immediately after the report came out. In Leiden, eight local council parties asked questions about the university’s policy.

World.title: Cabinet collapse looms as VVD pledges to vote against tax plan
World.content:
The right-wing liberal VVD will vote against its own cabinet’s tax plan if its coalition partners help pass an opposition amendment raising taxes on the very wealthy, the party’s parliamentary leader said on Thursday.

Ruben Brekelmans told MPs during a reopened debate on the 2027 tax plan that the VVD would not back the bill if the amendment, drawn up by left-wing Pro and pan-European progressive party Volt and supported by centrist D66 and the Christian Democrat CDA, is adopted, broadcaster NOS reported.

Brekelmans repeated party leader Dilan Yesilgöz’s call for a “fundamental reset” of the cabinet and said he had also been caught off guard by the deal. Yesilgöz, who is also defence minister, said on Wednesday evening that it breached the coalition agreement.

Several MPs, including anti-immigration PVV leader Geert Wilders, asked how the VVD could vote against the tax plan while staying in government. Brekelmans declined to say what would happen next. “I’m not going to speculate about what-if questions,” he said.

Earlier in the debate, Wilders accused D66 and the CDA of stabbing the VVD in the back. D66 parliamentary leader Jan Paternotte dismissed this as nonsense.

The amendment introduces a new top rate of 38.5% on returns above €60,000 on box 3 taxes, the levy on savings and investments, while the basic rate falls from 36% to 35.5%. The €1 billion raised will go towards cutting the lowest rate of income tax.

It is not certain the amendment will pass. Christian-social ChristenUnie and pensioners’ party 50PLUS, which had conditionally backed the tax plan, have doubts about how the package is funded.

Only €588 million of the €1 billion is linked to specific measures. The remaining €412 million is a target to be met by tackling tax constructions used by the wealthy. Pro and Volt have suggested an “exit tax” on millionaires who leave the country, to prevent capital flight.

The ChristenUnie and 50PLUS haven’t yet said how they will vote. If they oppose the amendment, it may fail, leaving D66 and the CDA without the senate majority they need. According to NOS, the VVD is urging the ChristenUnie to vote against, while Pro leader Jesse Klaver is trying to win over its leader, Mirjam Bikker.

The three parties in Jetten’s minority cabinet have 66 of the 150 seats in parliament, 10 short of a majority, so they rely on opposition parties to pass legislation.

Economic impact

Employers’ organisations VNO-NCW and MKB-Nederland said the country could not afford a political crisis, and objected to businesses potentially footing the bill.

But ING chief economist Marieke Blom told NOS the amendment would have very little effect on the Dutch economy, and said she did not expect millionaires or companies to leave the Netherlands because of it. “A cabinet collapse would create new political uncertainty, and I’m worried that we would grind to a halt,” she said.

Prime Minister Rob Jetten said “yes” when asked on arrival whether things would work out. Votes on the amendments and the full tax plan are due after the debate.

If the cabinet does fall, an early general election could be held alongside the provincial and water board elections on March 17 next year, NOS reported. It would be the second cabinet in a row to fall within a year.

World.title: Rozendaal council to dissolve after 200 years of independence
World.content:
After 200 years as an independent council, Rozendaal is seeking to merge with the neighbouring Gelderland councils of Rheden and Brummen, bringing its free-standing era to an end.

The smallest council on the Dutch mainland has some 1,800 residents, and Rozendaal’s council say its independence is no longer viable both financially and organisationally.

“Continuing independently would require significant, ongoing investments in personnel, expertise and systems,” mayor Ingrid Timmer told broadcaster NOS. “We simply do not have the financial capacity for that.”

A merger appeared to be the next best option, and Rheden and Brummen were chosen as both councils are currently going through their own reorganisation process and have close ties to Rozendaal.

The mayor thinks that by merging with them sooner rather than later, Rozendaal can have equal input into the new council, although the other two councils still have to approve that.

Rozendaal Blijft

Some Rozendaal residents are dissenting, saying they feel the process is moving too quickly. They’ve launched a petition with 500 signatures so far asking the council to reconsider.

The local initiative Rozendaal Blijft – Rozendaal Stays – argues that there’s not a compelling, substantiated reason for the council to disband.

“There is no clear indication as to why a decision must be made today, rather than in a few months’ time,” said the group.

“Difficult yet responsible” choice

“The steps we have taken were consistently driven by new insights,” responded mayor Timmer, who acknowledges this was not the outcome officials had hoped for. “As early as the first phase, it became clear that we needed to look beyond the option of continuing as an independent municipality.”

Rheden and Brummen are expected to decide by the end of the year if Rozendaal will join them. Then comes the so-called Reclassification Design, with all three councils deciding, among other things, on the design and name of the new council, its services and finances.

Residents will have an opportunity to respond to the plan, with the aim of forming the new council on January 1, 2030. Early council elections are slated for November 2029.

World.title: Nearly 1 million households face higher mortgages: DNB
World.content:
Some 950,000 Dutch households will pay more for their mortgage in the next two years when their fixed interest rate runs out, the central bank DNB said on Thursday.

For the typical household, the monthly bill will go up by around €150 before tax relief. A quarter of the group will pay less than €50 extra, but for another quarter the rise will top €300.

Most Dutch homeowners fix their rate for at least 10 years, and many signed up when rates were at record lows. Five years ago the average rate on a new mortgage was 1.6%, now it is close to 4%.

DNB’s figures cover people with a variable rate or a fixed rate that ends before the end of 2028. They account for 19% of the mortgage debt held by banks.

The central bank said most of them should be able to cope, because wages have gone up sharply in recent years and mortgages are smaller compared with incomes and house values. The typical household will spend 24% of its net income on the mortgage, up from 20%.

But the number of households spending more than 40% of their income on their mortgage is expected to double to around 60,000. The OECD and the ECB see 40% as a sign that a household could run into financial trouble.

People who face a big rise in payments just as their income drops, because they lose their job or retire, are most at risk, DNB said.

More people will be hit after 2028. The rate on another 27% of bank mortgage debt is due to reset between 2029 and 2033.

World.title: Frisian gold coin from 16th century breaks record at auction
World.content:
A Frisian gold coin dating back to the Eighty Years’ War has raised a record amount at auction.

The rare gold half Philipsdaalder from 1580 sold for a whopping €369,000 on Wednesday at Heritage Auctions Europe in IJsselstein. It set a record for the most expensive Dutch provincial coin.

The coin features an image of Philip II, the king of Spain and ruler of the Spanish Netherlands at the beginning of the Eighty Years’ War, which broke out in 1568. Despite the revolt, his image still appeared on coins in the early years of the war, hence the coin’s name.

Half Philipsdaalders were minted only in small numbers in Friesland, and just two silver examples from the province are known to exist. The gold coin was last on display in Leeuwarden in 1877, when it belonged to former mayor Rengers.

The auction house hasn’t said who its new owner is.

According to Jacco Scheper of Heritage Auctions Europe, reports AD, the coin fits into a broader trend of exceptional and rare pieces fetching record amounts, whether they be coins or rare Pokémon cards and retro video games.

World.title: Business bankruptcies up 27% on a year earlier in October
World.content:
The number of companies declared bankrupt in the Netherlands rose by 27% in October compared with a year earlier, according to figures from national statistics office CBS.

A total of 322 businesses went bankrupt last month, 69 more than in October 2025 and one more than in September, the CBS said on Thursday.

It is the third month in a row in which bankruptcies have been higher than in the same month a year earlier. Before that, they had fallen year on year in six of the first seven months of 2026.

The bankruptcy rate rose to 8.5 per 100,000 businesses, from 6.8 in October last year. That is still below the levels of 2024, when the rate peaked at 11.3 in July. The CBS said the rate has fluctuated between seven and eight since the middle of 2025.

Hospitality had the highest bankruptcy rate in October, at 25.1 per 100,000 businesses, up from 23.3 a year earlier. Industry saw the biggest increase, from 19.5 to 24.8. Construction was one of the few sectors where the rate fell, from 14 to 12.5.

The number of company failures fell by 15% across 2025 as a whole.

World.title: Minister: goal for zero homelessness by 2030 scrapped
World.content:
Long-term care minister Mirjam Sterk told parliament on Wednesday that the government’s goal to reduce homelessness to zero by 2030 is impossible, saying she wanted to “tell the honest story”.

The fourth Rutte cabinet set that goal in 2022 in its National Action Plan for Homelessness, seeking to move away from temporary emergency shelters towards permanent housing, backed by a €450 million annual budget.

“We remain committed, but it’s incredibly tough,” said the minister, who had informed parliament of her intentions in a letter last week. The announcement took some MPs by surprise.

“I did expect some urgency from this cabinet, but what I see is indifference,” socialist party SP MP Sandra Beckerman said.

And while the government says it will do its best to bring down the rising numbers of homeless people via existing plans to arrange suitable housing, parliament members from Pro, the ChristenUnie, D66 and CDA remain unconvinced.

The mayors

In response, the mayors of the four major Dutch cities wrote a letter to the House of Representatives on behalf of 40 other large councils asking for an additional €100 million to provide more emergency shelters and help treat crack and cocaine addicts, among other things.

Alderman Arjen Dubbelaar of The Hague says he needs €14 million to offer shelter to homeless people. “That deficit is only increasing,” he said. “We don’t want people to sleep in parks, but at the same time our reception locations are packed.”

The minister says that money won’t be forthcoming until the Chamber first figures out where the current allocation is being spent, and no new targets have been set.

Some 33,000 people aged between 18 and 65 in the Netherlands currently have no permanent place to live, most of them in the big cities, where it is relatively easy to earn money. The real figure may be higher, as it is not known how many people are staying with family or friends.

World.title: Poland dismisses Russia’s claim of breaking up Polish spy network as “disinformation”
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. After Russia announced that it had dismantled a Polish spy network and arrested two alleged agents, Poland has dismissed the claims as “disinformation” and a “provocation”. On Wednesday, while Poland was celebrating its national Independence Day, Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB) announced that it had “disrupted the activities of an intelligence network of the Polish special services operating in Kaliningrad”, a Russian exclave that borders Poland. It claimed to have detained two “agents”- one working for Poland’s Military Intelligence Service (SWW), the other for the Internal Security Agency (ABW) – who had been “collecting and transmitting information about military personnel and facilities” and “the socio-economic situation in the Kaliningrad region”. The FSB added that seven Polish citizens and three Russians who had had contact with Polish intelligence agencies had been “officially warned”, and that the Polish citizens had been banned from entering Russia. The agency also published a film containing images of alleged suspects being detained and various documents and telephone messages in Polish. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the arrests would not further worsen relations with Poland given ties between the two countries “essentially do not exist right now,” reported the RIA news agency. In a statement on Wednesday morning, Jacek Dobrzyński, the spokesman for Poland’s security services, said that he regarded the Russian announcement “as yet another provocation and act of disinformation”, especially as it had been released on Polish Independence Day. He added that he would not comment further and “appealed to everyone not to amplify hostile narratives or play into Russian propaganda”. Speaking to news website Wirtualna Polska, Maciej Wewiór, the spokesman for Poland’s foreign ministry, said that Poland was working to verify the information announced by the FSB. However, he urged “extreme caution” when dealing with such claims from Russia. “Let’s not fall for Russian propaganda and become pawns in this game,” he said. Jako rzecznik ministra koordynatora służb specjalnych nie komentuję materiałów zamieszczanych w sieci przez rosyjskie służby. 🛑 W dniu Narodowego Święta Niepodległości traktuję je szczególnie jako kolejną prowokację i dezinformację. 🛑 Apeluję o niepowielanie wrogiej narracji i… — Jacek Dobrzyński (@JacekDobrzynski) November 11, 2026 Polish fact-checking and investigative journalism service OKO.press also raised doubts about the material shared by Russia. It notes that the alleged Polish-language phone messages released by the FSB have unnatural wording and appear to have been translated from Russian. It also points out that the footage showing the alleged detentions appears to have been recorded much earlier, judging by the green folliage on trees. This assessment was echoed by Stanisław Żaryn, who served as spokesman for the security services from 2016 to 2022. He said that “fabricated propaganda materials” were clearly “prepared in advance” and “fit the Russian security services’ ongoing campaign against Poland”. “It should be assumed that, in its operation against Poland, Moscow will resort to fabricated evidence, and today’s FSB statement will be used to legitimise earlier accusations against Poland of preparing an attack on Kaliningrad,” he added. #InfoAlert. Kolejna rosyjska prowokacja. FSB twierdzi, że rozbiła polską siatkę szpiegowską pracującą w Obwodzie Królewieckim. Analiza komunikacji rosyjskiej wskazuje, że mamy do czynienia z zaplanowaną sekwencją działań informacyjnych. Wpisuje się ona w stałe oddziaływanie… pic.twitter.com/s6bTV9pIK8 — Stanisław Żaryn (@StZaryn) November 11, 2026 The FSB’s announcement came a week after Poland announced that it had detained and charged six people – five Poles and one Russian – suspected of running an operation to illegally supply Russia with military components, which were smuggled over the border into Kaliningrad. Poland also sent additional security personnel to its regions along the Russian border this month following intelligence reports suggesting a planned act of sabotage or other provocation there. Prime Minister Donald Tusk later claimed that “individuals with flashlights” had been spotted at the border but “we very quickly mobilised the appropriate forces and managed to prevent a provocation”. Poland recently launched a special operation along the Russian border after receiving information that acts of sabotage may take place there in the coming days. For more, see our report from yesterday:https://t.co/RVaXb6SQJI — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 3, 2026 Poland has seen a sharp rise in cases of espionage and sabotage carried out on behalf of Moscow in recent years. The ABW launched 48 investigations related to espionage last year, more than twice as many as in 2024. In those two years taken together, there were more espionage investigations than over the previous three decades combined. Earlier this year, the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism published a report identifying Poland as the “primary focus” of Russia’s campaign of sabotage in Europe. In response, Poland has successively closed down all of Russia’s consulates on its territory, prompting Russia to do the same with Polish consulates in a tit-for-tat move. World.title: Poland indicts Ukrainian man for assisting in rail sabotage on behalf of Russia

Polish prosecutors have filed an indictment against a Ukrainian man accused of working on behalf of Russian intelligence and assisting in last year’s sabotage of a rail line in Poland. The accused, who can be named only as Volodymyr B. under Polish privacy law and is pictured above, will stand trial for espionage, sabotage and causing the risk of a major transport accident. He could face up to life in prison if convicted. Prokurator z mazowieckiego wydziału PZ PK skierował do Sądu Okręgowego w Warszawie akt oskarżenia przeciwko Volodymyrowi B. w śledztwie dotyczącym aktów dywersji na torach kolejowych, do których doszło jesienią 2025 r. w miejscowości Mika i Gołąb. ⬇️https://t.co/N2vK7thpKe — Prokuratura (@PK_GOV_PL) November 12, 2026 In November last year, the Polish authorities discovered acts of sabotage on two sections of a rail line running between Warsaw and the eastern Polish city of Lublin. In one case, a device containing military-grade C4 explosive was detonated in an apparent attempt to derail a freight train near the village of Mika. However, it caused only minor damage to the floor of the train. The following day, in the nearby town of Puławy, a passenger train carrying 475 people had to brake suddenly due to damage to the line. However, no one was injured. Soon after, Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced that the perpetrators had been identified as two Ukrainian citizens working on behalf of Russia. They had entered Poland from Belarus and then fled back across the border immediately after the incident. In December, Interpol issued red notices for the men, identified as Yevhenii Ivanov and Oleksandr Kononov. However, the pair remain at large. Meanwhile, a third Ukrainian man, Volodymyr B., was detained in Poland a few days after the sabotage and was charged with assisting in carrying out the attack. In their statement regarding the indictment of Volodymyr B., published on Thursday, the National Prosecutor’s Office says that he assisted Yevhenii Ivanov in conducting reconnaissance of the area, selecting a place to plant the explosives and installing recording devices and metal elements on the rails. “These actions created an imminent threat of a disaster, threatening the lives and health of many people and significant property damage,” wrote prosecutors. “Their goal was to seriously intimidate many people and influence public opinion.” They also say that Volodymyr B. was “participating in the activities of Russian intelligence”. The most serious charge he faces is for acts of sabotage on behalf of foreign intelligence, a crime that carries a minimum prison sentence of ten years, ranging up to life. Interpol has published red notices for two men that Poland says were responsible for carrying out the sabotage of a rail line last month on behalf of Russia The pair immediately fled to Belarus after the incident and their current location is unknown https://t.co/RnahHDQkC8 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 18, 2025 Earlier this year, the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism published a report identifying Poland as the “primary focus” of Russia’s campaign of sabotage in Europe. Such actions have often been carried out by Ukrainians and Belarusians. Last month, the trial began of four men – three Ukrainians and one Belarusian – accused of being part of a criminal group that carried out a series of arson attacks in Poland and Lithuania on Russian orders. This week, Poland announced that it had detained and charged two Ukrainians accused of carrying out espionage and acts of sabotage on behalf of Russia. World.title: Polish deputy foreign minister charged over alleged misappropriation of millions of zloty
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A Polish deputy foreign minister has been charged with misappropriating millions of zloty entrusted to him and taking steps to prevent creditors from recovering money owed to them. Prosecutors say that Władysław Teofil Bartoszewski used the money for personal expenses and to buy three apartments in Warsaw. His wife has also been charged in the case. Both of them deny the allegations, and Bartoszewski says he “will defend the truth and my good name”. Prokurator z mazowieckiego wydziału PZ PK przedstawił posłowi na Sejm RP Władysławowi Teofilowi Bartoszewskiemu dwa zarzuty: przywłaszczenia powierzonych mu środków pieniężnych znacznej wartości oraz udaremnienia zaspokojenia wierzyciela. Komunikat: ➡️ https://t.co/EXZ3NsovBh pic.twitter.com/Lmp2f3Bw2r — Prokuratura (@PK_GOV_PL) November 10, 2026 The case dates back to before Bartoszewski had entered politics. In 2019, he became an MP for the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL). In 2023, after PSL became a junior partner in the current ruling coalition of Prime Minister Donald Tusk, he was made deputy foreign minister. From 2004, say prosecutors, Bartoszewski was entrusted with managing the assets of Polish art collector and philanthropist Andrzej Ciechanowiecki, who was Bartoszewski’s godfather and a friend of his late father, Władysław Bartoszewski, a former Polish resistance fighter, Auschwitz prisoner, and later foreign minister. From 2005, Władysław Teofil Bartoszewski, who has waived his right to anonymity in the case, also managed funds belonging to the Non Omnis Moriar Foundation, linked to the collector. According to prosecutors, Bartoszewski used some of the money to buy and renovate three apartments in Warsaw between 2005 and 2006. From 2009, Ciechanowiecki began asking Bartoszewski to account for the funds, but he allegedly failed to do so and began avoiding contact with Ciechanowiecki. In 2012, Ciechanowiecki and the foundation terminated their agreements with Bartoszewski and demanded the return of funds, say prosecutors. The following year, they filed a lawsuit demanding that Bartoszewski pay them around £1 million, 7.2 million zloty, €650,000 and $76,000, plus interest. According to prosecutors, Bartoszewski then took steps to prevent the money from being recovered. A company owned by him and his wife sold three apartments in Warsaw, after which the couple disposed of their shares in the company. His wife also donated a property to their underage children. “As a result of these actions, Władysław Teofil Bartoszewski and his wife possess no assets from which the creditor’s claims could be satisfied,” prosecutors said. In March 2024, a Warsaw court ordered Bartoszewski to pay the foundation more than 13.2 million zloty, plus interest. Prosecutors note that the judgment is not yet binding as an appeal is still pending. Od półtora roku sąd nie wyznaczył terminu apelacji w sprawie Władysława Teofila Bartoszewskiego — dowiedział się Onet. Sąd pierwszej instancji nakazał wiceministrowi spraw zagranicznych zwrot aż 13 mln zł, jakie powierzył mu jego chrzestny https://t.co/JzPwcJG4KU — Kamil Dziubka 🟡🇵🇱🇺🇦 (@KamilDziubka) November 4, 2025 Meanwhile, in 2023, representatives of the Ciechanowiecki Collection Foundation at the Royal Castle in Wawel, which now holds the assets of Ciechanowiecki (who died in 2015), filed a notification to prosecutors of alleged crimes committed by Bartoszewski and his wife. Earlier this year, the prosecutor general, Waldemar Żurek, asked parliament to lift Bartoszewski’s immunity so that prosecutors could bring charges against him. However, he voluntarily waived it on 6 October. At the time, Bartoszewski told newspaper Fakt that he “absolutely does not feel guilty” and “the evidence confirms this”. He also claimed that there is “a political element to my case”, though he did not elaborate further. Sejmowa komisja regulaminowa opowiedziała się we wtorek za uchyleniem immunitetu posła PSL Władysława Teofila Bartoszewskiego w związku z wnioskiem prokuratury w sprawie podejrzenia popełnienia przez niego między innymi przestępstwa przywłaszczenia mienia.https://t.co/ydA0jNNUQ8 — tvn24 (@tvn24) October 6, 2026 On Tuesday this week, prosecutors announced that they had charged Bartoszewski with misappropriation of funds of significant value – £1 million, €405,000 and 6,683,705 zloty – entrusted to him by Ciechanowiecki and the foundation. The offence carries a prison sentence of between one and 10 years. A second charge concerns allegedly taking steps to prevent or reduce the recovery of money owed to a creditor. It carries a prison sentence of between three months and five years. Prosecutors say that, on the same day, they “brought similar charges” against Bartoszewski’s wife and that both of the accused denied guilt. Wiceszef MSZ Władysław Teofil Bartoszewski oświadczył, że nie przyznaje się do popełnienia zarzucanych mu przez prokuraturę czynów. Zapowiedział, że będzie bronił prawdy i swojego dobrego imienia "tak długo, jak będzie to konieczne". https://t.co/tGodfs9Gzi — Interia (@Int_Wydarzenia) November 10, 2026 In a statement issued later on Tuesday, Bartoszewski issued a statement rejecting the allegations and saying that he “will defend the truth and my good name in every instance, for as long as necessary”, reports the Polish Press AGency (PAP). “I am convinced that both the criminal proceedings and the ongoing civil proceedings will confirm my arguments and rights to my property,” he added. “I consistently maintain that all actions related to the acquisition of the real estate were consistent with the original will of Andrzej Ciechanowiecki expressed at the time of their purchase, and the premises were intended to constitute permanent financial security for my family.” Asked whether the prime minister would dismiss Bartoszewski following the charges or wait for a court ruling, government spokesperson Adam Szłapka said that the deputy minister “is currently on leave and decisions regarding this matter will be made upon his return”. World.title: Annual Polish Independence March passes through Warsaw
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The annual march held in Warsaw to mark Poland’s Independence Day has passed through the city without major incident. This year’s event took place amid heightened security following the deadly terrorist attack in Kraków just four days earlier. Hundreds of thousands of people, including President Karol Nawrocki, marched through the city amid a sea of white-and-red flags. The event, which is organised by nationalist groups, also acted as a display of unity among the right-wing and far-right opposition ahead of next year’s parliamentary elections. Figures from the more liberal government, as always, avoided the march. Prime Minister Donald Tusk celebrated Independence Day hundreds of kilometres away in the city of Szczecin, where he issued an invitation to the opposition-aligned Nawrocki to visit his home for talks. This year’s Independence March was held under the slogan “Polak w Polsce gospodarzem”, which translates roughly as “Poles are in charge in their own country”. The slogan was chosen to “emphasise our opposition to foreign influences on Poland and underscore that Poland should be a nation-state without mass immigration”, said Rafał Buca, the march’s spokesman. “In Poland, Poles should rule – not some foreigners, not the European Union, not big corporations.” On the morning of the march, the organisers shared an image showing Tusk as a puppet of European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. “Time to cut the strings of foreign influence,” they declared. Czas odciąć sznurki obcych wpływów i marionetkowych decyzji! W naszym własnym kraju to my – polscy obywatele – jesteśmy jedynym suwerenem i to my ustalamy reguły! 🇵🇱 POLAK W POLSCE GOSPODARZEM! pic.twitter.com/8Htr8s0klx — Marsz Niepodległości (@StowMarszN) November 11, 2026 The main organisers of the march are associated with Confederation (Konfederacja), a far-right group that sits among the opposition in parliament. But it is attended by a wide range of people, from the mainstream right through to the radical right. Leading figures from other opposition parties, including the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), centre-right Development Plus (Rozwój Plus) and radical-right Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), were present, as well as Nawrocki, who last year became the first Polish president to attend the march. A member of the march’s organising committee, Marcin Osowski, told broadcaster WNET that around half a million people were at today’s event. The municipal authorities, which are under the control of Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party, later put the figure at around 250,000. That would make today’s Independence March the largest ever other than the one in 2018, when a broader event was organised to mark the centenary of Poland regaining its independence after World War One. The opposition was aiming to show a united front amid their ongoing protests against the recent takeover of the constitutional court by a group of government-backed judges and ahead of next year’s parliamentary elections, at which they hope to unseat Tusk’s government. “It’s about showing our strength and, at the same time, for this march to be a springboard for the election campaign,” said Jarosław Kaczyński, leader of PIS, during the march, quoted by the Niezależna news website. “Unity is important.” Meanwhile, one of the leaders of Confederation, Krzysztof Bosak, told the crowd in a speech that, “while we have different experiences and views, under the white-and-red flag we form one community”. “Next year, we must turn this community into an election victory…We must remove the current clique from power and form a pro-Polish government,” he declared. “We do not accept the violent takeover of state institutions. We demand respect for the law.” Na Marszu Niepodległości jesteśmy u siebie! Przyjeżdżamy z różnych stron, mamy różne doświadczenia i poglądy, ale pod biało-czerwoną flagą tworzymy jedną wspólnotę. Każdy jest w niej potrzebny. Także ten, kto dziś czuje się samotny, odrzucony i traci poczucie sensu. Ta wspólnota… pic.twitter.com/L5pYU1RVv0 — Krzysztof Bosak 🇵🇱 (@krzysztofbosak) November 11, 2026 However, Confederation’s other main leader, Sławomir Mentzen, shared a picture of himself at the march in front of a banner showing images of both Tusk and Kaczyński crossed out, alongside the word “Reset”. While Bosak’s nationalist faction of Confederation is seen as more amenable to the idea of working with PiS to form a potential future coalition government, Mentzen’s libertarian faction is less enthusiastic about the idea. In the past, the march has sometimes seen violence, with participants clashing with police. However, in recent years it has generally passed peacefully, and that was again the case today. The city’s mayor, Rafał Trzaszkowski, who is a deputy leader of KO, said on Wednesday afternoon that, other than the illegal use of pyrotechnics (such as a flare held up by Mentzen), the march was proceeding without incident. Local authorities in Warsaw had put in place additional security measures following Saturday’s terrorist attack in Kraków, in which a 24-year-old Polish man, Michał Oksiński, killed six people and injured over a dozen more by shooting an AR-15 rifle from his car. Oksiński’s rampage was quickly brought to a halt in a shootout with armed police, and he died from his injuries on Monday. On Tuesday, the justice minister revealed that evidence uncovered so far shows “strong traces of right-wing extremism” in Oksiński’s activity. There are "strong traces of right-wing extremism" in the activity of the man who carried out the mass shooting in Kraków, says Poland's justice minister. His search history included websites relating to Anders Breivik, the Norwegian far-right terrorist https://t.co/UhVbkWSaCq — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 10, 2026 Tusk, meanwhile, celebrated Independence Day in the city of Szczecin in northwest Poland. “All of us, without exception, are responsible for ensuring that Poland remains strong, secure, free and independent forever,” said the prime minister. “Everyone who holds Poland in their hearts must understand that independence, freedom and a secure republic are a common good.” Tusk noted that, since the recent crisis around the constitutional court broke out, Nawrocki has refused his offer to meet and discuss how to find a solution to a crisis that has pitted judges appointed under the former PiS government against those chosen by the current ruling coalition. The prime minister today renewed that offer, inviting Nawrocki and his family to visit Tusk’s home in the build-up to Christmas. “We must be able to discuss things together, without bitterness, without hatred,” said the prime minister. Note: This article has been updated to include the official estimate of attendance at the march. World.title: Poland and US sign statement of intent on strengthening defence industry cooperation
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz and his US counterpart, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, have signed a statement of intent on strengthening cooperation between their defence industries. “Today, we are taking the next steps in our alliance,” declared Hegseth, while Kosiniak-Kamysz said that the move signalled that Poland is now “not only a model ally…but has become a strategic partner of the United States”. The Polish defence minister added that he would also push for equipment jointly manufactured by Poland and the US to be eligible for EU defence funding. “Poland is the US ambassador in the EU,” he declared. Wicepremier W. @KosiniakKamysz z #Waszyngton: to chyba moja najważniejsza i przełomowa wizyta w USA. To moment, w którym mogę powiedzieć, że Polska jest nie tylko modelowym sojusznikiem, ale stała się strategicznym partnerem USA. pic.twitter.com/75xdgzIaG0 — Ministerstwo Obrony Narodowej 🇵🇱 (@MON_GOV_PL) November 10, 2026 Kosiniak-Kamysz was welcomed by Hegseth in Washington to discuss a range of issues relating to security cooperation. A major item on the agenda was Poland’s desire for a new permanent US military base on its territory. After the meeting, Kosiniak-Kamysz told reporters that there was a “green light from the Pentagon” for the base, with the final decision now resting with the White House. He said that was expected to be made in early December. Hegseth, meanwhile, praised Poland for embracing the “NATO 3.0” concept, under which the US wants Europe to take on more responsibility for its own defence. “Poland is building one of the most formidable armies in Europe, ready to secure and defend its territory,” said the Secretary of War, who noted that Warsaw is “leading by example” with its high levels of defence spending. Hegseth also welcomed the fact that Poland is investing significantly in US equipment, including Abrams tanks, F-35 fighter jets, Apache helicopters and Patriot air-defence systems. “You are building a fully modernised, interoperable force, and our two nations are…giving military cooperation industrial depth as well,” said the secretary of war. Hegseth also reaffirmed Washington’s desire for a peace deal in Ukraine and “encouraged Kosiniak-Kamysz to continue Poland’s steadfast support of Ukraine”, said Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell. American defense technology is driving innovation and creating new opportunities for transatlantic industrial cooperation.@USAmbNATO Matthew Whitaker, Assistant Secretary of Commerce David Fogel @CommerceGov and @USAmbPoland Tom Rose met with Deputy Minister of Defence… pic.twitter.com/5etw1L3X5A — US Embassy Warsaw (@USEmbassyWarsaw) November 10, 2026 Kosiniak-Kamysz said that the statement of intent he had signed with Hegseth was aimed at ensuring more US equipment was manufactured and maintained in Poland itself, including technology transfers. He also said that he wants to secure European funds for jointly produced US equipment. The EU’s SAFE programme of defence loans, for example, largely excludes US manufacturers. “We want American equipment manufactured by Polish-American companies to benefit from European funding. I will present such a position next Tuesday at the meeting of EU defence ministers,” said Kosiniak-Kamysz. “Poland is the US ambassador to the EU.” The meeting between the two defence secretaries also coincided with the Transatlantic Defence Industry Access Forum, which brought together 70 Polish and 80 American firms, with the aim of strengthening ties between the two countries’ defence industries. W ostatnich dniach dobra decyzja o utworzeniu w Polsce centrum serwisowego rakiet Patriot, a dziś podpisaliśmy kolejne porozumienie z USA, które przyspieszy współpracę naszych przemysłów zbrojeniowych. Chcemy, by więcej uzbrojenia powstawało i było naprawiane w Polsce. To nowe… pic.twitter.com/j24E2xON66 — Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (@KosiniakKamysz) November 10, 2026 Last month, the United States chose Poland as the location for a planned facility for servicing and maintaining Patriot missiles – the first to be located outside the US itself. In July, it was announced that Polish state defence group PGZ would become the first European producer of American Barracuda-500M cruise missiles. In May, an agreement was signed to establish a centre in Poland for servicing the engines of Abrams tanks. That same month, President Donald Trump announced that his country would station an additional 5,000 troops in Poland, prompting Warsaw to formally request the establishment of a new US military base, which President Karol Nawrocki has suggested should be called “Fort Trump”. World.title: Two Ukrainians charged with spying and sabotage for Russia in Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has detained and charged two Ukrainian citizens accused of carrying out espionage and acts of sabotage on behalf of Russia. The men, aged 24 and 25, were allegedly paid to conduct reconnaissance of critical infrastructure and military facilities across Poland. They are also accused of setting fire to several vehicles with the aim of stoking anti-Ukrainian sentiment. Funkcjonariusze Agencji Bezpieczeństwa Wewnętrznego zatrzymali w Mińsku Mazowieckim dwóch obywateli Ukrainy w wieku 24 i 25 lat podejrzanych o szpiegostwo i prowadzenie działań dywersyjnych na zlecenie rosyjskich służb specjalnych. ▶️ Mężczyźni rozpoznawali i robili zdjęcia… pic.twitter.com/G3i8hEsBHT — Tomasz Siemoniak (@TomaszSiemoniak) November 10, 2026 The suspects were detained by Poland’s Internal Security Agency (ABW) on 3 November in Mińsk Mazowiecki, a town just outside Warsaw, the capital. ABW officers also searched their residences and other locations connected to the investigation, seizing data storage devices and narcotics. According to investigators, the suspects were tasked with setting vehicles on fire after changing their licence plates to ones used by Ukrainian military vehicles. This was “aimed at fueling anti-Ukrainian sentiment”, says the National Prosecutor’s Office. Prosecutors have charged the men under Poland’s espionage law with working against Poland on behalf of a foreign intelligence service – a crime that carries a minimum prison sentence of five years – and sabotage on behalf of foreign intelligence, which is punishable by 10 years to life. At the prosecutor’s request, a court ordered both suspects to be placed in pretrial detention for three months. In recent years, Poland has seen a huge rise in cases of espionage and sabotage carried out on behalf of Russia. The ABW launched 48 investigations related to espionage last year, more than twice as many as in 2024. In those two years taken together, there were more espionage investigations than over the previous three decades combined. Earlier this year, the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism published a report identifying Poland as the “primary focus” of Russia’s campaign of sabotage in Europe. Four men – three Ukrainians and a Belarusian – have gone on trial in Warsaw accused of being part of a criminal group that carried out a series of arson attacks in Poland and Lithuania on behalf of Russia https://t.co/i4czRb9DYZ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 12, 2026 Last month, a Polish man was jailed for five and a half years for spying on behalf of Russia. The tasks assigned to him included reconnaissance of an airport as part of a possible plan to assassinate Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky while he travelled through Poland. Shortly afterwards, the trial began of four men – three Ukrainians and one Belarusian – accused of being part of a criminal group that carried out a series of arson attacks in Poland and Lithuania on Russian orders. In July, a Russian married couple with refugee status in Poland were convicted of working as spies on behalf of Moscow. In October, a member of Poland’s military reserve, who holds both Polish and Ukrainian citizenship, was detained on suspicion of espionage. World.title: “Strong traces of right-wing extremism” in activity of Kraków terrorist, says justice minister
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s justice minister, Waldemar Żurek, says that investigators have so far found “very strong traces of right-wing extremism” in the activity of Michał Oksiński, the man who carried out Saturday’s mass terrorist shooting in Kraków that left six people dead. The perpetrator’s search history included websites relating to Anders Breivik, the Norwegian far-right terrorist who killed 77 people during two attacks in 2011. Żurek’s comments come amid intense debate and dispute in Poland over the beliefs and motives of Oksiński, who on Monday died from the injuries he sustained during a shootout with police that brought his rampage to an end. W. Żurek ujawnia nowe ustalenia po zamachu w Krakowie. Tłumik w samochodzie sprawcy i ślady zainteresowania Breivikiemhttps://t.co/nd1XPBlmrI — Radio Kraków (@RadioKrakow) November 10, 2026 On Tuesday, Żurek, who also serves as prosecutor general, spoke to local broadcaster Radio Kraków about the progress of the investigation into Oksiński. He confirmed that the perpetrator had not left behind any letter or other kind of message revealing his motives. “Those motives are being investigated,” said the minister. “There are very strong traces of right-wing extremism. I can already confirm some information because the services have access to the perpetrator’s computer. Indeed, visits to websites related to Anders Breivik are visible.” Żurek also pointed to the fact that, as prosecutors announced on Sunday, a so-called Gadsden flag (showing a snake above the words “Don’t tread on me”) had been found in Oksiński’s home. Prosecutors say a "Don't Tread on Me" flag was found hanging at the home of the perpetrator of the attack in Kraków They emphasise that the flag is not associated with any one ideology or organisation and that they are still trying to determine the shooter's motives and beliefs pic.twitter.com/yoNfh7cHwU — Daniel Tilles (@danieltilles1) November 9, 2026 Although the National Prosecutor’s Office emphasised that the flag is not associated with any one ideology or organisation, Żurek noted that it was displayed during the attack on the United States Capitol by supporters of Donald Trump in 2021. “We know well that during the attack on the Capitol, there were quite a few of these flags among far-right groups in the United States,” said the minister. “This flag [in Oksiński’s home] also sends a signal to the security services and the prosecutor’s office.” Żurek added that a search of the perpetrator’s workplace had also identified “symbolism there that could point to this thread [of right-wing extremism]”, but provided no further details. The minister noted, however, that investigators are also taking into account the potential for “mental disorders” playing a role in the actions of Oksiński, whose parents and sister were found shot dead in his home. Żurek’s remarks come following controversy in Poland over a statement by interior minister Marcin Kierwiński on Saturday, in the immediate aftermath of the attack, when he said that early indications suggest that Oksiński had held “very radical views”, including a “fascination with far-right ideologies”. Over the following two days, Kierwiński refused to provide evidence supporting those claims, and in a TV interview on Sunday evening said that he had simply been sharing “first hypotheses”. That led some right-wing opposition politicians and commentators to accuse Kierwiński of spreading false claims, either through incompetence or as a deliberate attempt to associate the attack with the right. However, speaking to Radio Kraków on Tuesday, Żurek said that “it seems that what Minister Kierwiński communicated in those first hours is confirmed by the evidence”. Poland’s interior minister, Marcin Kierwiński, is facing growing pressure to present evidence to back his claim that the Kraków shooter was driven by far-right ideologies, amid criticism from opposition parties that he is seeking to exploit the tragedy for political reasons. — Jakub Krupa (@JakubKrupa) November 9, 2026 On social media, many people have also been sharing alleged images of Oksiński’s past activities, both online and in real life, claiming that they show he held left-wing views. However, some of those images have proven to be false, such as one purporting to show him at a pro-refugee rally (the photograph is genuine, but the person in it was not Oksiński) and another purporting to show him shaking hands with Kierwiński (the image was AI-generated). Further alleged images from Oskiński’s social media accounts remain unverified and also depict posts that were made six or seven years ago. Another fake that is being widely shared. While the photo is genuine, the person highlighted is not the Kraków shooter. Other images from the event clearly show it isn't him, while fact-checkers @konkret24 actually tracked down the guy in the photo: https://t.co/4HeofUdOUm pic.twitter.com/pTfdkCZlAL — Daniel Tilles (@danieltilles1) November 9, 2026 On Monday, digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski told Polsat News that there had been an “enormous wave of disinformation” in the wake of Saturday’s tragedy. He criticised “pseudo-journalists and politicians” who had shared such content. “Digital platforms acted very responsibly, removing this content quickly,” said Gawkowski. However, he added that X, the social media service owned by Elon Musk, had been an exception and was “where the most radicalisation occurred”. Meanwhile, the interior ministry’s spokeswoman, Karolina Gałecka, announced on Monday that they would notify prosecutors about the creation and dissemination of the AI-generated image of Kierwiński shaking hands with Oksiński. She said it had been spread by social media accounts associated with right-wing broadcaster Republika. World.title: What is at stake in Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal dispute?
World.content:
Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support.

By Aleks Szczerbiak

Poland’s escalating Constitutional Tribunal (TK) dispute is no longer simply a legal argument about contested appointments but a struggle over who defines constitutional legitimacy.

As the liberal-centrist government and right-wing opposition and president advance rival rule-of-law claims, the conflict risks entrenching a system of legal dualism in which judicial authority depends on political allegiance rather than broad constitutional consent.

The roots of the crisis

Poland’s 15-member TK is a powerful body that rules on the constitutionality of the country’s laws. The roots of the current dispute trace back to late 2015 and began immediately prior to the right-wing Law and Justice (PiS) party taking office following its October parliamentary election victory.

In its final weeks in power, the outgoing government, led by the liberal-centrist Civic Platform (PO, now Civic Coalition: KO), fast-tracked the appointment of five tribunal members who were replacing those whose terms were set to expire in November and December.

Upon winning an outright parliamentary majority, the incoming PiS-led government refused to recognise these appointments, elected a slate of five new tribunal members, and party-backed President Andrzej Duda swore them in.

Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025

The tribunal (still largely composed of pre-2015 judges) ruled that three of the outgoing parliament’s appointments were lawful, so only two of the new ones could stand. PiS refused to accept this, creating the so-called “understudy” judges (dublerzy) controversy.

As further vacancies arose, the new parliament gradually installed its nominees, culminating in the appointment at the end of 2016 of one of them, Julia Przyłębska, as tribunal president. Przyłębska’s leadership was contested on procedural grounds, as was that of her 2024 successor Bogdan Święczkowski, a former senior prosecutor closely aligned with the 2015-23 PiS administration.

All of this led to the then-opposition parties and much of the Polish legal and the EU political establishments denouncing the tribunal as legally compromised and politically captured.

Total non-cooperation

Following the autumn 2023 parliamentary election, a new coalition government headed up by KO leader Donald Tusk embraced a policy of total non-cooperation with the tribunal, refusing to publish its rulings.

The battle for control took a new turn when, after initially not filling any tribunal vacancies, from March 2026 onwards the new parliament elected successive waves of new members, reaching eight by September.

However, PiS-aligned President Karol Nawrocki (who succeeded Duda in August 2025) refused to swear in five of these nominees, including former minister and close Tusk ally Maciej Berek. In response, the government took the unprecedented step of swearing in the contested nominees directly in parliament, a move that both Nawrocki and Święczkowski rejected as illegal.

The standoff between the government and president over Poland’s constitutional court deepened today, as Maciej Berek, whom the prime minister recently described as his “right-hand man”, took his oath as a new judge without the presence of the president https://t.co/MrExiJRsEN — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 14, 2026

The conflict escalated sharply at the end of last month, when, backed by the government and tribunal members elected by the current parliamentary majority, Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, one of the five contested nominees but having the longest judicial tenure, asserted her seniority to order a one-month suspension of Święczkowski and his deputy Bartłomiej Sochański in their official duties and assumed temporary control.

Justice minister Waldemar Żurek submitted requests to lift Święczkowski and Sochański’s immunity as the newly appointed members, and the new nominees entered the tribunal building under State Protection Service (UOP) escort.

This triggered protests by right-wing opposition supporters at the building’s gates, prompting a heavy police presence and tense stand-off. The severity of this was underscored when Nawrocki cut short an official visit to Senegal mid-flight, returned to Warsaw and entered the tribunal building in the early hours, condemning what he described as a violation of the constitutional order.

During a visit to the Constitutional Tribunal last night, President Nawrocki clashed physically and verbally with judges involved in an attempt to take control of the court. The president is today seeking talks with political leaders to discuss the crisis https://t.co/7HmBnuIaDG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 31, 2026

Korwin-Piotrowska then convened a tribunal general assembly which critics argued lacked the legally required two-thirds quorum because only eight of its 15 nominal members (the newly elected ones, including the five who had not taken the presidential oath) attended.

Her supporters maintained that the quorum was met because the suspension of Święczkowski and Sochański, and exclusion of the last remaining “understudy” judge, reduced the pool of eligible members to 12.

The government’s “transitional justice” logic

For the Tusk government and its legal defenders, these exceptional executive and parliamentary countermeasures were framed through the logic of “transitional justice”: as painful and extraordinary but necessary to restore the rule of law after PiS had violated the constitution and European standards, systematically packing the tribunal with political loyalists.

Justifying its non-recognition of tribunal rulings, the government argued that the presence of three defectively elected “understudy” members and their successors, together with Przyłębska’s and Święczkowski’s procedurally flawed presidential appointments, fundamentally “contaminated” the entire body, thereby invalidating its rulings.

In its efforts to restore democracy, the government may sometimes take actions that are “not fully compliant with the law”, admits @donaldtusk. But he says this is because of the legal chaos deliberately created by the former PiS government https://t.co/AWlM6hRLie — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 11, 2024

To provide what it argued was authoritative external confirmation of this defect, the government relied heavily on landmark European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) and EU Court of Justice (CJEU) rulings which determined that, thus constituted, the tribunal could no longer be considered a legitimate body established by legal standards.

From this perspective, refusing to recognise the tribunal’s allegedly unlawful rulings was framed as the only available mechanism to neutralise a partisan weapon that PiS had left behind to block the government’s legislative agenda.

Alternative parliamentary swearing-in procedures were justified on the grounds that the president’s role in receiving oaths was purely ceremonial, not a constitutionally mandated requirement.

Despite his recent political role, Berek’s appointment was defended on the basis that he played more of a technocratic-expert role within the government, and was highly qualified to undertake the extraordinary transitional measures required to repair a damaged institution.

Defenders of the tribunal leadership’s suspension and occupation of its headquarters argued that by blocking the new nominees from taking up their roles, Święczkowski had paralysed the institution and decisive measures were necessary to restore its proper functioning.

A “coup d’état”?

PiS and Nawrocki, on the other hand, maintained that the Tusk government’s actions amounted to an authoritarian attempt to operate completely outside of constitutional powers, treating legality as an option when it conflicted with its political agenda.

They insisted that all of its 2015 appointments were in full accordance with the law, correcting an improper attempt by the outgoing PO-dominated parliament to entrench its influence after electoral defeat, and that the tribunal’s ruling on the legality of these three “understudy” judges went beyond its jurisdiction.

Successive tribunal general assemblies, they argued, validly and legally selected Przyłębska and then Święczkowski as presidents, and the Tusk government had no constitutional right to pick and choose which tribunal rulings it would recognise. They said that, by delaying the election of some new members when vacancies arose, the government violated existing procedures.

The constitution, they said, explicitly required these new nominees to take their oaths directly “before the president” and that by conducting improper parliamentary swearing-in ceremonies they had effectively renounced their offices.

The International Commission of Jurists has criticised the takeover of Poland’s constitutional court, saying it “contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary” But it also criticised the president for refusing to swear in judges https://t.co/2kBv3GT20d — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 4, 2026

The candidacy of Berek, a recently active politician with doubtful professional qualifications, they said represented its own form of institutional capture and selective legality.

The suspension of the tribunal leadership and occupation of its headquarters amounted to an unlawful power grab or “coup d’état” that completely disregarded established constitutional procedures.

PiS rejected the “contamination” thesis and argued vigorously that Poland had never transferred jurisdiction over the organisation of the national judiciary to EU institutions and European courts, who had no authority to evaluate the legality of tribunal appointments.

They accused the EU political establishment of double standards, weaponising “rule-of-law” arguments to help a politically aligned government while ignoring the Tusk administration’s own executive overreach.

PiS also argued that by delegitimising a tribunal which had in the past ruled that the Polish Constitution superseded EU law, the Tusk government was paving the way for controversial social and economic policies to be pushed through without any domestic judicial oversight.

Tusk’s liberal critics

On the other hand, more ideologically supportive liberal critics of the Tusk government’s approach acknowledged the original 2015 irregularities but warned that selective non-recognition of an entire institution, combined with attempts to install a new tribunal without presidential participation, risked creating the same dual legitimacy problem that they accused PiS of having started.

They stressed that lasting repair required broad political consensus and careful adherence to formal procedures so that future majorities did not simply invert the non-recognition tactic. They noted the tension with earlier condemnations of PiS for elevating politically aligned figures or recently active politicians.

While sympathetic to the goal of reforming what they believed was a deeply compromised tribunal, these critics argued that, by employing legally questionable shortcuts and executive force, the Tusk government risked setting dangerous precedents and deepening the very disorder that it was claiming to correct.

Interestingly, the government’s broader “transitional justice” justificatory logic – that ordinary procedures would not adequately address a systemic capture and the priority had to be functional restoration rather than abstract purity – mirrored the arguments PiS itself advanced for its own judicial reforms after 2015.

The right-wing party argued that the post-1989 judiciary remained dominated by a post-communist elite that required deep structural overhaul rather than incremental change.

A high-risk escalation

The latest escalation is likely to entrench and intensify the profound systemic polarisation that characterises the Polish political scene, for a long-time embodied in the KO-PiS duopoly, with the conflict framed in existential terms of either “restoring the rule of law” or “defending the constitutional order”.

This fierce dispute lies at the heart of the Tusk government’s broader political “reckoning” (rozliczenie) agenda involving visibly removing PiS’s influence from key institutions.

For the ruling coalition, this was a central 2023 election campaign message, and being seen to deliver on it is an absolute political necessity to satisfy and mobilise its electoral base. A confrontational approach thus serves to consolidate the government’s support among these core voters, who have grown increasingly impatient and want to see decisive action.

However, the government’s strategy is fraught with political risk. High-stakes tactics risk uniting its right-wing opponents and alienating moderate voters increasingly exhausted by endless, hyper-partisan institutional confrontation, legal brinkmanship and the optics of police deployments around a key state body.

They provide the president and right-wing opposition with a powerful counternarrative of constitutional vandalism ahead of the next parliamentary election.

Escalation is also straining relations within the ruling coalition, especially among more conservative or legalistic coalition partners who believe that a more fundamental constitutional “reset” based on a cross-party settlement is required to break the impasse in the longer term.

The leader of one of the parties in Poland’s ruling coalition has proposed a “constitutional reset” to resolve the crisis around the country’s top court. It would involve removing all current judges and choosing new ones in a more consensual process https://t.co/xDwpRUVHxG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 6, 2026

Internationally, although the EU political establishment remains supportive of the Tusk government’s actions, they invite uneasy scrutiny of the stability of Poland’s legal system and have drawn explicit criticism from the US embassy.

The reliance on a “transitional justice” framing that echoes PiS’s earlier justifications for systemic change, combined with the appointment to the tribunal of a recent minister despite prior criticisms of politicised nominations, also undercuts government claims of consistent principle and provides the right with a powerful narrative of hypocrisy.

Legal dualism

Ultimately, this bitter dispute has paved the way for a protracted and deeply destabilising “legal dualism” that could plague the Polish state for years to come, with a tribunal simultaneously legitimate and illegitimate depending on who holds power.

By treating the tribunal as an illegitimate entity when its nominees did not control it, the current government has established a precedent.

Even if it now appears to have secured a clear majority for its own nominees, a future right-wing government and sympathetic president will have every incentive to use the exact same playbook: treating the reconstituted tribunal as a captured instrument of the liberal establishment, and regarding it as no more legitimate than the Tusk government did the PiS-era one.

Consequently, the tribunal’s authority, and legal certainty in Poland more generally, have been further eroded, leaving the country without a widely accepted arbiter to resolve constitutional disputes. There are no immediate prospects for a durable resolution of this conflict.
