World.title: Baltic communal singing may no longer bring everyone together, study finds
World.content:
Communal singing across the Baltics may not be as inclusive today as its reputation suggests, with a new study finding some groups are increasingly left out of the experience.

The Integration Foundation presented the findings Wednesday from "Crises Established Singing: investigating the inherent potential of collective singing in times of social crises in the Scandinavian and Baltic regions" (CRIES), a research project involving cultural scholars from the Baltic states and Denmark.

The study examined how communal singing, long seen as a force for bringing people together, can also exclude certain groups.

Researchers found that growing numbers of people in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania do not identify with the idea of being a "singing people."

Those who do not speak the local language also take part in communal singing less often, as do unemployed and older people, who may lack the means or money to attend public gatherings and large events.

Generations of men's choir singers performing at the XXVIII Song Festival in Tallinn. July 6, 2025. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

In Estonia, choral singing is even losing ground in larger cities, where residents have more leisure activities to choose from.

Chances for 'not good' singers

"We're used to thinking that singing together includes everyone and that everyone in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania sings," said Rūta Muktupāvela, a lead researcher and professor at the Latvian Academy of Culture who led the study.

Each country, however, is also home to people who don't belong to its primary ethnic group and are less likely to take part in communal singing or song and dance festivals, she added.

Muktupāvela likewise noted that some people would like to take part but feel like they aren't good enough singers.

She said opportunities should be created for those who may not consider themselves talented enough but would still like to join in communal singing.

Choir singers of all ages and backgrounds at the XXVIII Song Festival in Tallinn. July 6, 2025. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

World.title: Estonian pilot: We keep our jets at least a kilometer from Russia's border
World.content:
Estonian pilots stay at least a kilometer from the Russian border, never flying east of Lake Peipus, one Air Force flyer told Maaleht.

In an interview with the weekly, Second Lieutenant Jasper Vimm, a 28-year-old captain, said no aircraft takes off without a planned route; pilots keep away from the border once airborne, and as GPS signals are liable to evaporate once you near Russia, flights are planned around ground landmarks.

Estonia's Air Force (Õhuvägi) is small compared with some other countries', but has four main aircraft: two Czech-made L-39 Albatros trainers leased from an Estonian firm, one of which is currently undergoing maintenance, and two Polish PZL M28 Skytruck transport aircraft used for maritime patrol and exercises.

The L-39s date from the 1980s and 1990s, fly at subsonic speeds of about 700 km/h, carry no weapons, cannot climb vertically, and have airframes with a service life of 5,000 flight hours, of which this one has a little over half left.

The Air Force currently has between 10 and active 20 pilots, Vimm said, though changes are afoot - the Estonian National Defence College will graduate its first class of pilots next year, after which new Air Force pilots will come through every year.

With its relatively compact size, flying from one end of Estonia to the other takes 30–40 minutes in a trainer; about half that in a larger fighter at cruising speed.

There have been proposals recently for Estonia to take on light fighters, what type is not yet known, but Vimm said once in country these would perform the same roles as the full-blown fast jets, differing mainly in size and speed.

He said new aircraft would be "a source of joy" for pilots, who would be able to do more in the air and practice using aircraft weapons using their own aircraft.

As for drones, Vimm said 'these are suited to destruction and reconnaissance and are replacing some missile roles, but pilots are not going anywhere for the time being: human-piloted planes perform a wider range of tasks and someone must still sit in the cockpit to achieve this.

While the disparity of state of the art fighters costing millions going out to intercept cheap drones, Vimm said the cost of human lives lost, infrastructure destroyed, far outweighs aircraft maintenance and the cost of air time; Ukraine has even mounted machine guns on slower, old piston-driven aircraft to hunt quadcopter-type drones, he noted.

The original Maaleht interview is here.

Since the Air Force, organizationally a part of the Estonian Defense Forces (EDF) currently has no fast jets, NATO allies provide that capability flying out of Ämari and from Šiauliai in Lithuania. Turkey's Air Force currently holds that role at Ämari with its F-16s.

World.title: US officer accused of Russian spying is set to be charged in UK, official says
World.content:
LONDON: An American Army officer who was arrested in the United Kingdom on suspicion of spying for Russia had not handed over any information to Moscow and he is expected to be charged in Britain in the coming days, a US official said Thursday.

After the British charges are filed against Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner, expected on Sunday or Monday, the intention is then to prosecute him under the US military justice system, the official said. No information made it into Russian hands, the official said.

A second US official also confirmed Tyner’s name and said he had been previously deployed to Afghanistan, Iraq and Qatar. Both spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive military matters.

Tyner was a senior human resources officer and had been assigned to a NATO unit at a base near Gloucester, England. He was arrested Tuesday on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service and obtaining or disclosing protected information.

The Metropolitan Police announced the arrest this week and said its counterterror forces worked closely with the FBI and US military.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov denied that Russia has any connection to the US officer.

“This arrest does not concern us in any way. We don’t know what it’s connected to,” Peskov told journalists on Wednesday, according to Russian news services. “We have nothing to do with this and it has nothing to do with us.”

Tyner was serving in NATO’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps at Imjin Barracks near Gloucester. The multinational land unit within the NATO military alliance is designed to quickly respond to crises or short-notice operations. According to the unit’s website, it is made up of forces from 20 nations but is led by the British.

Police said the arrest was not related to other counterterrorism investigations, indicating no connection with a suspected terror plot linked to Iran in September at a US-run base in Britain, RAF Fairford, near Gloucester.

World.title: Saudi foreign minister and Chinese envoy discuss Houthi attacks and regional security
World.content:
RIYADH: The Saudi foreign minister, Prince Faisal bin Farhan, and China’s special envoy for the Middle East, Zhai Jun, discussed regional security, diplomatic efforts to ease tensions and the protection of vital shipping routes on Thursday.

The talks during their meeting at the Foreign Ministry in Riyadh focused on continuing Houthi attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, and their implications for regional stability, the Saudi Press Agency reported.

The officials also reviewed bilateral ties and diplomatic efforts to contain regional crises and prevent further escalation. Maritime security and energy supplies were a particular focus, with both officials emphasizing the need to maintain stable energy markets and safeguard freedom of navigation.

They also highlighted the importance of protecting commercial shipping routes, particularly those that pass through the straits of Hormuz and Bab Al-Mandab, to ensure global trade and supply chains keep moving without disruption.

World.title: A way of life is disappearing on Cambodia’s Tonle Sap lake
World.content:
CHONG KNEAS, Cambodia: At the edge of Cambodia’s great Tonle Sap lake, a wall of red, blue and yellow metal drums rises bright against the muddy water.

Meas Chou stockpiles these drums wherever he can and sells them to families who use them to keep their houses afloat on Southeast Asia’s largest lake. About 1.5 million people live on Tonle Sap, their homes rising and falling with the ebb and flow of the lake’s water levels.

This year’s record-breaking El Niño is predicted to bring hotter, drier weather across Southeast Asia, threatening both fisheries and farms. For Cambodia, which is already in a time of extreme drought, this could stunt Tonle Sap’s annual water flows from the Mekong River, which usually refill the lake each monsoon season.

In early October, the water level in the town of Prek Kdam — about halfway between the capital city of Phnom Penh and Tonle Sap — stood at nearly 7 meters (nearly 23 feet). That’s more than a meter below average and 1.5 meters (about 5 feet) lower than last year.

Lower water levels mean meager fish catches and less business for Chou. Higher fuel prices due to the Iran war also are hurting his sales and other aspects of life on the lake. There’s little he can do but hope the rain comes and the fish return.

“If fishermen can earn a lot, I can sell my goods a lot. But if they earn less, I sell a little less too,” he said.

Pressures mount on Cambodia’s great lake

Tonle Sap rises and falls with an extraordinary natural rhythm that scientists call a “flood pulse.”

Each year, monsoon rains swell the Mekong River so much that its water flow reverses direction, sending water back upstream into the lake, which then quintuples in size. Sediment-laden flood waters carry nutrients from forests and grasslands into the lake, and the fish follow.

This makes Tonle Sap one of the world’s most productive freshwater fisheries.

It is a nursery for some of the world’s largest and rarest freshwater fish. That includes the critically endangered Mekong giant catfish, which can grow up to 3 meters (10 feet) long, the Mekong giant barb, which is the world’s biggest carp species and can weigh up to 300 kilograms (660 pounds), and the Mekong giant stingray, the world’s largest recorded freshwater fish.

The annual floods turn dusty roads into busy waterways. Some floating houses become bustling markets. Fishermen pass the hottest hours of the day by playing billiards on the riverside. Crocodile hatchlings chirp from net-covered plastic buckets, to be sold for meat or leather.

But this way of life is imperiled as upstream dams and sand mining alter the flow of the Mekong. With climate change, rainfall has become erratic and droughts are disrupting the seasonal flooding that the lake depends on.

Conversations among fisherfolk on the lake often mention two wars: the Iran war, which has driven up fuel prices, and a simmering border conflict with neighboring Thailand, which has disrupted trade, travel and tourism.

Chinese envoys visiting Cambodia in the 13th century described Tonle Sap as a vast inland sea teeming with fish. But that “unbroken thread” is about to snap, according to Abby Seif, author of ‘Troubling the Water: A dying lake and a vanishing world in Cambodia.’

“You have a disappearing way of life ... a disappearing culture and you have a disappearing history,” she said.

El Niño to bring worse drought

El Niño is a natural climate cycle marked by unusually warm ocean temperatures. This year, it is expected to bring extreme drought, heat waves, flooding and other climate-related disruptions to South America, Africa and Asia.

In June, the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization found that Cambodia was at high risk of severe drought during this El Niño cycle, which could affect about 314,000 acres (about 491 square miles) of farmland. This works out to about 3 percent of Cambodia’s arable land, according to data from the World Bank Group.

It adds to the hardships for Tonle Sap’s fisherfolk, since most farm to supplement their meager incomes from fishing, said Brian Eyler, director of The Stimson Center’s Southeast Asia Program in Washington, D.C.

Drought also could make the sometimes flooded forests around Tonle Sap more vulnerable to fires. Between 1993 and 2017, about a third of those forests stayed dry and were lost to fires and agricultural clearing, a 2020 study found.

“When you get a very dry year, you have less fish, less food and more fire. And all of those add up to a bad situation for people living around the lake,” said Zeb Hogan, with the University of Nevada, Reno, who runs the research and conservation project Wonders of the Mekong.

Vulnerable communities face climate extremes

Like many poorer countries, Cambodia is facing severe consequences of climate change that far exceed its own contribution to the problem. The nation of 18 million contributes less than 0.2 percent of the world’s annual greenhouse gas emissions.

Many of the people living on Tonle Sap have little to no land or other assets and few have anywhere else to go.

Yim Nary watches her husband head out to fish before dawn, each day hoping for a good catch. What he brings home usually barely covers their main expenses of fuel, rice, vegetables, drinking water and electricity.

When fuel is too expensive, her husband rows instead of running his boat’s engine. When he falls sick, Nary cuts and cleans other people’s catches to make up for his lost income. With three children, there is little leeway for anything to go wrong.

“I don’t know what the future holds for my children,” she said. “All I have is fish and family.”

World.title: Hegseth awards medal to soldier who rebuked his group outside Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
World.content:
WASHINGTON: Defense ‌Secretary Pete Hegseth awarded a medal on Thursday to a US Army sentinel who appeared to admonish him and his aides ​for failing to adhere to proper decorum outside the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on Veterans Day.

Hegseth posted a picture of him pinning a medal on Army Specialist Thomas Iglesias as he stood alongside members of his unit, the 3d US Infantry Regiment, known as The Old Guard. Hegseth wrote: “We love soldiers. We ‌love standards. Well ‌done, Specialist. Carry on Patriots.”

In a ​video ‌that ⁠went ​viral online, ⁠Iglesias on Wednesday shouted toward Hegseth, his wife and senior aides after they were seen on video taking pictures and speaking to each other on the steps of the memorial at Arlington National Cemetery following a Veterans Day event. Laughter was heard.

“All visitors will maintain an ⁠atmosphere of silence and respect at all ‌times,” Iglesias exclaimed.

Sitting at ‌the heart of Arlington National Cemetery, ​the Tomb of the Unknown ‌Soldier is a sacred site and the grave ‌of three unknown American service members, including one from World War One. It is widely known as a place for mourning and for reflection on military service, and sentinels guard ‌the site 24 hours a day.

Hegseth, a former Army National Guard soldier who served ⁠in Iraq and ⁠Afghanistan, prevailed this week when the House of Representatives rejected a Republican lawmaker’s effort to impeach him.

At a rare Pentagon press conference on Tuesday hours before the vote, Hegseth called the impeachment effort a farce and defended his record, which includes championing the unpopular Iran war, launching strikes on suspected drug vessels in Latin American waters and firing senior military officers.

Democrats who won control of both chambers of Congress last week have ​promised to investigate ​Hegseth for his stewardship of the US military and have not ruled out another impeachment effort.

World.title: Iraq discusses reforms with IMF to support economy
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Finance, Falih Sari, and officials from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) discussed a reform path designed to enhance financial sustainability and support the Iraqi economy.

According to a statement released by the Iraqi Finance Ministry, Sari and IMF representatives wrapped up their discussions in Amman, Jordan, after making progress in negotiations for a reform program that the international organization will support in the coming years.

The reform program aims to improve the performance of Iraq’s public finances. It also aims to provide a clear monetary framework to sustain monetary policies, increase their effectiveness, and have a more favorable influence on economic activity.

The discussions covered plans to develop the banking sector—including both state-owned and private banks—and enhance efforts to combat money laundering and terrorism financing.

According to Sari, the talks centered on developing a medium-term reform program for the coming three years with the goal of improving fiscal sustainability and strengthening the Iraqi economy’s ability to face potential challenges.

Sari indicated that expert-level conversations will continue in the near future to develop a joint document between Iraq and the IMF.

The document will provide a framework for budgetary changes and a timeline for implementation over the next three years.

World.title: Iraq’s oil production surges to 4.88 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil output rose by 489,000 barrels per day in October 2026 compared to September, according to data from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) based on official Iraqi estimates.

Iraq’s oil production rose from 4.39 million barrels per day in September to 4.88 million barrels per day in October, a monthly increase of approximately 11.1 percent.

Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair said recently that Iraq seeks to negotiate with OPEC to raise its oil output and obtain a larger export cap.

The Iraqi minister indicated that Iraq deserves a rise in output to secure the financial revenues needed to expand infrastructure and implement government goals.

Additionally, Khudair reiterated Iraq’s commitment to the 4.43 million barrels per day production cap set by OPEC.

In early September, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called for an increase in oil output to reach 10 million barrels per day by 2030.

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq’s oil output should be proportionate to its reserves, oil production capabilities, and the growing number of the population, allowing it to satisfy its residents’ needs as well as development requirements.

Iraq’s oil production reached approximately 4.5 million barrels per day by the end of 2025.

World.title: Iraqi, Iranian leaders meet at COP31 in Turkey
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi President Nizar Amidi met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Wednesday on the sidelines of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey.

The two leaders reviewed recent developments in Baghdad-Tehran relations and emphasized the need to enhance constructive engagement and expand joint cooperation in different areas.

Amidi emphasized the significance of coordinating regional and global efforts to address current challenges in the Middle East, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Presidency.

During his participation in COP31, Amidi delivered Iraq’s national message, emphasizing that the country has lost more than 50 percent of its agricultural area due to desertification and climate change.

During his stay in Antalya, Amidi held additional bilateral meetings with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

Held between November 9 and November 20, 2026, COP31 brings together heads of state, government officials, and international leaders, though notable leaders from several G7 and European nations are absent.

The summit centers on climate change financing and adaptation for vulnerable nations, loss and damage funding, and clean energy transitions rather than just new targets.

World.title: Protests in Northern Basra: Oil wealth vs. service deprivation trigger renewed unrest
World.content:
Basra (IraqiNews.com) – Widespread popular demonstrations and open-ended sit-ins have swept across the northern districts of Iraq’s oil-rich Basra Governorate—spanning Al-Sadiq, Al-Qurna, Al-Dair, Al-Nashwa, Al-Suwaib, and Al-Thaghr—since late October and early November 2026.

Residents, tribal figures, and local clerics have mobilized near the gates of major strategic oilfields, including West Qurna 1 and Majnoon, demanding immediate public service delivery, infrastructure rehabilitation, local employment quotas, and environmental remediation.

Despite sitting atop some of Iraq’s largest crude oil reserves, northern Basra communities cite severe developmental neglect, broken promises, and deteriorating living standards. Protesters—organized largely under the Al-Sadiq Movement alongside coordinated community sit-ins—have framed their demands around several urgent priorities:

Infrastructure and Public Utilities: Residents demand the immediate completion of stalled public works, including paving neglected roads, rehabilitating the Qurna–Basra highway, completing the Al-Sadiq–Izz al-Din Salim bridge, expanding potable water and sewage networks, and addressing acute shortages in schools and primary healthcare clinics.

Petrodollar and Social Benefit Allocations: Protesters are calling for transparent disbursement of Basra’s statutory petrodollar revenues, border-crossing tariffs, and the mandatory “Social Benefits” (al-Manafi al-Ijtima’iya) funds paid by international oil companies (IOCs) to develop communities hosting extraction operations.

Employment and Local Hiring: Facing high youth unemployment, residents are demanding priority hiring for local graduates and laborers within foreign and national oil companies operating in Majnoon and West Qurna.

Environmental and Health Crisis: Communities surrounding the fields have raised urgent alarms over rising rates of cancer and kidney failure linked to gas flaring, industrial pollution, and the confiscation of agricultural and tribal lands for oil expansion without adequate environmental safeguards or compensation.

The current wave of unrest reignited in late October when the Al-Sadiq Movement re-established sit-in tents outside the entrance of the West Qurna 1 oilfield, protesting the government’s failure to fulfill prior pledges to maintain service-effort machinery (al-Juhd al-Khadami).

By November 7 and 8, demonstrations expanded into Al-Dair district, where hundreds of residents led by local clerics including Sheikh Muthanna Al-Rubaie declared an open-ended sit-in. Simultaneously, residents from Al-Jazeera, Al-Nashwa, Al-Suwaib, and Al-Thaghr staged demonstrations directly outside the Majnoon oilfield perimeter on November 9, warning against continued administrative procrastination.

In response to mounting pressure near vital export arteries, Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi dispatched a high-level ministerial delegation on November 9—headed by the Minister of Oil alongside the Ministers of Construction and Housing, and Planning—instructing them to conduct on-the-ground inspections across northern Basra districts and submit an actionable report within 48 hours.

Following negotiations between protest representatives and federal officials on November 7, organizers in Al-Sadiq agreed to suspend escalatory blockades around oil installations and maintain peaceful sit-ins in exchange for the immediate reactivation of municipal service machinery and street paving operations.

Meanwhile, on November 12, Parliament’s Finance Committee convened an oversight session to audit Basra’s withheld petrodollar dues and border-crossing revenue shares, pledging to establish a clear funding roadmap prioritizing strategic development projects across northern Basra districts.

World.title: US dollar approaches 170,000 dinars across Baghdad and Basra markets
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar continued its incremental climb across major domestic parallel markets on Thursday morning, November 12, 2026, nudging closer to the psychological 170,000 IQD ceiling in Baghdad and Basra after stabilizing near 167,000 IQD per $100 throughout the previous week.

According to morning monitoring figures across primary commercial hubs, physical cash rates traded as follows:

Baghdad: Currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 169,500 IQD against buying offers of 168,000 IQD per $100.

Erbil: Currency desks recorded slightly softer retail sales at 169,200 IQD, with purchasing bids holding firmer at 169,000 IQD per $100.

Basra: Foreign exchange offices matched the capital’s pricing spread, quoting selling rates at 169,500 IQD and buying offers at 168,000 IQD per $100.

This upward pressure widens the spread between secondary physical cash markets and the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official cash rate—fixed at 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar) since October 7, 2026.

The divergence reflects ongoing friction between formal customs/tariff disclosures and informal trade financing, keeping physical greenback demand elevated outside official electronic transfer channels.

World.title: Crude oil from northern Iraq smuggled to Iran, Afghanistan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Crude oil and major petroleum products are being smuggled from the Kirkuk and Sulaymaniyah fields into Iran via the Bashmaq and Parviz Khan border crossings, according to an Iraqi intelligence investigation.

After being mixed and repackaged to avoid international sanctions, the illicit oil eventually finds its way to markets in Afghanistan and Iran.

According to intelligence findings reported by Al Arabiya News, the network uses what investigators call the “eastern route.”

Operators use official papers to secure oil quotas assigned to areas in Sulaymaniyah before diverting some of the supply to smuggling networks.

Crude oil and main derivatives are transported to the Iranian border by small and medium-sized tanker trucks. The supplies enter Iran through Iraqi Kurdistan’s Bashmaq and Parviz Khan border crossings.

The smuggled Iraqi oil is processed and combined with Iranian petroleum products at small refineries once it enters Iran.

The mixed gasoline is sold under false origin certificates to get over international restrictions, with Afghanistan being the main destination for the re-exported products.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi established a multi-agency investigating group to confront larger oil smuggling networks.

Iraq’s Federal Commission of Integrity opened an investigation targeting the oil smuggling network.

World.title: Indians top again: 9.3L get OECD citizenships in 5 years
World.content:
Indians continue to top the list of people acquiring citizenship in advanced economies, with around 9.25 lakh Indian citizens acquiring the nationality of an OECD member country between 2020 and 2024, according to the 'International Migration Outlook - 2026' report released on Thursday by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), reports Lubna Kably.

The figure marks a sharp increase of 41% from just over 6.5 lakh Indians who acquired citizenship of OECD member countries during 2015-2019. India remains the largest country of former nationality among those acquiring citizenship in OECD member countries, ahead of Syria and Mexico.

OECD countries took nearly 87L new citizens during 2020-2024

India remains ahead of Syria and Mexico. whose nationals accounted for around 5.9 lakh citizenships in OECD countries each during the five-year period 2020â2024.



Interestingly, while China was the sixth largest source country whose nationals acquired OECD member country citizenship, the numbers fell by nearly 12% to 3.4 lakh in 2020-24 as compared to the previous five-year period. OECD comprises 38 member countries â notably US, UK, European nations, Australia, Canada, Japan and South Korea.

According to additional data shared with TOI, during 2020-2024, OECD member countries embraced nearly 87 lakh new citizens â Indians constitute around 10% of its new citizens.





In the previous five-year period, nearly 65 lakh individuals acquired citizenship of an OECD member country â once again the composition of Indians was 10%.

OECD also shared year-on-year India-specific data with TOI, showing that 2.3 lakh Indians acquired citizenship of OECD member countries in 2024, mainly in Canada (87,320), US (48,820) and Australia (28,969). In 2023, the overall India-figure was marginally lower at nearly 2.2 lakh, with the same three countries accounting for most of the citizenship acquisitions.

The latest figures underline the growing permanence of Indian migration to advanced economies. While immigration flows measure the number of people moving to another country, citizenship acquisitions offer an indication of how many immigrants have progressed to acquiring the nationality of their destination country.

Indians also continued to move to OECD member countries for work and study, although the pace of migration slowed.

India remained the largest origin country of new migrants to OECD member countries in 2024. However, the number of Indian-origin migrants moving to OECD member countries fell by 19% in 2024, from 6.1 lakh in 2023 to 4.9 lakh in 2024.

âMigration remains high, and immigrants now account for 16% of employment across the OECD,â Mathias Cormann, OECD secretary-general said. âWith ageing populations and slower productivity growth, countries cannot afford to waste the skills migrants bring.

That means helping migrants move into jobs where they can contribute most, and giving immigrant entrepreneurs better access to finance, networks and business support,â he added.

One in five STEM graduates across OECD member countries is foreign-born, and immigrants are over-represented among researchers and founders of innovative firms. Yet immigrants are also more likely to work in lower-productivity sectors, with their skills often underutilised, states OECD. The report finds that immigrantâs contribution to productivity depends on how effectively countries make use of their skills â many countries have expanded programmes to attract highly skilled workers.

The gap between Indian and Chinese students studying in OECD member countries narrowed, with 8.3 lakh Indian students and 8.5 lakh Chinese students studying in these countries.

World.title: Rajasthan SSR draft counts 1  1  L more voters than SIR list
World.content:
JAIPUR: Rajasthan's latest draft electoral roll, published Thursday under the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027, has produced a fresh numbers puzzle. It records about 5.26 crore voters - about 11 lakh more than the 5.15 crore in the final Special Intensive Revision (SIR) roll published in Feb.

But the number is still far below another official figure in circulation: State Election Commission's final electoral roll, which stood at 5.45 crore voters in early Oct.

That leaves Rajasthan with three voter counts in less than a year - 5.15 crore in the final SIR roll, 5.45 crore in the SEC roll, and now 5.26 crore in the ECI-linked SSR draft. The latest figure sits between the two, but does not settle the central question: why official rolls for the same state show such wide variation.



According to Chief Electoral Officer Naveen Mahajan, the SSR draft has 2,75,24,780 male voters, 2,51,42,052 female voters and 584 transgender voters.

The qualifying date for the revision is Jan 1, 2027. EC has opened claims and objections from Nov 12 to Dec 11. The final roll will be published on Jan 4, 2027.

The difference between SIR and SSR is critical to understanding the numbers. SIR is a deeper verification exercise in which booth-level officers conduct house-to-house enumeration.





Existing voters are given pre-filled forms and are required to submit them for their names to be considered in the revised roll.

SSR begins with the last published final roll. Existing voters are generally carried forward and not required to prove eligibility afresh merely to retain their names. The exercise is meant to update the roll through additions, deletions and corrections.

Changes in Raj rolls can be sought till Jan

This difference in method explains why a draft SSR roll may not mirror a final SIR roll.

But the wider problem is the coexistence of sharply different official numbers. The SSR draft is around 11 lakh higher than the final SIR roll, yet around 18 lakh lower than the SECâs early-Oct roll.

The draft rolls have been shared with recognised political parties and uploaded on the CEO website. Voters can seek inclusion, deletion or correction through the prescribed forms before the final roll is frozen in January.

World.title: Kashmiri wazas stir Valley pot with 10 pm wazwan deadline, politics takes back seat
World.content:
Kashmiri wazas stir Valley pot with 10 pm wazwan deadline, politics takes back seat

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: At the end of the marriage season, wedding chefs, called wazas in Kashmir, have created a storm in the Valley by announcing that they will stop serving wazwan, the traditional multi-course Kashmiri meal, after 10 pm in an attempt to curb increasingly late-night wedding feasts. The decision is being widely debated on social media in Kashmir and politics, it appears, has taken a backseat for the moment.The dinner deadline will take effect from the next marriage season, which begins in May, according to All Kashmir Waza Association president Ghulam Nabi Baba. Under the new proposed arrangement, Baba said lunch wazwan would be served at 2 pm and dinner at around 10 pm. He said members who fail to follow the associationâs rules would be removed.Baba said the decision was taken at an association meeting at Rajouri Kadal, in Srinagarâs old city, on Wednesday in response to the growing trend of delayed groom arrivals at wedding venues. Some grooms, he said, reach the brideâs home as late as 3 or 4 am, when they should be having a feast much before 10 pm.âFrom next season, starting in May, this will not be tolerated,â Baba told TOI. With the changing security situation in the Valley, late-night weddings have become the norm, but the wazas are not happy about it.They have their reasons. Baba said serving wazwan past midnight creates problems as younger people are reluctant to join the profession, presuming it more demanding, while labourers hired for the day are unwilling to work through the night after remaining on duty for long hours.Baba said the timing decision would be implemented through the association, which is 60 years old and has chefs from across the Valley as members. âOur association is registered and has at least 40,000 members,â he said. âWe will introduce an agreement that the groomâs or brideâs family hiring us will have to sign,â he said.In South Kashmir, Nazir Ahmad Waza said the delays were affecting the livelihoods of chefs and their ability to manage bookings. âThe lack of fixed timings is affecting our business. We are unable to commit to dates due to delays. The delays are hitting everyone hard â customers and guests who come to enjoy the feast,â he said.The associationâs announcement has prompted wider social media debate. âI have a request for the Waza Association. Please do not accept processed spices, cockscomb, garlic paste, colourants or powdered milk. Give us the original wazwan we once cherished and do not make more than seven dishes,â reads a post on Facebook.âRestricting the timing of wazwan functions and ensuring that they do not continue beyond reasonable hours is certainly a need of societyâ¦ But there is another equally important issue: Who is monitoring the rates charged by wazas?â read another post.One social media post accusing them of experimenting with more mutton dishes and making a marriage feast a costly affair shows mutton dishes prepared in grenade and AK-47 shapes in response to Babaâs deadline statement. Baba said the association will encourage its members to follow the traditional seven-course meal.

World.title: TNPDCL seeks nod to procure 3,000 MW
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited (TNPDCL) has increased the quantum of its proposed power procurement from 1,500 megawatt (MW) to 3,000 MW through a medium-term tender agreement.

The TNPDCL, which submitted the proposal to procure 1,500 MW to the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission (TNERC) in February this year, has now doubled the quantum.

A senior TNPDCL official said amid a power demand of about 19,000 MW and an extended summer, it has been proposed to buy 3,000 MW of round-the-clock (RTC) power for five years, under the Finance, Operate and Own guidelines.

TNERC will take up the application for medium-term power purchase, along with requests for deviation from the guidelines and permission to float a short-term tender to procure RTC and peak-hour power for the period from February to July next year.

TNPDCL submitted in its application that the annual power demand had increased to 22,000 MW from an average of 18,000 MW due to various factors, including changes in weather pattern, increasing migrant population, and a surge in electric vehicle sales, with the State set to face an energy shortage of 7,000 MW by 2029-30.

The senior official said the long-term power purchase agreements signed for a quantum of 2,830 MW would expire by 2028-29, prompting new procurement plans.

The estimated cost of the medium-term procurement is around ₹5.50 per kilo watt per hour, with the annual expenditure pegged at ₹6,150 crore.

When the State faced a power shortage this October, TNPDCL had to purchase power at a cost of ₹30 per unit to bridge the peak-hour gap.

World.title: Yemen’s Houthis say they targeted Saudi East-West pipeline, port city of Yanbu
World.content:
Yemen's Houthis said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that their forces targeted Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and an oil facility in the port city of Yanbu on the Red Sea.

The pipeline, which ends at Yanbu, has become increasingly important to the world's largest crude exporter, allowing it to get its oil to market after Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula at the outset of the West Asia war.

Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said in a post on X that one operation "targeted Pumping Station No. 7 on the East-West Pipeline using a drone", while a second "targeted the Yanbu oil facility using a ballistic missile".

He claimed both attacks — as well as two others launched at a Saudi airport and an airbase not far from the Yemeni border — had been successful.

The Houthis have repeatedly targeted the East-West pipeline, and on Monday (November 9, 2026) Saudi Arabia said an attack on the conduit had sparked a fire but had not affected operations.

Saree also said the Houthis had attacked state-run oil company Saudi Aramco in Riyadh with a drone, though there were no immediate reports of damage.

A skyscraper belonging to the oil giant was hit on Sunday (November 8, 2026) by what authorities described as falling shrapnel from an "attempted attack".

The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis announced on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night of having intercepted a drone in the Riyadh area.

It previously said it had knocked down several other missiles and drones from Wednesday (November 11, 2026) night through Thursday (November 12, 2026) morning, though it was unclear whether they were the ones mentioned by the Iran-backed group.

On Thursday (November 12, 2026) morning, the coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, said it had intercepted a drone in the Riyadh region and another in Saudi Arabia's east.

It also said on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) night that it had destroyed two ballistic missiles targeting western Saudi Arabia.

Two more drones were destroyed in the country's south and the region around the holy city of Mecca, it added late Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

According to the Saudi civil defence, missile debris fell in the village of Sabouha, about 35 km from Mecca.

Since fighting resumed in July, Saudi Arabia has come under regular fire from the Houthis, who have attacked airports, energy infrastructure, military sites and Riyadh's financial district.

But the Houthis have repeatedly denied targeting the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.

World.title: Widespread outage hits Microsoft apps
World.content:
A widespread outage hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Thursday (November 12, 2026), with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts and other errors across the tech giant's suite of apps.

Nearly 1,30,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook just after 1 p.m. ET. New reports have since fallen from that peak, but many said they couldn’t send and receive emails, or had trouble loading their inboxes altogether.

Thousands also reported issues with Microsoft’s workplace messaging app Teams, as well as its AI assistant Copilot and wider Microsoft 365 services.

Microsoft said that it was investigating disruptions, notably related to its email and Teams applications.

In updates posted on social media, Redmond, Washington-based Microsoft said it was aware of users “experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas.”

Microsoft later explained that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” — which it said was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors.” The company determined a number of servers were “unexpectedly unavailable” due to a problem that caused them to fail during automated checks.

Microsoft did not immediately provide more information around what might be causing that failure, but added that it was testing a fix.

“We’re aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact,” the Microsoft 365 Status account wrote on X.

Earlier in the day, the company said it had “successfully restored” problems related to Microsoft Teams in North America, although some users continued to report connectivity issues.

World.title: Five held for kidnapping, assaulting youth in Keralam’s Tirur
World.content:
Five people, including three women, were arrested for allegedly kidnapping and assaulting a youth from Pattambi after plotting to end his relationship with one of the women.

The arrested were Safana, 19, from Pattambi, Nadia, 20, and Rabeeba, 25, both from Annara, Tirur, and their male friends Irshad, 28, and Azharudheen, 25, both from Paravanna. The police arrested them from Thazhepalam, Tirur.

The police said Irshad and Azharudheen had faced action under the Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act (KAAPA) and were involved in several criminal cases, including drug trafficking, attempted murder and assault.

The five were produced before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court at Tirur and remanded in judicial custody.

World.title: Three of Malappuram family killed in Fujairah road crash
World.content:
Three members of a family from Kunnumpuram near Kondotty in Malappuram district, including a three-year-old child, were killed in a road crash in Fujairah, UAE, on Wednesday night.

The deceased were identified as Mohammed Asmil, 21, his twin sister Misna Jubin, 21, and her three-year-old son Mohammed Faiz.

The accident occurred on Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Street near the entrance to the Emirate of Fujairah. According to preliminary reports, a truck that went out of control rammed several vehicles, triggering a massive pile-up.

A few others were also reported to have been killed in the accident.

World.title: Karnataka to write to Prime Minister asking for inclusion of enhanced quota in Ninth Schedule
World.content:
After the High Court of Karnataka quashed the Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Seats in Educational Institutions and of Appointments or Posts in the Services under the State) Act, 2022, the State government will write to Prime Minister Narendra Modi to include the enhanced reservation for SCs and STs in the 9th Schedule of the Constitution.

“A letter will be sent to the Prime Minister in this regard. If a meeting with the Prime Minister is possible, this matter will be discussed,” Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar told presspersons after chairing the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Development Council meeting on Thursday.

“The matter came up for discussion during a meeting of legislators and Ministers from the SC and ST communities,” said the Chief Minister.

On the Special Leave Petition filed in the Supreme Court against the Karnataka High Court order, he said the responsibility of deciding who should argue on behalf of the State in this legal battle and monitoring the case has been given to Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara, Ministers Satish Jarkiholi, and K.H. Muniyappa. “We are confident of getting justice in the Supreme Court,” he said.

Social audit on impact

He also said that a vision group would be constituted to decide on the contours of new programmes to be implemented for the welfare of the communities. The Chief Minister said that a Cabinet sub-committee has been formed under the leadership of Mr. Parameshwara and preparations are under way to implement the programmes announced in the party manifesto.

“Our leaders have pointed out that certain schemes are overlapping. It has been decided to get a social audit conducted by reputed institutions to study the impact of grants provided through SCSP/ TSP programmes,” he said.

Following suggestions by legislators and Ministers from these communities on new schemes and ideas at a meeting with the Chief Minister on Thursday, deliberations will be held under the chairmanship of Mr. Parameshwara for two days. Discussions will be held with the Finance Department on whether any changes can be made before submitting a report to the government.

“It is our government’s intention that ₹44,631 crore allocated for SCSP/ TSP scheme should reach the beneficiaries. The government has also decided to hold a convention of SCs and STs to inform people about the promises we made before the elections and what has been fulfilled. The leaders will decide on the venue,” Mr. Shivakumar said.

Pending Central grants

The State government will also write to the Centre, requesting release of ₹1,937 crore that is pending for 2025-2026 under Centrally-sponsored schemes. Of the total Central share of ₹3,497 crore, the State has received ₹1,560 crore. While the Centre did not release grants, the State had also not released grants, resulting in a setback in implementation of several schemes. The Finance Department has now been asked to release the grants irrespective of grants received from the Centre.

New look school uniforms

Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Thursday said that the government has instructed the Education Department to provide new look to hostels and school uniforms. “We implement these from next year. Let the government school children wear good uniforms just like those in private schools. If that requires a little extra money, we will provide it,” he said.

World.title: Private passenger ship service between Beypore and Lakshadweep soon
World.content:
A private passenger ship service between Beypore and Lakshadweep is set to commence operations following the arrival of the vessel Theja at the Beypore port on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

The initiative aims to restore maritime connectivity that has faced prolonged interruptions. As part of the trial, the ship, capable of accommodating 250 passengers, anchored safely at the port wharf in the morning. Official clearance procedures and regulatory approvals are in progress, with the maiden commercial run anticipated this month.

According to port officials, the initiative aligns with Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan’s ‘Mission Samudra’ development framework, which seeks to leverage Keralam’s extensive coastline and port infrastructure to catalyse new economic and commercial prospects. Representatives of the operating company had recently met the Chief Minister to brief him about the project’s progress and strategic importance, they said.

Stakeholders noted that beyond streamlining passenger transit, the service would give a fresh momentum for maritime tourism at the historically significant Beypore port, while strengthening socio-economic and commercial ties between Keralam and the archipelago.

World.title: Kin convicted for raping minor
World.content:
The Special Court trying offences booked under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO), Thodupuzha, convicted a close relative of a minor girl for 30 years’ imprisonment, besides imposing a fine for raping the survivor.

Sessions Judge Ash K. Bal sentenced the 37-year-old accused in the incident which took place in October 2021.

The relative was convicted for trespassing into the minor’s house and raping her. The court also ordered a compensation of ₹5 lakh for the survivor from the victim compensation fund.

Special Public Prosecutor Pious Mathew and Francis Pious and Ancy Philip appeared for the prosecution.

World.title: 11 killed, 2 injured as passenger van plunges into river in GB's Ghizer: police
World.content:
GILGIT: Eleven people were killed and two injured when a passenger vehicle plunged into a river in Gilgit-Baltistan’s Ghizer district on Thursday.

According to local police, a passenger van was en route to Ghizer’s Yasin Valley from Gilgit on Thursday evening when the driver lost control near Morkah Bridge, causing the van to plunge into the Yasin river.

Police initially said rescue teams retrieved the bodies of 10 passengers, including two women. They also rescued three injured passengers, including a child, who were taken to the Gupis Civil Hospital for treatment.

In an update, police said the death toll had risen to 11, including an infant, while two were injured.

Police said the deceased and injured were residents of Yasin Valley, adding that an investigation was under way to identify the cause of the incident.

GB Chief Minister Amjad Hussain expressed deep grief and sorrow over the loss of lives in the accident.

He directed the district administration, rescue agencies, and relevant health department officials to ensure the injured were immediately transported to nearby hospitals and to utilise all available resources to provide the best possible medical facilities.

He also instructed the administration to ensure that no negligence occurred during rescue operations, and that the medical treatment and care of the injured were carefully monitored.

Expressing heartfelt condolences and sympathies to the bereaved families, Hussain said the loss of human lives in the tragic accident was “deeply distressing”.

He prayed for eternal peace for the deceased and strength to their families to bear the loss, while hoping for the speedy recovery of the injured.

Three people were killed and 13 others injured in a collision between a coach and a motorcycle in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Dera Ismail Khan on Wednesday, according to Rescue 1122.

Last week, eight people were killed and 30 others injured when a passenger bus travelling from Gilgit to Islamabad collided with a dumper truck near the Havelian Interchange on the Hazara Motorway.

The day before, a collision between a passenger bus and a truck claimed the lives of 11 people and left 33 others injured near Punjab’s Pakpattan.

World.title: 3 terrorists killed, 2 civilians dead as attack on Mastung post repelled: state media
World.content:
Security forces killed three terrorists on the N-25 highway in Balochistan’s Mastung district while repelling an attack on Kandawa Post, state broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported on Thursday, citing police.

According to a spokesperson for Balochistan Police, terrorists belonging to Fitna al Hindustan attempted a “cowardly attack at Kandawa Post on National Highway N-25 using an explosives-laden vehicle”.

The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

Security forces repulsed the attack through timely and effective action, the police statement said.

However, two civilians lost their lives in the incident, while at least 13 others were injured, according to a list of names in the police statement.

Three Frontier Corps personnel were also injured in the incident, the statement added. “The explosion caused damage to nearby houses and a mosque.”

In the ensuing retaliatory operation, three terrorists were killed, the police said.

The injured people were taken to medical centres for treatment.

“The attack demonstrates that these terrorists have no connection with the people of Balochistan,” the police stressed.

“Operations against elements seeking to undermine peace, development, and prosperity in Balochistan will continue, and the protection of the lives and property of the people will be ensured under all circumstances,” it affirmed.

Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist activities in recent years, prompting security forces to intensify counter-terrorism operations.

Earlier this month, a soldier was martyred and 17 terrorists were killed in two intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan’s Kachhi and Kharan districts, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.

In early October, security forces killed five terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan in Mastung, Pakistan TV reported.

Pakistan witnessed a significant improvement in several key security indicators during October, with terrorist attacks declining by 37 per cent compared with September, according to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS).

Balochistan recorded one of the most significant improvements, with terrorist attacks declining by 46pc, from 132 in September to 71 in October.

World.title: Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO after reports of extramarital affairs
World.content:
Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday, ending his 33-year run at the helm of the AI giant he co-founded after revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China.

The company’s board said Huang had stepped down as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while keeping her finance role, and the board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent replacement.

It named former Synopsys CEO and board member Harvey Jones as its first-ever board chairman.

Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump said that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should replace Huang at Nvidia.

“Now that Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump, who was close to Huang, said on his Truth Social network.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and is its fourth-largest investor with a stake of about 3.61 per cent, will exit the board as well.

Nvidia shares fell more than 10pc in premarket trading, and weighed on the broader market.

Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing.

Nvidia’s board met on Wednesday to consider his ouster, a person familiar with the matter said, after reports earlier in the day that Huang also had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him.

Huang’s exit plunges the $4 trillion company into uncertainty and threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped bankroll by pouring Nvidia’s swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry’s biggest labs.

“The risk is not that Nvidia suddenly loses its technology roadmap … that roadmap is largely visible for the next several years. The risk is execution. Jensen has been the chief conductor of an extraordinarily complex system,” said Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments.

“In a world with real bottlenecks, that coordination is a competitive advantage in itself.”

Investor sentiment toward AI stocks has already been shaky as soaring cash burn and rising debt at traditionally cash-rich tech giants fuel doubts over whether the AI boom will pay off.

The departure could also have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy, given Huang’s push to preserve access to the Chinese market and his close ties with US President Donald Trump.

Trump said on Sunday that Huang had “done an amazing job for our country” and that the Nvidia chief had told him he had no idea the Chinese woman he had an affair with was a spy.

Huang’s rockstar status

For years, Nvidia was best known to gamers chasing top-tier graphics. But its chips’ ability to perform many calculations at once has made them the oil of the AI boom and a strategic prize in the US-China race to dominate the technology. It also made Nvidia the world’s most valuable company.

That turned Huang into a rockstar CEO, mobbed by fans in Taiwan and South Korea who ask him to sign books, posters and sometimes even their bodies. Such is his pull that stocks moved at his mere mention of company names at events.

But scrutiny of his conduct has intensified in recent days after reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed, who US authorities have concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset.

The two, who have been photographed together in Taiwan, Singapore and California, are not related.

Washington has also investigated Megaspeed, a coveted official Nvidia cloud partner with priority access to its chips, over suspicions it helped China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls, according to media reports. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy.

Earlier this month, Nvidia’s board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time.

The controversy escalated on Wednesday when the New York Times reported Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reported to him.

World.title: Imran's key message from jail is to 'stick firmly to the ideology': PTI secretary general
World.content:
Incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan wants his party leaders to “stick firmly to the ideology” of the party, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said on Thursday.

Following the Islamabad High Court’s order to jail authorities to facilitate meetings for legal consultation, lawyers Barrister Salman Safdar and Advocate Latif Khosa were able to meet Imran and his wife, Bushra Bibi, at the Adiala jail on Wednesday.

According to both lawyers, the meeting lasted at least three hours and mainly focused on the couple’s legal and health issues. However, they did not divulge further details; the government often objects to lawyers using such meetings to make political statements.

Speaking on Geo News programme ‘Capital Talk’ on Thursday, Raja said that he had multiple detailed conversations with Barrister Safdar following the latter’s meeting with Imran.

“Imran Khan’s fundamental message was to stick firmly to the ideology,” the PTI secretary general said, conveying details he heard from Safdar.

“I have also been directed to stick to [our] ideology,” Raja added, noting that Imran’s “fundamental message is not to bow”.

He further said Imran reiterated his support for National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, whom the PTI founder had picked for their respective roles.

He quoted Imran as saying that Achakzai and Abbas were not individuals who would “bow down or be sold”, and he had nominated them after deep contemplation.

“Imran Khan sahib’s directives will be acted upon,” the PTI secretary general declared.

He added that Imran had also issued instructions on the issue of the formation of new provinces during his meetings with Safdar, including the one on Nov 2.

“Imran Khan is not ready to step back from his ideology of democracy and public welfare […] the rule of the people is the foremost priority of Imran Khan,” Raja stated.

He said that Imran considered concerns related to his well-being as unnecessary; however, the party was concerned about his health, as Imran’s blood pressure was not stable.

Raja claimed that Imran had also reported in yesterday’s meeting about his blood pressure “reaching 193 on Saturday”.

Asked whether this message could be considered political and thereby hinder chances of future jail meetings, Raja contended that although a handful of matters were discussed during the three-hour-long huddle, everything was monitored and recorded via microphones.

He noted that Khosa, who was also an MNA, has made several statements after the meeting, which “compelled Safdar to clarify matters”.

Regarding himself, the PTI secretary general said Imran had issued instructions to him regarding standing with the principles and reorganisation of the party.

He acknowledged that there was a small faction in the PTI which is displeased with him. However, he emphasised that Imran’s directives conveyed to him were different.

“Imran Khan’s message for me is to create space while upholding the principles and move forward,” Raja said, denying other notions coming from different circles within the PTI.

Regarding directives issued by Imran on a possible 28th constitutional amendment, the PTI secretary general said he would put this matter before the party leadership first.

The directions were related to standing with democratic principles and the rights of small provinces, he said, adding that the PTI founder had always supported the creation of new administrative units.

However, Raja noted that there had been some concerns related to the “context” behind the formation of new administrative units and stressed the importance of the public’s opinion.

Imran’s meeting not linked to 28th amendment: Sanaullah

Meanwhile, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah denied speculation that Imran’s meeting with his lawyers was linked to the process of introducing a 28th constitutional amendment.

“This was just a simple meeting between lawyers who agreed to present an argument in court and enable it to decide on an appeal,” he told Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada ke Saath’, noting that people have been trying to link the meeting to the 28th amendment or other matters.

The PM’s aide explained that Safdar and Khosa did not present their arguments before the IHC, contending that they could not do so without meeting their clients.

“The IHC chief justice said that if they promised to argue the case, he would arrange a meeting. As a result of the commitment, the meeting was permitted and both of them were able to meet [Imran and Bushra],” Sanaullah said.

“This political theory that the meeting was held to discuss the 28th Amendment is completely incorrect; there is no such thing,” the PML-N leader maintained.

He was then asked about the government’s knowledge of the matter, considering the lengthy meeting allowed Imran to discuss political issues with his lawyers.

In response, Sanaullah said officials of the interior ministry were aware of the meeting as it was their domain.

Asked whether there was any “distance” emerging between the government and the “institutions”, the PML-N leader replied, “Distancing from us can never begin, and neither will it.

“There is exemplary coordination between the military and civilian leadership,” he affirmed.

Highlighting Pakistan’s achievements in the diplomatic and military arena, he said: “This situation should remain, and everyone should pray that this situation remains forever.”

World.title: Naqvi suggests referendum as 'solution' to debate on new administrative units
World.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Thursday suggested that political parties hold a referendum to gauge the public’s opinion on the creation of new administrative units or provinces, terming it the “solution” to the ongoing debate.

The security czar has whipped up a political storm over the past few months since he called for the formation of new administrative units in the country, saying the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

Replying to a media query at the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) in Lahore on Thursday, Naqvi noted that each political party had a right to disagree with another party or individual.

At the same time, he observed that all parties stressed democracy and the supremacy of the people. Therefore, he said: “My only request to all political parties is that this is such an issue […] so they should hold a referendum.

“Whatever the public’s opinion in the referendum is; if the public says [new units] should not be created, I am 100 per cent with them that they should not be created. [But], if the public says they should be made, then they should.”

Naqvi noted that political parties had varying stances on the debate, with the PPP “having its own stance [and] some parties having their own stance while not saying anything officially”.

He again stressed that the solution was to take public opinion into account, suggesting that if there was a proposal for a “better solution”, that should also be presented to the people.

Acknowledging the importance of allies in the ruling coalition, he said: “Everyone is a part of this government, and nothing will happen against their will. And if something does happen, then it will be after taking everyone’s consensus.”

“My only recommendation is that if we were to conclude this debate, then we should just take the people’s opinion,” he said.

The minister had also affirmed in September that any new administrative units would only be formed with the public’s consent, while also doubling down on his call for new provinces.

Naqvi claims he and Bilawal ‘nearly on same page’

Responding to another question, Naqvi recalled recent remarks by PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, wherein he had called for a “political reset” and encouraged unity among political parties.

The security czar contended that he and Bilawal were “nearly on the same page”.

“He (Bilawal) said that political matters are about to be reset, while my suggestion is that overall matters are about to be reset,” Naqvi elaborated.

In his remarks on Tuesday, the Bhutto scion had called for a “political reset”, wherein all political parties must unite for the sake of the country, rather than indulge in “unnecessary debates”.

His call for political unity followed exchanges of harsh remarks in recent weeks between federal ministers and veteran politician Maulana Fazlur Rehman, who has now decided to strengthen his ties with the opposition.

The PPP chairman also questioned the need for “new experiments” when the country was confronted with much bigger challenges, particularly the economic crisis arising from the Middle East tensions.

The same day, PPP’s Punjab chapter also strongly rejected any move towards the creation of new provinces, asserting that doing so will neither address soaring inflation nor rampant unemployment.

While Naqvi said he and Bilawal largely shared the same views, the PPP chairman in September had called for a parliamentary debate on the creation of new provinces.

“So instead of [speaking at] business forums, Mohsin Naqvi should visit [Parliament],” he had remarked, an apparent reference to the first instance of Naqvi stressing the need for more administrative units while speaking at the Pakistan Economic Summit 2026 in July.

PPP, which rules Sindh and is also an ally of the PML-N government at the Centre, has strongly opposed the creation of a new province within Sindh. It has also maintained that any decision on the subject must be taken through the constitutional and parliamentary processes with political consensus.

Defence Minister Khawaja Asif’s recent statement regarding the creation of 12 more provinces has also added to the debate on administrative units started by Naqvi.

‘Corruption exists across entire Pakistan’

In his talk with reporters, Naqvi was also asked about federal minister Chaudhry Salik’s recent remarks over alleged corruption in Punjab.

In response, he said: “If someone is saying that no corruption is taking place in Pakistan, then apologies but corruption exists across the entire country and it is our responsibility to end it.”

The interior minister stressed the importance of highlighting corruption where it was present.

The conversation on corruption started after PML-Q’s Salik criticised the incumbent Punjab government led by PML-N, alleging that he regularly heard complaints of corruption.

Incensed by his remarks, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz sent a Rs5 billion defamation notice to Salik for levelling allegations of corruption against her government and demanded that he retract his remarks.

Naqvi was also asked about a Capital Development Authority (CDA) notice issued in relation to the residence of the JUI-F chief, which he defended, stating, “This (CDA) campaign has been ongoing for months, and it is not against a certain individual.”

World.title: High-speed diesel price dips by Rs4 per litre, petrol by Rs3
World.content:
The government on Thursday reduced the price of petrol by Rs3 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4, marking the eighth consecutive decrease.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs332 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs360 on Nov 13 (Friday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Oil prices edged higher on Thursday after earlier losses, as persistent geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and Russia offset pressure from rising crude output.

Brent futures were up 65 cents at $93.40 a barrel at 7:25pm PKT. US West Texas Intermediate crude was up 1 cent to $86.54; both contracts fell more than $1 per barrel in early Asian trading. They were also headed for a weekly fall.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17 , the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

Additional input from AFP

World.title: Canadian mining company signs MoU with Mari Energies in South Asia push
World.content:
Ivanhoe Mines signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Mari Energies on Thursday, the Canadian company’s chairman Robert Friedland said on the sidelines of the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum.

Friedland said Ivanhoe is in the early stages of setting up a local office in Pakistan and will sign another MoU on Friday.

Mari Energies’ mining unit, Mari Minerals, has multiple mineral exploration projects, including copper and gold in Pakistan.

The partnership marks the Canadian miner’s entry into South Asia, expanding its presence beyond its major mineral projects in southern Africa.

“We’re excited to be here in Pakistan,” Friedland said.

‘Significant evidence’ of placer gold in Punjab rivers, says CM Maryam

At the forum, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz said that there was “significant evidence” of “sufficient quantities” of placer gold flowing in the province’s five rivers.

Maryam said Punjab was the land of five rivers and that gold was “literally flowing” in all five, particularly in the areas of Mianwali and Attock.

Describing Pakistan as a “pot of gold”, she said its wealth lay both above and beneath the ground and needed to be explored and converted into tangible wealth.

“The wealth beneath Punjab was never a problem, never a problem, just like the whole of Pakistan, just like all four provinces and the federating units. The chaos above ground was the actual problem,” she said.

Maryam said the provincial mines and minerals department’s revenue stood at around Rs10 billion two and a half years ago but had since increased to Rs40bn.

“And it is just the beginning,” she added.

She also highlighted the province’s iron ore reserves, saying Chiniot had 261.5 million tonnes of iron ore.

She said the provincial government was taking steps to facilitate investment in the mining sector and create an enabling environment for investors.

The Punjab chief minister said her role as chief executive of the country’s most populous province was to facilitate investors and create an enabling environment by eliminating red tape, bureaucratic delays and unnecessary hurdles.

The provincial government was offering one-window facilitation to ensure investors did not have to run from pillar to post to complete the necessary procedures, she added.

Maryam said the government was also making substantial capital investments to reduce investors’ capital expenditure and prevent them from having to tie up funds in purchasing expensive land.

Additionally, the government was offering concessional financing of up to Rs5 billion and would provide solar-powered energy solutions to investors to help offset high energy and fuel costs.

Dar says provincial partnership vital for mineral development

Dar said Pakistan’s constitutional framework made provincial partnership indispensable, adding that the provinces were essential partners in the national undertaking and that their constitutional authority and ownership of mineral resources must be respected.

Addressing the event, he said the federal government was working alongside provincial governments and their leadership through national coordination, investment facilitation, policy alignment and international engagement.

Dar said Pakistan’s mineral resources were central to the next phase of the country’s economic transformation, stressing the need to diversify exports, strengthen the industrial base and attract long-term investment.

He said Pakistan possessed substantial and diverse mineral resources, including significant copper and gold potential along the Tethyan metallogenic belt in the west of the country. The country also had deposits of iron ore, chromite, lead, zinc, coal, rock salt, marble, gypsum, gemstones and other industrial minerals.

The deputy PM said the Reko Diq copper-gold project in Balochistan demonstrated the potential of international expertise, national participation and provincial ownership in attracting major long-term investment.

He stressed that Pakistan’s ambition should extend beyond extracting minerals and exporting them in raw form, saying the country needed to develop the capacity to process and refine them, as well as manufacture mineral-based products domestically.

Dar said Balochistan was central to Pakistan’s mineral future, adding that the development of its resources should contribute meaningfully to the provincial economy and the well-being of its people.

He also emphasised the importance of local employment, skills development and the participation of Pakistani companies, saying local communities must be active participants in and beneficiaries of mineral development.

The deputy prime minister further stated that environmental protection, workers’ safety and the rehabilitation of mining sites were essential to a successful minerals industry.

The Reko Diq copper-gold project in Balochistan is one of Pakistan’s most ambitious mining ventures, with significant potential to boost the country’s mineral wealth through the extraction of gold and copper.

Designed as an open-pit mining and processing operation, the project will initially process 45 million tonnes of ore annually, with capacity expected to double to 90m tonnes after the completion of Phase 2.

The mine has an estimated operational life of 37 years, which could potentially extend to 80 years through further exploration and resource development.

World.title: CEC Raja alleges federal govt wants to 'sabotage' Islamabad local govt polls
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Sikandar Sultan Raja on Thursday accused the federal government of trying to sabotage the local government elections in Islamabad, clarifying that the polls would be held as scheduled.

The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has scheduled the polls for Dec 20. The last LG term expired in Feb 2021, and the ECP was supposed to conduct elections within 120 days. However, the federal government and the ECP spent the last several years carrying out delimitations and announcing election schedules, only to postpone the polls later.

On Thursday, a three-member bench headed by the CEC heard the case about alleged violations of the electoral code in the NA-77 by-election.
