World.title: More Chinese Regions to Require Autumn and Spring School Breaks
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019236/More Chinese Regions to Require Autumn and Spring School Breaks
World.content:
More Chinese regions are implementing autumn and spring breaks in compulsory education, expanding a decadelong national initiative. Some have also waived fees for students on break and rolled out support measures to help parents take leave at the same time as their children.

Spring and autumn holidays across all compulsory education schools have been rolled out provincewide in at least 15 provinces, as well as numerous cities in other provinces, such as the southern megacity of Shenzhen, domestic media reported last week. In China, compulsory education lasts nine years, encompassing primary and middle school. Breaks will occur in November and April for four to five days each.

The reform dates back to 2004, when Hangzhou, capital of the eastern province of Zhejiang, piloted the breaks. In 2013, the initiative expanded nationally when the State Council issued an announcement encouraging local governments to adopt it, and the rollout accelerated again in 2025 when central authorities urged more schools to implement the holidays.

Chu Zhaohui, a researcher at the China National Academy of Educational Sciences, told domestic media outlet Red Star News that the holidays actually boost learning.

“Learning isn’t confined to schools or taught only by teachers and parents,” Chu said, adding that the holidays give students space for self-exploration.

At the same time as introducing spring and autumn holiday policies, many cities have also added supporting measures so parents can sync their leave. In October, Longnan city in the northwestern Gansu province encouraged employers to implement paid leave and prioritize compensatory rest for employees with school-age children, aligning staff leave with school holidays.

Foshan, a city in the southern Guangdong province, also issued a proposal on Nov. 3 calling on employers to prioritize arranging leave for employees with children during the autumn holiday. The city’s five-day autumn break begins Nov. 11.

Many tourist spots are also waiving entrance fees for children during the upcoming fall break. In the eastern city of Wuxi, a theme park dropped entry fees for students 16 and under throughout November; 15 top tourism sites in Huangshan in the eastern Anhui province, a city known for its mountain of the same name, are now entry-free for children under 18; and the Dujiangyan scenic area in the southwestern Sichuan province waived fees for primary and middle school students between Nov. 12 and 16.

The breaks have significantly boosted travel demand, according to online travel booking platform Qunar. Data from Qunar revealed that in November, air ticket bookings for children 12 and under increased 1.6 times year on year, while parent bookings rose by 50%.

Wang Qiyan, director of the Leisure Economy Research Center at Renmin University, told Red Star News that spring and autumn breaks “enable off-peak travel, avoiding the packed scenic spots of winter and summer vacations.



Editor: Marianne Gunnarsson.

(Header image: Tourists take photos of St. Sophia Square during the autumn break in Harbin, Heilongjiang province, Nov. 4, 2026. VCG)

World.title: World leaders set out clashing priorities as COP31 turns to negotiations
World.content:
LIGHTS ON. A drone light show displays the COP31 logo during the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, on November 11, 2026.

Developing countries reiterate requests that they have made during many years of UN talks for rich countries to provide more finance to help them shift to cleaner energy, adapt to a warming world, and repair climate-driven destruction

ANTALYA, Turkey – World leaders have set out competing positions and made clashing demands in two days of intense speech-making at the COP31 climate change talks in Turkey, leaving negotiators with a tough task to draft a meaningful deal that all can agree.

Small island states, among the most vulnerable in the world as global warming makes sea levels rise, pleaded for urgent cuts to greenhouse gas emissions.

European leaders, meanwhile, lined up behind a proposal to expand global electrification, developing countries asked for more finance from rich ones, and fossil fuel producers said oil, gas, and coal should continue to be used.

“We reaffirm our sovereign right to strengthen our energy and oil industry as a driver of our national development,” Venezuela’s acting President Delcy Rodriguez told the conference, after UN leaders had made the case for bringing to an end the age of fossil fuel.

Apart from trying to accommodate incompatible national positions aired on Wednesday, November 11 and Thursday, November 12, conference host Turkey and negotiations lead Australia also have the challenge of trying to make progress when wars and inflation have pushed climate concerns down the political agenda.

“It’s my job to steer consensus, not to bang tables and demand any particular action, but to steer consensus to the strongest, most ambitious possible outcome within the constraints of that consensus-driven process,” Chris Bowen, Australia’s COP31 president of negotiations, told Reuters.

Asked what a good deal might look like, he said: “I have many more hours of consultations with partners to do.”

Climate activists say short-term political concerns should not get in the way of addressing an issue that will get more pressing if ignored.

A UN report last month found the world was already on course to break through the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warming limit that countries had agreed to pursue under the 2015 Paris Agreement to prevent the worst effects of climate change.

“The situation could not be less under control. The planet is not dying. It is being killed,” Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg said on the sidelines of the UN conference.

“It is being killed by the very same people often thought to come to our rescue. No one is coming to our rescue.”

Britain’s Burnham backs renewables

Earlier on Thursday, the leaders of small island states including the Bahamas, Tuvalu, the Solomon Islands and Saint Lucia called for swift action.

“Major emitters must move beyond the usual promises. They must reduce emissions that the climate crisis demands,” said Saint Lucia’s Prime Minister Philip J. Pierre.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham backed a proposal by Turkey to increase electricity’s share of world energy consumption to 35% by 2035, from a little over a fifth now, to help advance that goal. Turkey has not specified whether the extra energy used would be renewable.

Burnham told the conference that energy supply disruptions from the US-Israeli war with Iran and Russia’s war with Ukraine showed clean energy was the wise choice.

“It is now plain for everyone to see that if we depend on energy we do not control, then we leave ourselves exposed to prices we cannot control,” he said. “The shift to clean energy is the only route to energy security.”

Developing countries reiterated requests that they have made during many years of UN talks for rich countries to provide more finance to help them shift to cleaner energy, adapt to a warming world, and repair climate-driven destruction.

Fernanda de Carvalho, the head of climate policy for the World Wildlife Fund environmental group, said he found the leaders’ speeches underwhelming, especially as COP31 is the first UN conference since scientists have publicly said the world is set to breach the 1.5C threshold.

“It is worrying that the climate issue is not as high on the global political agenda as it needs to be,” he said. – Rappler.com

World.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down in big blow to AI boom
World.content:
The departure could also have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy, given Huang's push to preserve access to the Chinese market and his close ties with US President Donald Trump

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down, leaving the AI industry without its biggest champion and clouding the future of the chipmaker he built into an AI powerhouse.

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said on Thursday, November 12. It named former Synopsys CEO and board member Harvey Jones as its first-ever board chairman.

Play Video

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and is its fourth-largest investor with a stake of about 3.61%, will exit the board as well.

Nvidia shares fell more than 10% in premarket trading, and weighed on the broader market.

Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing.

Nvidia’s board met on Wednesday, November 11, to consider his ouster, a person familiar with the matter said, after reports earlier in the day that Huang also had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him.

Huang’s exit plunges the $4 trillion company into uncertainty and threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped bankroll by pouring Nvidia’s swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry’s biggest labs.

“The risk is not that Nvidia suddenly loses its technology roadmap…that roadmap is largely visible for the next several years. The risk is execution. Jensen has been the chief conductor of an extraordinarily complex system,” said Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments.

“In a world with real bottlenecks, that coordination is a competitive advantage in itself.”

Investor sentiment toward AI stocks has already been shaky as soaring cash burn and rising debt at traditionally cash-rich tech giants fuel doubts over whether the AI boom will pay off.

The departure could also have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy, given Huang’s push to preserve access to the Chinese market and his close ties with US President Donald Trump.

Trump said on Sunday, November 8, that Huang had “done an amazing job for our country” and that the Nvidia chief had told him he had no idea the Chinese woman he had an affair with was a spy.

Huang’s rock-star status

For years, Nvidia was best known to gamers chasing top-tier graphics. But its chips’ ability to perform many calculations at once has made them the oil of the AI boom and a strategic prize in the US-China race to dominate the technology. It also made Nvidia the world’s most valuable company.

That turned Huang into a rock-star CEO, mobbed by fans in Taiwan and South Korea who ask him to sign books, posters and sometimes even their bodies. Such is his pull that stocks moved at his mere mention of company names at events.

But scrutiny of his conduct has intensified in recent days after reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed, who US authorities have concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset.

The two, who have been photographed together in Taiwan, Singapore and California, are not related.

Washington has also investigated Megaspeed, a coveted official Nvidia cloud partner with priority access to its chips, over suspicions it helped China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls, according to media reports. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy.

Earlier this month, Nvidia’s board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time.

The controversy escalated on Wednesday when the New York Times reported Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reported to him. – Rappler.com

World.title: Padilla to prosecution: ‘Bakit issue ‘yung pagpunta sa China?’
World.content:
While some senator-judges were frustrated by the “evasive” answers of a defense witness to questions about trips to China, Senator-judge Robin Padilla was puzzled why it was even an issue in the first place.

Padilla expressed his confusion over the matter at the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte. on Thursday, November 12. This was days after the first defense witness, Davao City Assessor Jaime Adalin, irked some senator-judges to the point of contempt warnings, after he evaded, then brushed off, the question of prosecutor Jay Tolosa about a China-sponsored trip just the past year.

Like Adalin, Padilla also did not see the relevance of the question. “Bakit po issue ‘yung pagpunta sa China (Is traveling to China an issue)?” Padilla asked the prosecution.

He shared that he had been to China several times, once with former president Rodrigo Duterte, but he could not recall the names of the places that he visited.

“Di ko rin ma-recall saan ako nagpunta kasi di pumapasok sa isip ko po na ‘yung mga lugar sa China siguro di talagang familiar sa akin. At tinanong ko pa staff ko saan ako nagpunta dahil di ko matandaan. Totoo po ‘yan. Problema po ba ‘yun kung di mo matandaan kung saan ka nagpunta sa China?” Padilla asked prosecutor Terry Ridon.

(I also couldn’t recall where I went because it didn’t enter my mind, the places in China are really not familiar to me. And I asked my staff where I went because I couldn’t remember. That’s true. Is that a problem, if you can’t remember where in China you went to?)

Ridon reiterated the prosecution’s response at the Monday hearing that the queries on Adalin’s foreign travels were made to test his credibility as a witness. He also stressed the issue was not Adalin’s travel to China but his failure to give direct answers about the trips.

“‘Yung pagpunta sa China ay bahagi ng pag-test ng credibility ng witness. Walang usapin kung naging maagap ang testigo sa pagsagot ng tanong patungkol sa biyahe sa China. Wala naman sanang debate kung agad-agad inamin mismo…. Ang issue ‘yung parang di pagiging matapat sa harap ng korte,” Ridon said.

(The questions on the trip to China are part of testing the witness’ credibility. There should have been no issue if the witness immediately responded to the question about the trip to China. There would have been no debate if he admitted it immediately…. The issue is that he did not appear to be honest before the court.)

Play Video

On Monday, Adalin, as Senator-judge Panfilo “Ping” Lacson described it, “almost made a mockery of the court” when he smirked and deemed as “irrelevant” a prosecutor’s question about an alleged all-expenses-paid trip to China in November 2025. After contempt warnings, the Davao City assessor eventually regained his memory and recalled the trip.

At the trial on Thursday, Padilla said witnesses’ responses should be respected, echoing the reminder of Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero at the start of the trial that morning. He called on counsels and the impeachment senator-judges to exercise restraint and give witnesses due consideration when they say they are unable to recall certain details.

Escudero, however, was apparently referring to another witness, Gencorp in-house counsel Suzette Balucanag-Punay, who faced intense grilling from some senator-judges the day before. She had testified that the Vice President received over P2.1 million in “return of capital” from Gencorp between 2022 and 2025 from what she called a “loose investment.” – Rappler.com

World.title: BIR chief Mendoza goes to Customs, DOF usec Ligon is new tax chief
World.content:
The BIR continues to face extortion complaints while the Customs bureau is trying to address port congestion and other issues

MANILA, Philippines – President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. reshuffled the heads of the government’s top two revenue agencies, his third major leadership shakeup of these Department of Finance (DOF) offices since assuming the presidency in mid-2022.

In a statement on Thursday, November 12, Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) Commissioner Charlito Mendoza confirmed that he is moving to the Bureau of Customs (BOC) replacing Commissioner Ariel Nepomuceno.

“I look forward to working with the men and women of the BOC to carry out the priorities of President Marcos Jr. and [Finance] Secretary [Frederick] Go — strengthening border protection, sustaining revenue collection, and facilitating legitimate trade. We have important work ahead of us, and I am ready to get started,” he said.

Mendoza held the top BIR post for a year after Marcos appointed him on November 13, 2025.

The BIR continues to face complaints about corruption. Last September, a Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PCCI) officer testified before a Senate committee on trade, commerce, and entrepreneurship that BIR examiners were still extorting businesses via letters of authority (LOAs) and asking for illicit deals in exchange for tax settlements. Prior to that exposé, the BIR had vowed reforms in the LOA system. (READ: [Ask the Tax Whiz] Why is the BIR auditing your business?)

Finance Undersecretary Rolando Ligon Jr. replaces Mendoza in the BIR. As undersecretary, Ligon supervised the BIR and the Customs bureau. Ligon is the third BIR chief under the Marcos administration. Romeo Lumagui Jr. was Marcos’ first BIR commissioner and served from July 2022 to November 2025.

Ligon, more specifically, was the supervising finance undersecretary that handled the DOF’s Revenue Integrity Protection Service or RIPS. RIPS is officially described as the “anti-corruption arm of the DOF,” which investigates allegations of corruption in the BIR, Customs, and other finance-attached offices. If warranted, RIPS then files charges against erring public servants.

Ligon was a tax lawyer for the Campos, Canobas, Sy, Selva, Ligon & Dato Law from 2018 to 2025, and is a part-time professor for law on taxation at the Lyceum of the Philippines University, according to his LinkedIn account.

PORT CONGESTION. Customs Commissioner Ariel Nepomuceno and other officials join a meeting led by Finance Secretary Frederick Go on addressing port congestion and other stakeholder concerns, on November 11, 2026. Photo courtesy of Department of Finance FB

From the Customs bureau, Nepomuceno will now head the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA), replacing its president and CEO Joshua Bingcang.

Bingcang, an engineer, is moving to the Philippine Export Zone Authority or PEZA, the country’s second largest investment promotion agency, Secretary Go announced on Thursday.

Nepomuceno was appointed Customs chief only in June 2025. This new post marks his third under the Marcos administration. He has been trying to address complaints from the business community about port congestion, which is delaying the release of goods, particulary in the port of Manila.

According to the DOF, among the agreed measures in a meeting this week are the expansion of container-yard capacity and faster withdrawal of overstaying laden containers. The Customs bureau reported that 45% of these containers had been cleared as of Monday, November 9.

Prior to being Customs chief, Nepomuceno served as administrator of the Office of Civil Defense under the Department of National Defense from December 2022 to June 2025. He held various posts in the Customs bureau during the Rodrigo Duterte administration.

The BCDA has been in the news lately as the Marcos administration does the finishing touches to the framework agreement on Pax Silica, expected to be signed by end of 2026, according to a trade senior official. – Rappler.com

World.title: Like a brother? Duterte’s defense witness has close ties to Mans Carpio
World.content:
WITNESS. Atty. Anel Martin Antero takes the witness stand on Day 43 of the impeachment trial of Sara Duterte on November 12, 2026.

'Whether the Vice President and her spouse is leading a modest life. This is central to the allegation of unexplained wealth," says prosecutor Amando Virgil Ligutan

To explain lawyer Mans Carpio’s big purchases, the defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte brought in lawyer Anel Martin Antero to the witness stand on Thursday, November 12.

During his testimony, Antero attributed Carpio’s nearly P200,000 credit card bill in May 2023 to a group meal in Japan.

But instead of dwelling on the explanation, the prosecution used its allotted time for cross-examination to cast doubt on Antero’s credibility. Specifically, the prosecution doubled down on the lawyer’s close ties to the Dutertes.

Prosecutor Amando Virgil Ligutan displayed several of Antero’s social media posts that revealed his pro-Duterte leanings on different issues.

At one point, Ligutan also showed a post where Antero referred to Duterte’s 2026 impeachment complaint as “flimsy.”

After minutes of being in the hot seat, Antero finally admitted his close ties to Duterte and her husband Mans.

“Now, do you also confirm that you have a close relationship with Attorney Carpio? Close relationship this time, not merely acquaintance, close relationship, these are two different things,” said Ligutan. “Yes,” said Antero.

“And you treat Attorney Manases Carpio like a brother, correct?” the prosecutor continued. “Yes, sir,” the lawyer responded.

Play Video

Ligutan traced the money trail linking Carpio and Antero to show the extent of their relationship.

“Mr. Witness, did you ever receive money from Attorney Manases Garpio?” Ligutan asked.

“I am part of his firm, sir. From time to time, I receive some compensation from my professional services, sir,” said Antero.

The inquiry into large credit card purchases is meant to show that the Duterte family lives lavishly, despite claiming a modest lifestyle. This forms only a small part of the remaining article of impeachment.

The prosecution team relied on lawyer Alex Cabrera, an expert witness, to analyze Duterte’s financial records. He estimated that the Vice President had alleged P817 million in undeclared wealth from 2022 to 2025.

Among the transactions in the report are ¥489,000 spent at a restaurant in Ginza, Tokyo, and P256,000 at the Nike Pavilion in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

Antero clarified that the Tokyo purchase was indeed for a meal, and it just so happened that they used Carpio’s card. He said he later paid Carpio for his part of the bill.

Play Video

“The issue in this case is whether P200,000 is an ostentatious [purchase]…. Whether the Vice President and her spouse is leading a modest life. This is central to the allegation of unexplained wealth,” said Ligutan. – Rappler.com

World.title: Ombudsman suspends mayor of Rosario, Cavite, for alleged casino gambling
World.content:
ALLEGED GAMBLING. Rosario, Cavite Mayor Jose Voltaire Ricafrente allegedly left a casino in Bacolod City with four companions and P10,000 worth of winnings.

The 6-month preventive suspension without pay of Mayor Jose Voltaire Ricafrente is a measure to guarantee an unbiased and unhindered administrative investigation, says the Ombudsman

The Office of the Ombudsman ordered on Thursday, November 12, the six-month preventive suspension of Mayor Jose Voltaire Ricafrente of Rosario, Cavite, over his alleged engagement in gambling activities at a casino in Bacolod City.

The order stemmed from a complaint filed by the Field Investigation Office (FIO) of the Office of the Ombudsman, which found that Ricafrente, along with four companions, entered the casino at a hotel on March 14, 2026.

The Rosario mayor allegedly played at a gaming table with P30,000 worth of casino chips and won P10,000 before leaving the casino.

Under Presidential Decree No. 1869 or the PAGCOR Charter and Memorandum Circular No. 6 s. 2016, government personnel are strictly prohibited from entering, staying, or playing in casinos.

“This Office finds sufficient grounds for the issuance of an Order for Preventive Suspension against respondent Municipal Mayor Jose Voltaire Ricafrente, Municipality of Rosario, Province of Cavite, considering that there is strong evidence showing his guilt; the charges against him for Grave Misconduct and Conduct Prejudicial to the Best Interest of the Service may warrant his removal from the service,” the six-page order stated.

Ricafrente will be preventively suspended without pay pending the resolution of the administrative charges against him.

The Ombudsman said a preventive suspension is not a penalty but serves as a measure to guarantee an unbiased and unhindered administrative investigation.

Ricafrente is a close ally of the Revilla dysnasty in Cavite. His municipality is within the Cavite 1st District represented by Jolo Revilla. Jose Voltaire is the son of the late former mayor Jose “Nonong” Ricafrente Jr., who served as provincial administrator when Bong Revilla Jr. was governor.

Rappler has reached out to the municipal government and Ricafrente’s office for a statement on the issue. This article will be updated with his reply. – Rappler.com

World.title: Witness: Romualdez cash inflows not traceable to DPWH, Co, contractors
World.content:
Former Ako Bicol Rep. Zaldy Co (left) and former House Speaker and Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez —File photos

MANILA, Philippines — A financial investigator from the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) said there was a “huge disparity” between the P57 billion in kickbacks the Office of the Ombudsman alleged Leyte Rep. Martin Romualdez had received from flood control projects and the P560 million that entered his bank accounts when he was Speaker.

Lawyer Jan Mark Busa made the disclosure on Thursday during an ongoing bail hearing in Romualdez’s P7.44-billion plunder case before the Sandiganbayan’s Third Division in connection with the kickbacks the former House leader allegedly took from government infrastructure funds in the national budgets from 2022 to 2025.

Romualdez, a cousin of President Marcos, is currently detained at the Quezon City Jail.

Article continues after this 

READ: AMLC files civil forfeiture case vs Romualdez

On questioning by Romualdez’s lawyer Rashel Ann Pomoy, Busa, a prosecution witness, also said none of the funds that had flowed into the former Speaker’s accounts could be traced to the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), to project contractors or to ex-lawmaker Zaldy Co during that period.

Co, who is currently at large, is a coaccused of Romualdez in the plunder case.

READ: Romualdez suspended for 90 days

In his judicial affidavit, Busa said he had looked into a total of 1,951 bank transactions across 35 bank accounts of Romualdez from April 2003 to October 2025. Romualdez resigned as Speaker in September 2025, after Marcos ordered an investigation following the public outrage over the flood control kickback scandal.

Article continues after this 

‘Two major peaks’

Busa said Romualdez received P560 million in his bank accounts when he was Speaker. The inflows included P335 million in check deposits and over P203 million in cash deposits, plus transfers of about P16 million.

Busa cited “two major peaks” in transactions—one from April 2003 to June 2007, before Romualdez entered politics, and the other from 2022 to 2025, during his speakership. He noted that from 2003 to 2007, there were P3.9 billion worth of recorded transactions and P4.5 billion from 2022 to 2025.

Article continues after this 

Romualdez’s bank transactions dropped sharply after he resigned with over P384 million recorded from September 2025 until the end of Busa’s search in October 2025. Transactions are defined as the movement of funds in and out of an account.

Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla disclosed on April 25, 2026, that the Court of Appeals (CA) had frozen Romualdez’s bank accounts.

During Thursday’s hearing, Busa said the AMLC had already filed a civil forfeiture case covering those accounts.

Business interests

Prior to the filing of the civil forfeiture case, Busa said the AMLC had filed an application to access the former Speaker’s bank documents following a referral from the Ombudsman.

During the bail hearing, Pomoy said Romualdez already had “substantial declared financial activity” before he ran for congressman. She cited his business interests in Atlas Consolidated Mining, Lepanto Consolidated Mining, Benguet Corp., BDO Inc., Aboitiz Equity Ventures and Cebu Holdings Inc. Busa agreed.

In response to prosecutor Alexie Jane Tadeo’s questions, Busa noted that the AMLC’s findings did not take into account the cash inflows that were not covered by the banking system.

“These are only the transactions that are captured by the banking system,” Busa said.

Also on Thursday, the AMLC said that the appellate court had frozen the bank accounts and other properties of a lawmaker and a businessman, who is a former government official, based on a complaint filed by the Ombudsman for alleged plunder and corruption in connection with the flood control scandal.

The complaint alleged the grant of exclusive contracts to corporations associated with the lawmaker when the businessman was in government service. The AMLC did not identify the two.

Freeze order

The CA issued the freeze order “after finding probable cause to believe that the lawmaker may have received economic benefits arising from the alleged plunder and violations of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act” and “wrongdoing by the businessman,” the AMLC said.

World.title: DOJ says P50-M bounty for Dela Rosa ‘legal’
World.content:
Justice Secretary Frederick Vida —Photo from DOJ

MANILA, Philippines — Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida on Thursday said the P50-million bounty being offered by the government for any information leading to the arrest of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa is legal, adding that the amount could be funded under confidential activities.

Vida, in an ambush interview, said the reward is meant to gain more information on the senator’s whereabouts. Dela Rosa, who as chief of the Philippine National Police was the lead implementer of former President Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, remains in hiding amid an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court (ICC) against him.

Vida was asked to comment on the issue weeks after Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said the arrest of Bato, who is supposedly under the protection of an unnamed armed group, could lead to a shootout and thousands of killings.

Article continues after this 

According to the justice secretary, the government has become a “laughingstock” because of the timeline of events that led to the escape in May of Dela Rosa from the Senate which had placed him under its protective custody.

READ: Nartatez: PNP getting tips in Dela Rosa manhunt

Vida said that, for his part, his order to the National Bureau of Investigation to implement the arrest warrant against the senator still stands.

“That is one of our obligations that we need to fulfill,” he added.

READ: Hunt for Bato dela Rosa sets 1-week ultimatum, P50-M bounty

Article continues after this 

Peaceful arrest possible

Meanwhile, Gilbert Andres, an ICC-accredited lawyer for drug war victims in The Hague, told the Inquirer that the arrest of Dela Rosa need not be violent and deadly.

“I think the Philippine government has shown before that they can actually implement a peaceful arrest of someone who has an ICC arrest warrant like Mr. Duterte,” Andres said in an interview.

Article continues after this 

He stressed that it is a “challenge” to the Department of Justice, through the NBI, as well as the Department of the Interior and Local Government, through the PNP, to implement the warrant “effectively and efficiently.”

Doing so should be in line with the country’s own law regarding such matters, specifically Republic Act No. 9851 or the Philippine Act on Crimes Against International Humanitarian Law, Genocide, and Other Crimes Against Humanity.

World.title: Chemicals, heat fueled ferry fire; 16 charged
World.content:
In this image, taken from video provided by the Philippine Coast Guard, remains of ferry MV June Aster that caught fire off Palawan province on Thursday Sept. 10, 2026. —Philippine Coast Guard via AP)

MANILA, Philippines — A chemical reaction involving hazardous cargo and intense heat from a malfunctioning engine fueled a ferry fire that killed 77 people off Coron, Palawan, in September, the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) said on Thursday as it confirmed the filing of a criminal complaint against 16 individuals.

BFP spokesperson Fire Supt. Anthony Arroyo told the Inquirer that investigators found calcium hypochlorite, a chemical classified as dangerous cargo, had come into contact with asphalt stored near the vessel’s engine exhaust outlet, triggering the rapid spread of flames and explosions.

The findings followed an investigation into the Sept. 9 fire aboard MV June Aster in the waters off Barangay Marcilla.

Article continues after this 

READ: 63 of 77 MV June Aster fire victims identified; probe ongoing

A document dated Nov. 11 and obtained by the Inquirer showed that the BFP filed a criminal complaint against 16 individuals, including four Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) personnel, before the Office of the City Prosecutor in Manila on Wednesday.

Arroyo said the chemicals were stored close to each other at the rear portion of the vessel’s cargo deck on its starboard side, where intense heat from the engine exhaust contributed to the chemical reaction.

A mechanical failure in the engine further increased the heat, he added. “The two chemicals came into contact, causing a chemical reaction, with heat also contributing,” Arroyo said.

READ: PNP backs task force, vows thorough probe into Palawan ferry blaze

Article continues after this 

The reaction triggered the rapid spread of flames to nearby combustible and flammable materials, accompanied by explosions, he said.

Arroyo clarified that the presence of 5.85 metric tons of calcium hypochlorite aboard the vessel did not automatically mean the chemical alone caused the fire.

Article continues after this 

Instead, investigators identified the interaction between the chemicals and intense heat as factors that accelerated the blaze.

Reckless imprudence

In the criminal complaint if filed before the Manila City Prosecutor’s Office, the BFP charged 16 individuals, four of them PCG personnel, with reckless imprudence resulting in multiple homicide, multiple physical injuries and damage to property under Article 365 of the Revised Penal Code.

The four Coast Guard noncommissioned officers, who were assigned to the PCG substation in Del Pan, Manila, allegedly did not exercise the necessary care, precaution and vigilance during their predeparture inspection of the vessel on Sept. 8.

According to the BFP, the PCG personnel failed to ensure the ferry’s compliance with maritime safety standards before clearing it for departure.

The other respondents included six officers and crew members of MV June Aster, three officers and employees of its operator, Atienza Interisland Ferries Inc., and three officers and employees of Mega Lifters Cargo Handling Corp., a third-party contractor of the Philippine Ports Authority (PPA).

The vessel’s crew allegedly failed to exercise the required care and vigilance in performing their duties involving the ship, its passengers and dangerous cargo.

The ferry operator’s personnel, on the other hand, were cited for alleged lapses in supervising operations and implementing company policies, while the cargo-handling contractor’s employees were accused of failing to exercise the diligence required under its administrative and operational policies.

PPA employee flagged

Separately, the BFP recommended an administrative review of a PPA employee over the entry of the hazardous shipment at its Pasig River terminal on Sept. 3, six days before the fire.

A BFP document obtained by the Inquirer identified the cashier-in-charge at the terminal when the bulk shipment of calcium hypochlorite entered the facility.

Arroyo said dangerous cargo was subject to maximum allowable quantities, although he did not specify the limit applicable to MV June Aster or whether the shipment exceeded it.

World.title: VP team drops 16 bank execs from witness list
World.content:
Members of the defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte at the Senate of the Philippines in Pasay City, in this file photo taken on Oct. 13, 2026. —Inquirer photo/Niño Jesus Orbeta

MANILA, Philippines — The defense in Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial has withdrawn its last witness from Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI), a move that denied prosecutors a chance to ask about bank records that they said could shed light on her alleged dollar accounts.

The ranking BPI executive was dropped from the list after the Vice President’s team also dispensed with 15 other bank officials who had been summoned to testify on her and her husband’s financial records.

Prosecutors noted, with mock dismay, that the defense had yet to directly challenge the allegation that Duterte accumulated P817 million in unexplained wealth, based on a computation of financial forensic expert Alexander Cabrera.

Article continues after this 

READ: Prosecution seeks clarity on VP Duterte’s alleged dollar accounts

They said her legal team chose instead to explain a P205,007 Tokyo dinner and a P256,882.50 Nike shoe purchase in Kuala Lumpur, both charged to the credit card of Duterte’s husband, Manases Carpio.

The witness withdrawn on Thursday was BPI senior vice president Paul Roderick Ysmael. Defense counsel and spokesperson Michael Poa told the Senate impeachment court on Thursday that Ysmael was needed only to authenticate a letter he had written.

Poa explained he had already acknowledged authorship of the letter in open court and that it had also been marked as defense evidence.

READ: Prosec: Defense withdrew BPI exec to prevent ‘Pandora’s box’ opening

Article continues after this 

Prosecutors said they wanted to question the BPI executive about a bank letter indicating that the Vice President had dollar accounts, as well as records that could help clarify the account issue.

“We were surprised. Well, it’s their prerogative. They decided not to call him anymore,” prosecution counsel Benjamin Tolosa Jr. said at a press briefing.

Article continues after this 

House prosecutor Joel Chua quipped that the defense has so far responded to issues only for social media consumption.

Dollar accounts

Private prosecutor James Bryan Ibrahim Alih manifested in court that the prosecution had intended to question Ysmael about BPI records concerning Duterte’s alleged dollar accounts. He cited a bank letter indicating that the Vice President had dollar accounts, which prosecutors said they had not previously seen because the subpoena did not specifically cover dollar accounts.

“Unfortunately, before we had a chance to cross-examine the witness about this dollar account, they dispensed with the testimony, so we were not able to ask about that anymore,” Tolosa said in a posttrial briefing.

Presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero said the defense had the prerogative to choose which witnesses to present. Prosecutors could raise their interpretation of the documents after the defense rested, through rebuttal evidence or a memorandum, but could not substitute their interpretation for records not yet presented to the court.

The BPI account issue resurfaced in early October when Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura testified that Sara and her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, held a joint account at the bank’s Julia Vargas branch in Pasig City. He said P9.1 million was withdrawn over the counter in a single transaction on April 8, 2013, based on a covered transaction report identifying both as account holders.

The account first figured in allegations raised by former Sen. Antonio Trillanes IV during Rodrigo Duterte’s 2016 presidential campaign. Trillanes claimed the former president and his daughter had undeclared bank deposits not reflected in their statements of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALNs), and that accounts linked to them contained as much as P227 million.

Rodrigo Duterte denied having hundreds of millions of pesos in undeclared funds. He acknowledged having BPI accounts but disputed Trillanes’ claims about their balances. He did not sign a bank secrecy waiver sought by Trillanes to allow the accounts to be examined.

Bank witnesses

The 15 other bank officials dropped by the defense on Wednesday were Olivia Barcarse and Alvin Go of BDO Unibank; Cesar Bernard Coloma of BPI; Marino Buban Jr. of EastWest Bank; Joselito Vallada of Landbank; Janella Marie Panlilio of Metrobank; Jose Manuel Jr., Rodel Mediavillo and Mary Ann Candaroma-Morales of PSBank; Joseph Anthony Lopez of Security Bank; and Joselito Banaag, Louiemel Panes, Rogelio Villos Jr., Jayah Deneserie Scalf and Gemma Lynn Del Mundo of UnionBank.

The defense separately dispensed with Quezon City prosecutor Vimar Barcellano after the prosecution agreed to stipulate to the authenticity of the public documents he was expected to identify.

Prosecution spokesperson and Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong said the defense had yet to rebut the computation of financial forensic expert Alexander Cabrera, who placed Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth at P817 million.

“What we were expecting was for the defense to explain the P817 million. They should debunk the P817 million,” Adiong said. “What they showed was only more than P200,000 worth of bill and another P250,000 worth of shoes. If you sum it up, that’s only less than P500,000.”

By the end of Day 43 on Thursday, the defense had presented six witnesses over four hearing days but had yet to directly challenge Cabrera’s estimate.

Dinner bill

Its fifth witness, lawyer Anel Martin Antero, testified about a P205,007.29 dinner at Ginza Inakaya in Tokyo on March 19, 2025, charged to Carpio’s credit card.

Antero said he and 10 friends, including Carpio, shared the cost. They used Carpio’s card because some had run out of cash and agreed to reimburse him. Antero said he paid 40,000 yen and, to his knowledge, all 11 diners contributed.

“We all contributed. It just so happened that the credit card of Atty. Mans was used to pay,” he said.

Antero said he was “very much surprised” by the bill but admitted the group had no photograph of the dinner or documents proving the repayments.

During cross-examination, he acknowledged being a longtime friend of Duterte and Carpio, having worked at Carpio’s law firm and being part of their legal teams.

Private prosecutor Amando Virgil Ligutan asked whether Antero recalled receiving P580,000 from Carpio in July 2020, as indicated in an AMLC report. Antero said he could not recall receiving the amount.

Ligutan also questioned him about a social media post calling the impeachment complaint “flimsy.” Antero later said he would not lie for Carpio or Duterte, citing his oath as a witness and his obligations as a lawyer.

Shoe purchase

The defense’s sixth witness, Chadrin Parian, testified about Carpio’s P256,882.50 purchase of Nike shoes in Kuala Lumpur in 2025 for members of Elite Philippines, a youth basketball team. Parian, a parent of one of the players, said Carpio treated the young athletes and their parents after the team won a competition in Malaysia.

Parian said the children and their parents “deserve” the shoes, noting that not all families could afford to buy them.

Private prosecutor Reynaldo Robles questioned whether the purchase was consistent with the “simple and modest living” expected of a public official’s family. Parian said he could not comment on Carpio’s thinking but believed the recipients deserved the gifts.

Lead defense counsel Sheila Sison asked the court to cancel Friday’s hearing because the team had no remaining witnesses scheduled for the week. Escudero granted the request.

Sison said the defense had around eight to 10 witnesses left to present when the trial resumes on Nov. 19. —With reports from Gabriel Pabico Lalu and Keith Clores

World.title: Basilan judge slain in Zambo gun attack
World.content:
BASILAN RTC Judge Joseph Wee Sit —IBP ZamBaSulta Chapter/FB

PAGADIAN CITY, ZAMBOANGA DEL SUR, Philippines — A judge in Basilan province was shot and killed in Zamboanga City on Thursday morning, drawing widespread condemnation from lawyers and provincial officials, with the Supreme Court among those mourning and demanding justice for his death.

Joseph Wee Sit, presiding judge of Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 2 in Isabela City, Basilan, would have turned 39 on Nov. 21.

Lt. Col. Shellamie Chang, Zamboanga Peninsula regional police spokesperson, said that Wee Sit was driving toward the Tumaga flea market around 5:25 a.m. when two gunmen on a white motorcycle pulled up beside his vehicle and opened fire. They fled toward the Tumaga Bypass Road after the attack.

Article continues after this 

READ: Supreme Court looking into killing of Basilan RTC judge

Policemen responded to the scene after receiving a report from a concerned citizen. They took the judge to a nearby hospital but doctors pronounced him dead at 6:30 a.m.

P2-M bounty

Brig. Gen. Elmer Ragay, PRO-9 director, immediately created a special investigation task group to track down the suspects and investigate the motive for the attack on the judge, who was known to handle controversial cases.

Last August, Wee Sit ordered the arrest of a town mayor and several others in Basilan for their alleged involvement in the killing of three persons hours before balloting opened for the midterm elections on May 12, 2025.

“We will exhaust all lawful means to identify and apprehend those responsible for this crime,” Ragay said in a statement. “We will pursue every lead, strengthen coordination among our operating units, and ensure that those responsible are held accountable under the law.”

Article continues after this 

Zamboanga City Mayor Khymer Adan Olaso offered a cash reward of P2 million for credible information leading to the identification and arrest of the suspects.

“This senseless act of violence is deeply disturbing and has no place in a city that values peace, justice, and the rule of law,” Olaso told reporters on Thursday.

Article continues after this 

He said P1.5 million of the bounty will come from his personal funds, while the remaining P500,000 was pooled by concerned citizens.

Committed lawyer

Born in Zamboanga City in 1987, Wee Sit, fondly called Anjo, studied law at Western Mindanao State University and was admitted to the bar in 2015. He served as prosecutor and later as public attorney before his appointment to the judiciary on Sept. 23, 2025.

Though his time on the bench was brief, his commitment to serving the public and upholding the law will not be forgotten, the Supreme Court said in a statement, extending its condolences to the victim’s family, friends and colleagues.

Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda has directed the Office of the Court Administrator to personally reach out to the victim’s family and ensure that the judiciary extends the necessary financial and other assistance during this difficult time.

The high court, through the Office of the Judiciary Marshals, said it is working closely with law enforcement authorities to investigate the incident and identify those responsible.

In 2023, the Supreme Court formed the Office of the Judiciary Marshals to investigate the unresolved killings of judges. The judiciary marshals are also tasked to probe corruption allegedly committed by justices, judges and other court officials.

‘Blow to judicial system’

“The killing of Judge Wee Sit is a painful reminder of the dangers faced by those who serve in our courts. No judge should have to fear for their life simply for doing their duty,” the high court said.

“When judges are threatened or attacked, it is not only their safety that is at stake, but also the ability of our courts to deliver justice freely and independently,” it added.

The Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP) also condemned the killing, calling on the Philippine National Police, the National Bureau of Investigation, and all concerned agencies to make the case a matter of the highest priority.

“This was not merely an attack on a judge. It was an attack on the rule of law and the independence of the judiciary. Violence against members of the Bench threatens the administration of justice and cannot be allowed to breed fear, intimidation, or impunity,” the IBP national directorate said.

Lawyer Quirino Esguerra Jr., IBP governor for Western Mindanao, stressed that Wee Sit’s murder “was a direct assault on the country’s justice system.”

“We are very sad [about] this news. The senseless killing of Judge Joseph Wee Sit is a big blow not only to the judicial system, but also an attack [on] the very institution that dispenses justice,” Esguerra said in a statement.

Chilling strike

Basilan Gov. Mujiv Hataman shared Esguerra’s sentiment and urged law enforcers to hold accountable not only the gunmen but also the masterminds behind the killing.

“When a judge is assassinated because of their work, it is not just a life that is taken. It challenges the very system of justice and the ability of our courts to perform their duties without fear,” Hataman said.

The Union of Peoples’ Lawyers in Mindanao described the attack as “a direct, chilling strike against the independence of the judiciary and the rule of law in Mindanao.”

“No magistrate should ever have to pay with their life for upholding the law,” it said. —With reports from Cong Corrales and Kathleen De Villa

World.title: Negros bishop leads push for antidynasty campaign
World.content:
San Carlos (Negros Occidental) Bishop Gerardo Alminaza —Contributed photo

BACOLOD CITY, NEGROS OCCIDENTAL, Philippines — The Diocese of San Carlos in Negros Occidental province is seeking to enliven efforts to legislate a measure against dynastic control of political power in the country, calling on clergy, Catholic schools, and lay organizations to intensify the collection of signatures for a people’s campaign to stop political dynasties.

In a circular letter on Nov. 11, San Carlos Bishop Gerardo Alminaza urged parish priests, mission station leaders, and diocesan heads across Negros Occidental and Negros Oriental provinces to help gather at least 38,084 signatures for Dapat Isa Lang (D1L) People’s Initiative to meet the local 5-percent benchmark across the diocese’s three legislative districts.

The D1L initiative seeks to gather 7.5 million signatures nationwide to trigger a referendum that would prohibit political dynasties, fulfilling a mandate under the 1987 Constitution, Alminaza pointed out.

Article continues after this 

READ: SC to Congress: ‘Injustice’ to delay anti-dynasty law

Immediate target

To qualify for a national referendum in 2027, the campaign must hit its target by Jan. 30, 2027, or by July 30, 2027, to align with the 2028 general elections, he said.

Alminaza, in his circular, said nationwide sign-ups stood at 22,244 as of Sunday midnight.

While far from the ultimate target, he noted a 175-percent weekly jump in digital signatures and a 137-percent increase in new website users—the highest weekly growth since the campaign site launched on Sept. 30.

The initiative’s immediate national target is reaching 100,000 signatures to build broader momentum, Alminaza said.

Article continues after this 

Within the diocese’s jurisdiction, sign-ups reported as of Nov. 10 totaled 76, against the 38,084 benchmark. Some 36 signatures were gathered in the first district of Negros Oriental against a target of 14,602; 30 in the first district of Negros Occidental against a target of 12,871; and 10 in the second district of Negros Occidental against a target of 10,611, he noted.

Alminaza stressed that the initiative is nonpartisan and directed against systemic governance issues rather than specific political families or parties.

Article continues after this 

Citing post-2025 election data referenced by the Supreme Court, he noted that political clans account for 19 of 24 senators, 212 of 254 district representatives, 71 of 82 provincial governors, and all elected mayors in Metro Manila.

The bishop also highlighted research linking dynastic concentration to persistent poverty incidence in the Visayas and Mindanao.

To drive local action, Alminaza directed parishes to set up D1L information desks following Sunday and daily Masses, incorporate the campaign’s themes into homilies and formation sessions, and mobilize volunteers to assist voters in completing the digital petition process at D1L.org.

The diocese framed the push as a concrete observance of the upcoming World Day of the Poor on Nov. 15.

Church leaders stressed that participation must remain strictly voluntary, with volunteers instructed to guide voters through the submission of voter location details, signature images, and identity verifications without coercion.

World.title: BARMM chief order: Prioritize ex-Moro fighters in low-tier jobs
World.content:
Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua —Office of the BARMM Chief Minister

COTABATO CITY, BARMM, Philippines — Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua has ordered ministries and agencies in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) to give priority to veterans of the Moro revolution from the ranks of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) and the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) in filling the lowest-paid positions in the regional government.

Bangsamoro Labor and Employment Minister Kitem Kadatuan Jr. said that Macacua issued the guidelines during a recent meeting with top officials of the new BARMM government, which was installed on Oct. 30.

In ordering the preference for hiring MILF and MNLF members in low-tiered positions, Macacua cited Article 305 of the Bangsamoro Civil Service Code, mandating that 30 percent of entry level plantilla positions, with Salary Grade (SG) 9 and below, shall be allocated to mujahideen/mujahidat, as the fronts’ male and female fighters are called.

Article continues after this 

READ: Macacua names new BARMM Cabinet members

They may also be hired as temporary appointees regardless of the number of applicants who are civil service eligible for positions under SG 9 and below categories. The starting pay for SG 1 to SG 9 ranges from P14,061 to P23,226 per month, subject to applicable taxes and other deductions.

Gratitude

Macacua headed the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces, the MILF’s armed wing, until he was removed last September by the front’s central committee for alleged insubordination.

Kadatuan said the hiring preference serves as a way for the regional government to express gratitude for those who sacrificed life and limb for the Bangsamoro cause.

He noted that many former Moro rebels are not college graduates, but they could be qualified for the low-tier jobs.

Article continues after this 

Candidates for senior posts must still meet the regular qualification standards and go through the normal appointment process, Kadatuan pointed out.

He said job order workers hired during the Bangsamoro transition period will be allowed to finish their contracts under the regular government but are not assured of immediate rehiring as ministry officials will review each case against the office’s staffing needs. —With a report from Edwin O. Fernandez

World.title: Cops bust drug suspect in Lanao del Norte; P374,000 in meth, gun seized
World.content:
POLICE INVENTORY Law enforcers conduct an inventory and marking of seized evidence, including a firearm and suspected illicit substances, following a police operation in Tubod, Lanao del Norte, on Wednesday. —Photo courtesy of Police Regional Office 10

CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY, Philippines — An alleged high-value drug trafficker known as “Boss Dexter” was arrested after yielding P374,000 worth of suspected crystal meth and a loaded handgun during a police sting operation in Tubod town, Lanao del Norte, on Wednesday morning, Nov. 11.

The 43-year-old local resident was cornered by operatives of the Regional Police Drug Enforcement Unit (RPDEU-10) and local police in Barangay Poblacion at around 9:25 a.m., according to a press advisory released on Thursday by the Police Regional Office-10 (PRO-10) based in this city.

During the arrest, authorities seized some 55 grams of suspected shabu concealed in a coin pouch and the P500 marked bill used in the buy-bust transaction.

Article continues after this 

READ: P3.6-M ‘shabu’ seized from alleged Lanao Sur big-time drug peddler

Police also seized a caliber .45 pistol loaded with four live rounds from the suspect following a search incidental to the arrest.

Brig. Gen. Nestor Babagay Jr., PRO-10 director, commended the operating units, noting that the arrest underscores their intelligence-driven push to dismantle local drug networks.

“We will continue to go after high-value individuals… This operation demonstrates our commitment to pursuing those involved in the drug trade and ensuring that they are brought before the law,” Babagay stated in the advisory.

The suspect is currently detained at the Tubod Municipal Police Station, facing charges for violations of the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act and the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act.

The seized contraband has been forwarded to the regional crime laboratory for forensic examination. /cb

World.title: Myanmar Faces Year of Blackouts as Regime Admits 30% Power Shortfall
World.content:
Myanmar’s rotating power cuts will remain in place through 2027, with generation expected to meet only 70 percent of national demand, Deputy Energy Minister Aye Kyaw announced Wednesday.

Addressing the regime’s rubber-stamp parliament, he said next summer’s 24-hour electricity demand is forecast at 5,010 MW, while generation capacity is only 3,540 MW.

“That’s why we need to continue the load shedding measures,” he said.

Despite having the poorest electricity access in the region, Myanmar made significant progress in grid connectivity under the National League for Democracy’s 15-year National Electrification Plan in 2015. By 2020, more than half of households had electricity access, and the NLD’s World Bank-backed plan aimed to achieve nationwide electrification by 2030.

However, the plan was scrapped after the 2021 coup, and regime mismanagement has since triggered rolling power outages across the country.

The World Bank says reliable supply has dropped sharply since the military takeover, affecting nearly half of connected households — with 41.6 percent receiving only enough electricity for basic lighting and phone charging, and 9.1 percent getting no electricity at all.

It blames the deepening generation crisis on the suspension of LNG power plants, declining domestic gas production, hydropower stress, infrastructure damage, and stalled investment.

In response, the regime reintroduced nationwide rolling blackouts, leaving residents in even major cities struggling to manage households and livelihoods.

“We have to be ready to fill up the water, cook meals, and iron our clothes the moment the power comes back on,” Ko Thant Zin from Insein Township in the suburbs of Yangon told the Irrawaddy.

He said the electricity supply rotates between four hours on and four hours off.

“Under the civilian government, the roads were bright with lights. Now, I have to open my eyes wide to see the way ahead while driving at night,” he commented.

The deputy energy minister told citizens to install solar panels if they want a reliable supply. However, import curbs and surging prices have put solar options out of reach for most urban residents.

“Forget about solar panels, most people can’t even afford a portable power pack,” a resident of downtown Yangong’s Botahtaung Township told The Irrawaddy. “Prices have been skyrocketing because of import restrictions.”

He added that power cuts would cause major suffering during the El Niño heatwave forecast for November through January.

“I can’t imagine how we will get through next summer,” he said, reacting to the rationing announcement. “It will be especially tough for young children and the elderly.”

Demand driven by outages has seen the price of solar panels surge to a record high. Yangon residents said a household solar power system now costs at least 10 million kyats (around US $4,760), putting it beyond the reach of ordinary families.

Last month, Yangon City authorities mandated that all commercial projects and high-rise buildings must install solar power systems to operate elevators and emergency lighting, as part of a nationwide push for solar amid deepening power blackouts.

The World Bank says chronic power shortages remain one of the main constraints on Myanmar’s economy, limiting its recovery and keeping poverty persistently high.

The deputy energy minister also announced plans to develop two 55 MW small-modular-reactors in cooperation with Russia’s atomic agency, ROSATOM, starting in fiscal 2028-29. The project is slated for completion in fiscal 2035-36 but locations have yet to be announced.

World.title: Three Years After Operation 1027, Hopang Transformed Under Wa Rule
World.content:
Friday marks three years since Hopang in the Wa Self-Administered Zone experienced its first taste of the joint ethnic offensive known as Operation 1027, when drones deployed by the Brotherhood Alliance bombed a monastery sheltering retreating Myanmar military personnel from nearby Kunlong base.

For the Myanmar military, which had controlled Hopang for decades, the drone strike was an early warning that its grip on the town was nearing an end. For the United Wa State Army (UWSA), it presented an opportunity to gain one of the most important towns in Wa territory without firing a shot.

Less than two months after the Nov. 13 drone attack, forces of the Brotherhood Alliance—which grouped the Arakan Army, Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army (MNDAA) and Ta’ang National Liberation Army (TNLA)—and allied groups entered Hopang with little resistance. Rather than holding the town themselves, they quickly handed it over to their ally, the UWSA.

Operation 1027, which inflicted one of the most devastating military setbacks in the Myanmar military’s history, had begun on Oct. 27, 2023, in Chinshwehaw, a border town just 8 km from Hopang. Just 19 km away, Kunlong, a key town on a China-Myanmar trade route, also fell after sustained drone attacks by alliance forces.

As Kunlong collapsed, its commander, officers and wounded soldiers fled to Hopang.

“A battalion commander and a soldier entered the monastery building and pleaded for shelter,” recalled a witness who was in the compound. “They told the abbot they had been under drone attacks for four days, and had only managed to retreat after receiving supporting fire.”

That same night, drones struck the monastery.

For Hopang residents, who had watched the fighting around Kunlong from hilltop pagodas, the attack on the monastery signaled that war was coming closer. By the next morning, many were fleeing the town, leaving their homes and shops behind.

Some local drivers found themselves ferrying displaced families back and forth, while others stayed behind to guard their properties. Residents feared not only a potential urban battle similar to the fighting in Kunlong, but also the prospect of Myanmar military airstrikes.

One restaurant owner recalled watching looters load crates of beer from his shop onto vehicles through CCTV cameras while he was fleeing.

Among those who fled were a monk who was injured in the November 13 drone attack, as well as health workers from a public hospital in Hopang.

Hopang was home to a military battalion and a police station, but all the surrounding towns including Kunlong and Chinshwehaw were controlled by the Brotherhood Alliance. At this point, Hopang was effectively isolated.

When MNDAA troops entered Hopang in early January 2024, the remaining military and police units reportedly surrendered with little resistance. Under a prior arrangement between the MNDAA and the UWSA, control of the town was then transferred to the Wa army.

Unlike Lashio, Laukkai, Chinshwehaw or Kunlong, Hopang largely escaped major battle damage. Yet residents say the town has since undergone a different kind of transformation, one increasingly shaped by Chinese capital and Wa administration.

The ethnically diverse town, home to Shan, Wa, Bamar, Kachin, Ta’ang and other communities, was once known for its Buddhist, Christian and traditional ethnic festivals. Today, residents say casinos, bars, hotels, massage parlors and prostitution-related businesses funded by Chinese investors have proliferated.

Some residents also complain of heavy taxation and a justice system that includes public executions, practices rarely seen under previous administrations.

The yuan now dominates much of the local economy, with residents increasingly pricing goods in the Chinese currency rather than kyats. In the healthcare arena, expensive Chinese-run private hospitals have emerged alongside the only public hospital.

Over the past three years, rumors have repeatedly surfaced that the UWSA will return Hopang to the regime. Residents say they see no sign that this is imminent, however.

The town, which participated in the 2010, 2015 and 2020 elections, did not take part in the regime-organized 2025 poll and is absent from the list of constituencies scheduled to be put to a vote in additional elections scheduled for April 2027.

Recently, regime Defense Minister and peace negotiator Lieutenant General Yar Pyae visited Panghsang, the UWSA headquarters. There was no indication that Hopang’s status was discussed during his meetings with Wa leaders, however.

While the UWSA remained officially neutral during Operation 1027, it emerged among the campaign’s biggest beneficiaries. Without openly joining the offensive, it gained full control of Hopang and Panlong, while also securing partial control along with the Myanmar military over Tangyan, a strategically important town on the route to Lashio, the largest town in northern Shan.

Three years after the first drone bombs fell on Hopang, the town has changed beyond recognition for longtime residents.

During Operation 1027, the MNDAA and TNLA went on to seize almost the whole of northern Shan State including the capital Lashio and all vital trade routes with China.

However, under strong Chinese pressure, in 2025 the ethnic armies were forced to halt fighting the Myanmar military and hand back several liberated towns to the regime.

World.title: Myanmar’s Coup President Barred From Upcoming 49th ASEAN Summit
World.content:
The Philippines announced Wednesday that Myanmar regime leaders remain barred from joining the 49th ASEAN summit and high-level meetings in Manila from November 15 to 17, upholding a ban imposed after the 2021 military coup.

Myanmar will instead be represented by the Director-General of its ASEAN affairs department, according to a statement issued by Manila’s Department of Foreign Affairs.

“We welcome this official confirmation that there is no place [at the summit] for junta leader Min Aung Hlaing,” Khin Ohmar, a prominent Myanmar democracy activist and founder of the Progressive Voice human rights foundation, told The Irrawaddy.

“ASEAN made the right decision in line with its principles. We have been demanding that no junta member be permitted to join the summit.”

She added that ASEAN would have sacrificed its credibility and responsibility to the people of Myanmar by inviting the junta leader, who faces a genocide ruling at the international court later this month.

Confirmation that the ban remains in place came after domestic and international rights groups warned the regional bloc against legitimizing a regime that is intensifying violence against civilians.

On Monday, the Special Advisory Council for Myanmar (SAC-M) and ASEAN Parliamentarians for Human Rights urged regional leaders “to immediately confirm” that Min Aung Hlaing and his junta cohorts would be excluded from the summit.

It also called on ASEAN leaders to adopt “measurable benchmarks for compliance” with the bloc’s Five-Point Consensus (5PC), along with “a series of escalating punitive steps” if the junta continues to defy the peace plan.

Regime leaders were barred from regional summits for failing to implement the April 2021 consensus, including an immediate end to violence and constructive dialogue with the opposition.

The regime largely ignored the 5PC before formally rejecting it in a July 2026 vote by its rubber-stamp parliament. However, it continues to pay lip service to the plan.

During his latest talks with ASEAN special envoy Theresa Lazaro in Naypyitaw in October, Foreign Minister Tin Maung Swe claimed the regime was implementing the 5PC “without compromising its national interests and sovereignty in accordance with its own roadmaps and objectives.”

The UN reports that at least 8,384 civilians have been killed by regime forces since the coup, in an escalating military campaign that has also left over 4 million displaced. Meanwhile, nearly 23,000 political prisoners remain in detention, including deposed democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi.

However, ASEAN members began bilateral engagement with the regime after it rebranded in civilian clothing in April following elections widely condemned as a sham. Since then, coup leader-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing has been invited on official visits to bloc members Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia and Malaysia.

Both Malaysia—once a vocal critic of the regime—and Thailand drew widespread condemnation from rights groups for hosting the junta leader.

Both nations defended the visits as pragmatic re-engagement in search of solutions to challenges they face, such as refugee repatriation for Malaysia and transborder issues for Thailand.

Critics have warned that bi-lateral engagement may sway a collective ASEAN decision to reintegrate the regime.

However, the move to uphold the summit ban marks a major setback for a junta desperate for legitimacy on the international stage.

“This is a huge blow to the junta. I am sure it has not expected this kind of decision,” Khin Ohmar commented. “It also signals that the junta’s election farce failed to confer legitimacy, since even those advocating its return to the international stage want to avoid being seen as complicit in its violence.”

World.title: Myanmar Junta Seeks Record Military Budget as Millions Struggle With Poverty
World.content:
The Myanmar regime plans to increase the military budget to a record high for the 2026-27 fiscal year, even as approximately one-third of the country’s population lives in poverty.

Since 2021, the regime has been waging war against several established ethnic armed organizations as well as newly emerged resistance forces, including the People’s Defense Force, across the country, spending a large portion of its budget on military expenses.

Last Thursday, the regime’s rubber-stamp Union Parliament (Pyidaungsu Hluttaw), where the military-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party (USDP) and its allies hold a majority of seats, debated a supplementary budget allocation bill.

The proposed allocation would bring total defense spending to 10.53 trillion kyats (US$5.01 billion), combining the initial 2026-27 fiscal year estimate of 7.95 trillion kyats with a supplementary grant of 2.58 trillion kyats.

Chit Swe, an Upper House lawmaker representing Ayeyarwady Region’s Constituency No. 11 and first deputy chair of the Joint Public Accounts Committee, urged parliament on November 5 to approve the regime’s proposed budgets, including the record-high military budget.

He said the committee had only eight days to verify the budget, with some items requiring ground observation, and that at least two weeks would be needed for verification.

If the supplementary allocations are approved, the budget deficit is projected to surge from 8.98 trillion kyats to 11.41 trillion kyats, he stated.

The military budget has surged continuously since the coup.

Under the last civilian government, led by ousted democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi, defense expenditure for the 2020-21 fiscal year stood at just 3.4 trillion kyats.

In the 2023-24 fiscal year, it increased to over 5.6 trillion kyats. Although defense expenditures for the remaining years were not officially released, the current budget figures show that spending has nearly doubled compared to 2023-24.

Meanwhile, approximately 17.9 million people are “multidimensionally poor”, while two-thirds of the population are either poor or at risk, according to a UN Development Programme (UNDP) report published on October 8.

After five years of military regime rule, Myanmar people continue to suffer from soaring prices of basic goods and living costs amid the civil war, and face personal safety and security concerns.

Although the budget is still in draft form, the proposed military expenditure has drawn widespread criticism from the public.

“The budgets that should be spent on the country’s education, health, social welfare and nation-building are instead being used to kill the people,” said Naung Yoe, a military defector who now works with the Myanmar Defense & Security Institute (MDSI), a research institute.

According to the MDSI, the Directorate of Defense Industries, which manufactures ammunition and aerial bombs used in the regime’s indiscriminate attacks, has consumed the largest share of the military’s budget since the coup.

“It is deeply tragic and unfortunate,” he said.

World.title: Mideast Crisis Fuels Oil Conflict in Myanmar’s Heartland
World.content:
Myanmar’s small-scale oil prospectors are under fire from all sides as rebels and the military battle to capture a cottage industry that is becoming increasingly lucrative amid the ongoing Middle East crisis.

“As long as we work here, bad luck can kill us,” said Htun Aung, a worker on an oil well in Myanmar’s arid heartlands.

“But if the reality of death is hard to face, then making a living is even harder,” said the 52-year-old, speaking under a pseudonym for security reasons.

Myanmar imports 90 percent of its fuel oil, official figures show, making it particularly vulnerable to supply issues caused by the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

But the central region of Magwe hosts a hardscrabble industry of domestic prospectors manning grimy derricks that squelch up crude oil in humble quantities.

The area is dubbed “Anyar Dubai,” associating the Anyar or central dry zone landscape with the oil boom emirate, despite the pitiable US$50 per week earned by workers like Htun Aung who spend their days drenched in foul crude run-off.

With prices at Myanmar’s petrol pumps nearly double what they were in late February, the underground “black gold” is a coveted prize.

“We just want to live in peace,” said Htun Aung. “But now they strike from one side and the others strike from the other—they keep attacking each other.”

“We’ve had to flee three, four, five times already,” he added. “We run here, we run there. We fill up our motorbikes with fuel and run again.”

Digging in

Pro-democracy rebels claim to have controlled oil fields in Magwe’s Myaing Township since 2023.

They patrol the dusty territory in a westward crook of the Irrawaddy River in ragtag columns and outfitted with rocket-propelled grenades, flak jackets, tote bags and flip-flops.

Air and drone strikes in Myaing so far this year have already exceeded 2025’s total, according to ACLED, a monitor that estimates more than 100,000 people have died since the 2021 putsch.

Rebels shelter in foxholes, camouflaged among thousands of oil wells dug in an unregulated practice dating back centuries.

Engine winches chug day and night, plunging plumbing tubes dozens of meters down boreholes before dragging them up filled with crude oil slurry.

Prospectors pay landowners up to $3,500 to lease a spot to drill, one veteran said, with no guarantee they will hit oil.

Some wells yield dribbles while others gush, filling tarpaulin-lined pits and barrels with oil hauled off to improvised refineries for processing into petrol and diesel.

“Anyar Dubai” has been “going viral” for its plentiful supply, said rebel spokesman Pyae Phyo Kyaw, at a time when regime-held areas are rationing petrol.

He touted recent offensives fending off military advances but admitted being battered by counter-attacks.

“We see it primarily as an attempt to destroy what has been a strong supply route and source of revenue for us,” said the 35-year-old.

Myanmar’s military could not be reached for comment.

In September, the military claimed a month-long military operation captured over 130 wells in Myaing and 735 more in neighboring Pakokku Township.

Black market

Scores of pro-democracy factions and ethnic armed groups are fighting the military.

As the war grinds on, all sides battle to fill their war chests with the tax or trade of natural resources: gem mines, rare earth mineral deposits, gold or teak.

Oil projects are not generally contested.

The major ones are under staunch military guard, and on-the-books output is tiny by international standards at around 6,000 barrels a day last year, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

But the artisanal fields are coveted by rebels precisely because of their modest size, according to Thomas Kean, a Myanmar consultant for the International Crisis Group.

“Part of the reason why they’re significant is because they’re not globally significant,” he said, explaining that they are small enough to thrive under the radar yet big enough to fund guerrillas.

Spiking oil prices may not directly drive conflict, said Kean, highlighting a broader military campaign to evict rebels from heartland footholds by squeezing revenue sources.

But as the spoils of war become more profitable, the stakes get higher.

“We’re talking about millions of barrels a year coming out of these oil fields,” he added. “With global prices what they are, that’s a significant amount of money.”

World.title: Shan State’s Scam Industry Expands Under Protection of Regime-Aligned Militias
World.content:
More than two years after high-profile anti-regime military offensives shattered many of Myanmar’s most notorious scam enclaves near the Chinese border, cyber-fraud syndicates have metastasized across the interior of Shan State, the country’s largest state.

Rather than wiping out the illicit multi-billion-dollar industry, the fall of Kokang’s capital, Laukkai, in January 2024 triggered an influx of scammers deeper into Myanmar—chiefly into Shan State’s interior and Karen State in the country’s south.

By mid-2026, cyber-scam syndicates had expanded across more than 63 percent of Shan State’s 55 townships, establishing footholds in at least 35 of them. This assessment is based on official enforcement and crackdown data published by the military regime’s Ministry of Information, alongside reports from four ethnic armed organizations (EAOs)—the United Wa State Army (UWSA), the National Democratic Alliance Army (NDAA), the Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army (MNDAA) and the Ta’ang National Liberation Army (TNLA).

The entrenchment of telecom fraud comes as Shan State continues to bear the brunt of decades of civil war. Observers point out that these conditions have fostered an acute crisis in which the unchecked proliferation of scam syndicates not only expands organized crime networks, but also threatens local socioeconomic stability and lures local young people into the illicit economy.
